Paint my universe in your colors

by reddishues

Summary

"Why would you show up here in your nurse uniform?"
"Wouldn't dare to miss our meeting."
The child stared at Mydei for a second, before pointing at Phainon. "Mydei, he's funny, can we keep him?"

Or, Mydei accidentally adopts a child and a certain white-haired, blue-eyed nurse keeps on running into him and lighting up his world with vibrant colors again.

Notes

“Stay here for a bit then, we're going to sleep together,” he told him, with a kind and patient voice, then ruffled his hair lovingly. “So I can protect you,” he poked his nose playfully, “from all kinds of monsters.”
“Really?”
“Mhm, all kinds of evildoers will meet their end before they ever get to you, as long as I'm here.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.html:
Screams and cries filled Mydei’s ears, some desperate, some asking for help, some the last prayers of the ones too far gone to have a chance to be saved. He looked around him, a land set ablaze from who knows what, and a lot others trying to help to get the civilians living there to a safer place to treat their injuries.

That was often one of the mild scenarios he'd seen during his years as a firefighter, but it didn't make it any easier. Somehow, this fire seemed way too spread out for it to be a gas leak or accidental, but they luckily got out almost everyone.

He ventured into the last room, where the fire was more intense, and most likely the place it started from. It was hard to breathe, even at floor level, but he heard a cry, and he couldn't stop himself from trying to save whoever was in there. He quickly scanned the room and heard a few sobs not too far away from him, then saw a child trembling on the ground, almost spasming with every sob. He moved closer and dragged him out of the room, making sure not to let him go.

Usually, children his age either yelled and pleaded to save their parents, or they were scared, but this kid did neither. He just trembled, terrified, not even reaching out for someone to hold. He was crying, but he didn't even react when he picked him up, almost as if he was way too terrified of something that his eyes couldn't see to worry about the fire that almost killed him.

In the end, he was able to get him out of the building, albeit with some difficulties, but his state was the same. He was trembling so much that he couldn't even stand up, and, at that point, leaving him alone in a crowded area to let him get treated felt more like a death sentence than a helping hand. Quickly shuffling through his options, Mydei ultimately decided to keep him in his arms, letting his tiny hands grab onto the hem of his orange uniform.

“Hey,” he called out at first, without much success. He decided to gently tilt his head towards him, finally meeting his gaze, and asked again, “Hey, baby, can you look at me?”

The kid blinked a few times, most likely while still processing what just happened, and he closed his fist around his uniform, before he bursted out crying. It wasn’t a normal cry, it was almost painful and desperate, cutting through the air like a deep red and black slash of a scythe. Just after a few seconds, the cries morphed into terrified yells into his chest, and he couldn’t take it anymore.

He held him closer, letting his head rest on his shoulder, gently moving him up and down, ever so slightly, to try and help soothe him, even by the tiniest amount. He could feel his hands holding onto his shirt, his hecting breaths calming down and tiny sniffs and sobs replacing the desperation that shook his fragile, little body so violently.

Mydei turned his head towards him slowly and whispered with a warm voice, “You're safe. It’s all over, you’ll be fine.”

The kid nodded in acknowledgement, but still buried his head in his shoulder, starting to silently cry again. Mydei let him, fully aware that now he needed to let his emotions unwind and force himself to feel everything.

“Mydei,” his colleague called out, catching his attention. He turned towards him, without putting down the kid in his arms. “Is that child the only one you rescued from that room?”

“Yeah, most of the room was completely on fire. Furniture fell down and there was a lot of smoke. It’s a miracle the kid didn’t get caught in an accident before I could get out.” He answered, diligently describing the room he was met with, before he could grab the only person who was still alive out of it. He sighed, shifting the child sitting on his arm to a more comfortable position for both.

His colleague nodded, before glancing towards the child. Mydei knew that look, unfortunately, and it often meant that someone died and they couldn’t save everyone. With the way he was looking at the kid, he already knew what he was about to say, and he gestured to not utter a word of it. At least, not there.

Nodding, he walked away and left them alone again, going to check on the rest of the victims and how the situation was continuing to unfold.

Mydei looked around him, checking if there were people with grave injuries, but it looked like most of it were a few slight burns on their skin and fear that had to lower itself down to a normal, bearable level.

With a swift movement, the child crying on his shoulder lifted his head up and finally looked at him again, with teary, red, exhausted eyes. The sight wasn't something he was unfamiliar with, it happened before already, but he never saw a child so terrified that he didn't even seem to notice he was about to die from a fire so big. He had his theories, but he wanted to talk to him for a while first, both to calm him down and see if his parents dying in that same fire was a tragedy or a blessing.

“Can you stand up?” He asked, with the gentlest tone he could master. It apparently worked, because he nodded and let him put him on the ground, without ever letting his gaze off of him.

Mydei smiled at him and crouched down, offering him a hand. “I'll stay here, don't worry.” He reassured him, even if a little hesitant. The child was still trembling, even if it was less than before, but he was still worried.

Maybe he was cold , he thought. 

“Are you cold? Do you want a blanket?” He asked then, at least expecting a gesture with his head to indicate an answer, but that wasn't what happened.

Instead, he looked at him with his big, honey colored irises full of guilt and regret.

He was so short and thin that he didn't even know if he understood what those two words meant , that seeing him display them so quickly almost broke his heart.

By that point, he needed to know if his suspects were true, because, if they were, he'd have taken this child home and raised him himself. He couldn't stand seeing a child that barely knew how to form words so utterly broken and terrified of the world around him.

“What’s your name?” He moved to ask suddenly, startling him slightly.

“Astraea…” He answered, a little shyly. He took a deep breath, before he could whisper, “What's yours?”

He smiled, moving to kneel in front of him. “Mydei.” He watched, as Astraea obviously wanted to hug him again, but he had to refuse, for the moment. It broke his heart seeing him like that, but he needed a few answers. “Can you tell me something? You have to be completely honest with me.”

He quickly nodded, now visibly more focused on him and what he was saying. Mydei gathered all his strength as he posed a simple question, “Did your parents start the fire?”

Immediately, the child panicked. It was obvious it would be them, but he wanted to know what happened and how he managed to survive it. Above all, he needed to know just how safe this kid felt before the fire and how safe he would have been if he did leave him here with others to take care of him.

“It was an accident…” He finally answered, continuously sucking on his lower lip.

At that point, Mydei couldn't take it anymore and he let him hug him, with his head buried in his chest and his hands closing around the orange fabric of his uniform, searching for any type of support. He smiled as he caressed his back, keeping him as close as he wished. 

After a few minutes, though, he had to continue with a couple of questions. “Can you tell me what happened?” He asked, with a calm and soothing voice.

He raised his head, perplexed eyes looking at him, while ash attached to his hair fell on his forehead. Mydei slowly raised a hand to move it out of his face, immediately noticing the reaction to that simple motion. He turned his head away, almost expecting an impact, instead of a gentle caress through his hair. He moved his golden blonde hair out of his eyes and forehead regardless, but he made sure to do it in the most delicate way he could. 

The kid slowly turned to look at him again, his honey-colored eyes wandering, partly in fear and partly in wonder, and he moved his hands at the center of his chest, closed in a punch without grabbing Mydei’s shirt. He looked hesitant, but somewhat trusting as well, if his body language was anything to go by. 

Mydei patiently waited as he gently rubbed his back to try and calm him down further, until he felt confident enough to open his mouth again. “My father was angry and drunk, so he ended up starting the fire…” he whispered, looking at the floor, “he and my mother tried to run away, but they couldn't.”

It was what he expected, but something about how he explained the situation didn’t sit right with him. He excluded himself from that answer, and the way he found him– alone on the floor, crying, without being fully aware of his surroundings, simply confirmed his worries about his living situation.

Mydei calmly moved his hand to gently grab his chin, forcefully tilting his head. He could feel the terrified stare from below him, but he tried to ignore it for a few seconds in favour of checking if the injury he had was from the fire or from what he feared instead. 

“Is this their doing too?” He asked with a whisper, barely touching it. He dropped his arm and smiled at him gently. “Did your parents hit you?”

His expression dropped, almost as if he let down the last semblance of an armor to protect himself from his own situation he had left. Mydei made sure he’d feel his presence as a support and not an obstacle, gently caressing the cheek without injuries and letting him lean on his body whenever he needed. There wasn’t really a right way to start a conversation like that with a child he just met, but he looked so broken and alone that he couldn’t just leave it alone, and now the only thing he could possibly do was approach it gently and hope that everything would have gone in the right way.

Astraea let out a heavy sigh, before he hesitantly looked up to him again, still a little scared, but there was a little more trust in the way he moved and approached him.

“I… my father was really mad, so I ran away…” He explained, trailing off as he thought of what he should say afterwards. His breath hitched while he recalled the events that quickly led to where he was now, and Mydei prepared himself if he had to intervene in any way. By the looks of it, he could start hyperventilating any moment, and he’d better be ready to help him out of it. 

His breathing picked up again, and that was his signal to start doing something.

“Hey, follow what I do.” He said, catching his attention immediately. He looked up to him with innocent, pleading eyes, fully focused on what he asked him to do, even if he was scared. “Breathe in,” he said, subsequently breathing in and waiting for him to do the same, “keep it there, and slowly breathe out.” He concluded, doing what he instructed and watching as he repeated what he said a few other times.

When he looked at him again, he was beyond surprised, and a little proud of himself. Mydei smiled and rubbed his hand on his back, as if to congratulate him. The child faintly smiled back at him for the first time, and he instinctively hugged him, for a reason he didn’t fully understand yet. Maybe he wanted to protect that smile, or he reminded him of something he didn’t want to remember upon looking at a child that young.

As he let him go, he noticed he was doing a lot better, still keeping himself close to him, but no longer needing the support to stay standing. Mydei smiled, caressing his cheek and stealing another proud smile from him. “Better?” He asked, with a gentle voice.

“Thank you.” He nodded, his body language visibly more comfortable around him.

Mydei smiled, happy to finally see him excited to talk to him. He was bouncing his body slightly as he smiled, maybe because he was proud of himself for overcoming something he couldn’t control. Saying that he thought of it as adorable would be an understatement, especially after the consequences he has seen due to what had happened to him. 

“It’s my job.” He answered in the end, catching him when he eventually actually jumped against him, apparently trusting him that much already. Mydei moved to assume his earlier position and let the child twirl around to lean against his leg, but still made sure he looked at him. “Did you have something else to say?”

He quietly nodded, his shining smile fading from his face. “The fire already started, and…” he sighed, closing his fists around his own shirt, then spat out, “my father found himself buried under-”

Mydei immediately interrupted him and hugged him, finally understanding why he looked so uncaring of the immediate danger that fire posed. He probably felt guilty, terrified and confused, and his mind simply shut down because it couldn’t keep up with the sheer quantitude of feelings that he didn’t know how to process were rising within his body. He felt him tense for a second, startled by the sudden movement, but ultimately softened and leaned into that embrace.

“It’s not your fault.” Mydei whispered, almost as a reassurance to himself too. He gently kissed the top of his head, ignoring the horrid smell his hair had, given the amount of dirt and ash in it, along with smoke attaching itself to it instead of its usual smell. “It's not your fault,” he ended up repeating before slightly undoing the hug and gently tucking his hair behind his left ear. 

The way he looked at him right after that shattered his heart once more. He knew he couldn't do anything for him, even if he desperately wanted to. Those eyes were looking at him for the slightest glimmer of hope in a situation that should have left him with no semblance of trust in others, especially adults.

In the end, he saw himself in that kid, suddenly getting a stark, painful reminder of just how much he wanted someone to hold onto when he was a child. He picked himself up eventually, but he went through hell before even thinking of breaking those chains that held him still as he took punch after punch.

He didn't want him to go through it too, especially if he could do something about it.

“Mydeimos.”

The deep voice made him raise his head towards the source of it, just to see Gnaeus stare down at him with a few documents in his hand. He let go of the kid and stood up, almost out of respect, but still let the child hug his leg and rest his head on his thigh. “Is there a problem?” He asked, a little worried, but his voice was firm enough to not let that sentiment come through.

Gnaeus stared at the child for a second, before handing him the document he held. “Your permit.” He stated, looking straight at Mydei and waiting for him to take it.

“For…?” 

“The kid. We've already called his relatives, none of them want him. I'd send him to social centers, but…”

“It’s a pain in the ass when you already have someone that is thinking of taking him home?”

He nodded and took a deep sigh, taking a final look at the child. Then, he gazed back at Mydei and said, in an imposing tone, “Take a few days off too. You've never taken any, take care of the kid.”

“Thank you, sir.” Mydei answered, his head spinning already with the amount of information he had to process. Was he really adopting this kid? Isn’t that a little too soon? Is the kid himself fine with it? Why did no one want him?

He took a deep breath and looked towards the black sky, the stars hidden from the street lights of the city. He needed his head crystal clear and being able to think rationally.

“Am I a problem?”

To that question, his head snaps towards him, hurt that he would even think something akin to that.

“No. No, don't worry.” He tried to reassure him, his voice slow and kind. “I just need to think for a second to get us home.”

Astraea’s eyes immediately sparked as he looked at him with a curious and excited expression. He smiled upon seeing that reaction, letting him bounce his body up and down in ecstasy. “Can I come?” He asked, with a happy and eager voice, almost as if he was allowed to eat the biggest candy on the planet.

Mydei picked him up and laid him on his bent leg, then booped his nose. “That’s why I said ‘us’.” He said, expecting some other reaction out of him. He only got a hug that he exchanged, glad it wasn't too much of a bother for the people around them. “Can you walk for a while? My house is a little far, but I’ll carry you after you’re too tired.”

He nodded excitedly, before hopping down from his leg and waiting for him to say when they could start walking.

“Let’s go.” he announced, after standing up and stretching his muscles. He looked back at the child and he noticed him standing close to him, until a hand reached out to him. He held it without much hesitation, mindlessly following him. Something about it turned his stomach in the wrong way, but he ignored it in favour of focusing on what he had to do now.

He already thought about his options to actually get home, but the fastest one was probably by foot. He did have a bike, but it was at the station and the child with him was way too young and still way too overwhelmed to get on it, and his apartment wasn’t too far away from there. 

They walked in silence for another few minutes and Mydei could feel his steps getting slower by the second, despite him trying so hard to keep up the pace so that they could arrive sooner. After a couple of steps, he picked him up, gave him a sweet kiss on his temple and stopped to look at him for a few seconds. Astraea yawned and rubbed his eyes, trying to stay awake, ultimately losing that battle as soon as he laid his head on his shoulder. His chest began falling and rising, fully relying on the adult holding him in his arms.

His stomach turned around in ways he didn’t like, and he properly reflected on it while he was walking home. The thing that disturbed him was how much trust this child had in strangers, to the point that someone offering him basic kindness and some help warranted him to grow attached to him. Obviously, the situation he just went through was peculiar, but he feared what would have happened if he trusted the wrong adult in that scenario.

He took a quick look at him, mentally calculating what age he must have been. He weighed like a three year old, but he was probably a couple of years older, judging by the way he talked. Even then, he was so tiny that he just worried about his living conditions prior to that accident, with all the things he could observe in a little under an hour. It wasn’t enough to recognize the abuse right away, but it was noticeable enough for someone with a brain and enough interest about his well-being to notice it.

Mydei finally reached his apartment complex and unlocked the door, proceeding to walk up the stairs and reach the door of his apartment. Somewhere along the way, the child woke up, maybe due to the excessive bumping against his chest.

He felt his little fist curling around the fabric of his clothes as he yawned again, probably exhausted by now. He hoped he could go to bed soon enough, but he knew that he had to at least wash himself and eat, so it didn't seem too likely.

As he opened his door, he felt Astraea’s head raise from his shoulders, looking inside of the apartment. “Mydei,” he called out, “do you live alone?”

He mumbled in affirmation, before gently putting him down on the floor and letting him walk around for a while. He looked curious, but Mydei had to stop him immediately. “Hey, you need to go wash yourself,” he said with a gentle voice, then pointed towards the bathroom. “Call me when you're done and we can wash your hair.”

Astraea smiled and nodded, then walked towards the bathroom without many problems. Mydei followed him and took out everything he needed to wash, filled the bath and brought him a set of new clothes that he could wear. The kid let him do what he needed as he felt the temperature of the water, then looked as some ash attached to his skin got mixed with the water.

“Mydei…” Astraea whined, pointing at the dirt in the water. He didn’t add anything else and just looked a little worried, with a clear pout on his face.

He sighed and walked over to look at what he was pointing at, and he couldn’t keep in a light laugh. “Told you, you need a bath,” he just stated, then crouched down and tucked his hair behind his ear. “Wash yourself well, or you could get sick.”

“Why don’t you?”

“I'll take a shower later.”

“I mean… why don’t you help me?”

Mydei didn’t answer right away. He didn’t even expect a question about it, he simply thought that he absolutely didn't want a stranger to help him in such a vulnerable moment. It didn't matter how much he just helped him, he was still a stranger and that trust in him worried him more than the last time he thought about it. He would have understood if he was an adult who was already in his life, but he wasn't. That kind of trust made him feel almost uneasy, even if he knew that it wasn’t his fault and it was just the result of his upbringing and his extremely young age, but he could try to explain it to him now.

He took a deep breath, then smiled at him and told him, with a gentle, clear tone, “Because I don't know how comfortable you are in being seen in that situation by a stranger.”

His eyes wandered for a second, then pouted as he thought about what that sentence meant, and Mydei just waited in silence. After a few seconds, he looked up with the same big honey brown eyes and whispered, “But I trust you.”

“But we just met,” Mydei tried to make him notice, slowly explaining his point. “Would you let the other firefighters do that? Or your neighbors?”

“No... but you wouldn't–”

“I wouldn't hurt you in any way. But someone else could, right? Weight where, how and to whom to give your trust, that's alI I’m saying. Would you be okay with me seeing you completely naked now that we just met?”

He shook his head in shame, similarly to a child who was trying to sacrifice their wishes to make their parents happy and get compliments in return. Mydei was honestly glad to see that it was some kind of facade, almost forcing himself to act like a good child, but he really didn’t want to continue the treatment he got in his household. He didn’t want Astraea to treat him like his father or refer to him as such, and certainly not right away or in that specific way. 

“Remember I’ll help you with your hair, so only wash everything below your chin,” he repeated, catching his attention again. Astraea nodded, despite being still a little ashamed, and waited for the adult to step out and close the door behind him before moving at all.

Mydei let out a heavy sigh as he started putting his clothes away as well. He took off his uniform and folded it in a corner, with the clothes he'd have to wash the following day, moving on to wearing a half used t-shirt and a pair of pants he only used at home. Running his hand through his hair, he felt a few foreign particles in them, confirming that he absolutely had to take a shower before going to bed.

He stretched his muscles slightly, before going into the room next to his own and started to think of how he could arrange it for Astraea to use as a bedroom. That room was never something he liked to use, mainly due to the memories connected to it, so if he could replace them with happier ones he would take the opportunity immediately.

After a while of shuffling through a few ideas in his head– the bed against the wall or a little separated from it, where he could put a desk, which carpet and toys he had to buy for him, books he could read, pencils, colors, pens, crayons, all sorts of paint in case he liked to draw, where he could put furniture for his clothes, actual clothes that weren't of Ptolemy's kids that he had from the last time he babysat them– he noted all of them in his head, opting to just ignore them until the following day. It was late, and the kid would probably prefer to sleep with him for today.

“Mydei!”

Astraea’s voice came in, almost as if he heard his thoughts, and Mydei abruptly walked towards the bathroom, finding the child by the door holding up his hair with a humid towel that he probably used already. 

Clever kid , Mydei thought, before grabbing the brush and the products he needed and kneeling on the ground. He waited for Astraea to walk towards him, then he grabbed the shower-head and gave a little push to the back of his head to tell him to lower it.

He does, letting his hair fall in the general area inside of the bath in front of them. Mydei turned on hot water, gently playing with the shower-head and feeling the temperature every few seconds. Soon enough, he turned his wrist around to wet his scalp and hair, grabbing the brush with the other hand.

Knowing it would hurt, he started to brush his hair, undoing the rods he found and, eventually, stopped the water stream because he needed two hands to take care of them. Naturally, with that practice, came the first whines from the child.

“Sorry, your hair is in a horrible state,” he apologized, trying not to bring him too much pain. “It’s going to be pretty and it will have a really nice scent, so can you be brave for me for a few minutes?”

He felt a light nod and kept checking for rods and petting his hair, until everything was cleared out. As he worked on it, he noticed just how beautiful his light blonde hair was, and how much of it was white instead. Most of them were on the right side of his head and formed a white stripe that contrasted extraordinarily well with the rest of his hair. He doubted it would have stayed blonde, given the slightly strawberry red hair he found in between blonde and white hair that were gradually expanding, but that would have been for the better. With more contrast it would have looked even better.

Putting aside those thoughts, he proceeded with washing his hair and drying it, until it looked brand new. He figured that no one ever did that to him, because he took a bit of hair and smelled it, making a happy face.

Despite the excitement, though, he yawned and whined with a sleepy voice, “Mydei…”

He took him in an embrace, before picking him up and looking at him with a smile. “Are you hungry? Do you want to eat some food?” He asked, his voice low and gentle.

“Not too much.”

“We can eat something small, then.”

He walked towards the kitchen and sat him down, washed his hands, took out some pieces of bread and toasted them, then put tomatoes and oil on top of them and handed them to Astraea. He rubbed his eyes, but still took the bread and started eating it.

It was more of a snack than dinner, but he figured he did eat beforehand, since he said he wasn't too hungry and the fire occurred late at night. Contrary to his shifts, his parents probably had the time to go home and have dinner with their child before 10 PM. 

“Are you not eating?” Astraea asked all of a sudden, slightly tilting his head to the side in a questioning motion.

Mydei shook his head, then explained, “I’m preparing dinner for myself after you go to bed.”

Apparently, that wasn't a satisfactory answer for him, so he handed him a piece of bread. His eyes were shining, almost pleading him to eat it, and he just couldn't resist a similar request. “Well, thank you.” He smiled and took a bite from the bread, looking down just to see a happy face looking back at him. He lovingly patted him on the head and heard a soft giggle escape his lips, before he sat back again.

As they ate, Mydei took out a cutlet that he prepared a few days ago and put in the freezer for whenever he would need it and started cooking it so that he could eat something to function properly until the following morning.

“What’s that?” Astraea asked with a curious expression, after finishing to eat his piece of bread.

Mydei smiled at him and tilted his head, before asking, “Weren’t you sleepy?”

“I wanna see what you eat!”

“Nuh-huh, you need to sleep now.”

He quickly moved to catch him before he could walk out of the room and kept him in his arms as he was keeping an eye on his food. He didn't want to force him to go to bed, especially alone and after what he went through. He honestly wouldn't be surprised if he was pretending not to be tired to avoid being alone and in the dark. Given how young he was and what he saw in the few years he had been alive, it was the minimum that he expected.

Tiny fingers brushing against the marking on his cheek broke his train of thought. Astraea's eyes were shining under the dim artificial light that illuminated the kitchen, his mouth slightly open in wonder. 

Mydei smiled and let him analyze it. “Do you like it?” He asked, in the end, catching his attention again. He shifted all the child's weight on his left arm and showed him his right hand, full of the same red markings that continued up his arm. “I have these too,” he pulled down the hem of his shirt and showed some markings there too, “and these as well.”

Astraea's eyes lit up again, visibly excited after seeing the red markings all over his upper body. In truth, he had them on his thighs, legs and back, but those previous mentions were enough already.

He sighed and turned off the stove, placing his food on a dish. Turning to Astraea, he gently requested, “Go, it won't take me much to eat and take a shower.” He put him down, giving him a last pat on the head. “Try to sleep.”

The child didn't look too convinced, but he still listened to him and headed for Mydei's bedroom. He followed him with his eyes for a few seconds, before turning to his food. It wasn't the best he could have had, but he needed it to be something quick to cook and eat, and that was exactly what he needed. 

What he didn't need, on the contrary, was his ex-boyfriend calling him.

Mydei let out a heavy huff, debating whether or not he should be answering the phone. He knew that he wouldn't have given up until he gave him an answer anyway, so there wasn't much he could have done to avoid it. Regardless, it was the one person that he found hard to talk to, at the moment.

He pondered a little longer, without finding any kind of real solution to escape his impending doom. In the end, the neverending sound of the ringtone echoing in his eardrums made him abandon his feeble resistance and he picked up the phone.

“Good evening, Mydeimos.”

That calm, suave voice loudly echoed in his head like many other times before, a myriad of memories passing by his eyes as he recollected himself.

"Hephaestion,” he whispered, his mind suddenly clearer after that little moment of silence. He ate the last bit of his food, then stood up to eat some fruit, at least. “To what do I owe the pleasure?”

“There are rumors about you bringing a kid home,” Hephaestion almost meowed, with an interested voice. “Is it true?”

He hated hearing that voice.

He hated hearing the rivers of pure honey that he could no longer taste.

He hated hearing that sweet tone that he knew he used only with him, echoing in his head, recalling days that were no longer possible to come by again.

He hated hearing it once again, and wondered about the decision he took to not break off their friendship. Maybe, if he didn't, those memories wouldn't haunt him. Then again, he didn’t have the heart to leave him alone in this period, as much as he hated seeing him and hearing his voice in that state.

Maybe, he thought once again, his body and mind wouldn't ache with the desire to see him again. Even if he knew that they did it under agreement, even if he knew that they naturally grew distant with time, he wanted to travel back to those happier, simpler days.

Needless to say, neither of them were able to do that. Mydei still visited him and Hephaestion still called to check in, both with him and the rest of their friends. It was a stable situation, despite the looming shadow of death hovering over them.

“Mydei.”

That other voice made him violently snap back into reality after he felt a light pull on his hand. As he looked down, he saw a very frightened Astraea looking for him, and he instinctively picked him up, giving up on his research for fruit that he honestly almost forgot about.

Astraea dove his head in his chest, trembling slightly, and Mydei could only lull him to sleep in the best way he could as he kept answering the questions being asked on the other end of his phone.

“Yeah, he's here with me,” he confirmed, before looking back at the child. He was sure he was on the point of sobbing, so he left a kiss in his hair. “You really don't want to go to bed?”

He violently shook his head, clearly scared, but slowly calming down.

It's probably anxiety , he thought. He's probably afraid of the dark and he's so paranoid that he's seeing things that simply aren't there.

Mydei decided to hug him with his free hand, trying to pass the information that he would have protected him if anything would have happened.

A calm laugh could be heard from the other side of the phone, and Mydei had to mentally slap himself for thinking it was cute. “It’s not an everyday occurrence to see the fierce Mydeimos encounter obstacles on his way.” Hephaestion teased, obviously enjoying himself. 

“You would do the same, no one can say no to a kid like this.”

“The mighty Mydeimos defeated by a little child… Leonnius won't let you hear the end of it.”

“He certainly wouldn't,” he agreed, then falling silent. He bit back the need to ask him how he was doing, opting for the second closest thing. “How is the recovery going?”

He hated hearing about his worsening health. He hated it, but he knew it was a reality, and he had to face it, in a way or another.

Even before they broke up, he kept saying that he deserved better, that he deserved a life with someone else, that he didn't want him to remember him only from his illness. He knew he wouldn’t have, but he kept repeating it, maybe out of fear of his health falling again. It was something he had been dealing with for years now, and Mydei had always been right next to him to soothe him and lend a hand when he asked to.

Their relationship was definitely special, everyone always told them, but their break-up was nothing out of the ordinary. Very simply, both of them drifted apart with time after burning exclusively for each other for several years. It did have a horrendous impact on Mydei, but he would have moved on, with time. Eventually. Maybe.

After all, what they had couldn't even be described with words, and the fact that those warm, tender feelings were replaced with melancholy and distance for something that neither of them could control wasn't an easy situation to navigate at any point in his life.

Hephaestion sighed and stood in silence for a second. “I should be dismissed tomorrow morning,” he eventually confessed.

He hated all of this. He still loved him, and he didn't know if he would ever move on from him, and it was becoming almost an annoying feeling.

He thought for a long while without uttering a sound, careful to ponder his words correctly, without ignoring all his feelings of yearning, sadness, melancholy. Then, finally, he said what was heaving on his chest, as clearly as possible.

“I can pick you up. Let you meet the kid too.”

He despised himself for it.

He hated still having such a desire for someone that he knew was suffering and he agreed to break up with. He wanted to help, he wanted to somehow lessen the load on his shoulders, but he wanted some decent things for himself too, despite the fact that they were no longer as close as they were in the past.

Even if it was just one time, it would have been enough for him. Just knowing that Astraea would have known Hephaestion was enough. He believed in his resilience and strength, he knew that he would have pushed through this time as well, but he couldn’t be sure of it.

His heart ached at the prospect, so much so that the child in his arms looked up to him with a worried expression and scared eyes. Mydei honestly forgot that he could hear his heart from that position, but he calmly recomposed himself and petted his head to reassure him everything was fine. He did seem to silently understand, so he turned his attention to the phone again.

“How generous of you,” Hephaestion thanked him, with a genuine voice. “But don't feel forced to do such a thing if you don't want to.”

“If I didn't want to, I wouldn't have proposed it.”

“Mhm, as you wish. Have a good night, Mydeimos.”

“You too. Rest well.”

He was about to throw the phone across the room after that call.

Hephaestion’s voice was still ringing in his ears as he slowly put down the object in his hands, resisting the ever-growing urge to actually listen to his first instincts. The longer he thought about it, the calmer he became, repeating the logical answers to soothe himself down as much as possible. 

As logical as anyone would be in that situation, anyway.

It's not his fault, he's happy for you, you're still close friends, you have a kid to think about, focus on what you can do and don’t make an impossible leap.

He knew those sentences were true, and that was all he needed. He simply took a deep breath and turned his eyes to the child in his arms, who was already looking at him. Mydei smiled at him and left a quick kiss on his forehead.

“We’re going on a trip tomorrow?” Astraea asked, with a stable, curious tone.

Mydei smiled and nodded. “Mhm,” he mumbled before tilting his head and whispered a suggestion, “so, you need to sleep.”

He pouted, insecurity written all over his face, as his tiny hands played with the fabric of his shirt. Mydei patiently waited for him to find the courage to talk to him, standing still in silence. The child looked at his own hands, restlessly moving along his shirt, and sucked on his lower lip. He was visibly anxious, but he still whispered, “But… it's so dark…” 

Mydei expected a similar answer. He thought about making him understand that he didn't have to be afraid of the dark because nothing was there– most times, at least– but he didn't think he had the strength to do something even relatively similar to it. Instead, he smiled at him and asked, “Are you afraid of the dark?” 

Astraea nodded, with lucid eyes, and Mydei put him back down and kneeled in front of him. “Stay here for a bit then, we're going to sleep together,” he told him, with a kind and patient voice, then ruffled his hair lovingly. “So I can protect you ,” he poked his nose playfully, “from all kinds of monsters.”

“Really?”

“Mhm, all kinds of evildoers will meet their end before they ever get to you, as long as I'm here.”

He looked at Mydei for a few seconds, then offered him his pinky finger. “Promise?” He asked, with a hopeful tone.

Mydei immediately intertwined his pinky finger around his and whispered, “Promise.”

The child smiled and went to sit on the couch, then started playing with a tiny pillow happily. Mydei looked at him and smiled, before thinking of getting clean clothes and taking a shower before going to bed. He usually took a bath because he found it more refreshing and relaxing, but he was in a hurry, so he had to be fine with a relatively quick shower. 

Despite the fact that he didn't want to stay there for long, he couldn't help but use that time under the hot water to take a few deep breaths and try to blow away the enormous weight on his heart. He honestly didn't expect it to work, but he did end up thinking about the child in his living room again. He turned his face upwards and let the water wash over his hair and stream down his forehead, cheeks, jaw and neck, proceeding then to slide down his body.

He let out a shaky breath as he lowered his head slightly, thinking back to earlier that night. The frightened eyes of that child reminded him all too well about himself a few years back, without a home to go back to or someone to look up to, alone in the world until he picked himself up and charged through life. He just didn't want a traumatized child having to go through the same thing.

Looking at him, finding out some of his thoughts and behaviours and taking care of him made him realize even more just how much he needed him right now. He had a stable income, he could take care of him, he had enough friends to get some help if he needed it and he felt better about the situation with Hephaestion the second that the kid walked through his apartment door.

He genuinely wanted him to stay and he was growing attached to him at a worrying speed, but it wasn't something that he was scared about. On the contrary, he had the full intention of starting the adoption process the following day, after picking up his friend from the hospital. 

That word still felt almost foreign associated with Hephaestion, but what else could he describe him as? He was more of a friend, but definitely not a lover anymore. He still felt tenderness that ascended both definitions, but he couldn't do anything about it, if not accept it and try to cherish their bond until then. That sinking feeling was something he never wanted to recognize again, but he would have to bear with it until he fully accepted it and moved on, and taking care of a kid was something he would count as fitting to that request.

Mydei forcefully pushed those thoughts out of his head as he brought his attention to washing his hair properly, mentally pinning down what he had to do tomorrow morning. Even just thinking about it made his head spin, but he had to take care of everything as soon as possible and, hopefully, nothing would go south.

It probably will, but his brain genuinely couldn't compute it or it would have shut down immediately.

He let out another sigh and stepped out of the shower, quickly drying his body and putting on his clothes. He held up his wet hair as he was changing, then grabbed the hairdryer to finally put an end to that day, at long last. The last two hours felt like three weeks, and he needed to pass out until tomorrow morning.

As he opened the door, his eyes searched for his child– and he partly cursed his mind for already thinking of him as such already– and found him sleeping on the couch, faintly hugging a pillow. Mydei smiled as he walked towards him, crouching down and taking a few seconds to look at him peacefully sleeping, his tiny chest rising and falling and his slightly open mouth emitting relaxed breaths. Reaching out a hand, he gently caressed his hair and watched as he whined and rubbed his face on the pillow, without waking up at all. 

He has to be tired, after everything, he thought, right before lifting him up in his arms and carrying him to his room. Mydei didn't miss the slight grip on his shirt, and he was more than happy to offer that support to him. Even more than that, as soon as he put him on the mattress and let him bury his face in his chest as he searched for his protection, just like earlier that night, he was glad that he could help that kid and attempt to give him a second chance at a childhood that he never had.

Mydei grabbed and threw the sheets on top of both of them and he hugged him, then kissed him on the top of his head. “Goodnight,” he managed to whisper, not expecting an answer nor having enough strength to stay up for longer. He passed out almost immediately, with the child– his son, his mind insisted– in his arms gently hugging him close, almost like a little treasure he found in that fire.

He knew he wouldn't have let him go, as long as he would have needed him. That was everything he knew, and the only thing he needed to, before falling in the dark ocean of the night.

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"In the end, his curiosity was too great to ignore, and he ended up opening the photo. Mydei blinked at his phone for a second, baffled at what he was looking at. Now he was firmly sure: that was the worst decision of his life."

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

In all honesty, when Mydei stepped foot into the hospital with Astraea right next to him, holding his hand as he looked around him, he definitely didn't expect to see Hephaestion to look as healthy as he was. He expected some bags under his eyes, at least, instead of his skin glowing and his eyes full of life.

He greeted him with a smile and hugged him. “Mydeimos, punctual as ever,” he commented jokingly, then took a step back. “I see that having a child didn't impact your schedule.”

At the mention of his presence, Astraea shyly hides behind Mydei's leg, still holding his hand. He only raised his head to search for help to the adult he trusted the most in the room. He let his hand go for a second and patted him on the top of his head, affectionately brushing against his hair. “He’s a good kid. Prepared on time and all,” he praised him, as he let him grab him on his pants.

Hephaestion smiled and bowed down to take a better look at him, then extended his hand. “I’m Hephaestion, a long time friend of Mydeimos,” he slightly tilted his head, minding to keep his distance. “Can I ask what your name is?”

The kid retracted his head into himself, without moving. He looked at him with eyes full of doubt, before quietly whispering, “Astraea.”

At that point, Mydei desperately hoped that Hephaestion wouldn’t bring up the fact that it was a girl’s name. He prayed that he didn’t highlight that fact, because that was probably the only good thing that his parents left him to hang onto. He didn’t care if it was a girl’s name, and certainly Astraea didn’t either. It was a beautiful name and he had worn it for a few years already and he absolutely had no intention of changing it.

After that pause, Hephaestion crouched down in front of him, keeping on smiling at him, and gently extended his hand, patiently waiting for him to grab it. Astraea hesitated for a few seconds, before taking and shaking his hand with just a slight uneasiness left in his eyes.

“Mister,” a doctor behind them called out, looking at Hephaestion. He stood up again, giving him his full attention. “You need to do a last check up before leaving.”

“Oh, of course,” he nodded, taking a deep breath. Turning to Mydei again, he passed a hand on his shoulder, making him tense up for a second, before he dropped his arm along his side. “I'll be right back.”

Mydei looked in his general direction for a few seconds, before he could notice the loss of the weight and grip against his leg. Quickly, he looked around himself, almost scanning the room to search for him. He didn’t think he could have gotten far, but not being able to see him triggered an uneasy sense of discomfort and fear, his mind starting to work on its own to show him the worst possible scenarios.

Panic quickly settled in his chest and his legs started working on their own, frantically walking around the hallway, his eyes scanning every corner they could reach. “Fuck,” he hissed under his breath, still looking anywhere to find him. He was getting abnormally scared, starting to listen to the endless worries in his head about kidnappings, falling off to his death, getting found by the wrong people, getting taken–

“I’m sorry! Sir!”

The sudden yell suddenly interrupted his thoughts, clearing his mind of everything else, only a striking ray of hope making its way in his mind. As he turned towards the source of it, he noticed a white-haired, blue-eyed man, but he didn't recognize anything else after he saw Astraea running towards him.

He didn't yell nor warn him, expecting already Mydei to catch him. Of course, he instinctively crouched down and opened his arms, letting him grab his shirt and quietly sniffle in his chest. He noticed him trembling while his own heart was beating at a speed that never did before, so he decided to permit both of them to feel at peace, even for just a second, by picking him up and kissing him on the top of his head.

Mydei let out grateful sighs as he petted his hair to make sure he would be safe in his arms. He closed his eyes and rested his cheek on his hair for a few seconds, letting himself process his presence, and planted another kiss on his forehead.

As he slightly leaned back, Astraea looked at him with his big, light brown eyes and waited for him to speak, maybe to be scolded or yelled at. Maybe even being hit, in some way.

Instead, Mydei cupped his cheek with his free hand and dried his tears with a kindness that he probably didn't recognize, given his confused and wandering eyes. “Don’t run away when we're so in the open, got it? You were lucky this time, but it's dangerous.” He reprimanded him, careful not to sound too harsh.

The kid in his arms still looked down, grabbing his own shirt, almost in shame, and whispered, “Sorry…”

Mydei smiled and kissed him on his temple, catching his attention again. “I’m just glad you're fine, don't cry,” he whispered, with a warm and reassuring voice.

“Aren’t you mad?” Astraea asked, his eyes confused and his expression almost scared.

He didn't know why he wasn't expecting that question. He wasn't expecting a child to miss completely every cue he gave him and still assume the worst. Maybe, that was what his parents used to do, and that was why his intentions didn't successfully calm him down.

The more he found out about what his past must have been like, the more he wished he could have helped him earlier. He couldn't even fathom anyone having the actual intention of hurting him, let alone both of his parents. He was neglected and ignored, the wrong look left to traumatize him further, and that was the result.

They lied to him and gaslit him so many times that now he doubted everything that he told him in a situation of danger.

Despite the anger towards those two adults, Mydei recomposed himself and looked at him again. “Do I look mad?” He asked, waiting for a response. As soon as he saw a hesitant shake of his head, he continued, “Then, I'm not mad. Don't run away from me, or I can't keep my promise. Okay?”

Astraea nodded and sniffled, before hiding his face in his shoulder again. Mydei kept him there as he stood up, giving him all the time and vicinity he needed, but he still looked towards the man that took care of him in his stead during those few minutes.

He was smiling at him, looking genuinely happy, but there was something darker and sadder in that demeanor, almost as if he was forcing himself to be someone he wasn't.

Despite what he just noticed, he moved on, taking a step forward. He knew he was staring, but he was used to it. He was very well aware of how good-looking he was, so he learned to ignore them, with time.

“Thank you for bringing him back here,” Mydei thanked the white-haired nurse, noticing just now how pretty he was. He was too panicked before, but after looking at him more carefully, he was unnervingly pretty. Maybe even handsome, if he said so himself.

His eyes accidentally travelled to his arms with obviously toned muscles, then back to his shoulders, almost as broad as his. He did have slightly slimmer hips, but he honestly found that more attractive.

Mydei shut down his brain as soon as that thought fully formed, knowingly ignoring it. It was a casual statement and it was objectively true. Yes, that was the reason why he thought about it.

“It’s not a problem,” the nurse said, interrupting his thoughts. Mydei almost snapped his head towards him, but neither of them really reacted to it. The man in front of him then extended an arm towards an empty position with a computer. “Did you need any help? I'm a nurse working here.”

Mydei blinked a few times before actually understanding that question and thinking about an answer. He was still thinking about the audacity of his brain to even give out such compliments to a complete stranger that was just trying to do his job.

This is what a year and a half of occasional sex did to you, Mydeimos , he thought, almost in shame. Admittedly, he was way too lost into his memories to start a committed relationship again, and none of the people he fucked looked like the right one.

Turning his eyes back to the man in front of him, he took a deep breath and finally answered him, insisting in a part of his mind to further process how he looked.

He suddenly felt a slight pat on his chest and shifted Astraea on his arm, before putting him down and keeping him close. Thinking a grand majority of what he just did with his son in his arms granted him a mental backslap, but he was glad that it wasn't too noticeable.

“Actually, I need to run a few check-ups on him.” Mydei answered, not really knowing how much time had passed. He didn't care much, but he was hoping that he wouldn't ask questions, at least.

Instead, he gave him a warm smile and nodded. “I can schedule an appointment for you two.”

Mydei bowed his head in a thanking motion and followed him to a nearby computer, most likely a place where they took appointments for the patients.

“I’ll need both of your names,” the nurse said, not bothering to stand down as he started typing something at a surprising speed.

“Mydeimos,” Mydei answered, then gestured towards the child with him, “the child is Astraea.”

He nodded in response, analysing which results his computer gave him. He looked slightly confused for a second, then looked back to Mydei. “Do you still have to adopt him?” He asked, with an innocent voice.

Right. He honestly could have imagined that he should have done that before taking appointments for him. He just hoped that the man who was helping him without second questions wouldn't think that he was a bad perso–

He stopped his thoughts right there, before they could progress further. Why did he even care this much? He could only be interested in his professional help, he didn't have anything to prove to him. That was certainly why he would even fathom to think such a thing.

“Yeah, I need to go today,” he settled on, making sure that his son was still close to him. He caressed his hair and Astraea grabbed his hand, partly playing with it. He let him, without any issues, and explained, “He moved in with me last night, he was one of the victims of yesterday's fire not too far away from here. Do I have to go there before checking on his health?”

He nodded, giving him an apologetic smile. “That would be following the protocol, yeah. He’s a child, there needs to be at least his legal guardian with him.”

“I understand. Thank you.”

“If you want, I can still talk to the doctor in the meantime. I will still be here tomorrow morning.”

There was something in his voice weirdly interesting, but he couldn’t quite put his finger on it, almost as if it was something foreign to him. It felt like a calm, gentle lullaby and the sound of a hammer beating a metallic sword into shape at the same time, and he had no idea what to make of it. He didn’t look menacing, nor had any bad intentions, but his behavior was something so fabricated that it pissed him off.

And yet, he was curious. That fake personality wasn’t to trick him into giving him trust, Mydei would have had to do that anyway since he was the nurse and if he wanted to harm Astraea they wouldn’t be there in the first place, so now he just wanted to know why he felt so put off by that behavior.

“What did you say your name was?” He ended up asking, after pondering a few seconds whether or not he wanted to get his answers or not. Unfortunately, he was at a point in his life where avoiding an annoying, interesting, good-looking guy that seemed to be into him wasn’t at the top of his list of priorities.

It wasn’t to say he was looking for a relationship or that he wanted to flirt with him– he absolutely wasn’t and flirting while the other was working was a low blow that he’d never agreed with– but he wouldn’t mind simply knowing a name to associate with the person. Maybe see him outside of the hospital too, but he didn’t want to hope for that much yet, especially when he didn’t know him at all.

The nurse smiled at him with a more excited mannerism, visibly happy being able to answer his question. “I’m Phainon.”

“Thank you, Phainon,” Mydei smiled back, thanking him with a nod of his head. He noticed Astraea getting closer to the other man and he let him, calmly moving out of the way, but not too far away from them. He faintly saw Phainon playing with him and heard a few giggles, so he finally decided to let him play along, since he obviously meant no harm to either and the kid liked him.

“We can go.”

A familiar voice on his left called out, before he could raise his head and see Hephaestion smiling at him. Slowly, he moved away slightly, trusting to still be at an arm's length from Astraea in case something happened.

“Is everything alright?” He asked, vaguely worried about his well-being.

He nodded, before almost yelling, “Healthy as a fish!”

Something didn't sit right with him after hearing that sentence, and he ended up glaring at him. He hated seeing fake smiles when he knew that the reality was only hurt and suffering, especially if it was from someone he held close.

Mydei stared down at his body, then back up to his face. “We both know it’s not true.”

“I jest, Mydeimos,” Hephaestion laughed, pretending to sound annoyed by that remark. “If I don’t crack a few jokes in this situation, I would die of boredom before the claws of death can actually claim me.”

He hated this. He thought those exact words so many times in the last 24 hours, but he absolutely despised that situation.

Thinking that Hephaestion of all people would risk losing his life and he couldn't do anything about it was making him go insane.

All he could offer were mere words and support, along with endless prayers that felt useless the more that he entertained the thought of keeping on doing it. He understood his wishes, but he just hoped that he would put up with it as little as possible.

“Of course,” he only answered, with a neutral voice and a deadpan expression. He just didn't have the intention of sugarcoating his feelings, or nothing that he had ever shown to Hephaestion during these long years of friendship would have had anything of value anymore.

He knew that weighing his words and which feelings to show was important now, but he didn't care enough, by that point.

Hephaestion, on his part, never agreed with his behaviour. He hated it, in fact.

He pulled him by his arm and dragged him away, a little more distant from Astraea and Phainon. Instinctively, Mydei looked over to the child, then back to his dear friend as soon as he made sure that he was doing fine.

“Mydeimos… you should go on.” Hephaestion added, his words precise and clear on his tongue. As soon as he saw him about to shoot a rebuttal, he stepped closer and whispered, “I’m out of danger now. I just have to come in once a week for tests and a couple of procedures, but the worst is over.”

He looked at him in silence, blinking in confusion. After a few seconds of recollecting his thoughts, he could only master saying, “... Seriously?” 

“Do you think they just expel severely ill people out of the hospital?” Hephaestion laughed, lightly teasing him about the shock on his face.

“So… you're safe,” he repeated, almost out of breath. “Out of danger.”

His friend had the courage of giggling at his face, visibly amused. Mydei pondered teasing back for a second, but he knew he would have bit him in the ass when he would have eventually made fun of how worried he was again. He may have loved and cared for Hephaestion more than he should have, but he fully knew how much of a little shit he could be, when he was in the mood.

So, since he didn't want to attract more of those remarks, he simply glared at him, as anyone would do when a close friend would keep joking about his death over and over again.

Hephaestion rested his hand in front of his mouth, trying to keep in another laugh out of respect towards his friend. He was sure he wouldn't have dared to usher ill words towards him, but he understood where he was coming from as well, even if his reaction was amusing, to say the least. “Yes, that's what I said,” he ended up answering eventually, finally acknowledging his earlier question.

For a second, Mydei stayed still in place, staring at him as if he didn't believe what he was hearing. Hephaestion didn’t speak, instead patiently waited with his hands held behind his back and a gentle smile worn on his face. He knew that he was running through all the information he had, thought he had and currently just found out in his brain, before choosing a sensitive approach. That was something he had always admired in him– and why he could only trust him to get him home after everything that had happened to him in those four walls.

Their break-up had been hard on him too, but he saw how much better he was faring now. Honestly, he had never felt like his equal, and it was hurting both of them even more after they started growing apart, in multiple ways, including his own sense of worth. He felt better now and, even if he knew that he still thought about him and he still avoided seriously dating anyone, he was on the right path too, if he just overcame his feelings for him.

Then, all of a sudden, all his thoughts stopped, and a huge weight was hugging him with a strength that he wasn’t entirely sure he could handle for long. Yet another reminder that he and Mydei would have never been on the same level.

Despite those feelings, though, the tenderness for him in his heart could never disappear, and he excganged that hug, permitting him to finally cease his useless worry.

“I’m glad,” he breathed out, then huffed out a deep, long breath. “I'm really glad, Hephaestion.”

Hephaestion awkwardly hugged back and let himself smile, although not missing the quick stare coming from the nurse not too far away from them. As soon as he looked at him, though, he was innocently talking to Astraea, who listened to him with eyes full of interest and wonder.

He was sure he was the direct subject of that staring and, knowing he was talking to Mydei before he came back, it wasn't hard to figure out what was the reason.

That conclusion, however, would have to wait to be uttered, since his insides were starting to feel uncomfortably squeezed together.

“Easy, Mydeimos,” he almost begged, lightly pushing him by his shoulders. “I am out of danger, but your muscles can kill me.”

He immediately stepped back, holding up his hands. “Sorry.”

Hephaestion smiled as a way to thank him, before turning back to the nurse, still playing with the child, then back to Mydei. “I meant what I said earlier, though. You should start dating again,” he suggested again, promptly ignoring his head moving sideways and his eyes looking at the ground. “It's been more than a year, Mydeimos. You should build a life for yourself again.”

Those words shook him, even if just slightly. “I know. I was… thinking about it, earlier.” He simply answered, relaxing again afterwards.

Mydei perfectly knew that he would have had to move on, and he knew he had the chance right there, just a few meters away from him, if he just wanted to, but there was still something stopping him. He didn’t want to start a relationship with someone who didn’t ask to always be with a man who couldn’t move on from his year and a half old break-up.

He heard Hephaestion sighing, and he raised his head towards him. “You should start with that nurse,” he nodded towards the man he talked to earlier and, despite that was just what he was thinking, his brain stopped working for a second all the same.

“Why?”

“He’s handsome, he's good with kids, he keeps looking at you…”

“What?” Mydei almost yelled, as he snapped his head towards him, faintly catching him moving his head away. He couldn’t help but let out a long sigh, almost in defeat. Why did he have to be interested in him? He hated being actually curious about someone he barely talked to, no matter how attractive or interesting he found him, especially if Hephaestion of all people noticed it.

He couldn’t really dismiss the points he brought forward either, Phainon did look like the perfect candidate if he had to choose someone to go on a date with, between the people he knew. There was interest on both parts, his son liked him, he was nice to both of them, saying he was gorgeous would have been an understatement and Hephaestion would have probably hunted him in his sleep if he didn’t ask him out.

Honestly, he was more scared of his dear friend’s judging stare than ever trying to date a stranger.

He huffed and rolled his eyes, finally admitting defeat. “ Fine . But only if I meet him again before tomorrow.”

“Oh,” Hephaestion perked up, even more interested in the matter, “a sign from the universe? How romantic, Mydeimos.”

“See it however you want to.”

“Mhm, I bet you will grant him that date.”

“Shut up.”

He only giggled in response, but he still reserved a smile for him. Despite all the teasing, Mydei knew that it was what he wanted for him, and he would have been happier if he simply moved on from their past relationship, as he was doing as well. They would have still been friends, they didn’t have ill intent towards each other, they both agreed on the break-up peacefully. Holding onto something that withered a long time ago would have only caused more pain than what both of them already had dealt with or deserved in this life.

Mydei felt something pulling on the hem of his sleeve, and promptly looked down, seeing Astraea looking at him with the eyes he used when he wanted to tell something to him. He wasn’t searching for kind words, at least, so he figured that it wasn’t related to something that upset him.

“Mydei,” he called out, before extending a hand with a piece of paper inside of it. Mydei looked at his side, towards the nurse, with a weird feeling settling in his chest. “Phainon sends this.”

If he found a phone number written down on that piece of paper, he would have stormed out of that room. No matter how kind and attractive that man was, using his son to ask him out while he was on the job was something that he didn’t like.

As soon as he unfolded the piece of paper, his face muscles immediately morphed into a disgusted expression, causing a soft laugh from the friend beside him that he promptly ignored. It was exactly what he expected– along with the drawing of a cat with a red marker in the right corner that, he had to admit, resembled him quite a bit. At least, the part about him liking cats was right.

“Yeah, I'm driving you home,” he announced, before storming off. He still didn’t know if he was mad, annoyed or just pretending to be either, but he knew that he had to tend to other commissions and he wanted to get out of that room. Whichever the right answer was, that feeling of curiosity lingered, despite everything else telling him it absolutely wasn’t a good idea.

If he didn’t already give his word to put his dear friend’s heart to rest about his well-being, he would have buried that thought and forgotten about him as soon as possible. Unluckily for him, he promised he would have earnestly tried to go on a date with him, at the very least.

Hephaestion quickly walked after him, with Astraea running next to him, albeit struggling to follow the two adults. Mydei acknowledged them and slowed down, quickly turning to take the child in his arms, most likely agitated by the sudden mood change after he gave the piece of paper to his main caretaker.

The kid blinked a few times, visibly confused, searching for an answer with his eyes on Mydei’s face. He just kissed him on the forehead and whispered, “Not your fault. Everything is fine, I’m not mad.”

Astraea quickly nodded and sucked on his bottom lip, without saying anything else to that. He grabbed the fabric of his shirt and spent a few seconds looking at him with a questioning stare, until Mydei smiled at him. He knew that he was anxious, he shouldn’t have stormed off so fast from where they were.

“Not even at Phainon?” Astraea asked, all of a sudden, with genuine worry in his voice.

At the mention of that nurse, Mydei sighed, before finally giving him the benefit of the doubt. “What did he tell you?”

“He asked me if I liked to be with you, and… if he could become your friend.”

“He asked for your permission?”

Astraea slightly tilted his head like a confused puppy, wearing a confused expression on his face. “What does that mean?”

“That he asked you if it was okay for him to do something,” he patiently explained, adjusting the weight on his arms. It wasn’t uncomfortable, but he feared that he’d be holding him there a lot longer than he initially anticipated.

The kid didn’t mind, and continued to answer his questions, careful to weigh and choose his words correctly. Mydei noticed he did it the day before too, and he wondered if that was a consequence of his parents getting mad often or if he just had some issues with words or his speech. Either way, they would have had to stop by the library that week, so he may have made space for another stop, before going home to eat lunch.

“I think he was a little worried about… talking to you.” Astraea continued, thinking back to what he talked about with Phainon. That answer sounded weird to Mydei, but he didn’t correct him, and just registered in his head. He didn’t look shy, he had been a pretty bright and extroverted person for the little he could see, but he was definitely aware of the fact that he may just need to be for the nature of his job.

He nodded, then quickly asked, “And you helped him?”

“He’s really nice…” Astraea confirmed, looking down at his hands still gripping at the shirt’s fabric. He almost sounded guilty or sorry, but he didn’t apologize as he usually did. Instead, he just explained himself, which was an approach Mydei greatly preferred. The child's big, light brown eyes looked at him again, this time looking a little more innocent than usual. “His voice is really shiny and…” he trailed off, before carefully opening his mouth again, “you looked happy talking to him…”

Now he was feeling guilty.

It was true that he got upset for the way that he asked him out, but it wasn't like anyone didn't try to go out with him before, either. He got demeaned as a way to catch his attention and ask him out– playing with his son and kindly asking for his support to impress him wasn't the worst he had seen during the years.

Maybe he was a little too rude and impulsive, this time.

“You should apologize, Mydeimos,” Hepheastion suggested then, still with a little bit of a short breath from the recent run he had to do to catch up with him.

He looked at him for a few seconds, before remembering what they were talking about when he did walk away and why he was so on edge to not think through his actions. “I would have to go on a date with him if I do.” He flatly stated, as if he was describing an objective phenomenon.

Hephaestion snorted, before crossing his arms and looking at him with a victorious expression. “How unfortunate.”

Mydei huffed and looked behind him, searching for Phainon to go and apologize, already feeling defeated yet again by Hephaestion's knowledge of his feelings and instincts.

There was no way in that life he could ever defeat him in that matter.

Luckily, Phainon was nowhere to be seen, at least in that room. He still didn't know if it was a good or a bad thing, but it was a reality where he didn't have to feel Hephaestion's stare on him and he would have supported it.

“He isn’t there anymore. I’ll apologize tomorrow,” he decided, finding a way out of that hole he accidentally dug for himself the second that he promised that he would go on a date with him under certain conditions.

“I mean… you do have his phone number.” Hephaestion reminded him, effectively blowing out of the water everything that he had left to celebrate.

Mydei sighed in response, even if he agreed with him. He perfectly knew that he was right, and he was aware of the fact that his hesitation was linked to lingering feelings of a time that he will never experience again.

Maybe, he should give him a chance, even just to lift a weight from his friend's tired heart.

While he thought, Hephaestion let out a pained, exhausted groan, almost scaring him. He was always so calm and composed in public, that he didn't think he would have ever done a sound even remotely similar to the one that just escaped his lips.

“I would throw myself into traffic to be in your situation!” He yelled, turning to him with a downright shocked face. “One of the most handsome, kindest men on the planet just willingly gave you his number after showing clear interest in you and you're conflicted about allowing him to go on one date with you? Really, Mydeimos?”

He stared at him for a few seconds, his words ringing in his mind, before he elected to actually listen to them at a later time. “It’s better if we start moving,” he suggested, without waiting for an answer, and walked out of the building.

Quickly, Hephaestion walked after him, grabbing the arm that he wasn’t using to hold Astraea to keep the pace with him. It was something he used to do even when they were younger, since Mydei was always faster than him. He never minded, and that moment wasn’t any different.

“You know I'm right,” Hephaestion answered, with a slight huff in his voice.

Mydei swung out the keys of his car and huffed in response. He didn’t like being forced to do anything, especially something that he could have done at his own pace the following day, but he couldn’t be mad at him. As if that wasn’t enough, the grateful feeling of being pushed to go on one date with that guy was creeping within him and he hated everything about it.

Without waiting for him to answer, Hephaestion grabbed his keys off of his hand all of a sudden, hiding both of his hands behind his back. Mydei looked at him dumbfounded, his hand still hanging in the air, not even registering Astraea’s soft laugh beside him.

“Send him a message,” Hephaestion says, almost as a menace, “or we’re leaving your car here until the end of time.”

Mydei stared at him, thinking about his options again, without seeing a real way out of that situation. If he got his keys back using his strength, he would have pressured him anyway and if he refused, they would have actually stayed there until they both died of old age. He could have left his car there and walked home too, but he would have eventually needed to get it out of that parking spot.

He sighed and put down Astraea, letting him take his hand anyway. “Fine,” he almost hissed out, taking his phone and doing what his friend had been asking him to. The child let his hand go so that he could reach the piece of paper in his pocket, almost as if he knew what he was about to ask him to do. It wasn’t the first time he noticed that he was pretty smart for a child as young as he was, but he didn’t make any further comment on it, out loud or in his mind.

He calmly copied the number on his phone with a deadpan expression, unsure of what to expect. He had the hunch that he had to act very detached when he talked to him due to his job, judging from what Astraea told him as well. 

It’s Mydeimos, from the hospital. Astraea explained to me what you talked about, sorry for walking away like that. I hope I didn’t hurt you, it was rude of me.

He didn’t really expect an answer to that, he probably was on the shift and he didn’t want to pry too much, but he immediately saw him typing, and he let out an exhausted sigh. He could already see the near future where Hephaestion was horribly right about this, and he would have had to thank his ex-boyfriend for setting him up with this guy.

You used this number!

Hi Mydei! No hard feelings!

Hope you like cats! ^-^ sorry for the drawing too, in case you don’t…

I hope we can be friends either way :D  

Oh, he’s stupid.

He’s so horribly stupid that he’s getting cuteness aggression.

He hesitated for a second, before writing back something that was hanging on his mind right after he received that message.

How did you know I liked cats?

I guessed! You look like one ^-^

(And Astraea told me to choose between cats and bunnies)

((Cats are easier and faster to draw))

He snorted at that answer. He got several comments about his resemblance to cats, he was used to them and he agreed with all of them, even if they said it was because of his personality. Rabbits or bunnies weren’t animals anyone could ever associate with him, but he could understand why Astraea thought of it. Since he met him, he saw Mydei in a very innocent light and held onto him for comfort, but he had the time to observe him too, maybe in a way no one else had.

Regardless, he was curious about the reason, so, since he probably knew the answer to that, he simply asked.

A bunny?

The answer didn’t arrive much later, just like before, and this time Mydei had to stop himself from smiling for how much he liked the sudden attention from someone that resembled way too much a human puppy.

He said that your hair looks like bunny ears :3

Very very cute <3

Astraea said that?

Yes!!!!

But I agree with him :3

Mydei felt a weird warmth in his chest, much similar to the emotions he went through whenever Hephaestion used to whisper sweet nothings next to his ear, but not familiar at all.

Phainon wasn't even present, he barely spoke to him and all they talked about was his son's medical exams, and yet, he was standing there smiling at his phone like an idiot after he told him he looked cute because he reminded him of a bunny.

He felt so utterly defeated after developing that crush at a worrying pace, only waiting to ask him out on that date that, at this point, looked unavoidable.

Not that he was complaining about seeing him outside of his workplace, he was genuinely happy about that, but he would have had to admit that Hephaestion was right.

He does like him and he does want to see him again, and if he didn't glance down to see the GIF of a happy puppy being pet he wouldn't have a dumb smile on his face that his friend definitely caught.

“Is that a smile?” Hephaestion immediately asked, catching that opportunity to poke some fun at him. Mydei just rolled his eyes and tucked his phone back in his pocket, ignoring him.

He didn't want to admit that he was right, not now and certainly not before he had a date with the guy in question.

“Mydei,” Astraea called, handing him his car keys. He looked at him with big, innocent eyes, all the body language of someone who just wanted to help him.

Smiling, he affectionately ruffled his hair and took the keys from his tiny, little hands. “Thank you, stardust.”

His eyes instantly glimmered of a newfound wonder, immediately hopping towards him to hold his hand, visibly excited about that little nickname. Mydei smiled, before picking him up and leaving a kiss on his cheek and on his neck, causing him to laugh loudly.

Knowing that he was still able to make those sounds, meaning every single emotion he felt during those moments, kept his heart at ease and reminded him who he was doing everything for now. He felt him excitedly move his legs as he giggled, before hugging him and resting his head on his shoulder.

He would give him the world, if it was possible.
