In such a short period of time– not even a day passed, he had to repeat to himself– he was sure he would have given it all for his well-being, no matter the cost. That little life depended on him, and he wouldn't have let him down after all the trust he gave him.

“Look at you…” Hephaestion walked closer, curiously looking at the two, “all happy in your own world.”

“A child changes your life, Hephaestion.” Mydei simply stated, feeling Astraea's face lifting up and tiny hands gripping on his clothes.

He nodded, seemingly in agreement, then took another glance at both of them. “Never said it didn't, but you're really happy. I haven't seen you like this for a long time.”

That observation made him think deeper, left wondering when was the last time he felt so… full. He couldn't remember a specific time, if not right at the beginning of his relationship with Hephaestion. They were young and in love, and everything felt so bright and joyous.

Except that not even those times could rival what he had been feeling as he was taking care of that child. He wasn't even his own, but he felt some kind of protective instinct that blossomed into waves of unconditional love in his heart, ready to do whatever it took to make him happier, even just by a little bit.

“Mydei, Mydei!”

That cheerful voice brought him back, and he found two tiny palms in front of his face. Without thinking too much, he kissed them, watching the excited reaction unravel right in front of him. He even let out a tiny, broken yell, visibly excited again.

He smiled, then opened the door of the car. “Off we go,” he warned, before putting him on the seat and protecting him by clicking the safety belt. The child let him, moving his legs and happily smiling at him.

Mydei heard Hephaestion open the door of the car and close it again, sign that he had to hop into it as well and actually drive him home. He closed the door next to Astraea and got into the car too, starting the car and starting to drive. Admittedly, his destination wasn’t too far away, but he knew that his next few stops would have needed a car just for the sheer amount of items he needed to buy and bring home.

They didn’t talk, but the silence was decently comfortable. Astraea hummed a few notes of a song he didn’t recognize, while Hephaestion looked content enough with how that morning turned out. He probably wanted to see Mydei move on, after all the time that passed and with how he avoided every dialogue about it when he visited him while he was in the hospital.

Mydei, on his part, was thinking about that bet he made about Phainon. He didn’t know if texting him to apologize counted as bumping into him, since he searched out for him out of basic kindness, but since it happened, he couldn’t get him out of his head. Hephaestion might have been exaggerating to push him to ask him out, but he was right about him being perfect for his situation and a good date for him.

He hated to admit it, but he was. It was completely different from Hephaestion or the people he slept around with, and maybe that was what he needed. He liked the… excited puppy behavior, despite how annoying it could be down the line. Regardless, it was cute. What’s more, he was objectively attractive and he felt comfortable about leaving his child with him.

Denying that he was slowly developing a crush for the guy was useless, at that point. Especially since he could feel his phone buzzing no stop in his pocket, certainly messages from him.

He sighed, then stopped the car next to Hephaestion’s place, waiting for him to step on the side of the road. He just wanted to keep his mind busy with anything else so he wouldn’t think about that stupid face and that even more stupid attitude.

“Bye-bye Hephaestion!” Astraea said, interrupting his thoughts. He just waved with a smile on his face as Hephaestion opened the door of the car, and Mydei was dreading the last words he would be saying to him.

“See you soon, little one!” He waved at the child, then turned towards Mydei and, with a lower tone, he said, “Keep me updated.”

He huffed. “So you can pick on me?”

“You know me so well!” He beamed, patting him on his right shoulder. “Have fun on that date, Mydeimos.”

He watched as he walked away, then inside of his apartment, and then he flung out his phone, with several messages from the same unsaved contact. If he didn’t come out insane from this, he swore he would have actually thanked every possible God he could. He skimmed through the messages, just a few sticking in his mind, and even those were odd.

Did no one ever call you a bunny?

Your hair really looks like bunny loops… It’s so cute!

By the way, I had the night shift, so I’m going to sleep after lunch

In case you try to contact me… I’m not ignoring you, I promise!!

[Image attached]

Tried my best!

[GIF attached]

He debated opening that picture. He didn’t know what he should have expected, but, given the context of earlier messages, he doubted he would have survived it. The GIF was just a bunny jumping around, looking rather happy, which just worried him further.

In the end, his curiosity was too great to ignore, and he ended up opening the photo. Mydei blinked at his phone for a second, baffled at what he was looking at.

Now he was firmly sure: that was the worst decision of his life.

It wasn't crazy in and of itself; it was just a piece of paper with a stylized version of himself with bunny ears instead of the hair perking up at either side of his head, with ‘bunnydei’ written right next to it with a red marker. Except, it was probably the cutest drawing of him he had ever gotten in his life and he was about to punch this man in retaliation.

For his own sanity, he put the phone down and didn't answer right away on purpose, electing to do so later. That is, if his phone didn't blow up in the meantime.

Mydei felt Astraea shift in his seat, before grabbing the seatbelt and keeping it close. As he turned to see what he wanted to say, he noticed the curious and innocent expression on his face, and his heart melted a little more. To even think that he was ever not his son or that he had to go through hell filled him with anger.

For the both of them, he had to carry those feelings and intentions, so that Astraea could live carelessly, at the very least.

“Where do we go now?” The child asked, curiosity and excitement crystal clear in his eyes. At least, all the pain that Mydei had seen on his face just the night before was being eliminated in favour of this kind of childlike wonder. He much preferred to see him like this.

“We’re going to the library,” Mydei answered, smiling at him. Astraea looked at him and nodded, a little confused by that sentence, to which he asked, “Do you know what that is?”

The child shook his head, eyes locked on Mydei's every move, expression and word. He looked like a lost little kitten, waiting for that answer.

For a second, Mydei wondered if his parents ever explained anything to him. He looked intelligent, but he didn't know basic things. Even a five year-old– which was the age Astraea said he was when he was asked before leaving the house, despite his stature and weight suggesting otherwise– should know what a library is, but he effectively looked lost on the meaning of that word.

He wondered if they ever explained any of their actions or the words they used, because, from what he had seen, he never interrupted two adults talking. He highly doubted he knew everything he and Hephaestion talked about, but he never asked either of them anything. Then, when there was silence, he followed it, not uttering a word.

He was probably taught that he just had to shut up and obey what the adults said, and it was something that Mydei vehemently, viscerally hated. Astraea was incredibly smart, he was just led to believe that he wasn't intelligent enough to speak when adults did, and it broke his heart.

As he looked at him, he imagined that must have felt like clipping his wings and stopping him from flying. He absorbed what he was told, and now he was afraid to simply ask the meaning of a word.

“A library,” Mydei started to explain, voice calm and patient, “is a place full of books. You can take some home, but you have to finish reading them and give them back.”

Astraea looked away, guilt and frustration written all over his face. “I can't read that well…” he whispered, almost like a secret confession that he didn't want to share.

Mydei smiled and reached out a hand to let it rest on his knee, almost offering it to him. He took it almost immediately, holding it with both of his tiny, fragile hands. He was clearly in distress over it, maybe because it was something new, maybe because he didn't want to let him down, but he wanted him to know that he was next to him, if he really didn't want to open up yet.

“We can take a few without many words and I'll help you with the rest,” Mydei suggested, as he let Astraea focus and play with the fingers of his hand. His eyes looked at him again, full of doubt and a faint sparkle of fear. He didn't let himself get distracted by it, and he asked, “You do like stories, right?”

Astraea nodded slowly, not completely confident in that decision, but electing to tell the truth instead.

Mydei smiled and gently patted him on his leg, a sign to get off of the car. “Then, come on, let's go.” He added, in case it wasn't entirely clear to him.

Leaving the car there, Astraea held his hand and silently followed him, still a little shaken from their earlier conversation. He looked at the ground and passively followed him, and it seemed to look at a flickering light about to stop functioning.

It was heartbreaking. To think that such a simple conversation completely changed his mood was something that he didn't think he would have ever had to witness. He looked fine ever since he rescued him, but he swore he heard a sniff just now.

At the first muffled cry, Mydei picked him up and kissed him on his forehead, looking at him with worried eyes. Astraea immediately grabbed his shirt and let a few tears flow, while a couple of sobs escaped his lips. A hand reached out to dry the wet cheeks clean, almost forcing the child to look at him with his lucid eyes reflecting apologies and guilt that he should have never felt just for not knowing what a word meant.

“You do know that I'm not mad at you, right?” Mydei asked, careful to keep his voice low and gentle. The last thing he needed was for that child to hide himself away more than he was doing already out of fear.

Astraea, instead, looked towards his hands, playing with the fabric of his shirt, and quietly whispered, “You will…”

“Why,” Mydei immediately shot back, still as gently as possible, “because you can't read?”

Maybe saying it out loud wasn’t the best idea, but he needed to understand the cause of it, first. It looked like an exaggeration to cry like that just because he didn’t know what a library was– and not knowing how to read seemed to be the right explanation for such a breakdown over simply picking up some books.

However, he expected him to cry a little more, maybe apologize again. What he absolutely didn't expect, not even in the worst situation, was seeing him wait for a scolding over something he had a difficulty with. 

Mydei waited in silence for a few seconds, looking at the child refusing to look at him out of guilt. He sighed, before he spoke again. “Hey, Astraea, baby,” he whispered, tilting his head lightly to catch his eyes again. It seemingly worked, because he raised his head, a little hesitant, but he did look at him as he smiled back. Astraea didn’t, instead biting his lower lip in fear.

It hurt to see him like that. He hated knowing what had to cause it, and he hated not being able to offer him a better solace yet.

“I won't be mad at you just because you can't read,” Mydei finally says, as softly and clearly as he possibly could.

He panicked almost immediately in response, trying to explain what was going on in his head. He was grateful that he felt safe enough to keep that conversation going, even if it hurt to see him in so much pain. “But I can't,” he whined, quickly gesturing with his hands, “and we're going there for…”

As he trailed off, Mydei sighed and crouched down, making him hop down from his arms. Astraea didn’t seem too excited about it, so he made sure to stay close to him, much like the previous night, when he saved him. “Astraea, listen to me,” he explained, voice low and gentle. He noticed the immediate attention he got as well, even with a little tint of anxiety in his body language. “It's normal not being able to read at your age. You'll learn, that's why I said I will help you.”

“But, Mydei…” 

“What’s the matter?” 

“You have… other things to do, right?”

Of course. He was afraid he would inconvenience him due to how much he just can’t do alone or on his own.

By that point, Mydei was losing his composure towards whatever his parents did to this child. It was obvious that he was echoing a sentiment that his parents repeated over and over again, and he thought that was just the cold, hard truth. That he wasted people’s time whenever he asked for help. That he just had to follow instructions and everyone else would have been happy and everything would have been fine. That, if he followed everything adults said and did it perfectly, he would have deserved the love and happiness in exchange.

He hated even thinking that those were this little child’s thoughts, but it wouldn’t be hard to believe that was the case, given how hellbent he had been about wasting his time and how often he apologized to him.

Mydei took a deep breath, forcing himself to keep his composure and offer the stability that he didn’t have before those last few hours. He was getting annoyed, but the last thing he wanted was the kid thinking it was aimed at him and not at his parents. He didn’t curse them just out of respect for keeping him alive and for the sake of the dead, but he couldn’t say that he didn’t think of doing it.

Astraea started becoming restless, even more anxious than before due to the sudden silence he received as a response, already treating it as a confirmation of what he believed. He lowered his head, almost in defeat, and stood in silence, patiently waiting, silently suffering on his own.

Seeing such a scene, Mydei gently ruffled his hair, slowly and gently, until Astraea decided to have enough courage to look up to him again. He smiled at him, tucking the long hair partly covering his left eye behind his ear, ever so affectionately. “I can always make time to help you,” he reassured him, in the clearest tone he could master. He needed him to understand that it was the truth of how he felt about the situation, at the very least. He didn’t need to believe it, just that his primary caretaker cared about him. “I'm here to help you, so don't worry if you can't do something. I'll be here to help you whenever you need.”

The reaction that followed was expected, but that didn’t mean it didn’t relieve his spirit any less. The boy stared at him for a couple of seconds, before heavy tears with no intention of stopping started flowing and loud wailing filled the parking lot. Mydei pulled him into a hug and let him bury his head against the fabric of his shirt, holding him as close as humanly possible. Caresses and hugs in those moments were a given and, even if he was used to dealing with children after having to babysit a few babies for Leonnius and Ptolemy, he wasn’t too sure where he should have gone from there. Most of them were younger, and definitely not in a situation even remotely similar to his.

The wailing gradually diminished across the following minute, so Mydei figured that it would have been safe enough to pick him up again. He kissed the top of his head immediately, trying to calm him down further. Astraea raised his head and finally looked up to him again, with his lucid, light brown eyes almost begging for his words to be true and his lips and tiny fists curled around the fabric of his shirt still trembling. Slowly, he let out a tiny sigh and reached up enough to hesitantly kiss him on his cheek, immediately backing up.

Mydei blinked for a few seconds, not registering that small act of kindness until he heard Astraea let out a small laugh. “Mom always said that I had to thank the people that helped me,” he explained, now with a small, shy smile on his face. At least, there were good things that his parents told him.

“Are you feeling better now?” Mydei asked, observing every inch of his face to make sure that, apart from the traces of tears on his cheeks, he wasn't too shaken up anymore. He didn't seem like it, even if it was a very sudden overturn of emotions and he was still worried about him.

He was five years old– almost six, but it was still a degree of emotion management that he wouldn't have expected from a teenager either. It almost felt as if he forced himself to abruptly wake up from a nightmare. It was a front, a farce, a way to shoulder part of a parent's duties.

Taking another look at him, though, all he saw was a child. A normal child, who liked to run and play, got excited about the smallest thing and had all the academic capabilities of a normal five year-old. Noticing all of it under the sun, so obviously, just made him understand even further just how fast he had to grow up and how much he wanted him to feel what other children his age felt instead.

Astraea touched his own chest, his little hand delicate like a feather in the wind, and quietly whispered, “It's still pepper and fire.” He raised his head, tentatively searching for some form of support. Then, after a couple of seconds, he muttered, “But… you can help?”

The biggest, most earnest smile spread on Mydei's face, and he held him closer. “Of course,” he whispered, hugging him as he did the same.

“Thank you…” Astraea added, right against his ear, with such a hopeful voice that his heart ached. He held him closer, just for a few seconds, until it was embedded in his mind just how much this tiny, little life completely relied on him to survive.

He let go soon enough, happy to see a smile on his son's face. He was genuinely joyful, slightly bouncing in his place. He smiled and put him down, feeling like he would have wanted to move around for a bit now. He forced him to be still at the hospital and sit afterwards, but he was still a child and he needed to run around for a while at least.

Astraea promptly sprinted in the direction he was going, jumping a few times while waiting for him, then turned around to hug him, all happily.

Ah, that child would have been the death of him. He feared the day he would have had to enroll him into school and not see him for an entire day.

At that same time, his phone started buzzing again, and he ignored it again, after muting it. He had no intention of knowing just how much that man was messaging him.

“So,” Mydei breathed, pushing away all his thoughts, “what stories do you like to read?”

He thought for a while, his eyes looking towards the sky as he held onto the fabric of Mydei's black pants. “I liked the ones Phainon told me,” he finally announced, looking at him again. “They were about… fairies and knights, they were so pretty.”

Of course he would like his stories.

Of course that man would haunt him every waking hour, now that he gave him his number.

Despite those feelings, Mydei kept on smiling at him. “Oh, really? What did he tell you?” He asked, with the kindest voice he could master. He didn't hate the idea of Astraea liking him, but even he didn’t know much about raising a child he just met, and he wouldn’t be surprised if Phainon didn’t either. Babysitting was one thing, but parenting was so impressively different and that little accident was a stark reminder of that fact.

It was true that he could see a future hanging out with that man and him being around Astraea, but he had to be careful. He wasn’t the only one in his thoughts anymore, he had to provide for a child and he had to keep it in the back of his mind if he would end up dating anyone.

“Mydei!”

He blinked, looking towards the kid. He must have lost himself in his thoughts enough that Astraea noticed it, and he wanted his attention back. Mydei admittedly didn’t know if that was the actual reason, but that idea settled in his mind and he couldn’t shake it off entirely. He smiled and crouched down again, welcoming his son in another embrace.

Mydei ruffled his hair and let him swing his arms around his shoulders, ever so excited about getting some attention and affection from him. “Sorry, stardust,” he apologized, with a soft voice, “were you saying?”

“Fairies are super pretty and they help people a lot.” He answered, keeping his eyes fixated on him, full of adoration and joy over simply telling him what he heard earlier that day. He noticed that he often placed his tongue in between his teeth when he stopped talking and smiled at him, as his entire body moved in excitement.

He was so cute. He wanted to hug him close and keep him safe every time he looked so happy and carefree, and he suddenly wondered if that was what his own mother felt when he was a child. Was she so full of love, fear, anxiety and pride all at the same time? Was she just good enough to not let it show? Did she feel this devastating weight driven by the knowledge that this small life completely relied on her to survive and grow up enough to make decisions on his own?

Mydei smiled as he looked at him still giggling, letting himself feel that warmth that was slowly spreading in his chest. “Do they, now?” He quietly asked, a tiny laugh sneaking in.

“That’s what Phainon said!” Astraea happily yelled, nodding in excitement.

“Do you want to get books about them?”

“Are there some?”

“I’m sure there are.”

Astraea smiled, satisfied with that answer, and grabbed his hand, slightly pulling it. Mydei laughed briefly, before standing up and listening to what he wanted to do. He was happy that he partly understood that he could ask for certain things, even if they were just minor and only the ones that overlapped with his suggestions. Small steps are still steps forward, he reminded himself.

They quickly walked into the building, but Astraea hesitated, without leaving Mydei’s side or letting go of his hand. “But… is it okay if I can’t read?” He asked, then looked up to look at him, the doubt in his voice tangible in the air.

“No one knows how to read, at some point. We’re here so that you can learn how to read on your own, at your pace,” Mydei got on his knees and explained patiently again until he saw him nod, the initial doubt vanishing to make place with a faint trust in his words. He looked around to spot the section where he could go search some books he liked on his own, without feeling too much pushing from an adult, and he pointed towards it. “Do you want to go around and search for something you like? Search for the butterfly and the owl. Do you know what that is?”

The child nodded with confidence. “A big, fluffy, scary bird.”

“Yeah, exactly,” he laughed in response, then affectionately ruffled his hair. “I'll wait here, okay?”

Astraea excitedly nodded, then yelled a little “‘kay!” and curiously walked towards the area pointed at by Mydei, starting to look at some books with a cute, little perplexed expression on his face.

He was so cute . He could thank every possible deity for that little miracle that was given to him.

Mydei smiled at himself and leaned against the wall, taking out his phone. Maybe it was the right time to check how his nurse was doing, since he left him unattended. As soon as he switched on his phone, though, he felt himself making an utterly disgusted face at the sheer amount of emoticons, GIFs and words full of typos. He audibly groaned, not really knowing what to even think. It felt like talking to a high schooler, instead of a man in his 20s.

Do you blow up everyone’s phone like this or am I getting some special treatment?

Mydei! Did you like the drawing?

:33333

It’s cute.

He didn’t know why, but he thought of an excited puppy again. Maybe that was just how he was, excited all the time that he got even just the slightest bit of attention.

Cute, he thought, before he could stop himself. He threw his head back and closed his eyes, exhausted. How could he go from someone as composed, mature and mischievous as Hephaestion to this? It felt like having to choose between an elegant siamese cat and the most annoying husky on the planet. And he was willingly choosing the latter. Something had to be wrong with him, by that point.

He looked down, noticing another few messages, one of them being the GIF of a smiling white dog. This man was about to destroy his life. Or his patience. Probably both.

Regardless, he left a question unanswered and, if he had to witness this charade, he better get an actual response.

[GIF attached]

Happy you like it!

You didn’t answer my question.

Absolutely special treatment ^-^

Lucky me.

He didn’t know if he meant it as a joke or not yet, but he didn’t let it bother him further. After all, they came to the library not only to get his sweet, beautiful child some books to read and help him to read. The few perks in having a close friend working in a library was, obviously, getting some books ahead of others, whether he wanted or not, since Ptolemy did it anyway whenever he saw a book he liked.

Mydei walked over to him, where he usually sat hearing about what the people who came in wanted to get or searched for, and his eyes immediately shined, obviously pleased to see him.

“Mydeimos!” He greeted him, with a smile on his face. Mydei did the same, a little awkwardly, since it had been some time since he last visited him in that place. Ptolemy looked over his shoulder for a few seconds, then back to him and he asked, “Are you babysitting again?”

He turned, catching Astraea holding a couple of books and uncertainty looking towards him, most likely thinking of giving him privacy. It was a nice thought, but Mydei just couldn’t stand that disappointed face, and gestured to get closer. The child, obedient as ever, quickly walked over to him and rested his head against his side, still holding the books tightly. 

Mydei caressed his head mindlessly, turning to his friend again. “No, I took him in,” he quickly answered, before moving on to the reason he was there. “Ptolemy, do you know if the books I asked for arrived?”

“Uh,” Ptolemy breathed, a little confused and taken aback, “yeah, they did, but– a child? You adopted a kid?”

“Why are you so surprised?”

“After your break-up, I didn't expect you to do it, that's all.”

Right. The break-up. He forgot how bad it was, for all of them. He threw himself on his job, took on other quick favors for his friends to keep his mind busy and, occasionally, ended up having one night stands. Hephaestion’s absence was a first for him too, and he didn’t know how else to fill that void. New friends were off the table, he was worried sick every day of getting a call announcing his untimely death and he struggled to see colors in his life again.

The break-up itself wasn’t the problem– everything that followed was. Some of those feelings that he agreed didn’t feel for Hephaestion lingered as he visited him in that stupid hospital room, forced to see him lying on that stupidly cold and anonymous bed on which someone else probably died, and he didn’t find the strength to go on.

That is, of course, until a day prior. He was starting to see the point of living again, and he slowly began to accept his situation. Whoever said that children could change anyone’s life for the better or the worse extremely fast was right. Even if a full day had yet to pass by, after he witnessed two breakdowns and a few other crises the child had, accompanied by a near-death experience for both, he felt pretty confident in saying his life was better now.

“Well,” Mydei sighed, “he had no one. I didn't want to leave him to social services.”

Ptolemy, for a mysterious reason that no one could properly, logically explain, simply laughed at him. He would have taken offense, if he didn’t know just how much the other knew him. “If that was the only reason, he wouldn't be here.” He spat, without many turnarounds or complicated words as he usually did.

He wasn’t wrong. He did have an actual reason behind that choice, seemingly made on a whim. 

“He reminded me of… myself. Before I met you.” He managed to explain, feeling the sudden gaze of the child on him too. He didn’t mind him knowing, but he would have made questions, and he didn’t know just how much he could tell him right now. He understood many things, but he was very sensitive too, and he didn’t want to burden him with an even heavier emotional baggage.

He ignored the tiny, little curious sound that came from him too, even if it hurt him. Maybe it was because he worked with a lot of kids around his age, but Ptolemy understood the situation and reached out a hand. “Little one,” he whispered, looking at Astraea with a gentle smile, “would you like to take those home?”

He turned to look at Mydei, in search of an affirmative statement. As soon as he got a slight smile and an almost unperceptive nod, he turned towards the librarian again and handed his books to him, shyly and with a tint of hesitation. “Thank you, sir,” he added, with the tiniest, most polite voice he ever heard coming from him yet.

He never acted like that with him, but they did meet in a peculiar way, and he had no idea how he first greeted Phainon, since he wasn’t there. He was shy with Hephaestion as well, almost as if he was afraid of others, especially adults, but Mydei wouldn’t know how to interpret it yet. He made a mind note to keep it under control, in case other factors added to it, but that was all he realistically could do.

“Ah, these are good books. You have a good eye,” Ptolemy exclaimed, registering them in the system, before giving them back to him and Mydei’s books in his hands. “Here you go.”

“Thank you!” Astraea smiled happily, keeping the books clutched to his chest. Mydei took his books too, then offered a hand towards the child to hold his as well. As a response, he got a violent head shake, which he silently accepted.

In the end, they calmly went back to the car, piling up the books in the backseat and hopping in the car again, same places as before. 

“Are we going home now?” Astraea asked with a curious voice, hanging his mouth open again, as he often did right after he spoke.

Kept the pacifier for too long , Mydei thought, perfectly knowing that was the cause because Leonnius told them all the time when they were younger. They didn't really care, but he still did it, as if laying his tongue against his palate was an epic adventure everyone just had to hear about.

“Are you tired?” Mydei asked, understanding how he could need a nap soon. He hoped he would last until their last destination, but those breakdowns had to be draining. “We have one last stop, we need food and some toys for you to play with.”

At the mention of the latter, he perked up, suddenly excited. Mydei let out a soft laugh, thinking again about how cute that little child was. He didn't need much– just a few toys, food, affection and attention. That was all that made him happy, at the moment, and luckily he was able to give them all to him.

Astraea's curiosity got the best of him, and he asked, with a little too much excitement, “What kind of toys?”

“We’ll find out when we get there.”

“After that?”

“After that, we get home, we eat, you take a nap and then we go and see if I can formally adopt you.”

He had no reason to sugarcoat any of what he intended to do, even with the adoption. He wasn’t a toddler, he understood most of what he told him, no matter how complicated it was, and he was starting to warm up to him. It wasn’t too far-fetched to assume that he would have agreed to being his son. That was what he hoped, at least.

Astraea, though, slowly tilted his head like a confused puppy. Mydei smiled, feeling pleasant warmth in his chest as he thought how cute he was. “Adopt?” He asked, with a perplexed voice.

“To live with me, we need to go through some procedures,” Mydei calmly explained, as clearly as he could. “It shouldn't take too long, but it's necessary for me to take care of you the way I did since we met.”

The kid gasped and brought his little fists in front of his mouth, his eyes slightly afraid at the opposite possibility. “I want to stay with you…” He faintly whispered, a tint of fear and anxiety in his voice.

Mydei immediately reached out a hand while he was driving for him to hold briefly, simply to get grounded for a moment. He caught it as soon as he saw it with both of his hands, rubbing against his skin. “Mhm, that's why we're doing it. It will be a bit boring, so you can take your books with you while we wait there.”

Astraea nodded, a little more confidently, and let go of his hand, letting him use it to drive again. The supermarket wasn’t far, really, but it felt like forever, so when they did arrive there, his child redefined the meaning of hyperactive. He jumped, hopped, ran, interested in every single item on the shelves, calling his name every two seconds.

It didn’t bother him. He was quite happy about it, in fact. He was partly afraid to lose him, but he had always been a good child and, no matter how excited he was, he always kept his vicinity with him because he wanted his attention all the time. He happily gave it to him, as long as he kept on smiling and came back to him.

One thing that he did outside of his dear son being more excited as he had ever seen him, though, was checking his phone, because he felt in his bones that the man that recently acquired his number wasn’t done sending him the most random messages yet. Thus, he wasn’t surprised when he saw a list of items and GIFs representing the said item, all just to get him to text him.

He was so annoying. 

And yet, he still texted back, instead of ignoring him.

Please, stop using my number as a grocery store list.

Ouchie…

Grown ass man saying ouchie. Via text.

Ah, but you feel closer now!

I feel like we’ll become great friends, Mydei!!

Sure thing.

“Astraea!”

The voice calling his son made him snap out of the attention he gave to the phone, looking in the direction it came from. As soon as he saw his child, his heart settled again from the initial panic, afraid that something might have happened. Luckily, it was just Phainon greeting him, dressed like a human traffic light. Mydei almost averted his gaze to conceal the look of disgust on his face over seeing those clothes. A part of himself prayed that he would have just decided to walk around in his nurse uniform instead, if that was the result of him trying to dress himself.

Astraea, bless his tiny, innocent soul, didn’t seem to care much and simply yelled a greeting, “Phainon!”

He smiled at the little kid, then took a quick look at Mydei and his eyes sparkled, as if they suddenly shone a new light just by looking at him. He didn’t know what to think of it yet, but his heart did skip a beat, after being looked at like that. Thankfully, his composure was still intact, and slowly walked up to him, fully knowing that he would have to respect the promise that he made to Hephaestion now.

By that point, he didn’t even know if he hated it or not.

“Do you always lose your kid?” Phainon joked, smiling brightly at him. Mydei noticed that the smile in front of him was genuine this time, so he did fake them earlier as part of his job. Disappointing.

“I don't,” Mydei bluntly stated, “he just greeted you because he likes you.”

“Oh, really?” He beamed, just like a little sunshine. He hated how much he didn’t bother talking to this guy, at moments even liked it. Phainon caught his attention again, leaning against his shopping cart with his arms, and smiling even more than before, somehow. “How is the adoption going?”

“We’re going to go this afternoon. I wanted to get him books, clothes and toys first.”

“Understandable! They will definitely grant you the adoption of that kid.”

Something about that statement stuck with him. He was so confident that he would have absolutely gotten that custody right away, even if he didn’t know either of them at all. Sure, he talked with Astraea for a while and Mydei himself texted him, but he didn’t know anything more than that. It was… a curious statement, one that definitely caught his attention again.

Despite that, he didn’t really have doubts about it. He knew that he would be granted the adoption because everyone is just too lazy to strip the child away from him if he already could raise him without problem. “I know,” he calmly answers, letting Astraea look through the toys and puzzles in that section, but keeping an eye on him too.

Phainon looked at him for a few seconds, almost observing him, before saying, “You look anxious.”

“I’m not.”

“You do look tense, though…”

“It’s your imagination.”

He truly didn’t want to talk much more about it, even if he didn’t have many doubts about that adoption. He was already sharing enough with this man, he didn’t need to open up his heart to him right away and about something as delicate as adoption, both for him and Astraea. He didn’t mind hanging out with him, but that needed to happen, before he would even be honest with private matters with him.

“Mydei!” Astraea’s excited voice interrupted his thoughts, butting in between the two. Both looked at him as he raised a giant dog plushie, basically the same height as he was. Mydei blinked, slightly thrown aback, while Phainon let out a quick affectionate laugh. “Can we buy this?”

“Isn’t it too big for you?”Mydei gently made him realize, not even sure he was able to hug it.

Promptly, Astraea put it on the top of his head, then innocently asked, “Pillow?”

Mydei stared at him, thinking about what to say, pondering about how he was going to say that, no, he didn’t need such a big plushie, he could pick any other one that was easier to carry around, and he already had pillows.

The only problem with this approach was, however, that he looked so awfully cute while making that question, and he couldn’t say no to him. “Sure, it can be a pillow,” he ended up answering instead, granting him yet another thing he asked for. That child was a light in the darkness that was slowly pulling out of his misery, but he couldn’t say the same was happening to his wallet.

“You’re buying a lot,” Phainon noticed, maybe taking a jab at how affectionate and permissive he was with anything his child did. Mydei didn’t know if that was the reason why he was smiling, but he decided to ignore it for his own mental well-being.

Mydei huffed, tilting his head towards him, looking slightly annoyed. “Would you be able to say no to him? He gets so excited.”

Phainon smiled and nodded, seemingly agreeing with him, but he quickly settled on a sadder expression, despite the smile still present. “He looks like a different child from a few hours ago…” He noted, then slightly tilted his head, curious. “Did something happen?”

“How do you–”

“I know my ways around traumatized kids! Nurse, remember?”

He always forgot how many traumatized kids there must be in a hospital that nurses had to tend to. Some had terminal illnesses, others had to deal with hard situations at home, and many others had a variety of problems that they shouldn’t have had to deal with at such a young age. Of course, he would notice the difference, after how much he talked with him earlier that day and seeing how ecstatic he was now.

“He broke down because he didn't know how to read,” Mydei quickly explained, calmly and with a monotone voice, as if he was explaining a fun trivia about some wild animal. It wasn’t like he could hide it by now, so he didn’t see the point in lying to him or not answering, especially since Astraea trusted him.

Phainon blinked, a little confused. After all, everyone would be, after a similar answer and no other context. “Really?”

Mydei let out a heavy sigh, nodding. “He feared that… not being able to read would warrant me abandoning him on the side of the road.” He recalled those moments, even if he hated remembering his child so afraid and desperate over such a small issue.

“And you… talked to him?”

“Took a while, but looks like he's internalizing it.”

Phainon smiled again, a genuine, kind, fond smile that he had yet to see on his face. It was pretty, he thought, before he mentally smacked himself for it. He just couldn’t like a guy like this, who couldn’t dress for the life of him and sent messages that felt more like a ticking bomb full of overflowing love, rather than scarce but important reminders of someone who cared.

That smile, however, was sweet, pleasant and somewhat caring. Mydei liked seeing it. It felt good, knowing it was aimed at him. It was different from the sweet nothings that Hephaestion used to whisper to him, it felt grounding and tangible, far from promises that faded away after mere seconds.

He would like to see it more often.

Before he realized what he just thought, Phainon distracted him, seemingly not being able to shut up. “You’re really good with children! Sure you can't help us in the hospital?” He asked, obviously as a joke, but there was some sort of hope in his stupidly bright eyes and he couldn’t tell if it was an actual suggestion for an outing or not.

Regardless, it wasn’t important. If he wanted to, he could ask him clearly.

Mydei huffed, turning toward Astraea, who was still skimming through the puzzles section. His eyes were focused and attentive, probably struggling to read what was written on the box. His heart ached for a second, but he was glad he was facing his problems head-on now, without hiding or running away from them. He felt a tint of pride in his chest, but he fought against himself to keep himself composed in that moment.

You’re talking to someone else, Mydei. You can feel proud and happy about your genius child later.

“I was able to do it because he's special,” he answered, turning back to the man with him. “He's so intelligent, he always understands whatever anyone says.”

Phainon excitedly nodded. Cute. “I noticed!” He exclaimed, never turning his gaze from Mydei’s figure. He didn’t hate it. “He's incredibly smart, for a child of his age.”

Mydei was about to try and kill his own mind. Stop making him compliments, stop thinking he’s cute, stop not being bothered by his constant staring. Except, he didn’t want to. His gaze hurt him like a spear trying to pierce his skin, peeling his every layer and understanding him more and more. There was some sort of desire– maybe lust– about simply knowing what kind of person he was.

And it excited him.

He stared back at him, eyes fixated on his face, just then noticing the slight tint of pink on his cheeks. He was unsure if it was embarrassment or excitement. Maybe both.

A hand tucked on his shirt then, making him pay attention to his child again, the image of Phainon’s face still vivid in his mind. “Mydei, Mydei, what's this?” He asked, mouth hanging open and curious eyes.

Mydei sighed, recomposing himself again, and grabbed the box. “A puzzle,” he answered, quickly reading what was written on it. Looking back at him, he handed it to him again. “A thousand pieces is a lot, Astraea, pick up another one. Two digits or three digits with 1 as the first number.”

He smiled and energetically nodded, before starting to look through the shelves again, with the same focused stare from before. Mydei followed him, his every muscle relaxing after witnessing him on yet another adventure. He could cry because of how much love he felt every time he did pretty much anything. Affection, pride, love, a need to protect him. He felt every single one of those constantly, lighting his chest ablaze with a quiet, nice light he wasn’t sure he would have ever experienced, if it wasn’t for him.

Maybe feeling like he stopped talking to him, Phainon finally stood up from the shopping cart he was leaning on and smiled at both again, genuine again. Mydei really liked seeing those. “I’ll leave you two to your shopping!” He announced, already moving to leave.

“Wait,” Mydei said, before even realizing, “do you want to hang out? After tomorrow.”

That simple question obviously threw him off. He stared at him, opened his mouth, closed it again, and just nodded, eyes eager with anticipation. Very cute. “Yeah,” he whispered at the end, a little out of breath. “Sure, why not! Cool! See you two around!”

With that, he disappeared behind shelves, leaving Mydei staring at the general direction where he disappeared with such a hurry. He felt his cheeks get slightly warmer, but he put the blame on the sudden heat of the doors opening not too distant from them, given the humidity and warmth outside. It was possible it brought in some more heat–

“Mydei is all red.” Astraea interrupted his half assed attempt at justifying himself, holding another puzzle in his hands. Mydei immediately turned and, embarrassed, he coughed and threw the new puzzle box in the cart without making sure it was appropriate for him to do, quickly pushing it again.

The child obediently followed him, asking for a hand to hold. Mydei obliged almost on auto-pilot, his mind still lingering on that moment from a few seconds before. He definitely didn’t blush because he thought that quick retreat after struggling to speak over being asked out was kind of endearing, and his son definitely didn’t call him out on it.

Mydei took a big, deep breath, as he approached the food aisle, thinking that morning was being way too long for his own good. The sooner it ended, the sooner he could have stopped thinking about that man.

Unfortunately, though, the universe is cruel, and he feels his phone buzzing again.

He was certainly never getting rid of that nurse now, wasn’t he?

Chapter End Notes

This took me forever to write but I wanted to put out the actual start for phaidei...... hope it was enjoyable at least :]
