chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

“You just felt and squeezed my boobs–”
“For fuck's sake.”
He truly found himself a first degree nuisance.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Mydei simply watched as his son let the nurse take his blood after the doctor that Phainon referred them to ran some general exams. He had to admit that the man had pretty good connections in that hospital– the doctor was nice, welcoming, patient and didn't sugarcoat what she thought those results meant. He liked that attitude and modus operandi. 

Looking at her, he wouldn't have imagined she'd ever be a doctor. She had pink and light blue hair in two pigtails at either side of her head, a gentle smile and pretty, shiny green eyes. If anything, she looked like she was cosplaying some character instead.

Maybe because he looked too lost in thought, his brows furrowed into an aggressive expression, she smiled and proclaimed, with a gentle voice, “Astraea is in perfect health! You don't have to worry.”

“Thank you so much,” Mydei answered, just as kindly, before trailing off. He tried to remember her name, but he was thinking so much about Astraea that he couldn't even recall that.

“Right! My name is Hyacine,” she introduced herself, in a way that implied that she didn't do it yet. Maybe, then, Mydei overthought the situation and she never said her name in the first place. His son reached out for his hand then and he promptly held it, letting him get as close to him as possible.

That was his first time getting a blood test done, probably, but he didn't even question what was happening. “What a good child would do” was what most people thought. He was well-behaved, always listened to Mydei and was extremely polite to other adults. All of it was true, he knew that, but he couldn't help but think where it came from. Was he actually well behaved, or was it drilled into his skull by his parents?

He knew that he wasn't allowed to ask questions already, so nothing would have stopped them from scolding him into being well-behaved to adults in general. At least, though, he was leaving those behaviours away whenever he was with Mydei. He could feel the adoration and love he had for him even in those little gestures, and it warmed his heart like nothing else before.

Hyacine stopped them for a bit before letting them go, giving them the date and place of their next visit, since she had her own study outside of the hospital. Mydei still didn't fully understand why they had that visit there, but he guessed that it was because she helped out often there, other than being on her own too.

He didn't know if he was happy about being able to walk into Phainon in the hallways or not anymore. Unfortunately, he did warm up to him and he concluded that he wanted to see him again, and Hephaestion was right.

As he noticed the doctor getting ready to send them off, he pushed out that thought. He watched as she waved kindly at his child, with a kind smile on her face, and waited until he waved back before walking out with him. It honestly went way better than he expected and he did a lot more exams than he thought he would. He understood why, he had no idea of which conditions he might have had and he wasn’t entirely sure how much he actually went to a hospital to get checked up due to the parents he found himself with, but he was happy that he followed what the doctor and nurse said.

“Does it hurt?” Mydei asked, looking at the piece of cotton on his right arm. Honestly, he would have never guessed his dominant hand was the left one, but he was glad that he didn’t feel too ashamed over it, at least.

“It stings,” Astraea answered, looking at that exact spot on his arm. “Like… the thing you made the other day.”

“... Eggplant?”

“Yeah!”

He didn’t like eggplant. That was something he recently learned as well, but he could eat it if he put a lot of cheese on it and, he guessed, if he concealed it in some way. When he suggested they would eat it for dinner the day before, he looked absolutely disgusted, but he luckily agreed to try it with cheese– because ‘Mydei could make even bad foods taste good’– and he ended up liking it.

At least, he had enough trust in his skills in the kitchen to eat anything he fed him and voice if he liked something or not. It took a few tries at first, but, especially after their time at the library, he was way more talkative and expressed himself more.

“Look who just got their first blood test done!”

His head whipped around after merely hearing that voice, finding Phainon smiling at the both of them, in his usual light blue nurse uniform. Mydei noticed just then the golden, sun shaped tattoo on the side of his neck, and he couldn’t help but think how beautiful it was. He would have smacked himself for that thought by now, but at that point he didn’t even mind. Astraea loved him, he liked him, he was interesting, he wanted to know him. There was no reason for him to avoid him.

Talking about his son’s love for that man, Astraea smiled at him and jumped in excitement as soon as he saw him. “Phainon!” He yelled, excitedly waving at him.

He smiled and crouched down, putting up both hands for him to give him a double high five, to which Astraea surely didn’t hesitate on doing exactly that, with the same excitement he always showed. Mydei smiled softly at the scene, beyond happy that he felt comfortable to play around with another adult the way he did with Phainon. Of course, maybe it was because he worked with children and he was good at dealing with them, but Ptolemy was too, and he didn’t get nearly the same reaction.

He was definitely going to get stuck with him, and he didn’t mind at all.

Despite that, he couldn’t help but tease him a little bit, almost like keeping up a play they pushed themselves into. “Do you actually work here, or do you just stand in the hallway until I happen to walk past it?”

“I am a licensed nurse and I do work here, thank you very much!” Phainon answered, standing up straight again. Mydei looked at him as he smiled, then gestured towards Astraea. “I just wanted to check if Astraea here was feeling well.”

“I do! The doctor was full of bubbles.” The child answered, leaning against Mydei’s legs acting a little shy about that specific sentence. He looked at the adult with his mouth agape, almost asking for help and his touch.

Mydei immediately ran his hand through his hair, a newfound warmth spreading throughout his chest when he heard him let out a soft giggle, then again when he grabbed his hand with his two tiny, little ones. He glanced at him with soft eyes full of love, before turning to a very confused Phainon again.

He could guess why Astraea felt shy about pronouncing those words, mostly because they had to be confusing to others. He learned that he used concrete experiences he went through to describe his feelings sometimes, instead of adjectives or the name of the feeling itself, but they were pretty easy for Mydei to understand.

“He means that he likes her and he feels safe around her.” He translated, immediately noticing his shoulder relax.

“Oh, yeah,” he agreed, even if he wasn't sure on what, “Hyacine is pretty popular among kids. She's cute and kind, right?”

He had to know her, if he talked with such a casual tone. He didn't mind, really, it was more shocking that this man actually had close friends as nice and respectful as she was and still didn't know the concept of personal space.

As he was about to ask him about it, though, he changed topics completely, leaning in with a smile on his stupidly pretty face. “It's still pretty impressive that the adoption was as fast as it was,” he noted, obviously asking for more information. He didn't know if it was something he liked or hated about him yet.

The adoption itself was… quite fast, but Mydei had to delay that visit of several days before he could be legally recognized as his father. He was sure that if Gnaeus didn’t put a good word for him and he wasn’t the only survivor of such a recent fire, he would still be on a waiting list.

“Yeah, well… I do have good credentials and this was a special case. They just asked a few questions, looked at the documents my boss sent them and realized that I was their best possible candidate.” Mydei calmly explained, as he let his child play with his hands while he made curious cooing sounds. Somehow, he was able to ignore it enough to see Phainon’s face morph into a perplexed expression, not completely sure about what.

Immediately afterwards, though, that questioning stare vanished, making way for his usual happy-go-lucky smile. The fake one. The one that Mydei wasn't too fond of. He wished he stopped doing that around him, even if it was just for courtesy. If he genuinely wanted to be his friend– or more, for that matter– he had to let it go or, alternatively, explain himself.

That, however, was running way too much for what they were now. You barely know each other , Mydei had to remind himself, it doesn't matter how cute you think he is or how much Astraea adores him. You barely know his name and his job.

“You did read the papers, right?”

Phainon's voice made him snap his head towards him, a little startled. He must have thought a little too much, and he lost himself in his mind. It was something he did without realizing, sometimes. His mind was a safe, familiar place where he could choose the best possible course of action before even letting his body move.

Unfortunately for him, Astraea and Phainon seemed to defy that rule that he had always taken for granted. Children weren't predictable, especially the one he took in, and the man in front of him was… elusive. Peculiar. Interesting. His behaviour challenged him in ways that any other friendship never had. He liked that feeling. Not even Hephaestion made him experience something even remotely similar to what he was currently effortlessly putting on the table through their every conversation.

Having considered all of it, his actual question was one of the most insulting to his intelligence he had ever received and he had to think twice about how to give an answer that didn't involve a straight punch to the face.

“Who do you take me for? Of course I read the papers before signing something that could have put a child in danger.”

Good. Normal, calm, controlled answer. Just accept that he has the maturity of a husky howling at three in the morning over a leaf falling into the house and that you're somehow attracted to it and everything will be fine.

Phainon smiled again, this time a little embarrassed, but it was at least more genuine than that stupid, useless fake smile devoid of any shimmer of light he insisted on showing him. If he could, he would write it out of existence. “By the way, how old is he? Do you know?” He asked, completely changing the topic. Mydei should have expected it, but he decided to let him off, for the moment.

“Almost six!” Astraea yelled, happily gesturing a number five with his hands. Smart boy.

“All grown up, then!” Phainon smiled, showing actual joy on his face again, before turning back to look at Mydei. This time, his eyes were soft and relaxed, almost weirdly melancholic. “Mydei, regarding what we talked about…”

Not melancholy. Anxiety and desire because he genuinely wanted to see him again.

Those were the moments when he felt something more than just curiosity for him. He was so bold, he acted so sure of himself in trying to impress him, but he had this fear of getting involved with him too much as well.

He wanted to know why. He wanted to know more about him. He wanted to be able to say that he was his friend, at the very least, because seeing him run away like that was starting to crack open his heart.

“Just tell me when,” Mydei calmly answered, after taking everything into consideration. He was always free, and he wanted him to know he wanted this too, so he added, “I will make sure to be free.”

Phainon gave him an apologetic smile, completely unlike what Mydei was expecting from him at the mention of that date that he promised him. He thought he'd be happy, with how much he was trying to get to know him and how badly he obviously wanted to meet him outside of working hours. Maybe not a proper date, but he at least wanted to hang out with him.

Instead, he shrugged and looked at him with clear interest in his bright blue eyes. Mydei was starting to struggle to understand what it was that he wanted by that point, and he felt invested in him once again. “First I wanted to ask… how old are you? I feel like I know more about your child, than I do about you.” He suddenly asked, completely ignoring his earlier question.

Mydei stared at him for a good minute before processing what he just said. Of all things when proposed to a date, he wanted to know his age? He was aware it was important in some cases, but he was obviously a grown adult with a job and able to sustain a child, and he was as well. Why would that be his first question, even?

Either way, he did answer. “Twenty-five,” he breathed out, still confused. “Can’t you look at my birth year on your computer?”

“Who did you take me for? It’s against policy, and I wanted to ask you first.” He explained, echoing his answer from earlier. Of course, he had to tease him about it, probably because his thoughts were easy to guess at that moment. Phainon tilted his head and smiled, his cheeks tinting a warm pink color, seemingly pleased by the answer. “You look older,” he added, as if to explain that reaction.

It didn't explain anything. On the contrary, Mydei was more confused than before. What was he so happy about? Was he older? Did he think he was suddenly cuter? Why the fuck did he have to pick someone with so many weird quirks and why did he kept on liking them?

He huffed as he felt his face get hotter, still unsure if for the annoyance or because that reaction embarrassed him, but his voice remained stable. “I get that quite often.”

“Well! I’m twenty-seven.”

“Good to know.”

Older, as he thought. He was used to it, all his friends were older and kept on pampering him, just like his mother and sister did. He was used to being the baby of the group. Regardless, he didn't know him that well, and no one had that reaction only upon hearing his age. He, on the other hand, was excited because of it.

“Mydei, is this one of the adult talks that I shouldn’t be listening to?”

He almost forgot Astraea was witnessing all of it. He didn't know if that was flirting or not, but he felt… guilty for bringing him into it without realizing it. There was something about that man that made him erase everything happening around him and use all his brain power only on him. Judging by his reaction, though, he knew that he made the same mistake, at least.

Mydei honestly didn’t know if this would be labelled as an adult-only conversation, with how excited Phainon was at the prospect of their age gap, but the fact that Astraea picked up on it probably meant that he shouldn't have been listening to it.

Seeing his panic, Phainon immediately brought back his question, maybe as a way to apologize for acting like that as well. “Is it fine over the weekend?”

“When? The weekend has 48 hours.” Mydei asked, affectionately petting his child's hair. He didn't want him to think he couldn't ask questions, but he also couldn't possibly answer honestly to that specific one either.

Astraea just turned and hugged him, maybe a little tired. He hid his face in Mydei's thigh, letting out soft, tired whines. They did wake up earlier and he didn't know how much he actually slept, given the nightmares he often had during the last few nights, so it might have been just related to it.

Mydei crouched down and the child crashed in his arms, holding onto him without a word. Poor child must have been exhausted.

He picked him up in his arms, letting him rest a little on his shoulder and gave him an affectionate kiss on his forehead for good measure. As soon as Astraea felt it, he hugged him a little bit tighter, pushing his head between his shoulder and neck.

Switching his attention to Phainon again, he smiled and answered his previous question. “Saturday at seven?”

Mydei nodded, keeping Astraea steady in whatever position he wanted. “See you then.” He greeted Phainon, who probably had to go back to working by now.

“See you!” He yelled back, finally walking away from them.

Mydei looked at him as he walked away, only for a few seconds, until he felt little fists curling around his clothes. He didn't turn towards the child in his arms right away– he suspected the reason and he didn't want to confirm or deny the situation. He has been holding onto him for dear life, not even being able to sleep properly if not with him, gravitating around him at any given second, to the point of his mood heavily depending on his presence. 

He felt his head brushing against his neck, searching for comfort, and he finally gave in. He left a kiss on the top of his head and held him closer, letting him know that he was aware of his requests and was willing to accept a discussion.

Hesitantly, he raised his head, fear clear in the way he looked at him. Mydei wished he could keep him in his arms forever, protect him from all those ugly feelings that he kept experiencing and give him all the love and support he deserved in their place.

Unfortunately, he couldn't. Whether he liked it or not, those feelings and thoughts would have stayed with him for a long time and he could just help guide him into feeling them less often, for the moment.

“You and Phainon are going out?” Astraea weakly asked, clearly afraid of the answer that he would receive.

That helpless, desperate voice almost broke his heart. He was so scared that he would just abandon him like his parents did that he couldn't even think about someone else being asked to babysit him. He probably didn't even want anyone else, except for Mydei, simply because he was the only person that he genuinely trusted and felt comfortable with. Even with Hephaestion he had to be pushed to simply talk to him.

Astraea started shaking lightly, his fists holding more strongly onto his shirt, his eyes welling with tears as he didn't receive an answer. Mydei didn't even control his body when he felt himself hug him instinctively. He simply held him, whispering promises that he fully intended to maintain.

“Shh, baby, I'm here,” he whispered next to his ear, trying desperately to ignore the little sob he heard escaping his lips. He hated knowing that the reason why he held onto him so strongly was because he was the first adult in his life that extended a hand to him and treated him as a child. He knew what it felt like, having a parental figure abandon their own kid, the ugly feelings it evoked, and being aware that he had no one either didn’t help. He held him a little tighter, letting him know that he was there for him. “I'll always come back and you will always be safe, I promise.”

The child’s sobs raised in volume as he looked up, almost shamefully, his shoulders trembling as hot, wet tears slid down his cheeks. Mydei had to bite back reassuring words and prevent himself from forcing his face to lay against his shirt, out of respect for being able to face him in those conditions. “But you want to go out with Phainon…” Astraea lamented, between a sob and another, with an almost guilty tone.

He should have been used to it by now. He always used it whenever his mood changed so drastically over a minor inconvenience, but he vehemently hated it. He didn’t even want to think of what he got told, if at five years old he felt guilty over asking for anything.

Mydei took a deep breath and left a kiss on his forehead, feeling his tiny, trembling body slightly slow down, eventually stopping. As he looked down at him again, he noticed the slight hope in his eyes, and he smiled at him. “If going out with Phainon is a problem, I won't go just yet,” he stated, slightly tilting his head. “Between him and you, I will always choose you,” he kissed him on the top of his head and smiled again, then whispered again, “Always.”

Astraea brought his fists in front of his lips, almost doubting the words coming out of his mouth. “Pinky promise?” He asked, still a little hesitant on wholeheartedly accepting the feelings and intentions he just expressed.

As an answer, Mydei smiled and shifted his weight on only one arm, then offered him his pinky finger. The child looked at it for a few seconds, then slowly intertwined his own finger with the adult’s. Glad that he could at least believe in him enough to trust what he just told him, he held him closer, letting him grab his clothes and lean into his shoulder.

“I love you so much, stardust. More than anything else.” He whispered, next to his ear, with the full intention of Astraea finally internalising that protective feeling. “If anything causes you pain or distress, I will fix it, including going out with Phainon.”

He didn’t know if he could manage feelings as strong as those, especially from an adult close to being his parent as much as Mydei was. He knew that he was often belittled and told he was a nuisance, and he felt like he had to be on the same level of an adult to be accepted by them. He had no idea how he would have reacted to those promises.

As he did before, he just started crying out of the blue. Probably, he was overstimulated with information, feelings he didn’t understand and he was going through so much that it was the only way his body was able to react to new information that he deemed important.

Calmly, Mydei tried to force him to relax while letting him cry as much as he wanted, offering his body as a safe solace. His head was buried in his shoulder, his tiny hands gripping and releasing the hold on his clothes, and he could just lull him back to a state that didn’t involve tears running down his face and the need to hold onto him for dear life.

“Shh, come here,” he repeated, as he rocked him in his arms and moved to a more reserved corner. He wasn’t in the middle of the hallway, but he figured that they would need more privacy, if they wanted to go out of that hospital without needlessly worrying the nurses and operators working there, at some point. “My most precious little star, everything will be fine, no matter how hard it looks right now, I promise.”

It took a few other convincing promises and a couple more minutes of staying in silence in Mydei’s arms to subtle the sobs and sniffles still remaining, then he brushed his face against the shirt he had been gripping for the past few minutes and finally raised his head again. He was immediately greeted with a smile and an affectionate kiss on his forehead, the man giving them to him instantaneously feeling Astraea relax at the contact.

At least, he was relaxing and let himself be vulnerable around him, even in those moments.

Astraea opened his eyes after a matter of seconds, waves of honey and uncertainty greeting him again. “Go out with Phainon,” he stated, looking right at him with the most serious face he had ever seen him wear. Mydei was about to say something in rebuttal, but the child immediately shook his head and looked away as he explained himself, “I was scared this morning, but… you told me to be brave and listen to the doctor, and everything was okay. Maybe…”

He trailed off on his own, not really wanting to say what was on his mind. Luckily, though, he expressed himself well enough and Mydei was able to piece it together. “Do you want to be brave again and stay at home without me? Are you sure?” He asked, tilting his head to look at him properly.

All Astraea did was weakly hold that eye contact and hesitantly nod, biting his lower lip. He wasn’t sure at all, he was scared, but he was well aware that Mydei had a life outside of him, and he understood completely every discussion he held with Hephaestion and Phainon in the past few days. Very smart kid, as usual, but mindful of his main caretaker’s feelings and happiness as well. Mydei was even more convinced that saving him from such a difficult situation and taking him in as his son was a gift from the Gods above to the both of them.

He smiled and tilted his head further to kiss him on a cheek, delighted when he saw a soft, excited giggle as a reaction. “Thank you, honeycakes,” he told him, then looked at him again. “I will come home as soon as I can.”

Astraea nodded and smiled, hugging him. “Love you lots, Mydei…” He whispered, almost as the first proper response that his mind could compute to that complicated display of affection that the adult showed earlier. 

“I know, don’t worry,” he answered, just to give him a decent acknowledgement and let his heart breathe after everything that his little, frail body just went through. He waited for him to let go, then took the argument a little further, since he felt like being completely transparent with him would have been better than having him find out and putting him in uncomfortable situations. “I'd ask Ptolemy to look after you– the man working at the library,” he explained, “do you like him?”

He nodded, even if a little hesitantly. Mydei knew that it was because it was someone else and not because he didn’t like him, but he didn’t know if he was ready yet. Maybe, they should approach this slowly, trying out with half an hour every day, then increasing the time alone, and see if–

A burping sound suddenly came from Astraea’s stomach, distracting Mydei’s every thought and bringing an embarrassed smile on the child’s face.

Mydei couldn’t keep in a soft laugh, figuring that, effectively, they didn’t have breakfast that morning because he had to do blood tests. “Someone’s hungry,” he remarked, glad that the heavy atmosphere finally lifted from around them.

“Can we eat now?” Astraea asked, slightly pushing on his shoulders with his hands with excitement. He had to be starving, after all the energies he spent crying as much as he did.

He put him down and tucked his hair behind his ear, smiling at him. Astraea gladly let him, almost enjoying all the care and attention that he was receiving, with less guilt washing over him this time around. “Special breakfast today,” he announced, watching as his eyes sparkled with excitement.

“Special?”

“We're eating at the bar down the street. You can get whatever you want.”

“Really?”

“Mhm. And, after that we can try to read those books you got yesterday.”

“Okay!”

Mydei smiled again and ruffled his hair, standing back up and offering his hand to hold. The child took it without question and followed him to the best of his abilities, his body brimming with excitement and curiosity over the surprise that he reserved for him. He enjoyed seeing him like that, even if he ended up having to help him eat the cream-filled brioche that he chose, his face stuffed with yellow stains and remnants of the brioche itself.

He always earned stares full of apologies whenever he couldn’t properly eat a bite of it, but he didn’t bother about it too much. They would have worked on it. For the moment, he just wiped his face clean and let him eat whatever he wanted in whichever way he saw fit. He would have figured it out eventually, he was smart and he had a lot of time to work on it without pressure being put on him.

In the end, Astraea did seem satisfied and they ended up going back home because the poor child was falling asleep in that bar. Mydei, in the meantime, could catch up with some of the bills he was supposed to pay a few days prior and texted his mother back, who was asking about how he had been doing. He didn’t mention Astraea, just a pretty big change in his life, and that he would have told her when the situation would have been more stable.

As he expected, his mother was curious, but she didn’t pressure him to tell her everything. She always drove home the fact that she trusted his decisions and believed that he was way more intelligent than he let on, so, if he was asking her to wait, she would have patiently waited for follow-up news about it.

Luckily, Astraea had no problems with naps. He fell asleep in the middle of the day or went to sleep on his own, confirming for Mydei that the problem he had with sleeping alone after dinner was the night and darkness around him. He probably still had hallucinations or felt paranoid, and that was why he absolutely wanted to sleep with him.

He didn't mind yet, he just worried for the future. He understood that it had been less than a week, and he may still have harsh, violent flashbacks to that day and all those years he spent with them. He loved Mydei, but he had a family for five years beforehand too. He absolutely didn't want to overstep and make him even more uncomfortable.

His son woke up just after a few hours, only to eat, then fell asleep right away on his chest calmly breathing down on his shirt and slightly drooling on it.

It wasn't much and Mydei himself didn't bother, it meant he was relaxed and he felt safe, but that was more of a future problem for his teeth after he kept the pacifier for a little too long, than an issue for the shirt.

As he was petting his hair and noticed just how much of it was quickly turning into a strawberry blonde similar to his own hair tips, Phainon called him.

Mydei looked at his phone for a few seconds, pondering whether or not to pick up. He doubted it was for something that he actually needed from him, but he couldn’t say he hated talking to him either, especially after how tired he was. Maybe, letting down his guard for a while and relaxing, as long as his child was sleeping peacefully, and listening to the voice of that person so hell bent on trying to know him better would have been a good choice.

Just the possibility of liking his voice in that moment was messing with his brain. He was probably just tired. Or he genuinely wanted to hear his voice again. Or both. None of those options were necessarily ones he wanted to think about.

He huffed in the end, picking up and bringing his phone next to his ear. The excited, bright voice that was sneakingly squirming through his brain in the past couple of days didn’t even wait for a greeting before beaming at him.

“Mydei!” Phainon greeted, the sheer excitement in his voice piercing through the phone call. Mydei wondered what made him want to call him, if he was so happy without even hearing his voice. There was something hidden about him that mesmerized him, but he didn’t know what it was and he was itching to reach out and grasp it.

Maybe it was pathetic. Maybe he was running a little too much, given he met him only a few days before. But there was something warm spreading inside of his stomach whenever he talked with Astraea so playfully, or whenever he texted him with another inconsequential thing that happened that day, or whenever he asked stupid questions to get to know him. It was stupid and simple, but he didn’t feel anything like that when he was with Hephaestion, because they knew each other like the back of their hands already when they did start dating.

He liked the chase. He liked to see how badly Phainon wanted to know him, past his body, past his somewhat mysterious demeanor, past his pretty face, even if he probably admired all of it in silence. Whenever he tried to talk to him, he did it with the intention of wanting an honest understanding of him as a person. He was used to compliments, but his advances had more curiosity and affections in them than the adoration and mindless flirts he was used to.

Mydei remembered how fast he walked away when they met during shopping, somewhat embarrassed after he told him he would have wanted to hang out with him. Cute. So cute that he almost mentally slapped himself for making that promise to Hephaestion, because he perfectly knew that he was right. He did like him, even if he knew virtually nothing about the man.

Stupid, stupid Phainon. With his stupidly cute smile and his stupidly toned body of his.

“Mydei? Are you still there?” The voice of the man he was thinking so intensely about rang again next to his ear. Mydei blinked and gulped, feeling almost guilty about those thoughts, even if they were mostly a silent, innocent hope of being closer. He even felt himself blushing, and he was suddenly glad that this was just a phone call.

Caressing his son's blonde hair, he tried to sound composed again as he answered him. “Why do you keep calling me?”

“You gave me your phone number and I only called you this time!” Phainon rebutted, the slight pout almost visible in his tone. Mydei weakly smiled, imagining it, a mix of a cute and an annoying image of that grown man– older than him, at that– acting like a spoiled child. It was almost endearing.

As he thought and imagined that picture way too fitting of a teenager, rather than a twenty-seven year old man, Phainon’s voice perked up again without the need of an answer. “But, Mydei, I did have something to ask you,” he confessed, his tone now a little lower, even if still relaxed.

This time, Mydei was a little curious. His questions were always stupid, little, innocent questions about what he thought of certain things simply existing, but he only asked for those over messages. He spent the better part of the days prior doing just that, in fact. 

“Let's hear it,” Mydei answered, readjusting the phone next to his ear in a more comfortable position. He tried to move the last amount possible, since he didn’t want to wake up Astraea. He needed that nap desperately, or he wouldn’t have been able to be awake until that night, when they would have actually gone to bed until the next morning.

Phainon let out a small noise, not clear in response to what, but it sounded happy, at least. “Salt or sweet?”

Mydei’s mind blanked at the question. 

He thought about those words, the reason why he could have said this and if he was truly just that annoying naturally or if he did it thinking it made him a somewhat more interesting person. After calling him only to ask him something that he could have asked by text, Mydei was convinced that was absolutely the most annoying man in the world, whether he forced himself to be or not.

“You called me to ask me if I prefer salt or sweet.” He repeated slowly, not fully believing what he was being thrown into. It was something he chose, to experience this relationship, but the stupid questions, annoying texts and sudden calls weren’t something he agreed to. He was simply subjected to them as a consequence of his stupidity in liking a man like this.

A soft laugh answered him on the other side, amused by the reaction. “I missed your voice.”

Right as he heard that, he was reminded why he was putting up with all of it. 

Sure, it was a bet with Hephaestion at first, but he quickly grew fond of him. His friend had good points about him– handsome, Astraea loved him, he was clearly interested in him too– but he was so boldly confident about what he wanted that he was instinctively attracted to him out of sheer respect and curiosity. The fact that Phainon was effortlessly cute like a little puppy itching to be adopted at a pet store, always searching for his attention and affections more than just being annoying was a bonus. For now, at least.

Mydei, then, decided to ask him directly what was on his mind. They both wanted to keep talking, there was no reason why he should avoid the question. “How can you say it so boldly?”

“Why do you ask?” Phainon asked, surely smirking on the other side of the phone, and Mydei instantly regretted asking more about him. Another innocent laugh made it to his ear, then that playful, teasing tone travelled to his brain, muttering, “Do you like it?”

Gods be damned.

His hand stilled on Astraea’s hair, his mind aware enough of his surroundings to not curl it into a punch, lest he woke him up. He almost thought Phainon sounded attractive, despite the incredibly annoyingly innocent voice he was so hellbent on using. Mydei recognized the flirting, but it somehow was delivered with such a tone that it angered and excited him at the same time.

“... No. Sweets.” he settled with, after a long pause. He sighed, ultimately realizing that the sooner he ended the call, the sooner he could stop thinking about him. Hopefully. He wasn’t too sure of it.

A pleased sound made it to his ear, almost imperceptible. The problem was that he did, in fact, hear it. And it was echoing in the back of his head. “Thank you!” Phainon luckily interrupted that curse, not waiting for an answer. “And about–”

“Look, just come over. I prefer that over my phone constantly buzzing for stupid questions like this.” Mydei interrupted him, not fully realizing what he just said yet.

He didn’t mean to invite him over right away, and he could tell from the sudden silence that Phainon wasn’t expecting it either. It wasn’t his objective, and Mydei didn’t know why he even suggested it. He refused to process the feelings his brain dangerously posed in front of him, instead opting to hold his breath until the other answered his suggestion.

It was the only thing he could really do, and it wasn’t exactly something that he didn’t want to happen. He was already hinting at it, just not so boldly and clearly, and certainly not for a possible dinner at his own apartment. 

“... I finish working in a few hours.” Phainon’s voice finally made itself known again, letting Mydei finally breathe again.

He pondered what to say next for a few seconds. Then, thinking back at the cute, embarrassed scene he made a few days prior and how much he was trying to get to know him, he threw it all out of the window.

“Then come in a few hours and stay for dinner,” he firmly stated, relaxing again now that his brain made more sense of the situation and he knew just how mutual those wishes of knowing each other were. “See you then.”

He hung up without waiting for an answer to avoid suddenly changing his mind on the matter. He still didn’t know if it was the right choice or not, for himself, Phainon or Astraea. All he knew was that he was interested in him, and those feelings were mutual. Maybe, it was time he would listen to the words his parents muttered to him a long time ago, when his father still had his head on his shoulders and his mother didn’t have to see him sink into the dark pit that devoured him.

Whenever in your life you will meet the right person, you will know. And when that will happen, Mydeimos, you will have to act first and think later. You are an intelligent, prudent child, but you have to promise me that you won’t let happiness slip right through your fingers.

He still felt guilty about it. It had been more than fifteen years since that accident, and he still couldn’t help but think that, if not because of him, he wouldn’t have lost his father. All he had of him were memories, a few photos and his voice echoing in his mind. The body they mourned during his funeral wasn’t him anymore. He died the moment Mydei could no longer hear the love and tenderness in his voice. That body finally withered away after four years that his loving father left this world. 

He and his mother didn’t cry by that point. Mydei almost felt numb to all of it. Maybe a little angry when people who loathed his father when he was alive showed up, begging for a bit of the money he left behind. He accepted all the condolences, but his all-knowing mother held him back enough so that no one would have left without a few teeth.

Those memories were always on his mind, even more now that he adopted Astraea. He promised himself that he wouldn’t have followed that path, even if something happened to him. Mydei was lucky because he had his mother, but Astraea had no one else. He couldn’t afford to do what his father did, even for a second. It was a reminder in the back of his head, along with how horribly abused that child had been until he picked him up. He dealt with enough bullshit for a lifetime, he didn’t need to experience what he did too.

And Phainon… maybe he was a back-up plan. If he did go down that road, Astraea would have had him, at least.

Maybe, his brain suddenly thought independently, it was the promise he swore to keep. The last wish that his father expressed for him. To find someone he was truly happy with, and not let them go, no matter what happened, as his parents tried so desperately to do with each other, for his well-being too. Hephaestion was the closest that fit that description, but what he felt whenever he talked with Phainon was something else entirely. It was like comparing the intensity of a warm fireplace and being thrown into the sun.

He would have had to thank his childhood friend– and thank the Heavens his brain finally started to register him as more than only his ex-boyfriend– at the end of that day, even if all he would get will probably be a bunch of ‘I told you so’s.

“Who was it?”

Mydei stopped in his tracks upon hearing the tired, sleepy, tiny voice below him. Astraea looked back at him, his eyes struggling to stay open, but as curious as ever. His hand offered a few caresses through his hair, delicate and loving, especially now that old, unpleasant memories resurfaced. He felt protective of him before too, but now he felt almost the need to know he would be safe at all times.

The child tilted his head and rubbed his eyes, still tired, but buried his head right into his chest again. Mydei smiled at that, beyond happy every time that he leaned on him so affectionately and with that absurd amount of trust.

“Mama…”

Saying that Mydei froze and saw his entire life flash by his eyes right after he heard Astraea calling him with that name would be a grave understatement. He was sure he stopped breathing for a few seconds, and he noticed the child tensing immediately too, almost as if that name slipped away before he could stop it.

“Astraea,” Mydei warned, without a proper follow-up. He didn't really have one, after seeing guilt on his face again. He clearly didn't want to call him like that, but he was tired and instinctively let it out.

Mydei considered for how long he thought of him as his son. Then, how long Astraea must have felt like he should have called him anything else but his name. Finally, how accepted that child must have felt after he showered him with love and tried his utmost to understand and help him.

It was natural that he would have called him something along those lines.

He seemed so desperate for a good, decent adult in his life that Mydei didn't even want to think of the far off possibility that Astraea could have been surrendered to social services. It would have been far too cruel.

“Sorry,” came the apology, the child immediately lowering his head in shame. He probably expected a refusal, maybe a lecture about how he shouldn't have called him like that, but Mydei didn't even entertain that idea for a second. 

He hugged him close, with urgency and affection, giving him enough space to talk, but held him strongly enough to make a statement. “You can call me however you want,” he stated, with a voice so sweet and considerate that it felt more of a promise, “I just fear that you’re running a little too much for your own well-being.”

It was true. He was scared, and he wanted him to understand that he could call him however he wished, but he also wanted him to remember his mother and not use him as a substitute without processing those complicated feelings. He knew it was a lot to ask, but it would have been worse if he ran away.

Astraea raised his head, looking at him with hesitation clear in those golden irises, but wanting to tell him the truth all the same, even if he was worrying. It was important for him that he knew, that much was clear now.

“Calling you just Mydei feels wrong…” He whispered, closing his fists around the fabric of his shirt, a motion that Mydei was used to, by now.

He stared at the kid, unwilling to tear his eyes away from Mydei's, and he held him as he sat up, before letting the little kid slide down to sit on his lap. His eyes were still fixed on him, begging for an answer to his explanation.

That kid was smart. Way too smart for Mydei's attempt at lying to him. So, he didn't. 

“I just don’t want you to force yourself to forget about your mother for my sake.” He stated, slowly and clearly, hopefully understanding what any of that meant.

Obviously, he understood right away.

“She was never Mama. Just Mother,” he answered, pushing himself up as he gripped his shirt again, his eyes intense and dedicated to prove his point to him. “I’m not forgetting her.”

Mydei, obviously, hesitated. He didn't know if he could take his word for it. Then again, no one except him could have known the truth of his feelings. He was a child, but he was intelligent enough to know what he was feeling and what he was comfortable with. 

He had no right to deny him a further explanation and he shouldn't judge him without trying to trust his word for it first.

As if to make his point more convincing after seeing that cloud of doubt, Astraea immediately pointed at his own head. “She’s still here,” he said, then laid a hand on his heart, “and here.” He took a deep sigh, gripping his own shirt and looking down, almost struggling to speak. “But you’re here too, and… more than anyone else.”

Those were all the reasons he needed.

Mydei immediately hugged him and left an affectionate kiss on the side of his head, feeling the amount of trust that tiny little child had in him with the hug he got in exchange. “Okay,” he whispered, smiling at him, “call me Mama.”

Astraea’s face beamed like the first rays of sunlight breaking through the clouds, giggling and sitting back again, wiggling his legs in excitement. He looked back at him almost immediately, stars in his shining eyes, glimmering with happiness. Mydei bent down to hug him properly, taking him into his arms again.

If that was something so important for him… he had no choice but accept it and trust that it wouldn’t lead to anything but a better path for both of them. Besides, he would have lied if he said that he didn’t like that development. He already thought of him as his son, but he didn’t expect him to validate those feelings so fast.

He kissed Astraea on the top of his head, noticing another excited laugh, and he smiled. This wasn’t what he had expected from that night, nor for it to happen so fast, but he was beyond thankful that he saw him the way he did and trusted him enough to see him as his mother, just as he trusted his own when he was his age. 

“What are we doing now?” Astraea asked, just as excited as a few seconds prior. “Reading again?”

Mydei laughed and shook his head gently, careful to not be too forceful with that answer. He was glad that he liked reading now, even if he still struggled and didn’t understand what a lot of words meant, but they had a guest over and they needed to get the house and dinner ready in a few hours.

“No, but I have some good news,” he announced, caressing his hair. Astraea promptly opened his mouth, obviously curious as to what was waiting for him, eyes focused completely on him. Mydei smiled softly, thinking again just about how lucky he had been before revealing the latest news for him. “Phainon is coming over for dinner.”

That simple sentence made him jump up with a speed that he rarely saw anyone being even able to pull off. He was so excited about that man coming over that Mydei thought for a split second that he had to keep him around, just to make sure he would be happy. Not that Mydei wouldn't be, if Phainon decided to stay or visit more often.

“Can I help preparing?” Astraea asked, with a big, enthusiastic smile on his face. He leaned on the couch, waiting for an answer, but all he got was a gentle pat on the head and a smile, before Mydei stood up and made his way to the kitchen.

Obviously, he expected the child to follow him with his big, curious, focused eyes, alert for any movement he could study and replicate. Quickly, he gave him some instructions, mostly easy tasks to prepare the food Mydei had to cook, but he explained to him what he was doing and what he was cooking as well.

He liked thinking about teaching him what his mother did, passing down knowledge that only he could give him. It was almost like giving him a piece of himself to carry throughout the rest of his life, and the feeling it gave him was unlike any other. It was a warm, gentle sensation, his heart was almost exploding from the amount of love and pride it contained in that moment.

Astraea kept asking questions, kept getting food on his face, neck, hair and hands, kept following his every instruction to the last bit. He was still hesitating and he was still afraid to do something wrong, but Mydei made it his mission to explain and show him that it didn't matter. He fixed everything every time he made a mistake, and that was enough to beat down a little bit more of that fear that clouded his heart.

Mydei laughed more than he ever did in his life, enjoying the lingering of those feelings in his chest more than he would have ever expected. He never had the intention of letting him go, but that day consolidated the reality that he would have had a son until he died. A beautiful son he was very proud of, he might add. Thinking that there could have been a future without Astraea in his life felt more than wrong. Almost impossible, really. He barged into his life and forced him to move on from a plan for his future that had been dead for a very long time, and gave him new life. He wouldn't have minded just being his dear, loving Mama for the rest of his life.

Those thoughts slowed to a stop as soon as he heard the bell ringing and Astraea flew towards the door, bouncing in place as he waited for Mydei to open it. The adult left to finish a few of the preparations, not even daring to look at the guest in the face. They would have had the time to talk, anyway.

When it creaked open from the outside to reveal familiar white hair and bright, blue eyes, Astraea immediately yelled his name, probably smiling at him. Mydei cracked a smile too, happy to know about how much he liked him and how much Phainon indulged him. He liked it, for better or worse, and he hoped he would see that kind of excitement more often, other than that weird feeling sitting in his stomach whenever he shared the same room with Phainon.

He ignored it, instead choosing to lean against the door and listening to their conversation. He never really got to see how Phainon talked or behaved alone with Astraea, and he was curious.

Unfortunately for him, though, Phainon noticed him right away and softly smiled at him, his eyes looking at him with sparkles in his eyes, almost like the bright, sunny sky devoid of clouds. They were a little too bright for Mydei's liking, he was sure they were almost creepy in the dark, but it added to the mystery surrounding him. A man so bright and with a personality so pleasant that it rubbed off of him in all the wrong ways that hid a deeper darkness that was determined to keep concealed, but still longing for his friendship so much that he had to beg his son to put a good word for him.

Phainon was always meant to be someone that Mydei would be so interested in.

“I see you've worked hard today,” Phainon suddenly said, still talking to Astraea. He smiled and high-fived him, dirtying his own hands in the process.

Mydei moved his gaze on his clothes, pouting upon seeing that he was still wearing his nurse uniform. He probably ran there as soon as he clocked out, without bothering with changing his clothes. It was… a little cute, even if he may have looked slightly pathetic at times.

Cute, mysterious, interesting, bright Phainon. So many adjectives that he could use, and yet he still didn't know much about him. 

It truly bothered him to no end. He already took so much space in his mind, how much more did he want to take? How much greedier did he still want to get?

Mydei sighed, his chest visibly rising, as he ignored the obvious gaze on his chest. “You came here in your nurse uniform?” He asked, slightly tilting his head.

Phainon smiled and stood up, shrugging at the question. “I wouldn't dare risk this chance.”

Curious answer. Mydei raised an eyebrow at him, wondering if that was his idea of flirting or if he thought he would have changed his mind if he took the time to change his clothes. Either way, it was, looked and sounded desperately pathetic.

At that point, Astraea turned towards him, pointed at Phainon and asked innocently, “Mama, can we keep him?” He then smiled, almost giggling. “He's funny!”

Mydei let out a soft laugh, somewhat agreeing with the sentiment. Apart from the interest he had in the man, he had to admit that days were hardly going to be boring with him around.

Phainon, however, had no reaction to those words. Instead, he was just looking at Mydei, almost admiring him like an art piece in a museum.

Mydei was used to being looked at– he was handsome. Gorgeous. Beautiful, sometimes. He was used to others checking him out, maybe flirting with him if they felt brave enough. But the staring he was being subjected to right now felt completely different.

He didn't feel any lust or desire right away, and all there was in those bright, blue eyes was genuine admiration and wonder upon seeing him. It was awfully noticeable, just how much the other cherished every second they spent together.

Mydei held his glare for a second, giving him something to hold onto, probably for the rest of the night.

If it wasn't enough, after all, he could always surprise him.

“Astraea, take a bath and change your clothes, Phainon and I will be in the kitchen,” he instructed as he looked at him, completely ignoring the other man now. He noticed him moving a little, maybe anxious to be looked at again. It was a subtle challenge, but one that Mydei very much enjoyed seeing just how much power his every action had on him.

Maybe, Phainon would turn out to be way more fun than he anticipated.

“You,” he finally looked at him, then pointed straight ahead of him, into a hallway, “take some clothes. We should have the same size.”

He refused to have dinner with someone still dressed like they did at work. Especially if it was sick people and the stink of medicine and chemicals stuck to the clothes.

Quickly, he gave him a light blue sweater and a pair of white pants, thinking they would fit him enough to not be a punch in his eye whenever he looked at him.

“Thank you!” Phainon beamed, happily grabbing the clothes and taking off the shirt he had been wearing for far too many hours.

Mydei stilled, and his breathing stopped for a second.

In front of him there was one of the most beautiful bodies he had ever seen, and the semicircular, golden tattoo that connected his shoulders across his very muscular chest didn't help the situation.

Then, as easily as that sight appeared, it was taken away from him. Maybe, looking back, it was the right thing to do. If he stared any longer, he didn't know where his mind would be by now.

He blinked and averted his gaze, before he could see his thighs too, only raising his head when he heard a few steps getting farther away.

Phainon turned and gave him another gentle smile, walking backwards just to keep his eyes on him. It was so painfully obvious that he was very interested in him and Mydei didn't exactly conceal it either. He was good-looking and he had a pleasant personality, he was good with kids, he had a smile that rivaled the brightness of the sun, his body was other-wordly– he had to know what they were doing there.

So why did it feel like he always kept a safe distance between them?

It wasn't something either of them wanted, clearly, but Phainon tended to avoid direct contact with him. He quite literally avoided touching his skin, showing him the best of what he could have, the intricacies of his character, and then he pulled away immediately. It pissed him off. 

Mydei was unbelievably curious now. If he didn't manage to know him better in a matter of seconds, he was sure he would have punched the wall in frustration.

“Sorry for… pushing a little too much?” Came Phainon's voice, immediately focusing his thoughts on a sole source. He looked at him, puzzled, trying to understand what he was trying to apologize for.

He was the one who invited him over, it was his house, he gave him clothes, he chose to prepare some food… there was no need for him to even think about apologizing. His mind scattered his memory for possible answers without asking the man directly, almost as if doing so would be admitting defeat. He liked thinking, trying to figure out what action led to another, but he didn't like it when it took him way too much time.

And, for better or worse, Phainon's thoughts and actions tended to lack sense.

He thought about it for another couple of seconds, until he finally found the answer he was probably referring to– the incessant influx of messages and the one call he made earlier that day.

Even then, it didn't make sense. Did he feel guilty of it now? After he blew up his phone for the past week or so? Now that they were finally having a date and Mydei was finally able to talk to him face to face, without the bother of that infernal device?

Mydei had to take a deep breath before answering. “If I didn't like it, we wouldn't be here,” he calmly managed to answer, hopefully removing those doubts from his mind.

“You like annoying men?” Phainon laughed, a little embarrassed. Maybe, someone else already called him out for that bad habit of his and he was awfully aware of it. Mydei didn't mind it too much, but it did bother him slightly seeing him in distress over something so insignificant.

He couldn't do much for him if those were his thoughts, after all. Except, maybe, turn that squint of embarrassment and shame into something more positive for the both of them.

“I like to see someone who knows what he wants and does everything in his power to get it.”

The sentence rolled out of his tongue before Mydei could stop it, but he didn't correct himself. He wanted him to see his point of view too and why he insisted on him coming over, if that meant raising his self-esteem a little. He was aware of how he looked and carried himself, many people likened him to a prince of rare beauty, so he would understand how that might look intimidating, if Phainon didn't see himself in high regard.

Mydei, however, didn't expect the sudden serious, worried eyes staring at him. “You’re not just something, Mydei.”

He blinked. Then stared at him. Then blinked again.

Did he just care more about Mydei than himself? Why did he jump at that part of the sentence and not anything else? By that point, consider him confused, curious and interested in anything this strange man came up with.

Mydei let out a soft laugh in response, at a loss as per what he could actually say in response to that. “Certainly not to you,” he settled with, staring at him, “for some reason.”

“Have you ever looked into a mirror? Do you realize how breathtakingly gorgeous you are?” Phainon asked him, almost physically reacting to those words. Mydei found it incredibly amusing. He tilted his head as a smile spread on his face, mentally memorizing all those exaggerated movements and all the emotions unraveling in front of him. 

Cute. He was so stupidly, pathetically, endearingly cute.

This time, he didn't stop himself from thinking about it. He found it to be true, and, whether he liked him or not, he had to give him a fair chance. He didn't dislike him, and he was growing fond of him. Maybe, Hephaestion was more right than he realized, and a part of Mydei wished that to be the truth, because he really, really liked looking at him making a fool of himself whenever he was anxious. He was so effortlessly cute.

However, that couldn't possibly let him forget about how much he didn't know about him yet, and he prayed– hoped, even– that he was attracted to more than his body and pretty face. Of course, he didn't know much past that, but people tended to lose interest when his personality was the direct opposite of what they pictured him to be.

Let this be different , he thought, maybe a little too desperately . I need this time to be different. If he thinks I'm some dominant alpha guy too, I will throw myself off of the window.

He was embarrassed to admit just how many times that happened throughout the last year or so. It was one of the main reasons why he opted for the occasional sex too, since everyone just wanted his body. This time, though, he actually wanted a relationship. For once, he felt greedy enough to ask for that tiny, little miracle.

“And that's the only reason why you're here?” Mydei opted to ask in the end, patiently and eagerly waiting for his answer.

Phainon smiled and shook his head violently, almost as if he was accused of a crime that he absolutely didn't commit. “That’s what knowing someone else is supposed to do, but we really weren't able to do that,” he explained, leaning towards him, even if only slightly. “I really want to know you enough to call you my partner, Mydei.”

Mydei almost choked on his own saliva.

The change in attitude from just a few seconds ago was hard to wrap his head around, but he noticed that he still didn't touch him. He leaned over, but his hands were behind his back and his clothes made him smell of a familiar scent. It almost felt like he was offering him the prize he was after and taking it right away, making sure he wouldn't reach it.

By that point, Mydei was unsure whether Phainon was trying to edge him or if he actually did have some degree of unpleasant experiences for which he was avoiding to touch him at all costs. He hated both options, but there was an obviously more evil answer, and he feared that it was the right one.

Despite those thoughts, Mydei didn't even move. He stood still, looking at him in those blue eyes that were piercing his skull. “Is that why you asked my age and if I liked sweets or not?”

“I just wanted to know if you were older or younger than me and make you a gift you would actually enjoy,” Phainon simply answered, only glancing down once when Mydei leaned back against the counter, keeping up the game that he started, widening their distance. He smiled, seemingly happy about that movement.

Mydei noticed it, but he didn't say a word. At least, now he knew that he was just a little shit and he didn't have to worry for him. “Does it make a difference?”

“I’m way more determined now!” Phainon mewled, visibly excited. Mydei remembered how happy he was when he found out that he was two years younger, and now he knew it was because he got off to it. It should have disgusted him, but it didn't– he even felt happy at the prospect, for better or worse.

He really looked like a puppy, by that distance. He was sure he would have wagged his tail, if he had one.

He's twenty-seven years old, Mydeimos. Get a hold of yourself and flirt normally.

Mydei had to repeat that to himself a few times, before he blinked back to reality and found a neatly wrapped present in front of his face. He stared at it, then at the soft smile behind it, blue eyes fondly looking at him just a few centimeters above it. “And here's the gift,” Phainon explained, almost dangling in front of him. 

That was annoying.

With a swift and annoyed motion of his hand, Mydei took it in his hands, as he let out a loud ‘humph’, only met with a happy giggle from the man in front of him. He promptly ignored him and put the box on the table, starting to unwrap it. The box itself wasn't big, but it wasn't too small either. Given the claim Phainon made just a while ago, he was almost fearing he bought him a ring.

Instead, as he opened it slowly, he saw honeycakes inside of it. His favourite food that he was sure he never even mentioned to Phainon.

“How did you know I liked these?” Mydei asked, pointing at them and turning towards Phainon. Someone must have told him. There was no way that he simply guessed.

Phainon, though, only tilted his head. “You do? I just picked what reminded me of you the most.” He smiled, obviously happy with that information.

Of course the guy obsessed with him and that felt a visceral need to know him simply guessed his favourite food on the planet. He had to accept that was his life now. A good-looking, considerate, unusually-obsessed-with-him nurse just knew which food he had to buy to breach into his heart even more.

And now he hoped that he would actually eventually become his partner.

He would have slapped himself right there if he thought of it more than he was meant to, but, luckily, his mind focused on the noise caused by Astraea running to the kitchen, all washed up, dressed and ready to eat.

Thank the Heavens for this little child.

“Mama!” He yelled, crashing against Mydei's leg, his hand instinctively reaching down to caress his hair and keeping him close. 

Smiling, he closed the box again, thinking to come back to it a little bit later. “Ready?” He asked, getting an excited nod as an answer. “Let's start eating.”

Weirdly, it all went smoothly. Phainon complimented Mydei for the food, delightly chatted with Astraea and happily ate whatever was in front of him. No weird motions or flirty sentences, but he did glance towards Mydei with almost excited eyes, as if merely breathing in the same room caused him extreme spikes of happiness.

Mydei started to ask himself if he truly was attracted to this man, with the way he was acting.

Even in that scenario, though, he noticed something interesting about him. Phainon seemed smooth enough earlier whenever he talked to his child, but, after a while, he began noticing repeated motions, answers that sounded straight out of a dictionary of how to deal with children, along with the usual happy-go-lucky facade he was already acquainted with.

He just sat and watched throughout the entire dinner, only speaking when Phainon and Astraea asked him something, satisfied with every look that Phainon gave him. Glances of curiosity and expectations flew towards him once every few minutes, anxiously waiting for some kind of reward. Mydei just ignored him, toying with him in the same way the other man did with him a while earlier.

Phainon would look at him, and Mydei would promptly let those eyes linger on him, without giving them the attention they craved. He kept his eyes on Astraea or his food, until he didn't feel them on him anymore and, even if he realized that this was a little childish, he was having fun.

Although, the tension between them rising minute by minute may have gotten a little too out of hand.

“I'm… gonna read,” Astraea said, after a few minutes of silence. Mydei glanced at him, no emotions passing through his expression, but he did wonder if he picked up what was going on in the room. He was smart– he never doubted it– but he didn't know just how often he had seen two adults flirting or if his parents were on good terms.

Despite those thoughts, he simply softly smiled at him. “Do you need some help?”

“I'll write down the words I don't know!” He answered promptly, so quickly and sure of himself that it easily put Mydei's heart at ease. He gently caressed his head and nodded, observing the excited reaction on his face, along with the happy noises he let out upon the fact that he granted him what he asked for.

Maybe it wasn't a big deal, but Mydei cherished those moments. He was sure that Astraea was ignored most of the time, if not directly getting yelled at or insulted, so, maybe, being acknowledged like that was, indeed, very important for him. And who was Mydei to take that away from him, if he could offer him joy instead?

He sighed, then whispered, “Okay. Don't go to bed too late.”

Astraea nodded excitedly, then laid his head on Mydei's thighs for a second, as if to give him a hug. He smiled, a little amused by the gesture, and gently caressed his head in response. “Have fun with Phainon, Mama,” he greeted him at last, before running away to his room.

Mydei blinked at the door, at a loss of words.

So, he did understand what was going on to some extent.

“That kid is way too intelligent for his well-being!”

Mydei's head finally turned to Phainon, breaking that silent game he was playing with him. He couldn't tell whether or not he was satisfied with finally being looked at, but he definitely wasn't sad about it. He was smiling brightly, looking at him with glimmering blue eyes, greedy for more and more attention towards him now that they were alone.

By the way he was acting, Mydei was wondering if he was jealous of Astraea. For both of their sake, he avoided answering that question.

Instead, he laid a hand on his cheek and indulged him, instantly noticing the slight blush over his face, up until the tip of his ears, pale enough to sell him away even if his behavior didn't change in the slightest. Mydei looked softly at him, golden eyes wavering between his flushed cheeks and excited irises, deciding what to do next.

Maybe he could throw him a bone, after all.

“You talk to him as if you had a manual,” Mydei mentioned, with an almost amused voice. He didn't mean for it to come out as such, but there wasn't much he could do now, besides waiting for his reaction.

Against all his expectations, Phainon only blinked a couple of times and let out a surprised whisper. “What?”

“I thought you were good with children, given your profession, but… you talk as if someone gave you a manual on how to understand and talk to them.” He explained, dropping both of his arms on the table, after slightly moving over the dish next to him. He would have had to clean the table, but he had far more important issues to take care of now.

Phainon let out a soft, apologetic laugh, almost embarrassed about the question. “Ah, you noticed…” he smiled awkwardly, slightly tilting his head in embarrassment. “I had a peculiar childhood, so I find it hard to understand them.”

That was… unexpected, to say the least.

Mydei raised an eyebrow, more curious than before now. “Peculiar?”

“My parents died when I was young, so my sister and I got thrown left and right between families even if she was willing to raise me, but we somehow stayed together every time.” He explained, his eyes weirdly looking down and full of some sort of melancholy that Mydei couldn't properly place. He decided not to mention it, but it felt more suffering than just sadness over what happened to him and his sister. Phainon, however, looked at him with different eyes, this time showing quiet acceptance of that same suffering in waves. “As it turned out, though… I wasn't an easy child to work with and I barely had any friends for too long.”

There was something weirdly depressing about that admission, and he didn't like it at all.

Truthfully, he didn't even know enough about him to try to make him feel better, but he absolutely hated seeing that look on his face. He sighed, shuffling the thoughts in his head and trying to decide what he could have done to make the knot in his stomach dissolve and cause those eyes to turn back to the glimmer and hunger for attention that Mydei grew so attached to over the course of the night.

Mydei clicked his tongue, immediately feeling a more interested gaze on him. He gave him a relaxed smile, almost neutral, as he tried to steer back the conversation. “You have some now.” He stated, almost as a matter of fact. 

“Are you one of them?” Phainon expectantly asked, slightly tilting his head as he weakly smiled at him. It was a hesitant question, his voice obviously scared to utter those words into reality.
