He could feel she had another goal and, sure enough, she tried to make him go out on a date, fully backed by both of their mothers. Mydei distinctly remembered Aglaea nodding and smiling at him as she chatted with her girlfriend– his mother– who was also visibly excited about the initiative.

He didn't mind that day, really, he had fun seeing his sister thinking way too hard about how much her little brother didn’t want to date these people. Despite that, she never forced him to be with someone, and he enjoyed infinitely more spending time with her than with any person he met in those few hours.

Of course, he suspected that seeing him like that– with red eyeshadow, lip gloss, flowers in his braid and a loose, white shirt that didn’t leave much to the imagination– would lead Phainon to have a composed reaction to it, but that was the only picture he had of himself, so it had to be enough for the both of them.

As soon as he sent it, he heard a choked gasp from the other part of the room. He turned calmly, already expecting that reaction. Even his own mother lost her composure for a second after she saw him that day, and he had to thank Aglaea for that– she was an excellent stylist.

“Oh, Gods,” Phainon whispered under his breath, turning towards Mydei with his mouth slightly open. “When did you even look like this?”

Mydei shrugged as he walked closer again, this time sitting on a chair near him. “Mother’s birthday a few months ago. Her girlfriend and my sister wanted to doll me up to see if I found a partner.”

“How the fuck were you single after that?”

“No one caught my attention.”

It was very simple. He would have dated people he was interested in– and there already weren’t many– and that were actually interested in him in return. There was a nonexistent percentage of both, at that party location. All he got were boring conversations and his sister hissing at the people that openly insulted him.

That was why it was fun, not for the people that were there.

“And I did?” Phainon asked, as he leaned over the table to rest an elbow and sustain his cheek with the palm of his hand. “I’m flattered.”

“I don’t know what you have that others don’t. But you… bring something new to the table.” Mydei almost confessed without thinking too much, only really thinking of giving an insight into his reasons to the man that asked for them.

It was too late when he realized that it sounded like a love confession. 

He didn't even know if he actually liked him or if he was just interested in knowing him better, it absolutely wasn't a love confession.

Unfortunately, Phainon seemed to live and breathe to annoy him. “So you like me,” he said, with a teasing tone. He looked like a puppy again, happily smiling with his eyes closed and satisfaction written all over his face. Mydei still imagined that fluffy white tail wagging behind him.

“Hold your horses, pretty boy.” Mydei warned, forcing his eyes open almost immediately. Phainon looked at him with a calm smile, waiting for whatever news he wanted to give him. He sighed, then added, “I said I’m interested. Whether or not I like you will depend on what you show me.”

It was true, in part. He was starting to like him– and maybe he did already– but he thought that running too much wouldn’t benefit either of them as well. All he knew was that he wanted to spend more time with him, because he genuinely liked talking to him.

However, Phainon looked like a rather intense person. He grew to like him as soon as he saw him, he already admitted to wanting him as a romantic partner and he spent the better part of the evening staring at him in awe. Mydei even sat on his lap for a long time, because he had all this love and want for him that genuinely captured his attention and decided to indulge his requests.

Because of it, his comments started to feel normal, even though he found them bold and out of the blue at the beginning.

“So if I’m lucky,” Phainon smirked, “you will kiss me one of these days.”

Mydei scowled as he stood up, looking right in his eyes. He expected a comment about it and, as he realized already, he was getting used to them. “I never said anything of the sort,” he answered, his voice stern and sharp.

“You didn't!” Phainon stood up as well, smiling at him. He leaned in slightly, enough to position his mouth right next to his ear. Then, with a low, knowing tone, he whispered, “That's more of an objective I personally have.”

Mydei didn't even flinch. He simply followed his movements with his eyes, only closing them when he felt his breath against his skin. He let out a small, amused laugh. “Cheeky and confident. Are you so sure that you will get what you want by the end of the night?”

Phainon leaned back enough to lock his eyes with Mydei's and smirked again. “I never said anything of the sort.”

He was unsure whether this man was annoying or interesting. He was constantly daring him, but he did so with such an overbearing attitude that he always felt both whenever he spoke.

Regardless, he didn't hate it. Quite the contrary, he was quite amused every time he brought up some sort of measurement with him.

“Is it a challenge?” Mydei asked, smirking right back at him, without moving from his position. Maybe it was a little childish, refusing the kiss of a person that he knew he liked, but he enjoyed the thrill of yet another game with him more than the kiss from a person he may have liked and barely knew.

Phainon looked at him with a satisfied smile. “If you want to see it like that,” he suddenly lowered his voice, “ Mydei .”

Gods, it was so hard not to huff right at his face. He knew that it was supposed to be flirting, but it just gave him second-hand embarrassment. Has this guy never been in a relationship before, or was he naturally this clumsy and pathetic?

And yet, whenever he didn't flirt or try so hard, he was cuter, funnier, more lovable. He wondered if something happened, or he was simply trying to impress him and it landed horrendously.

“I accept it, then.” Mydei answered, after sighing. He took a moment to himself to try and avoid morphing his facial expression too much after that.

Phainon stared at him for a second with an anonymous expression, without a clear emotion reflected in his eyes. There weren't many feelings at the same time, it was more of a void, not being able to pinpoint a way to respond to those words. Maybe, he realized the effect that his attempt at flirting had and wasn't really expecting him to agree to what he suggested.

Mydei wanted to tell him something else, maybe divert from the topic or tease him further to keep the conversation going, but something else caught his attention.

“Mama…”

His head snapped towards the door immediately, spotting Astraea standing in front of it, rubbing his eyes. He didn't look distressed, but there had to be something wrong, if he was searching for him. “Did we wake you up?” Mydei asked, with a tender smile on his face. 

Astraea shook his head, rubbing his eyes again. “Eyes burn…”

Mydei immediately walked up to him and crouched down, inviting him in his arms. He watched as the child fell on his chest, his arms immediately hugging him and holding him close. He wasn't scared, at the very least. He could be happy knowing that he didn't have new nightmares, this time.

“Because you don't sleep enough,” Mydei calmly explained, before picking him up and standing again. He turned towards Phainon too, smiling at him, then looked at his son again. “Which means, time to say bye to Phainon and try to sleep.”

Phainon walked closer and yawned, probably tired from still having to rest after a long work shift. He didn't blame him, instead fondly smiled upon thinking how cute he was again. He had this weird balance between being cute and objectively hot, all the while having a complex personality. Saying he was interesting and good-looking at this point would be a disservice to him.

Astraea whined on his shoulder, extending his arm towards Phainon. He was visibly exhausted, but he tried to stay awake, for a reason or another. Maybe his eyes actually hurt to that point, or maybe he was trying to stay up enough to say his farewells to their guest. Either way, he needed sleep. He woke up often in the middle of the night and he was oftentimes tired throughout the day… he could have reached his limit.

He held him a little tighter, hoping that he could offer a place to rest if he so wished.

“Phainon…” Astraea whined, smiling when he held the hand of the other adult in the room, “see you soon! Treat Mama super good…”

Phainon laughed warmly, lightly squeezing his hand. “I promise I will,” he whispered fondly. Mydei moved to look at him for a second, and he saw how he looked at his child then, blue irises full of the utmost form of love and affection.

Mydei's heart skipped a beat, but he didn't have nearly enough time to process it tht Astraea was pulling the hem of his shirt again.

“Mama, they still burn,” he whined again, puffing his cheeks in annoyance. It wasn't with him, he was genuinely feeling pain that didn't go away and he didn't like how much it lingered.

Mydei smiled, leaving a tender kiss on his forehead. “I promise you just need to sleep, sweetcakes,” he whispered, almost like a promise. “Do they burn when you close them?”

The child tilted his head for a second, most likely trying to understand what he just said. It wasn't a hard question and Mydei didn't think that he wasn't intelligent enough to answer, but he was exhausted. It was a miracle he still understood anything at all in the first place.

He did end up closing his eyes eventually, piecing back what was said to him. As he opened them, he guessed, “Less? But my heart hurts too now…”

“Mhm, so we need to sleep.” Mydei decided, walking over to his room again. He abandoned the idea of clearing the table, after that. Both of the people present with him made sure of it.

Phainon followed him quietly and he felt his son's cheek falling on his shoulder. When he checked, he found him peacefully sleeping there, his body completely leaning into Mydei's.

He smiled as he approached the door, shifting Astraea to rest on one arm without getting the slightest reaction from him. He must have been truly exhausted.

“See you soon, both of you!” Phainon greeted, as he stepped out of the door. He waited for a second in case he got an answer, but Mydei stood silent.

He didn't know why, really, but as soon as he saw him walk away, he grabbed his wrist and intensely looked at him. “Text me when you get home,” he requested, golden eyes fixated on bright blue ones.

Phainon softened and warmly smiled at him, moving the arm being held until his hand was holding Mydei's. “Goodnight, Mydei,” he whispered, walking as close as he could, his lips almost brushing against his skin. “Thanks for tonight.” 

Mydei shivered, and he feared that the other man physically felt it on his lips too. He probably did, by the way he was happily smiling at him. He kept on looking at him until their fingers were no longer knitted together, Phainon's steps growing more and more distant.

He was going to kill him. That man was going to mark his end. And he was probably going to let him.

With a heavy sigh, Mydei looked in the direction Phainon disappeared in, until he heard a little whine from his chest. Looking down, there was just Astraea peacefully sleeping, his ear practically next to his neck, probably able to hear his heartbeat from there. Maybe, it sped up when he grabbed Phainon’s arm and he noticed.

Mydei closed his eyes and huffed, exhausted. He really liked his time with Phainon despite his annoying behavior and horribly embarrassing attempts at flirting, there was no denying it at that point. Even his son picked up that much.

“What a nuisance,” he whispered to himself, briefly massaging his forehead with his fingers. He looked to the floor and sighed again, ultimately deciding that it was a problem for the future. Right now, both he and his child desperately needed to sleep.

He moved to close the door and rest Astraea on his bed, just for a few minutes, enough time to change his clothes and wash up, thinking back about the night. It wasn’t late at all, it wasn’t even 10 PM, but he was beyond tired after still settling as a parent and having to deal with Phainon for the better part of the day. Meeting him at the hospital, the call in the afternoon, the dinner in the evening… he couldn’t say that his intentions were ever subtle, but he preferred it that way. It was easier to understand and manage.

If he had to choose whether or not to accept his suggestion of being his partner, he would have accepted it, if they didn’t start that challenge over when Phainon would have kissed him. It wasn’t like he could back down, could he?

What’s more, right now he didn’t feel the need of a kiss. Just staying with him, cuddling a little like they just did, while they talked to each other to know each other better was more than enough for now.

Right? He didn’t need a kiss or hearing him call him pet names. He didn’t need romantic dates or sweet whispers either, and he certainly didn’t need to be more intimate with him. Not a chance.

He chased away those thoughts. Uselessly thinking about it now after just one date and feeling his heart continuously speed up and down would have led nowhere and just hurt the both of them. They had a nice friendship, for now. He wanted to preserve that.

As he returned to his room, he found Astraea still asleep, in the same position he left him in. He was drooling, sleeping soundly, and Mydei absolutely didn’t wake him up. However, he noticed that he received a few messages, and he wanted to check if they were from Phainon. After all, he did ask him to send one when he got home safely.

Sorry if I kept up Astraea :( 

Hope both of you are sleeping well!

Mydei smiled at his phone, shaking his head. Why would he ask that, if he was hoping they were, indeed, sleeping? He couldn’t have answered, if that was the case, and he clearly was waiting for a reply.

So, he didn’t make him wait for too much longer.

Not your fault, he just couldn’t sleep. He’s sleeping now.

I take you made it home safely.

I did :3

I’ll give you back your clothes later this week

You can keep them. I never put them on, they’re starting to feel too tight on me.

Thanks!

But damn, Mydei… you need to tell me what’s your workout plan >-<

Those emoticons at the end of half of his messages were helpful, other than plain annoying. It helped him understand how he felt, and he could act accordingly. It was something he struggled with, sometimes, and he could appreciate that silly part of him that made his intentions so known to him, even if he could figure out the majority of them.

Mydei smiled, both at the thought of some kind of date at the gym, or on a run together, and imagining him wearing his clothes in his day-to-day life.

Honestly, it felt more than a friendship already, but he wasn’t sure he wanted to process what that meant or made him feel.

If you stick around long enough, I will show you.

I told you, I’m very determined now ^-^

I’ll know everything about you, Mydei <3

Bold as always.

He stared at his phone for a while, thinking about how he could answer that. Obviously, he was eager to see him again, and Mydei couldn’t say he wanted to stop meeting up with him either. Phainon was simply more intense and communicated his needs and wants through his words, openly, without the fear of being pushed away.

Or, alternatively, he wanted to simply see his answer.

That made him more inclined to give him a more daring response.

Let’s see what other plan you come up with next time. You better not start boring me now.

Absolutely not!

Goodnight Mydei, see you soon :3

Mydei smiled and nodded to himself, at last sitting on his bed. He took a look over his shoulder, finding Astraea in the same position he left him, seemingly passed out. That poor little child must have had so many nightmares and anxiety attacks that his body needed to shut down completely now.

He turned, running a hand through his hair and getting a pleased noise in response, before he brushed his face against the mattress. Mydei smiled, wondering if he knew it was him. Maybe he did. The thought warmed his heart even more than it already was, and he finally decided to lay back next to him, sending one last message out of courtesy.

See you. Rest well.

Mydei turned the silence mode on and switched off his phone, putting it on the furniture right next to his bed, not even worrying to look at it. Instead, he turned towards Astraea and hugged him protectively, without putting too much force in that embrace, if any at all. The child whined for a second, probably feeling someone next to him, but he didn’t wake up. He simply rested his head against his chest and let him run his hand through his hair.

It was relaxing in a way he had never felt before. The knowledge that his son was safe, content and soundly asleep next to him after such a long day sparked a feeling of peace that he had never felt before in his life. Was that what his mother and father felt whenever he fell asleep in their arms or when he looked for their support when he was younger? 

If it truly was something he was going to feel constantly, he didn’t bother at all. On the contrary, he was sure he was going to enjoy that feeling more than any other.

That is, if Phainon didn’t keep on giving him pleasant sensations and emotions that he had never felt before. For now, it was just a couple, fleeting feelings, but he knew they would have increased. Those alone made him want to stay a little longer. Maybe, if they kept meeting up, he would have given him many more and his world could have experienced a few new colors again.

He thought about it for a few seconds before finally closing his eyes, but no color that he knew could have truly described him to the fullest. Maybe, if he stayed around a little longer, he could solve that riddle.

As darkness engulfed him in a warm, peaceful embrace, in his mind echoed the feeling of bathing in soft clouds and a bright blue sky all around him. He wouldn’t have minded that scenery to be a recurring occasion in his life at all.

Chapter End Notes

Sorry this took a long while !! I lost the word count at some point and I was figuring out how to tell Mydei's feelings and impressions for their date but hopefully it was enjoyable :] I've grown attached to the cat siblings so they're here too aha

Chapter Notes

CW: mentions of self-harm, child death

“Let me ask you something,” Mydei answered, “is he currently sleeping on top of me? Is he the one I’m with, right now? Is he the one Astraea calls Papa?”
“Astraea is just a child.”
“And yet, he noticed that I’m happier when I’m with you.”

See the end of the chapter for more notes

“Phai… please, stop pouting like this.”

Phainon let out a loud groan as soon as he heard that. He was laying on his bed upside down, his head hanging from the edge as he nervously looked at his phone. He read that message again and again, almost like a mantra, until his head could only think about those few words.

Can we move tomorrow’s date? It’s not the right time yet.

His thoughts were endless, trying to make sense of the situation. Nothing he was thinking was even remotely positive, instead insisting on the fact that he decided to slowly grow more distant.

He let out another groan, looking at his phone again. There was no way, right? He looked interested enough last time… why would he cut everything off?

It drove him mad.

He was so pretty and kind and strong and so utterly perfect, but he wasn't interested in him at all! If he could, he honestly would have punched himself in the face by now.

Not that he wasn't used to it, most people are attracted to him before knowing him. The difficult part had always been liking him past those first dates. He thought Mydei would have been different, but maybe–

“Hello? Phai?”

That sweet voice calling his name caught his attention. Looking above him stood Hyacine, the very same doctor that he suggested for Mydei's son. His roommate since university and one of his closest friends.

“I’m not pouting,” Phainon rebutted, remembering her sentence from earlier. It was even a miracle his brain registered it, with how intensely he was thinking about someone else completely.

Hyacine sighed, crossing her arms over her chest. “You keep saying, while pouting.”

Phainon groaned for the third time in the last five minutes. If he could, he would do more than just that, but he was way too tired to think of anything. Maybe he needed to take a nap. He came back from his night shift just a few hours prior– thanks to which he couldn't even try to hang out with Mydei during the week– and he knew he was tired.

But he couldn't stop thinking about Mydei and that alone was enough to dispel any need of sleeping he had. How could he sleep, when Mydei would never talk to him again?

He rolled over on the bed, enough to slam his face in his own pillow. He whined into it this time, opting to diversify his noises of complaint instead of solely groaning. Honestly, he felt miserable. He was so excited to go out with him again and see him again and spend time with him again, only to be told to wait again.

He couldn't! It's been so long since Phainon had last seen him and he wanted to see him again.

Hyacine huffed loudly, purposefully so he could hear her. He whined back, before finally sitting up and looking at her. “What’s the issue? Your prince didn't call you back?”

“He’s not my prince.”

She promptly laughed, then smiled at him. “Whatever you say!”

It was so obvious.

Everyone with half a brain could understand how much he liked Mydei. If they saw him, they honestly would have understood that Mydei seemed to do so as well just like Phainon did the last time they saw each other, but then again…

“He called off yesterday's date… he said that it wasn't the right time.” Phainon explained, in a bit of a disappointed tone.

Hyacine tilted her head slightly and wore a dubious expression on her face. “For what?”

“I don't know!” Phainon yelled, absolutely horrified by the prospect of Mydei not being interested at all in him. “Hyacine, I think I fucked up again.”

“I don't think so! He keeps messaging you, right? Didn't he send you a picture too?” She reminded him, probably trying to see points in favour of the situation.

Phainon was truly glad he had her as a friend. She was so bright that she could see the good in anything, and will gladly do so for a dear friend like him. She did bully him a little bit sometimes and used to slapping in his face that she got a higher mark in some exams, but who would want such a boring friendship with no competition and bickering?

“He did that when I last saw him… I look at it every day, but–”

“Phai… we both know what happened last time.”

Right. Last time. And every other time before that, honestly.

He had a bad habit of forcing himself on others before they were ready to commit to a relationship and growing attached way too fast, often resulting in break ups after only a couple of months. The fact that his personality wasn't as they imagined it didn't help either.

However, that wasn't the case with Mydei, he was sure of it! If anything, he looked more pleased to see his personality during that dinner while finding him attractive, if he had to judge the way he was staring at him and touching his chest. He still couldn’t believe that even happened.

His thoughts drifted away from those memories when the door opened, a smiling Castorice peeking from behind it. Her hair was slightly wet and she only wore a light purple dress with a flowered pattern all over it. He noticed Hyacine’s eyes shining at the sight, visibly excited to see her.

It was how a couple was supposed to act, after all. Phainon wondered for a second if he would have reacted in the same way if Mydei walked up to him like that after a shower. The sheer thought of seeing him with wet hair, skin glimmering and walking around with one of the sweaters that he so willingly gave him was enough to make his head spin.

“Good morning,” she greeted them, with her usual kind and meek voice. Hyacine smiled gently at her, but Castorice turned to Phainon instead, a little worried. “Phainon?”

Hyacine smiled apologetically, a little amused. “His dashing prince moved their date to next week,” she explained quickly, filling her in on the situation. Phainon's eyes moved to look at them and pay attention to their conversation. It was the least he could do, if they were going to talk about his private, love life.

Not that it was their first time, but he wanted to see what Castorice would have said about it. Usually she was neutral about it, she just wanted the best for him, unlike Hyacine's teasing whenever she felt like he could have gotten a crush.

“Oh, Mydei?” Castorice asked, a little surprised. She slightly tilted her head and pouted, deep in thought. “Last time I saw him, he mentioned something about trying to leave his son alone in the house little by little. Maybe it's because of that.”

Phainon's body almost moved on its own, standing up from the bed in record time. “Do you know him?” He asked before he knew it, almost running to stop in front of her.

She nodded calmly, evidently not surprised by that reaction. “I know his sister and his mothers. He wasn't home too often, but Cipher often put both of them in trouble.”

Hyacine smiled and looked at him, satisfied. “See, Phai? It was just for his child.”

He could have guessed it. Astraea had to be a pretty big part of his life now, especially since he just adopted him. He had to adjust to his new life, and he suspected that the child needed some time to heal a little before he could leave him at home on his own. He didn't mention it at the time, but he seemed in a bit of a panicked state back when he asked him out at the hospital.

Phainon felt slightly guilty about his previous thoughts and reasoning. However, that only meant that Mydei wasn't trying to put distance between them! After all, he still answered his messages and picked up his phone on the rare occasions he managed to to call him. Maybe he simply didn't have to worry too much, in the end.

“Mydei…” he whispered, laying his hand on his chest. He almost felt it aching by thinking about how much time he had made for him despite it all. Even if he was struggling with his child, he still made time to talk to him, regardless of how often they actually met. It was a tiny gesture, but one that he could admire simply for what it was– showing his love in his own way.

Castorice looked at him with a perplexed expression as he kept thinking. Swiftly enough for him not to notice, Castorice smiled brightly and took her phone in her hands, quickly dialing a number. “Hi, Mydei,” she almost immediately said, noticing Phainon's head snapping at her at supersonic speed. She smiled at him again, before turning to her phone. “There's someone looking for you, do you want to talk to them?”

Upon hearing that, Phainon's bright blue eyes focused on Castorice– maybe a little too much, given the cough that Hyacine gave him. He took a step back after softening his gaze, mainly to respect her private space and her girlfriend's request.

However, Castorice lended him her phone, the contact's name clear on the screen. Mydei, with an orange kitten emoji right next to it. Now that he thought about it, he did resemble an overgrown orange cat.

“All yours,” Castorice muttered, smiling at him as she waited for him to take her phone and talk to the person that had plagued his thoughts for the past few days.

As soon as he laid the phone against his ear, he heard that voice ask, “Who's–”

“Mydei!”

He couldn't even let him finish. He was so happy to hear that voice again that he was smiling with his eyes closed, his legs slightly moving at a fixed pace out of excitement.

“Oh,” he let out an amused laugh, “it's my annoying puppy. What do you need?”

Phainon was about to combust.

Even just hearing his voice made him so unbelievably happy, but the little nickname with that ‘my’ to precede it… he felt his own brain melt until the only thing he could possibly think about was him.

“To see you,” he quickly answered, a smile growing on his face wider and wider. “Please?”

A soft laugh could be heard on the other side, then the warm, soft voice he loved said, “You know where I live.”

Phainon felt so viscerally happy that he could start flying on his own. Before he knew it, he was already dressing himself, putting his coat on, mentally making a map of the path he had to take to get there as soon as possible.

“Can you keep talking while I get there?” He simply asked, his tone evidently excited.

Mydei sighed. “You should give this phone back to Castorice first.”

Right. He was thinking about it! He would have never taken the phone of one of his dear friends, after all.

But first, he had to know the answer.

“So you can?” He asked, practically bouncing up and down from the sheer happiness that answer could have given him.

“... Yes. Call me when you're on the way.”

“Oh, you bet.”

Phainon immediately hung up and handed the phone back to its rightful owner, before getting his own phone and going out of the door. As he walked through the exit, he yelled a tiny, “thanks, Cas!” and hurried to dial his number.

“Took you a while,” Mydei teased as soon as he picked up.

Ah, he loved him. He loved how playful and childish he could be sometimes, despite the appearances. How could anyone let this man go?

Phainon smiled at himself and muttered, “Are you mad?”

“Why would I be? I just expected you to throw yourself on the phone when I hung up.”

He was happy. He didn't think he would actually be mad at him, but the confirmation was nice to hear. Even if he made that question because he was teasing him, Mydei still answered honestly.

How cute.

His chest was burning, but with a kind, calm fire instead of a raging one. It was… oddly, pleasantly sitting in his chest, simply keeping his heart at ease.

Phainon let out a heavy sigh as he tasted that feeling for another couple of seconds. “I missed you,” he happily stated.

“Intense as always,” Mydei dryly answered. There, he held his breath for seconds that felt way too long, before adding, with the soft tone he almost exclusively used with his child, “But I missed you too.”

Phainon's heart skipped a beat.

Mydei… missed him. It's only been a week and he was missing him too. That news was so exciting to hear, the words still lingering in Phainon's brain and echoing the same feelings he held for him. ‘Glad’ didn't even encompass it anymore. He was ecstatic.

“Do you want to come over for lunch?” came from the phone. The sentence made his heart beat a little faster. “I'm buying groceries now, maybe you will finally eat something decent.”

“Ah, if it's not a problem?”

“I wouldn't even ask if it was an issue. I thought it was clear last time, but I don't like sugarcoating my feelings or lying to make you feel better. If I invite you to my place, it means I want you there.”

That was something that Phainon struggled to understand.

He perfectly knew that Mydei was absurdly honest, but past memories stopped him from being able to completely trust him. If it ended like all those other times with him too… he didn't even know what he would have done.

Regardless, he couldn't possibly refuse that invitation.

“I’ll come,” he stated, smiling to himself. That sentence came out before he could even think about the words he wanted to use.

Phainon heard immediately the soft laugh on the other side. “Do you have any requests?”

“For the food or for us?”

“... I still have a five year-old in that apartment.”

Was that the only complaint? That his son was in the house too? Or was it an excuse?

The fact that he didn't completely shut down the idea of taking some time to themselves made his head spin enough to the point of feeling nausea building in his throat.

Mydei liked him. Maybe. He wanted to believe that. What other reason did he have to say that and flirt back as much as he did? Inviting him to his place again so soon just because he missed him? It felt so tangible, and real, and something he could actually reach for.

And he was about to cook for him again. He was about to faint at the mere thought of that.

“Any food you want to make will be fine!” Phainon beamed, answering his previous question with sincerity.

“If you say so,” Mydei agreed, then completely changed topics. “How do you know Castorice?”

“Same university course for the first few months, then she dropped it to be a writer.”

“She has a decent following. I'm happy for her, she's always been kind to me and my sister.”

And yet, here he was, sleeping in his arms, searching for warmth and safety from him too. Phainon would have gladly given it to him, even if he didn’t fully understand why. He could just hold him until he wanted to crawl out of his arms, he was simply curious about the reason. He was probably just thankful he helped him and may have liked him since then… same as every other kid.

He should probably stop thinking about it. Maybe he would tell him, someday, if he was still around. If Mydei liked him enough to let him be around the both of them. Phainon wordlessly hoped for that to be the case.

Mydei walked closer and petted his son’s head, gently and careful not to be too abrupt. He was so dangerously close, of course, and Phainon knew that his muscles froze all of a sudden and way too much. He tried relaxing them in the following few seconds, without much success, left only with the option of hoping he wouldn’t notice.

“You can sit close to Phainon if you want, but you have your seat and your menu,” Mydei quietly reminded him. He waited for Astraea to open his eyes and look at him, still from the safe refuge on Phainon’s neck. Mydei rubbed his thumb on his child’s shoulder and whispered, “What did the doctor say?”

Astraea sucked on his bottom lip, darting his eyes to the side. “That I have to eat a lot to be healthy,” he answered after a few seconds, a little embarrassed.

“Exactly. You can play with Phainon later,” Mydei smiled at him, brushing the back of his hand on his son’s cheek. Astraea immediately sat up as he let out a happy noise, slightly wiggling his legs.

Phainon smiled too, amused by that reaction. He was sure that absolutely no one would be able to avoid falling in love with that little kid. He was way too adorable.

With that thought, he sat him down at what he assumed was his place, then sat down near him, in front of Mydei. They had already eaten together, but he would never get tired of that feeling of closeness and domesticity that moments like these carried with them. It warmed his heart to no end.

Regardless, he watched both Mydei and Astraea as they ate before he could even start his own food. The child didn’t seem too fond of what he had to eat– and Phainon couldn’t even blame him. It was an absurd amount of food for a little child, and a lot of it was vegetables, either mixed in with the main course or on their own. He could probably eat it without problems, but little, frail, small, tiny–

His brain clogs finally started setting in the right position to spin and let him reach the conclusion on his own. He was visibly underweight, even after a week probably spent with that kind of diet. Astraea ate everything without complaint, but Phainon wondered about how he ended up in such a state. Were his biological parents truly so neglectful? That would explain why he got so attached to him and Mydei so fast, but it didn’t hurt his heart any less to think about how difficult his life was up until that point.

Mydei cleared his throat as he looked at him with dark eyes. Stop looking at him and eat, they seemed to say.

Phainon obeyed almost on a reflex, only noticing that his hand moved on its own when his mouth tasted pork, tomatoes and salad on his tongue.

It was so pleasant. He ate something similar before, but it never tasted as good as it did at that moment.

“It’s good,” he said, maybe a little too surprised.

Mydei smirked at him. “I told you.”

Phainon smiled brightly, happily taking another bite. “You saved me!”

Partly a lie– he knew how to cook, thank you very much– but somewhat based in reality. That dish took as much as instant ramen or noodles, but it was healthier and with more nutrients. Maybe he would have eaten it again, from time to time.

“Mama, is Phai going to be Papa?”

Phainon almost choked on the piece of meat in his mouth.

“Wha–” he started, before he saw the truce expression across the table. He held up his arms, almost as if he was surrendering himself. “No, no! I swear I didn't tell him anything!”

Luckily, Mydei liked him enough to not rip off his limbs. Hopefully. Maybe.

“You’re just… so happy when he's around,” Astraea happily chirped, completely unbothered by the scene unfolding in front of him. After all, he knew that Mydei would have never raised his hands on him.

Phainon honestly expected a rebuttal, maybe a rejection. He didn't hate the idea to be something like that following his relationship with Mydei growing and growing, but nothing of the sort happened.

Instead, Mydei sighed. First, he looked at Phainon with almost scared eyes. Then, he looked at Astraea, and he stated confidently, “He’s not Papa yet.”

Yet. He wasn't Astraea's father or Mydei's partner yet.

That little word was going to make his head explode.

“... Yet?” he asked with hesitation, looking straight at Mydei.

He, on his part, only gave him a grunt. “Shut up and eat.”

Phainon hinted at a smile, before aiming to finally finish up his food as Mydei not-so-gently asked. It was so good even then, up until the last bite.

Astraea struggled a little to eat everything, but he did, then immediately crawled back on Phainon's lap. He played a little with him however he wanted, from just pushing his tiny hands on Phainon's chest and giggling to listening to a story he made up on the spot, to playfully tickling him.

He felt Mydei's eyes on them, gentle and tender, but he paid no mind to them. Knowing they were fully focused on them was an honour that only he wanted to cherish.

Excited laughs and gentle whispers filled the room, until Astraea settled on his lap. Phainon swung an arm around him, as if to keep him close, and the child quickly used his hand to play and loosely pass the time. He let him, gently relaxing his hand so he could bend his fingers however he liked.

After a while, of course, Astraea started to yawn, until he fell asleep right there, his little fingers still gripping onto Phainon's hand.

So cute and so relaxing. Phainon could have fallen asleep as well, since he still had to rest since the afternoon of the day prior. He was so, so tired, but he would have never passed on the opportunity to see Mydei. And now, he had his child sleeping on his lap and his eyes completely entranced by him.

This was better than any dream he could have had if he ever refused to go to his house.

The ringing of the bell suddenly put a halt on his thoughts. “That’s for me,” Mydei muttered, before walking to the other room to open the door. Phainon heard his voice almost resound from where he stood, focused on what he was about to say.

Astraea stirred in his lap, just to fall back on his chest and nuzzle his head there. Absent-mindedly, Phainon petted his head and let him lay his hands on his arm, whining for a split second. As he looked down, he saw the child half-awake and smiled, only to gently kiss the top of his head and listen to a few other whines as he lazily moved his legs. Just after a few seconds, he grabbed Phainon’s hand and turned on his side, hugging it almost as a last anchor.

Phainon looked at him with a vaguely curious expression on his face. He moved his finger to slightly brush on his jaw, watching as he moved his face closer to his hand. He smiled at the motion, noticing just now how much he resembled a cat napping. Absurdly cute.

If he ended up somehow not being Mydei’s partner– which he was praying to every God he knew not to happen– he at least wanted to babysit the little guy. Hyacine and Castorice would love him as well.

“Hey, Hephaestion,” he finally heard from the other room. He turned his head towards it, thankfully able to see the door and whoever was standing around it. There was another man standing in front of Mydei with long, soft peach colored hair, looking at him with familiarity and playfulness in his eyes.

He didn’t jump up just because Astraea was still sleeping on him.

The man looked in his general direction and gaped, then looked at Mydei with a devilish, satisfied grin. Phainon didn’t even know how he was supposed to feel about it. Offended? That was what he was most prone to feel at that moment.

However, Mydei didn’t react much, besides blocking his vision by moving in front of him. “No, don't even think about it.”

“I won our bet?”

“Yeah. Like all the other times.”

All the other times… it was the thing that echoed in Phainon’s mind. He was right, they were familiar with each other. That soft gaze and overly friendly attitude lit up alarms in his mind, but he still didn’t move. Astraea sleeping on him was probably saving him from royally fucking up his chances with Mydei.

If he understood that name correctly, that was Mydei's ex-boyfriend and childhood friend. The one person he was absolutely sure had a corner of his own in Mydei's heart. Just knowing he was in the next room was enough for Phainon to feel anxiety rise up in his chest.

“What can I say, Mydeimos?” the man asked, curling his mouth in a knowing grin. “I know your type very well!”

Mydei huffed, as if they had this conversation a thousand times. “It’s just been one date–”

“And he's already holding your child like that? Since when do you move so fast, Mydeimos?”

“Oh, shut it. He's just helping.”

Too friendly. All those little sirens in his head were starting to feel deafening, his vision starting to only be dots in an empty space, fog invading his mind before he could notice. He breathed out heavily, his vocal chords vibrating without he could stop them.

Calm down. You can't make a scene right here. Behave.

It was the only thing he could repeat in his head, almost like a mantra to keep himself sane. If he didn’t, he was afraid he would have ran away and that was the last thing he wanted to do after the long week he spent thinking about Mydei without being able to see him.

“Phai?”

Astraea’s voice somehow reached him, maybe because it was so much closer to him than the other two. He yawned and squeezed his eyes shut for a few seconds, trying to wake himself up. Phainon wondered if he ever got decently long naps, given he woke up so often between them.

The child slowly got on his knees and hugged him, silently lying his head on his shoulders. He didn’t say anything, but Phainon held him as close as he possibly could anyway, then buried his face in the kid’s neck, almost as if he was his last shred of hope he could hang onto.

Astraea didn't seem to mind. Phainon knew why, but he chased away those thoughts, fully focusing on feeling operational again.

He hated that feeling in his chest that made him feel worthless and unimportant to anyone in his life, he despised the ache in his stomach, turning and twisting, just because someone dear to him had another important person in their life.

Those ugly, disgusting feelings accompanied him for so long that he almost didn't mind being alone. Barely having friends and keeping them at a safe distance as well.

That was what should have happened with Mydei as well. When he felt a crush developing, he avoided them for a few days before completely erasing himself from their lives. It was easy. No one really cared that much to keep him around.

In the end, Mydei won't be different. It would have been just a little crush for both, if he just left his life forever.

It was all so painfully easy.

But he refused to. He wanted to keep him around. He needed him in his life.

And he would once again end up getting hurt for that decision.

If he could just leave him alone, he wouldn't be in that situation. What right did he have to take him away from his friends or ask him to only ever see him? How could he be the only one to–

“Are you okay?”

That low, warm, comfortable voice called to him, with a hand rubbing his back following it.

Phainon snapped his head up, eyes terrified and jaw trembling slightly. He didn't need this. He didn't deserve such a kind, loving man to repay him with so much affection.

Despite it all, the man was gone. It was just them, in the silence of Mydei's kitchen. He didn't feel safe even knowing that. So many dark, twisted thoughts swirmed in his head that even just looking at Mydei felt like a wrong enough act to run away from him.

And yet, he didn't.

Instead, he closed his eyes and leaned into his touch, gently letting him caress his cheek. He forced himself to stay in his place, even if his brain was yelling at him to run for his life. It would have ended badly for him if he stayed, like any other time. But his touch was so tender, and loving, and soft that he just wanted to feel his hand brush against his skin for a little longer. Even if that meant falling over and breaking his neck. At least, he would have died after being caressed so gently by Mydei.

“My apologies,” Mydei breathed out, “that was… my ex-boyfriend.”

Of course, he knew.

He did mention having a friend who bet on them talking too, and he figured that was the same person. Probably, they broke up peacefully and remained friends, since he was visibly happy about Mydei seeing someone else to the point of betting on it.

Despite that, he couldn’t get over that deafening thought. This won’t be different. You would still end up alone, in the end.

“Phainon?”

Mydei’s voice made sure he would raise his head to look at him. He looked worried. It was just slightly different from his usual neutral expression, but it was noticeable. Was he worried for him? Did he truly care that much or was he just feeling sorry for the mess of a person that he stumbled upon?

Phainon truly wanted to stand by his words with the same conviction he used to do when he was younger– he was still convinced that a relationship with him would have been the best experience he could have ever asked for, but there was too much holding him back to deliver on that promise.

“Sorry,” he whispered, trying to move Astraea to the side to stand up. “Sorry, I have to go.”

A powerful yank pulled him back into a sitting position as a hand pushed his shoulder against the back of the chair. Phainon looked slightly above him, slightly confused from the sudden force, only to find Mydei towering over him, pushing him back.

Phainon gulped, eyes darting from Mydei’s eyes, to his lips, to his eyes again. They seemed almost hurt from that action. His hand gripped his clothes, almost desperately keeping him where he was sitting, careful to control himself enough to avoid scaring his child.

Mydei rested a knee in between Phainon’s thighs, as if to gesture his resounding refusal to let him go. “We aren’t together anymore for a reason,” he stated, way too calm for the fire that seemed to burn relentlessly in his eyes.

“You said you have some feelings left for him,” Phainon somehow managed to answer, loosely remembering a discussion they had a while back. They approached each other with the intention of dating, but Mydei’s answers at first sounded like he was being forced to talk to him… and he absolutely didn’t like it.

He remembered being determined to change his mind and he thought he didn’t succeed so soon, but from what he was saying and the way he acted, he started to believe it little by little. Each caring text he sent felt like it brought more proof to what he wanted his reality to be, but he could never fully believe it.

After all, that was the case so many other times, and none ended well. Too intense, too quick, too useless, not satisfying enough, too much of a difficult person to deal with. Too many excuses to simply say that they all made up a person in his head that he simply couldn’t be.

Mydei had to be different. The fact that he was keeping him there with so much desperation gave him one last spark of hope.

“They aren’t feelings I have right now,” Mydei firmly stated, tearing Phainon away from those thoughts again. He was looking at him with soft eyes, almost suffering from his words. Maybe they even sounded like accusations to him, but Phainon didn’t want to look at that specific thought further.

Instead, he looked at him and slowly moved his hand to gently wrap around Mydei’s wrist, unsure how he looked at that moment. He was so beautiful and so close to his face that he couldn’t believe he was allowed to even touch him. His thumb brushed a couple of times against his skin and his mouth opened for a few seconds, before a hesitant, weak voice whispered, “Can I get up?”

It was a little scary and he was terrified that he would have left and hurt him like so many others before him, but so was Mydei. He clearly looked like it, at least.

“It’s raining and you’re tired,” Mydei whispered back to him, his hand slowly traveling to his shoulder to the crook of his neck. Phainon’s hand never left his skin, but he let out a shaky breath when he felt Mydei’s thumb brushing against his jaw. “You will get a fever if you leave now.”

The voice he used was gentle and caring, whispered almost against his ear, as his hold softened and felt more and more like an accidental caress that lingered for a moment too long.

Phainon exhaled and tilted his head as he leaned into the touch, finally bringing himself to give him an adoring smile. “I’m… not planning to leave. I think. If you’re okay with it?”

“Don’t leave,” Mydei repeated, almost like a futile, tentative prayer.

How cute, Phainon thought. At least, he had a reason strong enough to stay without having to listen to his own thoughts. Mydei wanted him to stay, so he would have stayed, no matter what his brain might suggest. For the moment, at the very least.

Without noticing, he found himself yawning and a sudden wave of tiredness hit him in the face. Sleep deprivation enjoyed playing so many tricks on him when he truly pushed himself and, unfortunately, night shifts were wearing him out. Maybe he should have slept in the last two days. Three days? He didn’t even know. He lost count. It didn’t matter.

“Hey,” Mydei whispered, cupping his face with both of his hands. Phainon could hardly keep his eyes open, but he let him look at his face, too tired to even hold on his wrist or oppose himself to his hold. His head pathetically fell on his chest, way too tired to raise itself up again.

Mydei sighed, sitting on his lap as he caressed the back of Phainon’s head and guiding it to rest on his shoulder. “Didn’t you sleep?” he asked, with a lower voice.

“Night shift,” Phainon mumbled, before turning his head to the side. He noticed that Astraea left who knows when. Probably when his father crawled on top of him. Good call. Intelligent child.

Phainon closed his eyes for a second, surrounded by comfortable warmth and almost feeling Mydei’s heartbeat lulling him to sleep. As it turned out, he needed a nap. He simply didn’t expect to take it on the shoulder of someone else. Especially someone he was interested in as much as he was in Mydei.

The hand holding Mydei’s wrist like a lifeline relaxed too, dropping on his lap as well. He was convinced he would have started sleeping soundly right there, but he evidently kept being wrong. He felt a sudden movement pushing his head off of the shoulder it was resting on, abruptly waking him up entirely again.

He groaned, dangling his head in the air, struggling to keep it steady and his eyes open. “What are you…”

That minuscule whisper got lost in the space between them apparently, because the next thing Phainon knew was that he was being lifted up, but he was definitely too out of it to say anything. He knew it was Mydei. That was enough to settle any possible anxiety he could have had.

“Just carrying you to my bed so you can sleep,” came his voice, sweet and kind.

Phainon rested his head on his shoulder again, opting to freak out about the fact that Mydei was princess-carrying him to his bed so he could rest. He was going to kill him if he kept doing things like those.

“If you keep saying things like that,” Phainon laughed, “I’ll start thinking you like me.”

“I do.”

“Huh?”

His brain short-circuited so suddenly and so violently that Phainon was sure he was smoking out of his ears. Did he just say that he liked him in such a casual way? Was he truly trying to put an end to his life?

Mydei put him on the bed and petted his hair, as if to reassure him. “I… like spending time with you,” he explained with a little hesitation. Phainon stared at him with a confused expression, still taking in all the information around him. All he felt was the back of a couple of fingers brushing on his cheek and a voice whispering, “Take a nap.”

At the immediate sound of steps getting away from him, Phainon gathered all his remaining strength and grabbed the back of his shirt, still struggling to keep his eyes open. “Can you stay here? Please? You said you liked being with me…”

He really didn’t want him to leave. He stayed so he could be with him, nap or not.

“... Fine,” he answered, after a few, deathly seconds spent in silence.

Phainon watched as Mydei crawled next to him, accepting without any issue the weight on his chest. He was so warm and soft. His fingers trailed hesitantly along silver locks of hair, lazily playing with them. Cute. Relaxing too.

“Sorry if I’m being too selfish,” Phainon whispered, slightly moving to look at the man above him. He was still tired, but he wanted to talk to him a little longer. He would have slept, just… in a few minutes.

Mydei huffed. “I prefer that over someone who’s okay with everything.”

Was that his preference? Someone who wanted him all to himself, not even bearing the sight of another in his vicinity? Phainon knew perfectly that he had seen the way he was acting… and yet, he preferred it?

He wondered if that man fit that description, or if he didn't and Mydei loved him all the same. They seemed so in tune with each other that it was impossible for him to even try to reach–

“Are you still jealous of Hephaestion?” Mydei interrupted those dangerous thoughts, for both of their well-being. As Phainon only looked at him without answering, further questioned, “You wanted to storm out as soon as I mentioned we used to be together. Wasn’t that jealousy?”

It was. He guessed so, at least.

Phainon knew he was jealous. He had always been, even with his older sister or his friends. Things got worse when those people who he felt so attached to started to abandon him. Ignore him. Forget him.

He was unsure when it spiraled. He only remembered the immeasurable hurt that came with it. He was getting heartbroken with such pain that the only way he could bear it at the time was by getting physically hurt on purpose.

Distribute it. Focus on something else. That bruise could be healed, he could focus on patching himself up and feel a ting of pain in the following days. The same couldn't be said for the wounds in his heart.

He abandoned that practice in favour of going to the gym and training until he had no energy left– or when he got kicked out, whichever he reached first– which led to the same result. Bruises, scars, pain, patching up, struggling afterwards.

Other than that, he understood how easy it was moving away from others. Detaching himself, walking away, ignoring them, pretending he hated them. It was so damn easy.

But he didn't want Mydei to see or experience any of it. He wanted to be with him and stay with him. Forever, if possible.

However, it was difficult. Managing those violent, intense feelings was so difficult. He had to stay on the topic, at least. “How do I even measure up to that?” he asked, as earnestly as he could.

He was worried that, even if he seemed sincere in wanting to stay there, he would have left too eventually. Phainon desperately needed him to stay.

“Let me ask you something,” Mydei answered, “is he currently sleeping on top of me? Is he the one I’m with, right now? Is he the one Astraea calls Papa?”

“Astraea is just a child.”

“And yet, he noticed that I’m happier when I’m with you.”

“You denied that?”

“I never did.”

He must have missed that very important detail. Or, alternatively, he assumed he didn't like him and the child was just seeing things, since he was… well, a child. It was probably the second option.

“Even so… isn’t your friend ethereal?” Phainon asked, blue eyes never leaving Mydei's face and gentle fingers still playing with silver locks.

“Oh, he is,” Mydei laughed. “He’s extremely beautiful, but a relationship needs more than good looks to work.”

Right. He knew that. Even so, it wasn't like they didn't have any amount of chemistry or they were anonymous to each other. If he was that same childhood friend Mydei mentioned, then… there was no way he could catch up.

They played together as children, probably hung out in middle and high school, this Hephaestion guy probably knew him better than anyone else– how could he ever be important to him when he already had someone like that in his life?

Phainon pondered whether or not he wanted to voice those thoughts. They were horribly selfish bordering on possessive and he perfectly knew that so many people didn't like them.

And yet, he wanted to anyway, simply because Mydei was warm and soft and he didn't want to let go of something like that.

“He’s known you for longer,” he quietly whispered. He hoped it would have been enough for him not to get too weirded out and understand that he cared.

Mydei let out an amused laugh. “Then ask me out more often, instead of sending me pictures of your furniture.”

Phainon blinked at him, not even taking into account the last part of his sentence. Huh? Is he asking me to take him out? Is he suggesting that he wants me to get closer to him?

His head was spinning with that new information, almost high on the mutual feeling that Mydei was offering him. “Next week?” he managed to ask, somehow still being able to form coherent sentences.

“Sure,” Mydei grinned, “I trust that you will choose an interesting date.”

He finally smiled brightly again, the spark of a new challenge igniting his energies again. “Of course!”

Phainon truly liked those little moments with him. The slight thrill of every challenge and the way he always indulged in whatever he suggested was becoming so pleasant to give himself into that he never wanted it to stop.

Mydei nodded and slightly pushed him off of him, moving to get up from the bed. “Go to sleep now.”

Sleep? Now? There was absolutely no way he could have done that. Not with a thousand thoughts running around his head at full speed, bouncing off of each other like crazed rubber balls.

Phainon grabbed his arm once again, weakly exhaling. He grinned as he rolled his eyes mischievously. “On second thought…”

“Phainon.”

“Why do you like me so much?”

Mydei scoffed, avoiding his very intense gaze. One of those days, Phainon really wanted to cup his face and look at his embarrassed, avoidant face. He must look so cute with a bright red blush on his face as well.

In the end, he forcefully removed his hand away from him. Phainon looked at his own hand, violently yanked away from the place it was staying on. As he glanced back to Mydei, he saw his child instead, looking back at him with big, brown eyes.

A soft smile appeared on his face. Maybe it was better like that. Slower. More comfortably. Calmer. Even if he slowed down a little, those two clearly would have still been there.

Astraea turned his head towards his father, standing still by the door. “Can I sleep with Phainon, if he can’t sleep?”

Mydei sighed. “Astraea–”

“No, it’s fine,” Phainon guaranteed, giving him a reassuring smile. “We can both sleep here without problems.”

The child immediately jumped on the bed, curling around Phainon like his life depended on it. A hand travelled to his hair, instantly met with an excited giggle.

It was so easy.

Slipping into that routine, only looking forward to love and trust from an innocent child that genuinely liked him and was incapable of hurting him like other people did was so impossibly easy. He wished he could take those gestures and just settle into them. Welcome them. Slowly change because of them.

But he couldn’t. Not right now. Not when he felt so happy whenever he spent time with them and going too fast could destroy everything.

“Phainon,” Astraea whispered, next to him, “I’m cheering for you.”

Phainon blinked. “What?”

Astraea pressed his lips together and sat up, quickly looking at the already closed door. Phainon guessed that Mydei left the room and closed the door after him to give them the peace and quiet they both needed to sleep. The child turned back to him, tilting his head. “If you don’t do something, Mama’s gonna die alone. Please, save him.”

Phainon couldn’t hold in a slight laugh. “Why would you say that?”

“He always refuses everyone, but he’s so much happier when you’re here. And I really like you.”

“Oh, do you? What did I do to gain this much trust?”

The kid stood there in deep thought. He probably didn’t know either. He was a very young child, after all.

However, it did seem like he had an answer. He was just struggling over how to explain it to him out loud. He just needed a little help, probably.

“Astraea, come here,” Phainon whispered, inviting him into a hug. The child blinked for a second, but he eventually threw himself in his arms, big brown eyes travelling to look up at him. “Is it just because I helped you? It’s fine if it’s because of it.”

He shook his head. “You’re very nice and warm,” he mumbled, lowering his head slightly. “You’re so kind and soft like Mama, and he likes you tons. I wanna believe you have a good heart.”

Phainon forced a tired smile and ran his fingers through his strawberry blonde hair. “Thank you for telling me,” he just said, planting a soft kiss on his forehead. Maybe he shouldn’t have, but it was so hard not to fall in love with this child who kept on reaching out for his heart.

His eyes fell on his hair and eyes, then his face. It was almost scary knowing that he was adopted. He looked identical to Mydei. If anyone told him that he was his biological son, he wouldn’t have even doubted it.

“You really look like Mydei,” he whispered, playing with one of his silver locks. Those were the only things that didn’t scream Mydei, along with his seemingly playful and rather loud personality.

Astraea nodded, excitedly sitting up again as he leaned into his chest. “Mama said we’re similar, too. He said we’re both puppies.”

Puppies? Sure, he was called a big dog sometimes, but he didn’t expect Mydei to say that his own son reminded him of how he acted. Maybe, they just had similar personalities and he simply likened them both to a puppy, but it was tugging at his own heart.

The thought of that child resembling the both of them still felt like a cruel joke and a beautiful blessing at the same time. He wanted it to be real, he meant what he said to Mydei about being his partner, but the longer he realized he still wasn’t, the worse it hurt to wait for the right moment. Ideally, next week’s date. Hopefully.

Phainon was so lost in thinking about that possibility that he almost forgot that Astraea was still a child and, as such, sudden and energetic movements were pretty normal to resort to whenever he wanted to say something.

“And! Look!” he practically yelled, shooting up again. Astraea held his white hair between his fingers, almost offering them to him. Phainon eyed the door for a second to check whether or not that high pitched yell bothered Mydei, but it seemed that it didn’t. Maybe it was something he often did, and… he would have absolutely believed that, honestly.

Turning his eyes back to the child in front of him, he smiled and took in his fingers the hair offered to him. He could honestly see the resemblance and knowing that his father liked him probably made him reach that conclusion. “Is that why you called me Papa?”

“I just wanna see Mama happier more often,” he shook his head, falling on his chest again. “He… he does so much for me, but never does the same for himself. Can you help?”

Could he? He definitely wanted to, but they would have needed time to actually know whether or not he was able to and if Mydei let him.

However, he knew what he wanted to answer and, for once, he spoke his wishes out in the world. “If he will let me… I absolutely want to make Mydei happier every day of my life,” he whispered, his fingers going back to pet the child’s hair.

He heard a slight giggle, but all sounds settled in a matter of seconds. Phainon looked at the child resting on his chest, sleeping soundly. His brows furrowed, almost as if he was studying the slow and rhythmic movements of his breathing.

Just how was this child sleeping?

It was normal for children his age napping throughout the day, but his naps were sporadic, quick, light and he fell asleep so easily on anyone, if he trusted them enough. If he had to guess, he most likely wasn’t sleeping during the night or he got exhausted really fast. Maybe both, given that he was underweight at that age and went through what looked like an extremely traumatic event.

Phainon held him closer for a second, leaving a gentle kiss on the top of his head. Astraea stirred in his sleep and let out a soft whine, holding onto him a little tighter. He could get used to this. He truly did want this to be part of his life, not just because this was Mydei’s son. He was a child that trusted him with everything that he had even after everything that he went through. He wanted to help and protect him too.

Slowly, Phainon repeated in his mind as his eyes grew heavier, maybe you will get to that point. Don’t rush things just because you’re afraid of losing them.

Maybe he should have listened to his brain this time.

The thought of being happy, there, just like that moment warmed his heart so much that he couldn’t help but fall asleep. Still holding that tiny life that leaned on him for survival and joy, he dreamed of warm amber eyes and gentle caresses barely brushing against his skin, along with a childish laughter filling the air. If he could have, he would have replayed that same dream in his head until the end of times.

Chapter End Notes

I'm not used to write in Phainon's POV but hopefully it's good !! And before anyone asks, the messages layout are different in this chapter because Mydei's phone is old as hell, more on that in next chapter ^-^ hope everyone enjoyed this one as well <3
