Mydei let go of another metallic item in his hands, banging against the floor with a loud clang. The third time in the last couple of hours. He honestly was about to go home out of frustration.

Maybe constantly thinking about Phainon wasn't helping at all. He kept feeling the faint frizzle his fingers left around his wrist, a stark reminder of how complicated this has always been. He trusted him, he liked him, he wanted more of this, but he was somewhat scared of being entirely honest with him.

It wasn't a lack of confidence in himself or in Phainon, but the feeling of being in a relationship with someone who wasn't Hephaestion– someone he has known for almost two decades– felt oddly bizarre. He knew he could trust him and he wanted to, he just didn't know just how long he would stick around.

He slept around, many people ended up being infatuated with him, but he knew it was just because of the sex. Mydei was fine with it, that was why he came to them, but he didn't want his relationship with Phainon to end in the same way.

He was probably overthinking it. That guy looked so far gone that he could menace to kill him and he would get turned on instead.

And yet, that light touch still lingered.

Damn you , he cursed, I can't even focus on my job because of you, Phainon. You better take me out on a perfect date just so this won't be lost time .

“Mydeimos!” a voice roared, way too familiar to his ears. He turned nonchalantly, without reacting much to it. Instead, he simply greeted the sight of Gnaeus yelling at him. It wasn't the first time, it won't be the last and he actually deserved it this time. “You don't have your head on your shoulders today,” he observed, after spending way too much time to approach him.

Mydei looked away, but he still acknowledged him. He was his boss, after all. “I apologize. I will–”

“You will do nothing except follow me and do as I say,” Gnaeus thundered, visibly annoyed.

Mydei didn't blame him. If it was annoying for him to keep getting distracted, he guessed it had to be beyond enraging for Gnaeus. He had always had a soft spot for him, but Mydei perfectly knew that he wouldn't escape his rage if he ever didn't pay attention to his work.

He bowed his head without complaining and whispered, “Yes, sir.”

Gnaeus nodded and started walking, not caring whether he followed him or not. Not that he had a choice– if he didn't, he would have been fired.

As he followed him in silence, hands in his pockets fidgeting with a hair tie and his phone’s cover, he gave himself time to be quietly excited about his mother visiting. She stayed where he grew up, while he moved to a slightly bigger city to try out something new. Staying there was starting to feel like a lost opportunity.

Even then, he never forgot his mother. He always messaged her, included her in his life, invited her over, called her in the dead of night. It wasn't a stretch to say that she was the only reason why he didn't go mad yet.

However, she still didn't know about Astraea or Phainon. She often asked him about when he would open up to someone else again, when he would stop isolating himself, when he would find his purpose. Now he was starting to see his future take a new shape, and he wanted to tell her.

“Tell me,” Gnaeus interrupted his thoughts, “how is the child doing?”

Mydei blinked at the question. He knew that he was annoyed and he wasn’t expecting such a personal question. It almost seemed like he was trying to boost his morale. Almost. He knew better than hoping for that.

“You just wanted to chat with me?” he asked, after staring at him for a few seconds.

Gnaeus looked at him with bored eyes. “You can't properly do anything else right now, apparently.”

Mydei was about to say something to excuse himself, but he stopped a second before he uttered even just a sound. He was right. He had his head in the clouds, thinking about the man who slept on his bed the day prior.

More than negative or positive feelings, it was an unsettling feeling in his chest. Almost as if he was anxious about having an interest in the man. Almost as if he was betraying his past feelings for Hephaestion. Even if he was basically pushing him in Phainon’s arms, he couldn’t help but think about the difference of how he felt for him back then and if he didn’t do enough.

Maybe he could have been a better partner. Maybe Hephaestion felt the hesitation in his gestures and suffered on his own, on top of the illness. Maybe Mydei simply felt safe with him around and didn’t properly think about his own feelings as much as he should have.

Did he even love Hephaestion? As soon as he started going out with Phainon, all the hurt over their breakup and the void he carried in his heart suddenly disappeared. He didn’t feel the need to distract himself over anything because he was there. Phainon was constantly in his life. Asking how he was doing, talking about something that happened at work, wondering about what Mydei liked or what he did. His heart was beating again, full of life, as if nothing over the past few years ever happened. 

It was unsettling. Creepy. Shameful.

How could he discard such an important person in his life– one who he had been thinking about for years, to the point of sleeping around with strangers to soothe that pain– the second he met another man he was attracted to? He wished that so many people didn’t care for him as much as they did so they could give him the punishment of a lifetime that he deserved.

Mydei breathed out, letting those feelings linger. It was important to remember them. He shouldn’t push them down. If no one wanted to admit just how horribly he treated his closest friend, he would punish himself. “Astraea is… fine,” he forced his brain to answer, “he's learning to stay at home alone these days.”

Gnaeus sighed, a little more heavily than usual. Mydei wondered if it was annoyance or slight anger about the situation his child was in. “Knowing his parents’ occupation and track record, I thought he would be used to it by now.”

Mydei honestly didn't want to talk about either of those people. He knew what they did and what kind of consequences their choices had on their own child and he refused to think about how alone Astraea must have felt back then.

Selling drugs wasn't something new, plenty of people did it and he could understand those situations, but involving their child in it to the point of getting hurt and scolded over his inefficiency was beyond any possible understanding he could have had for them.

They never cared about his safety. Maybe they were desperate, but the scars on his body and their behaviour when it came to raising him spoke on their own.

He pushed down those emotions instead, letting out a deep sigh. “He’s afraid I will leave him. I can't blame him,” he quickly explained.

“Is that the reason why you're utterly useless today?”

There it was.

Gnaeus might have been a little too honest, but Mydei appreciated the small hint of worry in that sentence.

“... No. I met someone,” he whispered, keeping himself close to him enough that he could hear what he was saying. Mydei felt his eyes on him immediately, but he didn’t turn his head. “Astraea likes him so much. He's handsome, and cute, and interesting. Makes me laugh. Let me feel his pectorals–”

“We’re at work, Mydeimos. It doesn't matter how much I can dote on you, rules apply to you as well,” Gnaeus instantly stopped him out of duty, but Mydei couldn’t help but smile.

“Nothing happened. I just gave him pointers for working out,” he answered calmly.

Gnaeus didn’t comment about it, seemingly letting it slide, but Mydei took the opportunity to think about that last sentence.

Was there even someone in his life who didn’t dote on him? His mother did, Krateros did for some reason, all his friends did and Gnaeus did as well. He didn’t need some kind of princess treatment but, honestly, he never felt anything his boss ever said to him as ‘doting on him’. Most times, it was just insulting him to push him to walk forward.

He wasn’t sure it worked, but it was how Gnaeus was, so he had to accept it.

Regardless, he still asked, “You dote on me?”

“Very,” Gnaeus answered with a sigh. “Do you think I would waste my time talking to anyone in our crew whenever they have a bad day?”

“I’m aware… Did you know Father as well?”

“No. Your mother and I were classmates in high school. When I got to know she had a son, I simply did her a favour.”

Mydei wondered what that meant. He was just his boss, he never was in his life the way that his mother or Krateros were. He was probably still looking out for him because he started out as one of the youngest there, but he never thought that he was overprotective or saw him as a child he had to look after.

His mother wouldn't ask him to do such a thing either.

Gnaeus stopped and leaned against the wall, crossing his arms. His lips curled in a weird way. Maybe it was a smile, but Mydei couldn't tell. “You are skilled and hardworking, it wasn't hard to get attached to you.”

“I haven't been in the past couple of weeks,” he pointed out. He knew that he could have that place at that job specifically for his efficiency and skills, he wasn't naive enough to think that his judgement of him as a worker would be clouded by this supposed request that his mother made. He sighed and asked further, “Will you drop me?”

He looked back at him for a few seconds. Then, a snort came out of his mouth. A snort from Gnaeus. It was something Mydei had to wrap his mind around, honestly. He barely even smiled at anyone, let alone laugh or snort.

“That child took after you,” he finally commented. With an exhausted sigh, he took a step towards him, dark brown eyes darting to his face and threatening to stare at him until he got a satisfying answer. “Are you still feeling guilty for your father's untimely death?”

He did. He knew it didn’t make sense, but he did.

In his eyes, he left because of him. He got hurt, he was unfortunate enough to end up in a coma for months– and the version of his father that he knew and loved died because of him. His mother managed to find him an accommodation and raise her son away from a violent man full of regrets and anger, but Mydei had always felt guilt along with a void in his heart much too similar to feelings of mourning for his father that was still living and breathing somewhere he wasn’t able to see.

He didn’t blame his mother for what she did. It was the necessary step to keep herself and her son safe. More than that, though, he didn’t know how to overcome something like that. He simply didn’t understand what happened and wished for clarity, but the old man left without a trace and died when he was only thirteen years old. Now he was just left with confusion and guilt over something that he didn’t even have a way to solve.

“Shouldn’t I be?” he asked, slightly tilting his head to the side. He truly didn’t think he would ever shake off that feeling. He could push it down and ignore it for a while, but it was always creeping in the back of his mind.

In that way, maybe, he understood Astraea’s fear of the dark. He was pretty sure he saw his father as well after what happened and that was why he didn’t seem to sleep much at night. He had no idea how to comfort him or help him because, much like himself, the person he would have had to reason with was gone forever. 

There was no chance for clarity, or understanding, or speaking his mind on the matter, they were both dead. And they were left with a shattered heart of glass and way too many negative feelings too difficult to navigate.

Maybe that was also why he took him in. Maybe they could understand each other’s feelings and heal together, slowly and steadily. He truly hoped that to be true for both of them.

Gnaeus sighed heavily, maybe noticing just how lost in his mind he was. Mydei didn’t react to the sound, apart from blinking to force himself to look at him again. He knew that it was going to be like that for the rest of the day anyway. 

“You know very well that it wasn’t your fault,” Gnaeus said, right before reaching out to rest a hand on his shoulder. “I won't drop you either. You just had a bad day.”

Mydei nodded, letting it sink in. He debated with himself whether or not he should have told him something that personal. After all, he was his family’s friend, so it couldn’t have been too bad. “It’s hard,” he dropped his head, “I've only ever known Hephaestion. Someone else is getting so close…”

A heavy huff made its way to his ears almost immediately. “You let me in. You let old Krateros in. You let that child in. Why don't you do the same for your pseudo-boyfriend?” Gnaeus asked, taking a step back.

He knew that it was relatively easy. Phainon made it even easier; he genuinely just wanted to spend time with him and be with him as more than just his friend. Mydei still thought he was hiding some of his thoughts, but he had no questions regarding his sincerity about his intentions. 

The day prior made him realize just how much he wanted what he claimed. He had to hold onto his son to simply stand being in the same place as someone who he knew dated Mydei in the past. Phainon was scared that he would have left him to get back with his ex-boyfriend, and Mydei was equally anxious at the prospect of seeing him leave.

He didn’t know why he felt so attached to him, but he felt… good. Spending time with Phainon made him feel whole again. He had fun, he wanted to see him again, he liked talking to him even via messages. He was always there, almost like a lifesaving line after years of drifting from person to person with no feelings for any of them. 

Trying and failing over and over again to overcome his breakup with Hephaestion made him tired of seeing new people in general, opting to wallow in his self pity instead for a long time. Of course, he still hung out with his friends and went to work, but the ugly, dark feelings he felt deep down in his chest were still there. That is, until he started seriously seeing Phainon.

Maybe Hephaestion knew, or at least hoped to see that outcome.

Mydei still didn’t know his stance or feelings about Hephaestion at that point, but he knew that they broke up while Phainon was utterly desperate to be with him. The right choice was crystal clear. He just hoped that one of them would actually ignore that little challenge that they both agreed to like two idiots.

He smiled, and Gnaeus immediately let out another annoyed huff. Mydei turned towards him with a confused expression, only met with bored eyes and a head slightly tilted to the left. “You hold yourself when you're anxious or overwhelmed now,” the older man observed, his eyes travelling to his hand, strongly squeezing the opposing arm. 

Mydei immediately dropped it, but he understood the question. Why do you think that is? Why do you rely only on yourself for comfort now, instead of others? Even in a hard period like the one he was going through, he never confided in anyone. He only relied on himself, unlike a couple of years prior, when his friends or mother knew what was wrong.

He hadn’t fully realized just how much he had changed since then. He had always been reserved, but he never had issues with laying down his feelings. If he believed the people around him had to know them, that is. Maybe he just thought that they simply didn’t and it was better to keep them for himself, coping with pain in other ways.

“Among the promises I made to your mother, she was clear on one thing,” Gnaeus continued, this time laying his hand on the top of his head. “If you see my dear Mydeimos struggle, you must help him. He is a good child, so treat him as you would your own. That was what she said back then, and I’ve always remembered that.”

Is that the promise that he made with his mother? It did sound like something that she would say, but he wondered if this was after his breakup or not. She most likely realized something was wrong, but she didn’t want to invade his space, so she asked Gnaeus to keep an eye out. He knew that his mother knew him like no one else, but it still surprised him at times.

Gnaeus removed his hand from where it was laying, letting Mydei move again. He turned and started walking again, without waiting for him to follow. “Your parents love you, and so do the two useless men that they asked to take care of you. You should give yourself the same grace, Mydeimos.”

Mydei followed him, but didn’t answer his suggestion. Maybe he was right. It wasn’t something he could accept at the moment, though.

His boss evidently wasn’t waiting for one either. “So? How is this person you met?” he asked with a neutral tone.

“His name is Phainon. He's a nurse. He caught Astraea after he ran away from me when I was picking up Hephaestion. He gave me his number.”

“It seems like you enjoy his company very much.”

“... I do.”

Gnaeus stopped and laid a hand on the door’s handle, turning to look at him again. With a monotone voice, he said, “Then, follow what you believe in. All of us will simply support you,” his eyes thinned and his lips pressed together, almost as if he was about to menace him, “but if this Phainon isn't strong enough to deserve you–”

“Yeah, you will destroy him. I know.”

Silly him for thinking any parental or mentor figure in his life wouldn’t go to war for him. He seemed to attract those types of people– or, rather, his parents had the same type of protectiveness. Kindred spirits will tend to flock together, after all.

The older man nodded and opened the door. “There are a few documents you can help me with. Follow me,” he gestured to follow him as he entered the room.

As it turned out, he actually had piles of documents to take care of, to get into the system, to make sure they would be in digital files. Mydei was unsure why he was the one tasked to do such a thing, but he didn't hate that kind of job. It was calm, it required order, it didn't ask him anything other than simply copy words and numbers on a screen. It was almost fun.

His mind kept wandering a few times over to Phainon sleeping peacefully in his bed as he was hugging his child. Mydei wouldn't have minded if that turned out to be a weekly occurrence. Even if it just meant that he would have visited a few more times a week, then he could have been truly happ–

“For you,” Gnaeus suddenly said, right above him.

Mydei looked at him and the phone he was holding out for him for a few seconds before taking it in his hands. He looked at the contact name displayed on screen in visible surprise, spelling simply ‘Gorgo’.

Didn't his phone work anymore? It didn't ring all day, not from Phainon's messages or his mother's calls that he usually got whenever she visited him. He did tell her to come over that day to explain everything about Astraea– he wanted her to know first. He wouldn't have survived a possibility of his sister knowing first and flexing that record holding to him and everyone else.

“Hi, Mother,” he greeted her in the end, his tone barely able to contain his happiness in being able to hear her voice again. They called pretty often, but it was different from living with her. Truthfully, even if he left of his own will, he missed her every single day.

Her deep, soothing voice he had always fallen asleep to didn't let him wait for too long. “Mydeimos, why isn't your phone ringing? You tell me I can come by today, but you won't answer me?”

That was what he was asking himself too. He knew that his phone was embarrassingly old, but he didn't expect it to actually break all of a sudden. His hand dug in his pockets and tried to switch it on, without results. “Wait a second,” he whispered to his mother, still playing with the device in front of him. After another few tries, connecting it to the charger and trying to force it to switch on, he gave up. “It's dead,” he announced with a sigh.

On the other end, Gorgo let out a soft laugh. “You will need a new one.”

“I will go to buy a new one on the way home,” Mydei decided, moving his phone out of the way. With a swift movement, maybe realizing that it was a private call, Gnaeus walked out of the room. He mentally thanked him and confessed, “Mother, I… need to tell you a couple things before you arrive today.”

Silence was what greeted him at first. He knew that his mother didn't like surprises, but he honestly didn't know how else to tell her. She probably wouldn't have had problems after the fact, but, despite how strong and independent she looked, she was still a mother. And, as such, she worried for her child first and foremost.

“I don't like that tone, Mydeimos,” his mother simply said. He heard a worried sigh, then her voice came back. “Are these things that I supposedly don't know about dangerous in any way?”

“No, they're just… big news?”

“Let’s start from the smaller big news, then.”

She was worried. He knew that. However, those were both positive developments in his life and he wanted to reassure her of that much, at least.

Mydei huffed and his muscles relaxed as he smiled thinking about Phainon. He was going to kill him someday. “I’m actively seeing someone else. Going on dates, hanging out, flirting… that kind of endeavours,” he explained, unsure of what reaction he might get.

Silence settled in the room again for a few seconds. Maybe it was normal, after how he spent his time after Hephaestion’s break-up and time in the hospital.

“This is the smaller one?” Gorgo asked, with hesitation clearly audible in her voice. 

Fear and worry again. He couldn't blame her.

“The other one is definitely bigger,” he tried to reassure her, even if he was sure that alone wasn't enough to accomplish such a thing.

“You’re scaring me, Mydeimos.”

“It’s positive. Just a big change.”

Mydei knew that he should have told her earlier– he absolutely knew that letting her know that he adopted a kid after two weeks wasn't the way she would have wanted to know, but there was nothing he could do about it now. It didn't make sense to sulk now on something that he couldn't change.

“I… adopted a child a couple of weeks ago,” he spat out.

Silence greeted him again, used to that being the answer that his mother was adopting all throughout that conversation. Honestly, he would have done the same.

A soft sigh made its way through the phone, followed by her voice whispering, “... Mydeimos.”

“I know, it was impulsive, but… I didn't have the heart to leave him there. He was holding on to me so strongly, he was so tiny and light, he yelled and cried so loudly. I don't think he would have survived social services.”

He didn't even know how many times he explained it by now. That had to be the tenth time during only those two weeks and it would be starting to lose meaning, if those images weren’t still vivid in his mind. Whenever he explained it, he felt his son’s hand on his shirt and heard his first desperate cries ringing in his ears. It was something he doubted he could ever forget.

“Don’t misunderstand, Mydeimos. I'm happy you listened to your gut without overthinking for once,” she instantly interrupted his thoughts. “Are you happy?”

“Mother… he's so cute and tiny. He loves so fiercely. You would adore him.”

“I’m sure that I will. If I ring at your place, will he open up?”

“I’ll call him.”

“Thank you, dear,” she let out a small sigh, her breath slightly shaky. She was probably walking there immediately now. “Listen to Gnaeus at work, he told me you're not having a bright day today.”

Of course he did. Mydei wasn’t surprised, especially since he now knew that Gnaeus and his mother were old friends. Of course, the man she asked to take care of her son notified her that he wasn’t doing too well.

“I will explain later,” he dismissed it, just because they would have had time later anyway.

His mother hummed. “And I will listen. As I've always done.”

“Thank you, Mother. See you soon.”

“Indeed. Have a good day, Mydeimos.”

Mydei switched off the phone, only standing up to open the door and handing it back to his boss. Gnaeus looked at him for a few seconds before taking the phone back in his hands. “How come is your phone not working?” he asked, with a judgemental tone.

“It died,” Mydei explained, “it was just a matter of time, it's almost a decade old.”

Gnaeus sighed in exhaustion. “No wonder I have issues calling you.”

Mydei never really cared about whether or not his phone worked well as long as it was able to call and text, but he understood it could have been slightly harder for others trying to reach him. Regardless, now he needed a new one and he truly didn’t need to spend even more money.

He let out a big sigh, wracking his brain about what he could do. He needed to buy a few more things for Astraea, food, some toys, other books… and now a phone for himself. He wanted to start saving money as soon as possible to get a new place for them to live as well. It was fine for the both of them to live in an apartment meant for one person for now, but he would have grown up. Fast. And buying a decent apartment required a lot of money.

A broken phone wasn’t something he needed to think about now.

As he kept on thinking of some sort of solution without much success, a hand slid right below his eyes. He blinked at the phone in front of him, then looked up to Gnaeus, much too serious to even guess what he was thinking.

“What is this?” he asked.

Gnaeus huffed, mildly annoyed. “Is your sight broken too today?”

“Whose phone is it?”

“I bought it for the stupid son of a dear friend a few years back and never returned it when he refused to replace his stupidly old phone that barely worked.”

He remembered that day. His phone shut down for a few hours and Gnaeus bought and tried to give him a phone, but he refused it and Peucesta somehow restored his old one. Mydei didn’t even know he knew how to fix phones, but he said it was… an interesting experience. Whatever that may mean.

The point was that he didn’t want to accept a phone from his boss– mainly because it wasn’t a light purchase and he didn’t want to be in debt with him even further. He basically gave him his job and was apparently looking after him… that was already more than he wanted to concede.

“You spent money on this,” Mydei observed. He wanted to get him to understand where he was coming from, even if he knew that he wouldn’t have bulged. As far as stubbornness, he was sure that not many people on the planet were able to rival his boss.

All he got in response was a deadly glare. He expected it, so he didn’t even react to it. “I give you your damn salary, Mydeimos. Use this stupid phone to call your son and text your equally stupid boyfriend.”

“He’s not my boyfriend.”

“Pardon, future husband. Get your head out of your ass and work or I will have to keep you here for the entire night.”

Mydei looked at the phone for a few seconds more, before giving up and taking it. He had to think about the money he could spend at that moment. “Yes, sir.”

Gnaeus left him almost instantly to finish what he was working on, while Mydei set up everything for this new phone, since he was directly ordered to. It wasn’t too complicated, it just took a few minutes and he wondered what kind of phone he was holding. Everything was so… updated. Round. A little more colorful.

Although, it didn’t matter what kind of phone he had, because the very first thing he received were, like every single day, Phainon’s alarmed messages.

He still hadn't done that yet, but Mydei was quite fond of it now. Phainon was handsome, it was the first thing that struck him, he was not going to deny it or refuse to look at a picture like that.

Mydei quite liked all the care and thoughts that Phainon willingly reserved for him. He almost wished that the following few days would hurry just to see him again and being able to be looked at by those blue eyes, warm like the sea at night and cold like a breeze on a sunny winter day. They still hid something he couldn’t quite grasp, but it will come out in due time. He was sure of it.

After calling his son and hoping everything would have gone well while his mother was there, he kept on working on whatever Gnaeus gave him. It mostly was just data about their department or transcription of old documents, but it didn’t bore him. He kind of liked it quite a bit, in fact. It reminded him of all the times he had helped Ptolemy and Leonnius write down notes and facts about whatever they were studying.

He was younger, more ignorant about a lot of things, but he had a very comprehensible and clean calligraphy, so he helped them to study from time to time. They were much older and they were often talking about topics he didn’t fully understand, but he absorbed pretty much everything that he wrote down.

Of course, he didn’t follow either of their paths, but he still studied those subjects. Partly, he actually enjoyed them, but they also made him remember those happy times. Doing this for Gnaeus evoked something similar to that and he happily focused on it enough to finish everything on time for the end of his day.

“Thank you again for the phone,” Mydei told him, a second before stepping out of the room.

“Hmph,” Gnaeus turned towards him, “go home and spend time with your mother, Mydeimos.”

He nodded, without adding anything else, and ran home– or well, rode home. He did have a bike he used to head to work, he couldn’t possibly have the energy every single day to make that leap between where he lived and where he worked. 

He was still a little worried about his mother and how he would have found Astraea, but he forced himself to not think about it too much. On his way there, he quickly greeted the owners of the bar next to his place, making a mental note to go there with Astraea some time. Staying in the house for so long wouldn’t have been good for him and he knew that Jing Yuan had been nagging him over letting him see the kid.

One of those days, those people would have forced him to let them babysit him, he was sure of it. He didn’t mind too much, but he only trusted Robin, their main singer and the reason why so many people visited around there. Her brother Sunday, the owner of the bar, was fine at taking care of Jing Yuan’s son, but it was probably because they’ve been dating for the better part of the last five years and he had learned to deal with him as his father’s partner.

Honestly, he was unsure of what Jing Yuan did, apart from hanging around there most of the day, but he was a decently interesting person to talk to, albeit a very peculiar type of annoying at times.

He ignored the way Jing Yuan moved as if to stop him and he sped up, promptly parking his bike and almost jumping off of it to head inside his apartment. Stopping to talk with him was the last thing he wanted to do.

As he unlocked the door, he saw his mother sitting in the living room, calmly sipping a cup of coffee. She smiled with a kind of affection that she only ever had for him and teased, “There was no need to run over here, Mydeimos.”

Mydei didn’t even wait to answer her. With a swift movement, he stepped towards her and almost desperately fell on his knees, laying his head on her lap and hugging her. “I missed you,” he whispered, allowing himself to show his vulnerability after days of feeling like he was about to shatter and fall apart completely.

Gorgo smiled and petted his head, slowly and lovingly. Mydei felt his eyes get heavier and his breath slow down to a peaceful pace, until he allowed himself to rest. 

For the first time since he adopted Astraea, he couldn’t think about a single thing. All he knew was that he was beyond happy to rest in his mother’s lap.

“I missed you too, my dearest child,” she whispered in the warm voice that Mydei had always wanted to hear before going to bed.

He stood in that position for only a few more seconds, before standing up again. He had to force himself, but he knew he couldn’t stay there fuck much longer now. “Did you meet Astraea?”

“Mhm,” she smiled as she gestured towards another chair next to her, “he’s sleeping.”

Mydei nodded and picked up the offer, sitting down. “I need to figure that out.”

“Is it a problem?”

“It’s… he sleeps way too much. I think he doesn’t sleep during the night.”

He was sure that it was something along those lines. Astraea had issues sleeping on his own– specifically during the night– since he took him in, but Mydei didn’t know how to approach the issue.

It was probably related to his parents and he had no idea how to start a conversation about it or how to help him. However, it wasn’t like he could let him keep having such an unstable sleeping schedule either.

His mother slightly tilted her head with a perplexed expression. “You said you rescued him. How did you find him in the first few days?”

Mydei didn’t think he would ever forget the sight of that little child for the first twenty-four hours after he met him.

“Abused, neglected and underweight. Scared of asking for anything. Scared of the dark to unhealthy levels,” he bit his lower lip and lowered his head, before whispering, “I found some bruises and scars on him as well.”

The sheer thought of anyone hurting a child made him tremble with anger. The fact that it was about Astraea just made it worse.

He knew, of course, that some of them were self-inflicted and he was still working on it. He was getting better at recognizing pain as something negative and asked for help sometimes, but he still had a long way to go.

Sometimes he questioned whether or not he would ever be able to help him. Mydei knew how much his own mother tried to, and he still ended up having issues he struggled to solve.

“It’s normal, then,” Gorgo smiled at him, sipping the last drops of her coffee. “Do you remember how scared you were when your father left?”

That was exactly what he was thinking about. His mother sacrificed so much for him and he still had to overcome that betrayal and those hidden pieces of truth behind the white lies that she wanted to keep up to protect him.

He chuckled and nodded towards her, then whispered, “I don’t think it’s something I overcame, honestly.”

“Don’t think he will,” she immediately shut down his every positive thought about the situation. He shyly looked at her and held onto his own arms, bracing himself for whatever words would leave her mouth. “Mydeimos, you’re the first adult that he can trust. He will need a lot of time to unlearn those behaviors and face his fears. You can’t do anything for him except accommodate him and be close to him. This is his fight, you can just offer him love, help and support.”

Mydei just nodded and pressed his lips together for a second. He knew that he was going to see that kid struggle with the baggage he was still carrying, just like he did all his life. He simply wished he could ease it a little for him.

He knew that he wouldn’t be able to lessen much of it right away, but if he could just think of something to help him sleep–

A lightbulb suddenly lit up in his mind. 

He quickly pulled out his phone, quickly scrolling through his contacts until his eyes met Phainon’s name. Surely, a nurse working in a department with traumatized children knew more than him about the matter, right?

“Can I make a call?” he asked his mother, before even standing up.

She nodded and smiled, right before she teased, “Is it to your new boyfriend?”

“He’s not– It’s too early for that.”

“What are you afraid of, Mydeimos?”

He stared at her. Upon hearing those words, he could only stare at her for a few seconds without uttering a sound. 

What was he afraid of? He didn’t know. Not completely, at least.

Mydei could feel that he was uncomfortable and scared, but he wouldn’t be able to pinpoint the reason or the possible solution to his problem. Even when he could sense it, happiness and excitement joined in, creating a mix he wasn’t able to process properly.

So, he didn’t answer. He didn’t have an answer– not a satisfactory one and not a disappointing one. He didn’t know if he was afraid of being abandoned, or if he thought he betrayed Hephaestion, or something else that was escaping his understanding. He simply didn’t know, and he preferred to leave that question in the air, rather than tell a lie to his mother.

Regardless, she knew him terribly well. He doubted there existed someone else who could rival her in that aspect.

As he stood up, he hit the contact he already eyed earlier and waited for his voice to excitedly greet him as he has always done. 

“Mydei! To what do I owe this call?” he answered, voice vivid and bright like a warm summer morning. Mydei's heart almost skipped a beat upon hearing it.

He didn't realize just how much he had missed his cute, excited, sometimes warm voice, but he was longing to hear it again.

“It’s…” he trailed off, thoughts about that voice flooding in his mind. He wondered how it would sound in way too many scenarios– some a little inappropriate– and he forced himself to shut down that trail of thought immediately. “I need an insight from someone like you.”

Maybe that sentence came out horridly wrong. Mydei just hoped that Phainon wouldn’t have taken it as some sort of insult.

“And what is that supposed to mean?” Phainon laughed, apparently amused by the way that question came out. Such a peculiar person.

“A nurse,” Mydei groaned, still frustrated over how he managed to deliver that sentence. “It’s about Astraea.”

Phianon hummed. “Is it about his sleeping schedule or tongue placing issues?”

Of course he would know about both without Mydei ever mentioning either to him. He was observant and he worked with kids from many households, he probably saw his fair share of traumatized children.

“The first one.”

“I have two hypotheses. First, he doesn’t sleep at night and recuperates during the day, but it’s never enough because he needs to sleep at least for ten or twelve hours. Second, he doesn’t have enough strength due to his little weight for his age, but I don’t think he’s that grave of a case right now.”

Mydei nodded, making a mental note of both opinions. “Do you have any ideas?”

“Mydei,” Phainon huffed, “we can’t do anything until we know why he doesn’t sleep.”

We can’t do anything until we know why he doesn’t sleep.

The way he used that word almost made his head spin. He was including himself in the life of his son and, sure, Mydei was the one who decided to ask him for help, but the thought of Phainon being a part of that life at home was making him feel… funny. Weird. Happy.

Astraea loved him, way more than he liked anyone else, and maybe he had made that choice for him already. Sometimes, he wondered what he would say if Phainon moved in with them or started to babysit him. Maybe he would like it.

“Phai is so nice,” he had often said, “when is he coming back?”

And then, there was how easily he fell asleep on him or how much he trusted him. Perhaps, he knew how much they were dancing around each other and he liked the idea of Phainon as a presence in his life. 

After all, he called him ‘papa’ last time. Maybe he truly did know.

“Mydei? Are you still there?”

Right. He was supposed to be talking. Enough fantasizing, Mydeimos.

“I know why, I just can’t do anything about it,” he answered, barely remembering what he last said. If it wasn’t about his son, he was sure he would have forgotten.

“Oh, so you’re giving up?” Phainon teased, his smirk clearly visible in Mydei’s head solely through his voice tone.

“Hmph,” Mydei huffed. He, like always, liked the challenge and the teasing that he offered him every single time, but he wasn’t going to give him the satisfaction. “You’re insufferable.”

Phainon laughed, knowing and oddly amused. “And yet, I was the first one you called. Don’t worry, I have an idea! It might not work, but we can try.”

We can try.

There it was again. He was including himself in whatever regarded Astraea.

It was probably on purpose. He was unsure whether or not he was doing it to flirt or to use his son to get closer to him, but he ignored that second option right away. It wasn’t taking advantage of his affection for his son, if Astraea actually liked him and wanted him to keep coming over. 

And he called him his father. Which was something that Mydei kept on trying and failing to forget.

Mydei bit his tongue. “Why are you involving yourself here?” he asked, as calmly as he could master. 

“Astraea called me Papa, so,” he sighed, before beaming again, “of course I need to help!”

“Right,” Mydei nodded. It felt like he was avoiding the topic, but he didn’t press on further. It wasn’t the right time. “When are you coming by?” he asked, slightly tilting his head.

“In a bit! Is your mother fine with it?”

“Sure, it’s not a problem.”

“Great! See you soon Mydei!”

Mydei heard the quiet beep after Phainon hung up, but he didn’t lower his phone until a few seconds later. He already missed it. His heart was beating slowly, drowning in an unfamiliar warmth spreading through his chest and a fluttering feeling in his stomach.

Somehow, after just two dates he was already long gone for that man. Curse Hephaestion and his knowledge about everything regarding his childhood friend, including his type and his inability to walk away from a bet. Regardless, if they did get together and that relationship lasted, he would have had to thank him personally on every single anniversary.

And curse Phainon for making him even think about celebrating anniversaries with him before they could even hold hands or kiss. He was sure he was going insane.

He finally decided to lower the phone and looked at the black screen, his mind immediately travelling to Phainon saying that he was coming over. He seemed like he was just waiting for Mydei to ask, just like last time. It didn’t matter what he was doing, he would have hopped over there at the slightest request Mydei made.

It was a weird feeling. He was worried for that man’s mental well-being, but Mydei liked being his first priority. He fully bathed himself in that feeling of importance and all those demonstrations of the truth in Phainon’s claims of wanting to be his partner at all costs.

As he walked to the center of the living room again, he tucked his phone in his pocket and turned to his mother. “Phainon is coming here,” he stated, dull and nonchalant.

He truly didn't think much of it. His mother tended to like his friends anyway.

She let out a satisfied laugh. “Is that his name? It’s not bad.”

Mydei almost didn't notice that he never mentioned his name. He talked about him to her and he even expressed some troubles and issues they were having, but he was so busy thinking about him that he forgot to mention that he actually had a name.

He was too far gone. Nothing seemed to lessen that downright obsession he had with the man, especially since last time.

He didn’t know what it was called, but it felt like baby fever for a husband and a father for his son instead. He felt something lacking every minute he wasn't around and extreme happiness whenever he even just talked to him.

What are you, a dog in heat? A wife waiting for her husband to come home every second of the day? Get over this absurd husband fever you have going on .

Absolutely ridiculous. His own thoughts were scolding him now.

He tried to ignore it as his mind visualised the image of Phainon holding Astraea so delicately as they both slept. As if he was so precious that he couldn't press too much on his skin or it would have hurt.

He remembered seeing Astraea snuggle his head against the man's chest and hum in satisfaction as well, almost like that was his rightful place. Playing with him, laying on his chest, laughing on his lap… he desperately wanted to see it more often.

Stupid fucking husband fever or whatever it was called. 

He needed to have him here, playing with his child and talking to Mydei every day, kiss or not. He was so cute and handsome and nice and perfect . He wanted to punch him in the face and kiss him at the same time in every single instance he thought about him.

“He’s a good person,” he explained to his mother, trying to seem as adjusted as possible, “although a little intense and loud…”

“You like it? He’s completely opposite to Hephaestion. Maybe that’s why you like him so much.”

“That’s the problem.”

It was the problem. He liked him too much. He wanted to be with him too much for too long and he was terrified.

The issue was… he knew Hephaestion. He knew how to act, react and behave around him under every single circumstance. 

Phainon, however, was new. It was like the gentle breeze that accompanied the waves at sea during the night. Nice, quiet, pleasing, but intense. Mydei never knew what to expect out of him. Not yet, at least.

How could he love someone so much without knowing him? How could he yearn for something so deeply drowned into the sea of the unknown? How could he even be that desperate to talk to him again when he knew that there was that little voice in the back of his mind fearing for the aftermath?

He knew Phainon would have left. Damn it, he knew he was head over heels for him too and he would have probably punished himself if he would ever hurt Mydei, but… so he thought for his father. So he thought for Hephaestion.

He couldn't shake off that feeling with anyone. He always felt like they could simply leave or never have the tiniest affection for him anymore.

Whereas Phainon seemed to struggle to trust his words about where he stood with Hephaestion, Mydei expected him to leave. So, he constantly braced himself. He tried to stop him when he wanted to leave, because he didn't want to see him walk away from him.

He would have let him walk away if that was what he truly wanted, but he would have stopped him when he could because he liked him. He liked him a lot, and he didn't want him to leave his life just yet.

His mother sighed and smiled at him with a knowing expression. “Mydeimos… you are very easy to love. You’re honest and genuine, and you have no issue showing others that love. But you were hurt a long time ago, and now there is a shattered glass in place of your heart. If you trust him, if you want him to reach out to you… you will have to let him fix that broken piece of glass too.”

Let him fix it… how could they do that when Phainon's own heart was so fragile that the sheer sight of his ex-boyfriend was enough to convince him to leave?

Then, the ache around his wrist came back. It was a slight, little caress, but it hurt like a new burnt spot on his skin.

Phainon grabbed it to ask him to stay that time. He wanted to, he truly did, but he was scared of his own emotions. He was confused, and he needed time on his own to figure them out before indulging in him further.

His child was in the equation, after all. If it wouldn't have ended the way they both wanted, he would have suffered as well. Maybe more than both of them.

Mydei needed to be sure that this wouldn't negatively impact Astraea at any point in the future. At the same time, he wanted to forget about all the responsibilities that came with a little child like Astraea.

He wanted to be with Phainon so desperately that his heart ached with that singular wish. Whenever he thought back to how at ease his child was with him he couldn't help but think that he was born to be his father.

Husband fever may just be a real thing.

Putting his thoughts slightly aside– because no matter what, he couldn't stop thinking about it– he answered his mother. 

“How do I do that?” he asked, a little lost. “The last time he kept touching me and asked me why I liked him… I want it to continue, but his touch is hard to withstand.”

Mydei didn't even know why he liked him. That question was what made him panic. He felt so much towards that man, but he wasn't able to pinpoint why. It wasn't only because of Astraea, that was the only thing he was sure of.

Maybe he had a type, sure, but he had never fallen for someone that quickly. It was very scary. But it was exciting too, and that made it even scarier. 

He thought he would have been with Hephaestion forever… and there he was. Absolutely not in a relationship with Hephaestion and coming from several months of sleeping around with strangers to cope with it.

It couldn't end like that with Phainon. Mydei didn't want to end up like that.

His mother sighed and crossed her arms, catching his attention again. “This is all new for you. It’s normal to be scared,” she pointed out, “but, Mydeimos, if you truly want him as much as you claim… let him in. Don’t make the same mistake twice.”

She was right. He knew she was.

Mydei knew that Phainon wanted him for himself too. He didn't like knowing he had someone else before him. He always shifted uncomfortably when he mentioned it.

Maybe it could work, after all. Maybe he wouldn't have had to brace himself for the impact of another abandonment. Phainon was so crystal clear on the fact that he wanted to know him the best and keep Mydei all for himself that he almost felt that possessiveness and obsession heartwarming.

As he thought of the man holding onto him for dear life when they were talking about it and how much comfort he had to give him over it, there was a knock at the door.

Phainon already.

Mydei smiled tenderly at the door, before moving to open it for him. He was calmer now, less afraid, happy that he actually arrived in record time.

His mother stood up and smiled at him as well. “This Phainon of yours really likes you,” she stated, before shrugging in an affectionate manner. “And it looks like you feel the same.”

Mydei smiled even wider, even more affection filling his heart and reflecting in his every movement. She was right and she was happy about it. He couldn't have asked for a better first impression.

“Mydei!” Phainon beamed as soon as he saw him from behind the door.

Mydei sighed. “Do you really have to yell my name whenever you see me?”

He nodded excitedly, obviously joyful that he could meet up with him again so soon. “I’m happy to see you every time!”

“So this is the man you told me about, Mydeimos.”

Gorgo’s voice made both of them turn towards her, Phainon's head snapping to the side a little more nervously than Mydei's.

He mentioned that he was afraid to meet his family, but he hoped that he would shrug off that fear soon enough while his mother was there. Mydei felt like she already liked him anyway.

“Ma’am,” he greeted her, offering a hand, “I’m Phainon, a friend of Mydei’s.”

She stood up and took his hand, gladly taking the opportunity to know more about him. Mydei was still pondering if that was a good or a bad thing.

“Thank you for being there for him.”

Phainon rubbed the back of his head in an embarrassing motion. “Ah, isn’t that a little overexaggerated?”

Mydei thought so too, but he guessed that his mother assumed that they went on more dates than two after hearing her son talk about him. Unfortunately for everyone involved, they were simply two idiots in love that fell for each other after only a few hours spent together.

His mother, however, didn't have to know that. Letting her believe that her son wasn't that much of a lost cause seemed satisfying enough.

As Phainon was making a fool of himself– and trying to believe that he wasn't– Mydei’s eyes trailed down to the bag he was holding. It was a pretty big linen white bag, with something inside that didn't look too heavy.

He wondered what he bought for Astraea that would help him sleep. He doubted there were meds– despite his playful attitude, he struck him as someone who took his job seriously and respected the rules that came with it. He wouldn't have given unprescribed meds to a child that young.

Mydei's shoulders relaxed instantly after having that thought. He didn't even realize how tense they were up until then, but it turned out that he was more stressed than he initially thought.

“What did you get?” Mydei asked in the end, with a splash of curiosity in his voice that he wished didn't escape his lips.

Phainon smiled brightly, as he always did. “A surprise for Astraea!”

“And I can’t know what it is?”

“You’re not Astraea, are you?”

It always baffled him whenever he acted smug and pretentious. Teasing him with everything that he could, challenging him with that arrogant voice.

Warmth spread again in his chest and Mydei mentally cursed his own body for reacting like that whenever Phainon talked to him. However, he didn't tell him off or commented on it. He liked it, he wasn't going to avoid being truthful to his face just because it was an unfamiliar yet welcomed feeling.

“At least tell me what it is about,” Mydei suggested instead. He was still Astraea's father (mother, at this point?) and he needed to know what he was about to introduce his child to.

Phainon gave him a proud smile. “Just a friend to help him sleep,” he explained, immediately realizing the truce expression on Mydei's face. He immediately smiled, somewhat embarrassed, and put his free hand in front of him, then yelled, “It’s not alive!”

Mydei looked at him for a few seconds with that same expression. Animals were the last thing he needed. 

“Okay,” he conceded in the end, relaxing his muscles once again.

He had a hunch it was a plushie with that little hint, but he didn't say anything. Instead, he let his mother ask questions.

“Phainon, tell me a little about you now that you’re here,” she smiled and sat down again, inviting Phainon to sit beside her on the same chair that Mydei previously occupied. “You have met Mydeimos recently, right?”

He looked at her for a few seconds, then at Mydei, who was busy getting a new seat for himself. Ultimately, he sat down on the spot indicated by the woman with them.

“I work at the local hospital as a nurse and I noticed a lost child a little scared, so I approached him and calmed him down, then Mydei showed up,” he explained calmly, playing with the handle of his bag.

Gorgo turned towards Mydei. “When was this?”

“When they dismissed Hephaestion,” he answered promptly, voice flat and almost bored. “He kind of… set us up.”

Phainon smiled and nodded. “Mydei really didn’t want to have anything to do with me. I think.”

What?

“No,” Mydei answered almost immediately, almost offended.

When did he even imply that he didn't like him? He was mentally fantasizing about his body as soon as he met him– wasn't it obvious? Wasn't that the reason why he wrote down his number?

It almost pissed him off. He understood his difficulty in believing others actually cared about him, but he told him so many times. He thought that he got the message by now. Even when they first met… he never hated him.

What did he think he was, a prisoner to his puppy-like charm and didn't actually like him from the start? That he solely indulged in him because Hephaestion told him to and not because he wanted it?

The only reason why he didn't voice his thoughts was because those affectionate feelings were stronger and his mother’s hand resting on his thigh, effectively stopping him in his steps.

He looked at her for a brief moment, before letting out a huff to slightly calm himself down.

Phainon, on his part, was more cautious than usual. Maybe he noticed the change in Mydei's mood. “No?” he ended up asking, genuinely confused.

It wasn't his intention. He had to calm down and open his mind to clearing that instance of miscommunication. “You seemed interesting,” he sighed, “I just didn’t think I could handle it after having just adopted a child.”

“Oh,” Phainon simply said, before smiling brightly again, as happy as ever. Like a puppy. He hated whenever the image of an overly fluffy white puppy wagging at him appeared in his mind. The man in front of him nodded and added, “Well, I’m glad!”

Again, that lightness in everything that was said to him. He was clearly hurt, but he didn’t even dare to show it. He constantly backed down from his other claims too, making them seem like a one-time boost in confidence.

Mydei couldn’t help but wonder… was the darkness that he kept seeing behind those blue irises just self-hatred? Self-doubt? A belief that he didn’t deserve what he was receiving?

His own hand grazed against his opposite wrist, around where he touched him. He wracked his brain around why he kept on feeling the ghost of a touch that didn’t have to mean anything for the past twenty-four hours and he refused to properly look at himself in the mirror as he searched for an answer.

Instead, he kept on thinking about Phainon over and over again, observing him, trying to understand him– know him, as he did with Hephaestion. Not even a glance to himself. Just like all the past few years, he refused to admit that maybe he had different reactions for reasons that only could lead back to himself.

Mydei let out a shaky, soft breath, curling his hand on that wrist, varying the degree of his strength to mirror which one Phainon used. He shouldn’t have done it at that moment, but he didn’t mind the staring. If he had postponed it, that feeling might have vanished. He could have even had no more courage to look at himself with that degree of honesty.

After a few tries, he found the right amount of pressure and his hand almost snapped away.

He felt his mother’s gaze on him, worried, but she didn’t reach out to him and he was thankful for the lack of that contact. Mydei’s eyes rested on his arm, observing that spot and letting himself feel that same sensation he did the day prior.

A long, heavy breath escaped his lips. “Did you truly think that I hated you?” he asked suddenly, eyes still fixated on his wrist.

He didn’t get a real answer. If he did, he didn’t deem it as important enough to listen to it. The feeling on his skin was the only thing he could focus on. It was gentle, careful, loving.

It hurt so much. 

It stung and burned. It carved itself under his skin, almost like a promise backing up any and every claim Phainon had been doing since they met.

He genuinely cared about him, his touch promptly carried that message, and he demonstrated it to him in many ways. Silly him for not realizing it sooner.

Mydei pressed his lips together, almost biting back whatever it was that he wanted to tell Phainon after that discovery, and raised his head to be greeted with worried, scared blue eyes. 

He could only slightly tilt his head and thinning his eyes, confused, before his mother reminded him, “You don’t notice it, Mydeimos, but you can seem to have a truce expression when you’re anxious even if you’re not mad. The fact that you overthink before reacting doesn’t help either.”

After a second of further confusion, he suddenly found his mother’s finger near his face, pointing at it. He slightly jerked his head back, blinking more than he should have.

“Right there,” she whispered, before turning to Phainon. “Was that the same expression?”

Phainon looked at him with a perplexed face, then nodded slowly. “Kind of, yeah... Now that I know that’s what it means, though, it’s cute!”

Of course he did. He found him cute way too often.

Mydei ignored him, instead turning towards his mother. “Mother…”

“I’m just here to help with explaining some things, Mydeimos. Cheer up, yet another misunderstanding is now cleared,” she happily chirped, straightening her back and smiling in front of her.

That was how it had always been. Mydei lost himself in the depths of his mind and his mother sustained and supported him throughout it all. He knew that he could focus on some things a little too much and he could be awkward at times, but he wasn’t ashamed of it. He didn’t care if others stared either, he was used to it. However, he was happy that he didn’t have to explain himself and his mother didn’t encourage him to either, if he didn’t want to.

His mother took a few looks at the both of them, until her eyes landed on Phainon. “You do know some things about each other, am I right?”

“We only hung out two times, and half of the last one was spent forcing him to sleep,” Mydei answered instead, with a flat tone again. That exercise of looking into himself after such a long day left him quite spent.

“Ah,” she breathed out, “so that’s why you knew what Astraea might have needed.”

Phainon nodded, his eyes a little hesitant. “I was just–”

“I highly suggest you tell the truth.”

Mydei didn’t even react to that sentence. That was how he was raised– to value honesty and loyalty. Above all, he knew how much his mother’s voice could shift and how much fear it could incite in one’s body and mind. This was simply one of those times, and Phainon’s first taste of it.

His eyes travelled to the white-haired man in front of him. All considered, he looked more embarrassed than uncomfortable. “Uh… I was…” he started, before looking to the side. Mydei didn’t judge his behavior right away, and he was satisfied when he heard Phainon lightly whisper, “Feeling a little down over not seeing Mydei that week…”

A tiny smile made its way on Mydei’s face. He didn't know why he didn't figure it out earlier. Despite being someone with so many dichotomies, one thing seemed clear– he liked him. His every decision seemed to weigh on that simple fact.

He let out a quiet, calm breath. His chest felt lighter and his mind clearer. In the past few weeks he was unsure about whether accepting those advances or not, but the answer seemed obvious now.

He had been thinking about him more than anyone else. He couldn't focus on his job because of him. He wanted to see him again. He liked him. Astraea loved him. There wasn't a single logical reason why he would refuse his requests.

“How come?” his mother's voice resounded in his mind, bringing him back to reality once again.

As Mydei turned towards Phainon, he noticed just how anxious he was in that position. He looked like a kid hiding candies who just got busted by an adult.

For some reason, warmth spread in his chest yet again.

“I was just excited to hang out with him, but he cancelled at the last second,” Phainon explained. “I understand why, I’m not mad at him! But, uh… I guess it was some kind of let down at first…”

How cute.

He explained the reason and it looked like Phainon had accepted it at the time– but apparently he didn't. Or, well, he pretended he was fine with it when he had such a strong reaction to it.

Mydei wished that Phainon could stop thinking his feelings weren't important.

Looking at him, he realized that he took it way more harshly than he had ever intended to. He wanted to lessen the weight that he partly gave him.

“Was that why Castorice called me?” he asked, voice calm and warm. He smiled as soon as he saw his eyes land on him and suggested, “Next time, just ask if I’m free and come over.”

Phainon blinked. “What?”

“I told you already, I like spending time with you.”

“I… Me too. We'll see each other more often, Mydei.”

With a calm, content smile, Mydei walked over to him and patted his hair slowly, as if he was complementing a dog. All of it was messy afterwards, but Phainon didn't seem to care.

Instead, he looked up at Mydei as if he was a God to be revered and served with no exception. Only he looked at him with those eyes, clear blue and shining with adoration.

Unlike the other few times he saw him in that perspective, though, he dropped his head all of a sudden and tensed his shoulders. Mydei took a step backwards, giving him space. He had no idea what he needed or if he had to say something of importance to him, given what looked like a change in his mood.

Regardless, he waited until he felt ready to speak, his eyes– soft and patient, just for that occasion– never leaving his figure.

Phainon let out a heavy sigh after only a few seconds. “Now that we’re on the subject… I kind of… lied to you last time.”

Mydei stilled for a moment. Of everything he expected, an admission like that right away wasn’t in the options he listed in his head. He didn’t strike him as someone who lied often and when he did, they would have all been innocent white lies. If he felt the need to come clean… he wondered if it was something bigger or if he just felt guilty for a little, selfish lie.

“About what?” Mydei asked, as calmly as he could. 

“I know how to cook,” Phainon answered, eyes darting immediately to Mydei. He gestured with his hands without giving it a real meaning and whined, “Don’t get mad! I just wanted to see you work!”

A soft laugh escaped Mydei’s lips. That was what he was worried about? That he omitted the fact that he could cook enough to survive just to see him cook a few times and eat his food? He looked so anxious about simply telling him that he knew how to cook, as if he did something unforgivable.

As he looked back to Phainon, he found him staring with wide, worried eyes, unsure of what he should have said. Mydei let out another laugh, quicker this time, before he answered, “It’s not a problem. Next time you’re cooking and I’ll rate it.”

It seemed fair. Phainon already ate his food a couple of times now, it was time to do the contrary.

Phainon gave him an apologetic smile, some of the brightness returning back to his eyes as the anxiety and fear dissipated. “Is this a challenge?”

“Absolutely.”

“I will absolutely beat you, then.”

“You wish.”

Mydei felt a kick of excitement in the back of his mind. Those stupid, insignificant challenges turning into a matter of life or death for both, unable to turn away from those declarations, were what made him obsessed with the man. Unlike anyone else, he was proudly engaging in those challenges over and over again– both times that Mydei proposed one, he accepted it and moved to win said challenge, no matter if he liked it or not.

“Please, lose.”

That was what he told him last time. He wanted to win desperately, but he wanted that kiss that they both agreed to keep hostage just as much. Admittedly, it was a foolish decision, but they were both having fun with it and neither of them wanted to back down.

And Mydei was sure that when one of them finally yielded, that kiss would have felt much, much better than it would have felt if they didn’t decide to indulge in that challenge. He was afraid the same would have gone for Phainon’s food.

“How about Astraea rates it?” Phainon suggested. He was grinning at him, probably excited about that new challenge. “He likes us both, he will be more of a neutral judge.”

It didn’t seem so neutral, since Astraea quite literally refused to eat much outside. He liked Mydei’s food so much that he wanted it to be the only food he ate. Phainon, however, didn’t know that and didn’t need to know that.

Mydei smirked right back at him and crossed his arm, sure of his victory already. “Fine by me. I’m his favourite anyway.”

“We’ll see,” Phainon bit back, without looking away from his face and never softening that air of security and challenge only for him.

As Mydei was about to answer him again, his mother anticipated him with a loud, excited laugh that he had hardly heard coming from her. “Good job, Mydeimos! I like this one.”

Phainon was the first to look at her, confused and utterly lost. Mydei just smiled at him, almost proud of how that evening had turned out.

“You wanted my mother’s acceptance,” he calmly stated. “You got it, congratulations.”

Gorgo slightly tilted her head and turned to Phainon. “Was it something that you truly wanted?”

Phainon laughed awkwardly, obviously embarrassed about it. Mydei immediately thought that it was a cute habit he had. “Well, the way Mydei was talking about his family was a little scary…”

“Mydeimos,” his mother instantly scolded him, “we don’t do that anymore.”

Mydei shrugged and puffed one of his cheeks, as he tilted his head and looked towards the ceiling. “I’m pretty sure Krateros would break his bones if given the chance,” he stated, knowing for a fact that he was right.

His mother huffed, recognizing that truth. “I will talk to him later,” she stated, before turning to Phainon again. “Feel free to take out Mydeimos, Phainon.”

Mydei turned towards him too, waiting for his reaction. He knew how badly he wanted his mother’s approval over what he was doing, but neither of them stated this same intention, nor that they were dating. Not so openly and earnestly as his mother just did, at least.

“Ah, uh… take out?” Phainon asked, a little thrown aback. He wasn’t used to the grade of earnest honesty that Mydei’s family seemed to have, but he probably would get the hang of it soon enough. 

Mydei’s mother turned towards her son, with a curious expression. “Did I misunderstand? Are you not dating, Mydeimos?”

“We are,” he confirmed, then glanced at Phainon for a second. He barely saw the temporary flicker of light in his irises, but he didn’t acknowledge him further. Turning to his mother, he added, “We’re going out in a few days.”

Phainon’s eyes were still on Mydei, hopeful and dreamy. He could feel that he was waiting for that confirmation from him, even if it was obvious they were going on dates. Perhaps, he was afraid that he was the only one who took them as such, somehow.

He seemed to be a stubborn type. Even if Mydei repeated it to him over and over again, he still didn't believe him. Then, he had to be more persistent. 

His mother's warm laugh resounded in the room, slowing to a stop all his thoughts on the matter. She laid her hands on her knees, smiling at both. “Have fun, both of you.”

Mydei smiled, feeling that warmth in his chest again. This time, it was simply because he was glad that his mother approved of Phainon and cheered them on immediately. He could indulge in his feelings without further worries now.

“Mama?”

That sleepy little voice caught Mydei's attention, his body already moving on his own to step closer to his child. It was something that he barely noticed, but it came like a second nature to him now. He barely talked to anyone besides Phainon, Gnaeus and his mother since he adopted Astraea that he started to become almost the only thing he thought about.

The little child naturally ended in his arms, snuggling against his chest, as Mydei picked him up. “Hey,” he whispered, then kissed him on one side of his head. Astraea weakly whined, slightly throwing his head back to try and look at him, but he couldn't even keep his eyes open. Mydei laughed softly and hugged him until he rested his head on his shoulders. “Good morning, stardust.”

He felt him yawn as he rocked him in his arms. He largely preferred it if he slept a little more if he was so tired, even if Phainon claimed to know how to make him sleep. If his strategy worked, he could have recuperated all sleep that night, at least.

Astraea whined and Mydei felt his head raise for a split second. Then, his arm reached out behind him and a quiet plea came out of his lips, tiny and weak. “Phai…”

Mydei smiled as his muscles relaxed and his son reached out for his… pseudo-boyfriend , as Gnaeus said. It was a pretty fitting label to whatever they had right now.

He heard a few steps behind him approaching him, until he felt Phainon's presence dangerously close to his back. He could almost feel his breath on his neck. In a matter of seconds, he felt his white hair brushing on his jaw and he turned to see him lovingly kissing Astraea on the top of his head.

Then, blue eyes looked at him with a knowing stare. 

Knowing? No, that didn't seem like the correct description. They were almost pleading, but they felt sharp and seemed to shoot another challenge to him. However, they only lasted a moment, and Mydei was left wondering if he just imagined it.

He most definitely didn't. He just didn't know what it meant.

Normally, he would have thought about it until he figured it out– but, in that moment, he decided to instantly let it go. 

This didn't work with Phainon. He would have told him eventually, after all. That thought simmered in his mind, convincing him that it was the best course of action for now.

His mother told him to stop overthinking so many times as well. Maybe it was time to put that suggestion into fruition.

“Hey, honeybuns,” Phainon whispered from behind him, his hand reaching out to ruffle the child's hair. “Have you slept well?”

The kid weakly nodded, reaching out a hand to hold onto his sleeve and the other to curl around Mydei's shirt.

Mydei smiled, thinking back to how much he wracked his head around whether or not he wanted Phainon to get into both of their lives. It truly didn't matter. Astraea wanted both of them, there was no reason to worry so much over his safety now that he knew him slightly better.

Astraea hummed a pleased sound, almost as if he was in the best place he could possibly find himself in.

“Phai brought something for you,” Mydei whispered, trying to keep him awake enough to get that gift so that Phainon could leave.

He didn't want him to, but he knew that he had other things to do. He didn't like to admit it, but he has responsibilities outside of them. Mydei still didn't know if he liked it or not.

Astraea’s head slowly rose up, sleepily looking at Phainon. He smiled before he showed him his bag, and stated, “A gift to help you sleep.”

Those words helped to wake him up a little bit further. Not too much, but he was able to form coherent words and put them into sentences with a logical sense, at least.

The child looked at Mydei and tilted his head, a little shyly. “Is it fine?” he asked, almost like a plea.

He wasn't used to gifts, Mydei knew that well, but he was relieved that now there was at least that wishful spark in his eyes.

Can I accept it, Mama? Can I open it, please?

They kept on saying that, over and over again, and Mydei was just unable to tell him no.

“Of course,” he conceded in the end, letting him off from his arms as Phainon gave him a wrapped gift. It wasn't too big and it wasn't solid at all.

Mydei said already that it would have been a plushie, but he was still shocked he had never thought about it. Maybe it was because Hephaestion often slept at their house and his mother was more than willing to let him sleep with her when he needed it, so he had never owned a plushie for that reason.

Astraea turned around his gift, calmly searching for the seal as he squeezed it to try and guess what it was. Mydei never expected him to tear it apart, but it was endearing how much he cared about the integrity of the paper.

As soon as he found the tape, he slowly and quietly thought about how to open it, trying a few times before reaching a solution. He smiled and bounced on his place as he opened it and looked inside, jerking his head towards Mydei as soon as he got the slightest peek at the present.

Mydei smiled and crouched down, slightly caressing his hair. “Do you like it?”

Astraea raised his head to look at him, almost bending it backwards, as he opened his mouth to let out an excited giggle. Then, he nodded happily and took out the plushie and hugged him close to his chest.

It seemed to be a cat of some sorts– maybe a feline– and Astraea buried his face into it, as if that was his last anchor to life.

Mydei pressed his lips together, thinking for a second about the possibility that he didn't understand what he needed so desperately. He was alone, he felt lonely, he had no other kids to play with and, even if he didn't seem to mind being at home, he needed to go out more often. Meet other kids. Socialize. Play in a bigger place. Be given the means to be a happy child past just staying with his parent.

His heart clenched for a second, but he didn't have the time to think about how big his limitations were before another voice resounded in the room.

“You can keep it for when you sleep,” Phainon suggested to him, kneeling in front of the child. Upon those words, Astraea finally looked up and Phainon added, “Think about a name first, it’s going to stay here for a loooong time.”

He wasn't wrong. Even if he eventually would have gotten more plushies if he so desired, they weren't going to throw away that one. And it could have been useful to lessen that sense of loneliness that he had to carry.

Slowly, Astraea stood up, still with that plushie close to his chest, and turned to Mydei.

“Mama, pen?” he asked, with an hesitant voice. He seemed unsure about that decision, but he didn't back down from it. 

That was already a good sign. He probably liked the plushie and the idea of it staying in his life for a good while.

Mydei smiled and stood up, walking away for a few seconds to grab a few of his child's books, some sheets and a pencil. He had started to copy some letters of the words that he liked, so he guessed that was what he wanted to do to name it.

“Pen, book and sheets,” he crouched again, handing it all to him. “Go on.”

Astraea looked at the object for a second, trying to figure out how he could bring everything to his room. He looked at the plushie and puffed his cheeks in frustration, burying his head in it again.

“Astraea,” Mydei called out, soft and loving, “do you remember when we talked about little steps? That you don't have to do everything immediately?”

He nodded slowly, chin still resting on the soft fur of the toy in his hands. Mydei gave him all the time he needed to figure out what he had to do in that situation. He wanted to fully understand that statement and how useful it was going to be for the rest of his life.

Just after a few seconds, the child squeezed the plushie in his arms and nodded excitedly, seemingly having found a solution.

He ran to his room, left his gift on his bed and ran right back, ready to take what Mydei was still holding for him.

“Thank you, Mama,” he squealed, happy and joyful again. He walked a little closer to give him a quick hug and ran off again, excitedly starting to work on the ground of his room.

All three adults looked at him with a fond expression for a few seconds, until one of them spoke up.

“He was so happy,” Phainon smiled, looking in his general direction.

Mydei’s eyes softened as he looked at the man, once again feeling that warm, kind embrace in his chest. Part of his initial worry was that Phainon got close to Astraea to flirt with him instead, or to use him to get closer to him, but it was safe to say that it wasn't the case now.

He could see how much he genuinely loved and cared for him, and it was completely separate from what he felt for Mydei.

With a smile, Mydei stood up again. “He still is. Don’t underestimate your own gesture.”

Phainon turned to look at him, a little surprised by that sentence. Maybe Mydei  had never thanked him for helping him since they started hanging out, but he meant every word.

He was glad that Astraea trusted someone else and he was beyond happy that it was Phainon.

Not too much time passed, though, that Phainon already took a step back. Avoiding being too involved after expressingly wishing to be included in his life. Again.

“Ah, I have to go back! I promised I’d help Castorice with a few things,” he explained, excusing himself. He turned towards Mydei and smiled at him. “See you soon, Mydei, Ma’am! Say bye to Astraea for me too.”

And off he went. Not even waiting for him to say goodbye.

He was so scared and he didn't know how he could convince him to stay longer, look at him without backing down or avoid running away when he realized he got too close.

In his foolishness, he tried to run after him right then, but his mother stopped him. She held him by his shoulder and he stopped right in his tracks almost by habit.

“Give him some space too, Mydeimos,” she suggested, trying to knock some sense into him.

Mydei didn’t turn and only looked at the empty hallway for a few seconds. He heard his mother and he agreed with her, but it hurt. Seeing him so cheerful and happy to be there and witnessing how scared he was to simply be cared for in a matter of a few seconds hurt him .

He hoped he would accept his help or lean on his shoulder, at some point.
