It was something his mother repeated over and over again. You won’t be able to always solve a situation, Mydeimos. Sometimes, the most you can do is be present and be patient until the right moment.

After all, that was all he could do at the moment. Both for Astraea, Phainon and himself as well. Wait and observe, and offer help when truly needed.

In the end, they would have figured it out. He saw the desire in Phainon’s eyes and he believed in the feelings that he laid out to both him and Astraea. There was no reason to fear rejection or abandonment.

Mydei had the feeling that this would have been… different, somehow. He already felt so much that he wasn’t used to or never felt and he was excited. He wanted to indulge him further, see his stupidly annoying texts again, hear his voice and hang out with him once more.

He took a deep breath and turned towards his mother, his mind still on that last thought. “It’s late, Mother,” he stated, “do you mind helping me with dinner?”

“Of course not, Mydeimos,” she smiled, letting him go. “Do lead the way.”

Mydei nodded and he just focused on the food he had to prepare. His mind occasionally travelled to Phainon and their next date, but he wasn’t worried or anxious anymore. He was just excited at the prospect of seeing him again. Maybe holding his hand. If that kiss happened… they would have dealt with it. 

The quiet sizzling on his wrist still stinged, but he wanted to keep feeling it. It still hurt and slightly burned, but it was so warm that he was willing to withstand it. He even hoped to feel it again. He hoped that Phainon would still touch him as he did a day prior– gently and demanding at the same time– until he no longer felt pain.

It was just a faint wish, but it was one that he believed was achievable with him. Maybe it was childish, but he allowed himself to hope for a future with Phainon in it.

For the first time in a long time, he wanted to reach out to someone else so earnestly and desperately, and not even that stubborn refusal of that man to step too close to him would have taken it away from him.

Chapter End Notes

I just wanted to give some insight into Mydei's mind and family/workplace before the actual date, i hope this was enjoyable as well !!

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

"What?" Phainon asked, a little anxious.
“What, what?” Mydei huffed, maybe a little annoyed, then turned back to him. “Do you think I would be here if I wasn't interested in you? I told you how many times already? If I didn't want anything to do with you, I would have said so.”

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Phainon honestly didn't believe that day seemed like any other. He went to work, rested at home, playfully discussed with Hyacine while Castorice wrote right beside them and left home in the evening. Like any other Saturday, if he didn't count the place he was heading towards. 

And yet, there he was– standing by Mydei's door while he was talking to Astraea. He was dressed casually, but there was an elegant air about him no matter what he did or wore. Maybe it was simply because he liked him more than should be possible after just a few weeks, but Mydei always looked like a prince walking among the masses, failing miserably to merge in with them.

He always shined of pure gold and carried himself with such nobility that Phainon had no better way to describe him if not a prince. Maybe even a princess sometimes.

“Be a good boy, alright? Listen to Ptolemy, we will be back soon,” Mydei reassured Astraea further. The child held the plushie that he was gifted a few days ago still close to his chest, occasionally squeezing it closer.

Knowing that something that Phainon gifted him was so important to him warmed his heart a little more. 

“Okay,” Astraea mumbled, his voice stuffed by the plushie he was keeping against his lips. He turned to look at Mydei again and smiled, almost to push himself to be more energetic. “Have fun!”

Phainon smiled at the attempt right as Mydei caressed his head to thank him for his courage. He looked behind them, at the man with them. Ptolemy, was it? He never heard of him, but he looked like a pretty polite and adjusted guy. He had short, ashy blonde hair and a gentle smile, along with an attire that he would have expected from a professor right out of the 1800s. Even by dressing like that, though, his muscles were clearly visible.

Were Mydei's friends all rather... toned? He remembered getting a glance at Hephaestion's figure– although regrettably– and despite how slim he was, he had some muscles as well. Was it something that he valued? Or did he develop his body after some of his friends did?

He honestly didn't think that someone like him would put too much weight on it, since all of his friend's body types were different. Phainon himself had broader shoulders than Ptolemy or Hephaestion himself, and Mydei still liked him enough to keep on going on dates with him.

Mydei gave a last smile to Astraea and waved at his friend before turning towards Phainon and closing the door of his apartment behind him. “What are you looking at?” he asked, slightly tilting his head on the side.

Ah, he didn't notice that he was staring.

“Who was he?” he asked, out of curiosity. He wasn't jealous, really, he believed Mydei's words about his feelings for him, and he knew that the only person he was ever interested in before him was Hephaestion.

Very simply, he just wanted to know him and his friends better.

Mydei huffed as he stepped down the stairs. “A friend. He has absolutely no feelings for me and he's a decade older than me,” he explained, before turning towards him. He looked so beautiful, touched by the last, weak ray of sunlight that day, that Phainon didn't even mind the rather annoyed eyes he was using. “I met him when I was thirteen and he was twenty-five.”

Admittedly, he didn't expect him to be so much older than him. Not because he was friends with Mydei specifically– he just looked way closer to their age. Phainon made a mental note of asking him whether he found an immortality elixir or if his skincare was just really effective.

“In what kind of circumstances did you even meet him?” Phainon asked, following him out of the building.

“He was a street artist,” Mydei answered. He put his hands in his pockets and waited for him a little longer, until Phainon could lead the way for both of them. Then, he kept narrating, “My mother often talked to him and gave him money, then I learned that he just wanted to work in a library. So, we suggested him to a bookstore, they took him and he started studying to become a proper librarian.”

He didn't expect anything less from them. Mydei and his mother both seemed selfless people who would help people if they needed it– and very accepting of anyone too, no matter how different from them they were. Meeting people so different and from different backgrounds probably made him into who he was now.

“It was very kind of you two.”

“He just reminded her of my father. Now he's completely different, but only because we were able to help him.”

“Is that how you met all your friends?”

Mydei shook his head. “Hephaestion was a neighbour. We have hung out since we were kids, while Leonnius, Peucesta and Perdikkas were people that Ptolemy met on campus. So, they're all around his age,” he explained, with a neutral tone. Maybe he was trying to hide his affections out of care for him. Phainon didn't know if he appreciated or hated it.

He didn't mention it.

Not the time for your baseless doubts, Phainon! Focus on the guy who has been on your mind since you met him.

Phainon took a moment to exhale and put his heart at ease again, focusing on what was going on around him. He knew that Mydei would have noticed it, so he had to keep ignoring those thoughts, no matter how loud they got.

He turned towards him, just then noticing that Mydei was already staring. Phainon tilted his head slightly as he kept that stare, curious and much calmer than a few seconds prior. “Have you always been the youngest for everyone?”

It was something that he barely noticed, but he looked younger sometimes. It was subtle, like the curves of his face or the way he ate. He was taken care of by so many people in his life. His mother, his friends, his sister, his boss… Everyone was older than him and everyone cared for him and protected him in different ways. After all, it was stupidly easy to love and get attached to him.

“Pretty much. My sister calls me ‘little lion', even if I never fit that adjective,” Mydei sighed, unsure whether it was a good or bad thing himself.

Luckily, Phainon had enough love for whatever Mydei didn't love or doubted about himself.

“It’s cute!” he beamed, brightly smiling at him. Of course, he genuinely found him cute because of that as well, but there were a million other reasons. Mydei was so incredibly adorable in so many instances, without even trying.

Mydei just huffed at that comment. “Of course you would think that.”

Phainon pouted in displeasure after hearing what he thought about it. He knew he probably didn't necessarily think of himself as cute, but it bothered him. Who and what made him think he wasn't? He's being pampered and babied by everyone in his life, it should have been hammered into his brain since he was a child.

Maybe he just didn't like it? He hoped that was all there was to it. Any other option made him a little too uncomfortable for his own sanity.

“You’re very cute, Mydei,” Phainon repeated, with a smile plastered all over his face. He sighed, then added, “And I'm sure Astraea would agree with me!”

Mydei sighed, almost annoyed. “Stop using my son to your advantage.”

Phainon gasped dramatically as he rested a hand on his chest and yelled, “I would never do that!”

He didn't expect to have much of a reaction out of him, it was just something stupid that he thought was funny, until he heard it. A tiny, warm laugh escaped Mydei's lips, more akin to a breath than anything else– and yet, it was still one of the most beautiful sounds that Phainon will ever hear in his life.

A smile appeared on his face too, relaxed and content, one that Phainon had yet to discover. Right at that moment, he wished to touch his face, feel every single one of his features, brush his own thumb over Mydei's lips… but life had other plans.

Mydei sighed, and it all disappeared. The warmth was still there, as always, but the brightness and sheer happiness that those rare moments carried with them was unparalleled, and now it only lingered in the air between them.

“Where are we going anyway?” Mydei asked, tucking his hands in the pockets of his jacket. He looked around him, maybe trying to guess, Phainon still hoping that he didn’t have a clue. Then, he turned around and pointed out, “You refused to tell me anything about tonight.”

Phainon smiled and beamed, “Because it's a surprise! But I think you'll like it.”

“We’ll see,” he answered, with a somewhat hesitant tone. He wasn’t upset or anxious, he probably just faintly wondered what it could have been. He was relaxed, maybe a little hesitant, but content about the situation.

Smiling again, Phainon slowed to a stop in front of a gate by the side of the road. “We’re here,” he announced, then pointed at a black plate on their right. There was just the name of the place, along with the name of a girl underneath it. He noticed Mydei’s slightly confused expression and explained, “It's a park built in the name of a young girl who killed herself. Her parents worked on it for years, and came up with this. It's similar to a forest in the middle of the city, they hold concerts and food stalls, and they also have a corner for children to play.”

Mydei’s eyes shone for a second and he looked inside, observing the place however he could. He definitely wasn’t familiar with it even if it was rather close to his place, but he evidently liked it.

Phainon leaned in closer, tilting his head to take a proper look at his face. “Do you like it?”

“Yeah,” Mydei breathed out, not even trying to hide his feelings. He then looked at him and smiled earnestly and whispered, “You did surprise me.”

Somehow, Phainon’s smile grew even wider. Hearing so much praise and wonder coming from him made something to his brain. He physically felt a switch turning in his head, almost like that comment alone made him discover something that he didn’t know he even liked.

There was no time to think about that more, though. He liked it and he wanted to hear those praises again, sure, but nothing was able to even rival the excitement he had felt in the hours prior to this date. If they didn’t start right away, he was sure he was going to go insane.

“Come!” he beamed as he grabbed his wrist, dragging him along. He felt Mydei’s muscles tense for a second, but he relaxed soon enough. Phainon smiled and pointed at the stage in front of them and said, “I think there's going to be a rock band tonight.”

Mydei looked in that direction, then at his surroundings. Phainon saw his eyes travel from the band, to the tables with a few people sitting down there already, then to the food stands to the side. Everything was pretty calm even if there were quite a few people, probably for the chill atmosphere immersed in that corner of green around them instead of the usual urban elements they were so used to.

“I really like it,” he whispered, eyes still full of wonder like the ones of a little child. Phainon immediately thought they were similar to Astraea, even if they weren’t blood related. The child was already so similar to him that it felt wrong to think of them as anything but parent and son. They had been living under the same roof for less than a month, and yet that view didn’t bulge. Astraea was his son in every possible way, so resembling each other’s reactions was only natural.

Phainon smiled in pleasure, looking at him with fond eyes. “I’m glad, Mydei!”

He turned towards him for a second and looked at him, stone faced, without saying anything. Phainon waited, maybe because he noticed that he often just talked when he thought was necessary, but he never got any kind of response, comment or question coming from him. Instead, Mydei grabbed his wrist and walked towards the food stalls to order something to eat for the both of them.

On his part, Phainon stared at him as he quickly kept up the pace with him, just as silent. He stared at his back, the black and red shirt he decided to wear delicately wrapping around his incredibly broad shoulders, and the way his black jeans hugged his much tinier waist… How could he have that kind of body? His thighs were so big and his pectorals were hilariously soft as well… 

His mind wandered about those thoughts for only a second, but that was enough for him to completely lose his sense of direction and space around him. His eyes were on Mydei, following him wherever he went, and his mind was fully focused on his body, the memory of touching his chest still awfully fresh in his mind.

He hoped to the sky for a second that it could happen again, sooner or later.

“Phainon.”

A stern voice broke his thoughts and Phainon raised his head to see a pair of suns looking at him. He blinked, finally snapping himself out of his own very inappropriate thoughts, even if the fingers resting on his wrist were, indeed, ever-present and a stark reminder of how far he had fallen.

Regardless, he tried not to show it too much. “I apologize!” he beamed, right before placing his order. It was a little embarrassing, but he didn’t feel that burden too much due to Mydei looking at him with worried eyes, instead of judgemental ones.

Even if he didn’t say anything, that was plenty enough. It made him feel a little guilty since he was fantasizing about his body so intensely that it worried him, but it was better than being judged. He would have explained too, if he asked– even if he preferred it if he didn’t.

They calmly got their food and drinks and proceeded to sit at one of the tables, Mydei refusing to say a single word. Instead, he looked at the band and listened to the music, which apparently was very much his taste. Phainon was glad that he liked it, at least.

His focused expression was so cute, no matter how Phainon tried to look at it. Knitted eyebrows, eyes fixated on a singular point of the space around them, pouty lips. Everything individually was so cute, but everything at the same time was so cute that he was losing his mind over it. In silence, of course. He wouldn’t have dared to bother him and interrupt that moment.

Mydei, however, noticed when they sat down and turned his head towards him once again. “What are you looking at?” he asked, sounding a little upset.

Maybe that was one of those instances that his mother mentioned, Phainon thought. It was better not to take offense or judge him, lest it to lead to misunderstandings like the last time.

“You look way more relaxed!” Phainon smiled, his eyes tenderly staying on his figure. “And you're so much prettier as a consequence.”

It came a huff in response, maybe in agreement. It was hard to understand its meaning, given how many he used, under any circumstance. Maybe Phainon should start keeping records of them so he could guess his emotions based on the type of huff he used.

More than anything, though, it sounded like exhaustion.

“Ever since I took in Astraea… I love him with everything I have, but it's so hard to take care of a child full time,” Mydei explained, confirming Phainon’s suspicions. He sighed again, taking a sip of… whatever he ordered. He had no idea of what that pink drink was. His attention, however, went back to him when he said, “Whenever he sleeps, I'm worried he might be suffering in his dreams and whenever he's awake I have to give him whatever he needs.”

It had to be hard, Phainon knew that. He just thought that Mydei could take it and make the best out of that situation without breaking a sweat– he looked so happy around Astraea, after all. Maybe he forgot to take into account that he worked, tried to entertain Phainon himself and made sure he didn’t think he abandoned him as well, all the while trying to care for a deeply traumatized child full-time. It was meant to be too much to handle for a single person.

Phainon stood up all of a sudden and walked over to stand behind him, his hands gently resting on Mydei’s shoulders. He almost did it as some sort of reflex, fully knowing that he most likely needed it.

“What are you doing?” Mydei asked, without even turning around. He just took a bite from his food– some kind of cold rice with vegetables and cheese mixed into it– and avoided even looking at him, much less stopping him.

“A massage,” Phainon responded, letting his fingers silently and gently draw circles on his shoulders in anticipation. “Can I?”

Mydei remained silent for a second, before whispering a tiny, “Yeah.”

With the consent obtained, Phainon applied as much force as he thought was necessary, which, for the record, was way more than he had ever done for a shoulder massage. It felt like trying to bend bricks, but he wasn’t the type to give up upon the first bump in the road. Especially because it was Mydei, and right now he was beginning to hear the hints of a few pleasured whines, only kept in check by the fact that they sounded more like heavy breaths than anything else.

He wondered if he would have made him break that self-control, at some point. Probably not tonight, but that was already a side of him that he had yet to witness and he liked it very much.

Fortunately for the both of them, it became slightly easier to apply that massage in a matter of a couple of minutes, and Mydei’s head instinctively flung back, resting against Phainon’s abdomen as his eyes fluttered shut for a few seconds. A few pleasured breaths escaped his lips as well, sounding more and more like quiet whines.

Phainon had to force himself not to stop to run his hands over his face. He was staring directly at his lips, thinking about how soft and glimmering they looked, how they could have tasted, how easy it would have been for him to just lean down and kiss him. The only thing that stopped him was, once again, that stupid bet. He had to yet decide if he preferred to admit to a loss or missing out on kissing him.

However, Mydei decided for him, suddenly opening his eyes again and looking at him.

He scoffed and smiled awkwardly at him, going back to his work, now with more nervous fingers. “You’re way too tense, Mydei!” Phainon managed to push out, before looking at him again with a grin on his face. “That just means I have to take you out more often.”

Mydei looked at him with his usual stone-faced expression, before reaching up with his hand and sliding a finger under the black leather choker around his neck, yanking it down. Phainon absurdly let him, giving him full control of his body. His face stopped mere centimeters from his mouth, his skin almost shivering whenever he felt his hot breath on his skin.

Calm down, Phainon , he reminded himself, you have a challenge to win. That’s just his way to push you to break and give him an easy victory.

“Are you going to give up so easily?” Phainon smirked, maybe a little too sure of himself. He could feel his sanity deteriorate a little more every second he stood there in that position, practically having to stop his every instinct to actually go ahead and kiss him.

Mydei hummed in thought. “I'm thinking,” he answered, not even bulging to let him go. As he looked at him again, he smiled and whispered, “Go back to eat.”

Phainon felt the instinct to whine and beg in the back of his head. It was pathetic, but he didn’t even put the blame on himself. Mydei was being so difficult that his own brain couldn’t formulate intelligent enough solutions to the situation.

Mydei's finger let him go, waiting for him to raise his head up again.

It didn't happen.

“Not even a thanks?” Phainon innocently asked, trying to get him to break and finally reach out to him.

He wanted that kiss! They've been running in circles since they met and then Mydei suggested that stupid, nonsensical challenge that Phainon idiotically accepted, and now they were on the third date without having even kissed once. Third! And he got his mother's blessing already as well!

It might as well be a twisted joke of fate by then.

Mydei looked at him dead in the eyes and just whispered, “Thank you. Now go eat.”

Phainon honestly should have expected that answer. It's so Mydei-like that it was his own fault for thinking he might have gotten anywhere further like that.

He left with a huff, heading over to his seat again. As he turned towards Mydei again, he noticed him gently brushing his fingers on his shoulders, right where Phainon had massaged him earlier, and watching towards the stage.

Maybe he truly did like places like that.

Looking more attentively at him, Phainon noticed his eyes almost losing their shine when the song headed to its conclusion, while his eyes continued to wander around the area of the stage.

“Do you like this song?” Phainon asked, starting to eat his plate. It wasn't cold, but it wasn't as hot as it was meant to be either. He didn't even remember what he ordered. Something yellow on the base and melted cheese on top of it, with some meat on the side.

It wasn't bad by any means, but he had never tasted it and he figured it would have tasted leagues better if he had just eaten it when it was hot.

Mydei finally turned back to him. “Yeah,” he admitted, “do you know the band?”

“It’s a cover band from around here. I'm sure you can ask them yourself later,” Phainon smiled, even if he felt absolutely useless for not having taken that possibility into account.

It had to be fine now, even if he didn't plan it. Hopefully. He was sure he or Mydei would have found a way around it.

Mydei ate a few more bites, before looking back at Phainon. “Do you still have night shifts? You mentioned a few times that you don't get much sleep because of it.”

Phainon nodded in defeat, already feeling those lost hours of sleep weigh on him, despite the night having just begun. “Yup…”

“Do you…” Mydei started, before shaking his head and excusing himself. “No, nevermind.”

He blinked at him a couple of times. Did he wish to ask him something? A favour, even? Something that he felt guilty asking? And he thought about him for it?

Phainon almost jumped up at the thought of that being the case.

“What?” he asked, now morbidly curious. Was it truly something that was impossible to ask for, or was it just embarrassment? Maybe guilt over asking it to him specifically?

He wouldn’t have minded if it was any of those options.

Mydei only sighed. “I told you, it was nothing.”

“But you wanted to ask something.”

It was so obvious. He nervously moved his fingers around his spoon, weighing the possibilities in his head.

And Phainon waited.

He waited for as long as he needed to, because he would have wanted to answer truthfully. He wanted it to be affirmative. Agree with what he said and help him with whatever he needed help with.

“Do you want to look after Astraea during the day?” Mydei asked in the end, locking eyes with him.

Phainon almost choked on his saliva. He coughed a couple of times, before asking, “You mean–”

“That’s why I didn't want to tell you,” Mydei interrupted him, looking away. He then whispered, as if to curse himself for even just thinking about it, “It's way too soon.”

He wasn't wrong. How long has it been? A month at best? Of course he trusted him with Astraea, but being around him so often while dating would have cemented him as a constant presence in his life.

Phainon didn't blame Mydei for being unsure about it. If something happened between them… Astraea would have gotten involved.

“That’s… true. But, Mydei,” Phainon pressed his lips together and looked at him with all the sincerity that he could master to make him understand how much he meant it, “I want you to know that my objective is becoming Astraea's father.”

He blinked a few times before realizing what he just said.

You're so stupid, Phainon.

He meant to at some point, of course, but not now! That wasn't what he wanted to say! 

His lips immediately parted to excuse himself, but Mydei's slight change in expression made him stop in his footsteps. Phainon expected a harsh, judgemental stare, maybe a little upset, but he was met with an almost pleased one instead.

Most times, Mydei's feelings were difficult to interpret without any explanation from him. Phainon recently started to vaguely be able to distinguish anger from happiness, but not much else.

It was in the littlest movements of the corner of his mouth, or the angulation of his face, or the shift of his eyebrows, or in the way his eyes softened or sharpened. Understanding Mydei was something he had to put his entire attention towards, lest he missed the smallest, vital movement that gave him an indication of what he was feeling.

He would have never asked Mydei to tell him how he felt, nor would he have ever forgiven himself if he misread what he wanted to convey.

At that moment, though, Phainon swore he saw his eyes soften and his muscles relaxing in an almost content stance.

Did he want him to be his son's father? Did he already think about it? Did it excite him?

Phainon almost wanted to believe that was the case. “Mydei–”

“We’ll decide later on,” Mydei immediately interrupted him, maybe fearing to hear something that his feelings agreed on. Even the thought was unimaginable in Phainon's eyes.

And yet, Mydei looked weirdly entertained by the thought. After all, he was the one to suggest it in the first place. Maybe he wanted him to trip and say out loud what he thought as well.

Phainon couldn't figure out if it was shyness of admitting to be wanting such a thing so early on in their relationship or eagerness to see him more often as a consequence of babysitting Astraea. Maybe it was both.

Regardless, the space between them, filled only by the cool, evening air around them started to feel uncomfortable. Silence swept in and, without neither of them noticing, it became almost unbearable after only a few seconds.

Now you've gone and done it, Phainon. He could now only dream of ever getting a request like that ever again.

He let out a shaky sigh, before raising his head again and seeing Mydei stare at him with a fondness in his eyes that he had yet to witness. He was just looking at him, but it was the best feeling he had ever had.

Getting lost in those amber irises resembling way too much the sunsets that he and his sister Cyrene used to look at and dreamily hope to see again the following day was doing weird things to his body.

He was familiar with his stomach turning when he was around Mydei, but this stomachache was something entirely new. Excitement. Trust. Need to hold. They were all mixed together, and he had no idea how to address all of them.

Instantly, he stood up and walked swiftly towards him, offering him a hand. One that he hoped he would take.

“Let’s walk around a little,” Phainon suggested with a smile. 

He waited for Mydei's answer, which luckily wasn't left unanswered for too long. Warmth spread on the hand he held out, and found him holding it. He still looked at him, but he didn't utter a single word.

Phainon didn't mind. As long as they were together, he would have accepted any way Mydei chose to communicate. As long as he didn't isolate and instead actually talked to him, he would have been happy.

Slowly, Phainon dragged him around the place, venturing in the area covered by tall, massive trees. He didn't even know how those parents were able to plant and grow them, but they have a certain… allure to them. It felt as if they were in an actual forest and there wasn't the entire city outside of the borders of that place.

Mydei looked around with wonder, carefully moving his head from one point to another, taking in all the information he could. Evidently, he liked it as well.

Phainon's eyes trailed down to Mydei's hand, still near his thigh, relaxed and so impossibly close. He blinked at it a few times before forcing his head to turn away. 

He didn't know why he couldn't bring himself to take it, but he felt like that was trespassing a limit that he should respect instead. He vaguely noticed how much Mydei forced himself to relax whenever he touched him and the way he pushed his hand away. Everything else that he did suggested an interest in this, he was sure of it, but touching him enticed a reaction that he didn't understand fully yet.

He didn't think it was rejection– maybe it was just about not being too used to his presence just yet. After all, this was just the third date. The first proper one. He had to be more patient and give him space, if he wanted this to end well.

As they walked, Phainon stopped in his steps and pointed towards a little separate space from the main road. “Oh, Mydei, this is the children's area I mentioned,” he explained, hoping that he would stop as well.

Thankfully, that was enough to catch his attention again.

He took a quick look around that area, his eyes focused on the big wooden boat in front of them.

“Is it handmade?” he asked, turning to Phainon.

“Yup! Maybe you can take Astraea here sometimes,” he suggested, walking towards the boat to step up on it. There was an easy path to follow to get on board though a small, wooden door and a little staircase, all to get closer to the wheel. 

Phainon quietly leaned onto it and smiled at Mydei, still following him with those curious cat-like eyes. “It kind of works too!” he beamed, before slightly moving it around. “See?”

Mydei smiled, decently amused by that display. “Quite well, captain.”

The playful nickname that Mydei definitely didn't think too much about rang in his brain like a beautiful melody. He imagined that he'd have a nickname for him– albeit in his dreams– but he didn't think about ‘captain’ of all things. Then again, it was fitting for that situation that he absolutely didn't think he'd find himself into.

He absolutely didn't hate it, though.

Victim of the adrenaline rushing through his brain in that moment, he winked and stroked a pose, a hand on the wheel and the other saluting him with v shaped fingers departing from his forehead.

Mydei didn't react for the first few seconds, but Phainon could notice even from there the glimmer of an idea passing through his eyes. He was really curious of what his brain thought of this time.

Immediately, he brought out his phone and showed it to him, without giving much time to react. “Pose again,” he requested instead.

Phainon blinked, a little surprised. “What?”

“Just do it,” came his voice from behind the phone.

He giggled and nodded, deciding to indulge him, but without making his life easier. “Already gave up on that bet enough to keep photos of me?”

“I sent one of mine and you keep sending me your selfies,” Mydei smirked, finally putting away the phone and showing his beautiful face again. “It's just right I take a picture of you to see if you're really that gorgeous, that's all.”

Gorgeous? Did Mydei indirectly call him gorgeous? He felt as if he was about to explode. He definitely needed that bet to end right now. He refused to resist any longer.

“So we can compile them in the photo album we'll make when we get married and how you fell for me?”

Since he was already knee deep into it, why not shoot his shot? He knew that they would have kissed at some point, or Mydei wouldn't have put up that ridiculous bet, and he'd rather it be sooner than later. Screw that challenge, he needed to kiss him right this second.

His thoughts were interrupted by a warm, soft, almost imperceptible laugh. Looking down, Phainon noticed the slight hint of blush on Mydei's cheeks. “Idiot,” he whispered, before he could follow it up with a yell. “Get down!”

Phainon didn't have any problems complying. He jumped down from where he stood, ending up in a spot just a few centimetres from Mydei. He looked… shocked. Maybe impressed? Perhaps, he liked it too, given how embarrassed he looked now. 

Oh, how cute and lovely he was from so close. That thought spread in his head like a calm wave reaching the shore, quietly running over the sand and retreating back into the sea to give way for another wave to do that same movement. His presence often felt akin to an ocean. Kind and fierce at the same time, but of a different heat from a sun or a fire. It was cooler, calmer, more comforting. Maybe that was the feeling that he kept getting addicted to when he was around his general presence.

His eyes were still intent on looking at him, when Mydei casually turned his head towards the other structures around them. Even that small movement felt too used to his presence, so natural and trusting in facing him with his back. Phainon smiled at the realization, feeling a rush of heat running towards his cheeks.

Mydei paid him no mind. Instead, he gazed at the wooden car not too far away from them and asked Phainon, “Is this supposed to be a car?”

He nodded, then pointed at the other wooden vehicle. “And that's a plane.”

As he turned towards it, he slightly tilted his head to the side like a confused cat, observing it for a few seconds. 

Phainon was sure that his heart stopped. He was so cute that he physically felt his heart stop beating in his chest. With the way his hair rested on his shoulder, akin to a lion’s mane, Phainon almost saw two cat ears spur from his head. Mydei was always so cute.

He smiled and barely kept in an amused laugh, before examining the car again. It looked almost prehistoric, but it had a seat someone could use even if they weren’t a child. “Look, Mydei,” he called as he sat down, pointing at a big metallic ring on the car right in front of him, “it can keep a drink here.”

Mydei stepped closer, curious after that statement. He stilled when he was next to him, crouching down to look better at what he was talking about. His eyes thinned and his hand reached out to touch it, then tilted his head to look at that object from another perspective. Phainon smiled as he noticed his other hand just a few inches away from him.

He could take it. He should, and stop acting like some teenager in love– after all, he doubted that Mydei would have refused him. And, if he did, they would just talk about it. Right? They did it already, when Hephaestion visited. For some reason, he felt like he was safe around him in more than one way.

After taking a deep breath– one that he felt the physical need to take in order to take any other step forward– Phainon sneakingly reached out his hand to hold Mydei's free one. At first it was just a fleeting brush against his skin with his fingertips, tasting the ground before he did anything else.

Mydei initially pulled away with a shiver, but there was a weird motion, pulling back towards his palm. Phainon looked at their hands barely touching, silently brushing against each other, still a little unsure about where they should go from there. However, it wasn't awkward hesitation– simply trying to approach each other in a slightly different way. It was a peculiar feeling, but not uncomfortable or unwelcomed.

Phainon's fingers finally decided to intertwine with Mydei's in a swift and fluid movement, the hand he was holding finally relaxing against his. He looked over to him, noticing the slightest blush on his skin, while his eyes were still focused on the metallic ring in front of him. 

With a smile, Phainon's thumb drew circles on the back of Mydei's hand, slowly erasing that anxiety or embarrassment from his face. He almost got upset over not being able to see such a beautiful flushed face anymore, but he gladly watched as he tested just how much he could help him relax.

Did he like it, he wondered? Maybe he did, if the degree of how much his muscles relaxed was of any indication.

Mydei, however, was still staring at that ring, probably unable to look anywhere else at that moment. How cute, Phainon thought, already leaning over to him, ending up impossibly close to him again. Maybe he was asking for too much or refusing to slow down for a second, but he wanted to see him up close so badly… and kiss him. He really liked that thought.

Phainon didn't dare to back down, but Mydei still looked over to him, refusing to let go of his hand. He almost felt like he was pleading him to close the distance between them or to do something about it in some other way.

If that was the case, though… maybe he could push himself to kiss him. If he stayed in that position any longer without taking action, he was sure he would go insane. Blue eyes wandered until they met Mydei's lips, seemingly soft and humid, probably tasting heavenly. He wondered if there were some cuts on them too, given his line of work.

Slowly, he gradually closed their distance, noticing that, for once, Mydei wasn't pulling back. He probably wanted this as much as Phainon did.

Even just thinking about being desired and wanted– maybe even loved too– by Mydei was making his head spin. He didn't even think about what he was doing anymore, and maybe he smashed his lips against his with a little too much strength. 

He didn't care, though.

Angling his face a little better, he kissed him again, slower and softer this time. He wanted to have his sweet time with him, at least with this kiss this one time. He didn't know if he would be granted another chance, so he opted to make the best with this one opportunity that he was able to seize. 

Mydei, on his part, was maybe more enthusiastic about it than he was. His free hand ran on his cheek, then held it by just below his jaw, making the skin below his palm crawl for a second. It wasn't fear, and he knew it. It was merely anticipation. Excitement. Hunger, maybe.

However, that was when it ended.

Of course, Phainon didn't expect some heated make-out session, but he was kind of sad that it was already over. Then again, he would have had other chances. Maybe. Probably. He kissed him back and initiated a kiss, so he had to like him back, right? At least a little bit? Yes?

Phainon looked at him with expectations that he shouldn't have had, as Mydei was mindlessly brushing his thumb over Phainon's lower lip. His gaze went back to the metallic ring. “I doubt it was created with that in mind,” Mydei mentioned in the end.

All he got in response was Phainon blinking at a nervously worrying speed. “What?”

“The ring,” he explained, before picking up a piece of wood right next to where Phainon's food rested. “There's a walkie-talkie here.”

Oh. Was he still thinking about that? Was it truly so much more interesting of kissing him? Or… was it something else, perhaps? 

Looking at him, he noticed he was almost avoiding to meet his eyes and kept the rest of his body occupied in the meantime. It didn't seem like anxiety, more like trying to manage his emotions… was he simply overwhelmed?

It would have explained his behaviour, but Phainon didn't even dare to ask for confirmation. If he was, he would have simply let him distract himself and play with that ring or his lips as long as he wished.

He could even entertain him as much as he wanted. He smiled and answered, “How do you know? Maybe they made it exactly for this reason, and the walkie-talkie was just an afterthought!”

He said it lightly, joking around and expecting a callback from Mydei, but he never got it. Instead, all he obtained was silence and hesitation. It wasn’t the first time he sensed conflicting feelings from him, but he doubted it was just embarrassment or directly related to not liking him– since he clearly did, or he wouldn’t have initiated a kiss and gotten so lost in it a few seconds prior.

Phainon slid a hand on his cheek, lightly brushing against his golden hair. He heard Mydei’s breath hitch for a second, right before his head turned away from his contact. It always broke his heart whenever he seemed to be so bothered with being touched, especially if it was heavy with feelings or silently brushing against his skin. Looking at those motions from his position almost looked like he was being burned barely from his touch.

“Mydei?” he asked with a whisper. His voice was insecure and hesitant, but he still let it come out. Maybe Mydei would catch onto it and open his heart to him, at long last.

Instead of what he hoped, though, Mydei just shook his head. “It’s nothing.”

It wasn’t true. He would have been happier– maybe not brimming with excitement, sure, but happy nonetheless– and he would have accepted his touches and advances more openly. Avoiding his hand, hesitantly approaching him all of a sudden… it wasn’t nothing . Phainon didn’t even have to observe him to notice that there was something bothering him, it was surprisingly obvious.

Phainon tilted his head and weakly smiled at him, mastering the strength to push further despite the possibility of him leaving or running away. He would have understood it, but it would have hurt anyway and there was no guarantee he would have walked back to him. However, the reality was that if he kept on running away and refusing to touch him like that and he didn’t get to the root of his issue, time wouldn’t have magically made it disappear.

Carefully, Phainon took a deep breath and tried to reason with him, keeping his hands to himself. “Why don't you stop pulling away?” he managed to whisper, as his eyes wandered all over his face. “I know you want the same, so why–”

“Because I want this to end well,” Mydei blurted out, cutting him off before he could even finish his question. He lowered his head and let out a shaky sigh, before explaining himself. “You seem… a complicated person, Phainon. I like you and I want to get to know you better, but I have responsibilities towards my child before anything else. I need to make sure this will be good for him and it won’t hurt him, in case it doesn’t last.”

Phainon pressed his lips together. He didn’t even think about the effects a break-up would have had on Astraea. He just took his request and held it close to his heart as if it was a permission from Mydei’s parents. 

He was a child. Of course he wanted to see Mydei happy, but he was still a child and he wouldn’t know consequences as complicated as a relationship gone wrong. In his eyes, Mydei was his saviour, the first adult he could rely on, someone he could run to for support and who actually loved and cared about him… of course he saw the way he was looking at Phainon and latched onto it as a way to repay him for his kindness. 

He didn’t think for a second about the slight guilt he felt on his tongue when he made that request either. He wanted to be somewhat akin to his father to help both him and Mydei? He couldn’t even understand such a simple thing as not treating him as an adult and trying to decide what was better for him.

Phainon let out a sigh, then looked back at Mydei, pushing through with the conversation anyway. It wasn’t like he actually did anything yet, so there was no reason to panic, right? They were just talking now and Mydei had a few fears that he wanted to help with– and he was sure that was what was going to happen.

“Do you not trust me?” he asked, slightly tilting his head. He didn’t fully believe it, but he wanted to be sure of what the actual issue was.

“It’s not about you,” Mydei sighed, finally looking at him. “It's the fact that we're rushing everything, and if it doesn't work–”

“It will.”

Phainon blinked, realizing too late that his mouth acted faster than his brain. He was looking at Mydei’s sad expression, full of doubt and more hesitant than he had ever seen him, and he couldn’t bear it anymore. If he could put all his questions to rest, if he could reassure him and alleviate even just a tiny little amount of his burden and his pain… he would have done it without thinking twice.

Mydei thinned his eyes for a second, almost as if he felt a sting of pain from those words. “You can't know that,” he pointed out, holding his hands together a little too strongly.

It hurt, seeing him so anxious over it. Was he… afraid, maybe, that after his last break-up left him a little too sad that it would have affected his child? It was a kind thought, but Phainon would have genuinely killed himself before ever thinking about leaving him. He wanted to treat him in the way he deserved, along with taking care of Astraea. And he wished he could make him understand his feelings properly as soon as possible.

“I do. If I ever hurt you or Astraea, I will end my life right there,” Phainon sighed, finally abandoning his smile for a second. He got closer, mindful of not touching him, but close enough so he could know what he meant and whispered, voice heavy with worry, “Mydei. I'm serious.”

“You–” Mydei blinked twice at him, before shaking his head and letting out a quiet laugh, “you're insane.”

Phainon smiled again almost out of reflex when he heard that soft laugh. Sure, he called him insane, but it didn’t matter. That sound was one that he prayed to hear every day of his life, no matter what happened between them. It was so warm in every circumstance. Comforting, bright, genuine. He loved it.

He shrugged, feeling happiness over being able to convey the right feelings to him and knowing he was still standing next to him despite it all. “For you? Any day.”

“Endearing. And insane,” Mydei laughed, evidently amused. “But I can work with that.”

Phainon made the mistake of closing his eyes at the half-compliment and acceptance of his feelings. In seconds, he found himself pressed against the back of his seat, Mydei kissing on top of him and a hand on his chest pressing him down. He would have panicked, if only that kiss wasn’t so steady and sweet that he doubted anyone else other than the man with him could pull it off. 

He didn’t even think before kissing back and cupping his face with his hands. He deepened the kiss and angled his head a little differently, just to be comfortable enough to gently push his tongue past Mydei’s lips and taste him properly. He felt his throat vibrate for a second as he let out a soft whine, but he followed his lead all the same. Phainon smiled against his lips and dropped his hands down on his sides, lightly squeezing the flesh under his fingertips.

A long, low whine made its way through his ears in response. He smiled again, pushing him back slightly and not letting his lips go. After all the time he had waited for that moment, there was no way he would ever think about stopping to kiss him.

That kiss, however, only dragged on for another few seconds before Mydei gently yanked his shirt to indicate his request of getting a few inches away from him, at the very least.

They were both panting, chests rhythmically rising and falling, without moving from either of their positions.

“Mydei,” Phainon said, breaking the thin layer of silence that formed in those few seconds, “I think you won our challenge.”

Mydei smiled and leaned in again, only stopping where he still couldn't touch his lips yet. “So, now you can kiss me whenever you want.”

It wasn't hard to kiss him again. A swift movement forward of his head smashed their lips together again, while Mydei's hands easily travelled on his cheeks, gently caressing them.

This one was a lot shorter, only lasting a few seconds, before Phainon let go and kissed his cheek, his jaw and his neck in rapid succession. 

Mydei laughed as he felt those affectionate kisses, only falling back on the ground when Phainon seemed satisfied.

How cute. Every time they did something new together, Phainon found new, more endearing sides to Mydei and he adored it.

Looking at him from there, it was obvious that the doubt that formerly clouded his mind completely disappeared. At least, he was more peaceful and happier now.

“Can I make a request?” Mydei asked, all of a sudden.

Phainon turned towards him, quietly nodding. Of course he wanted to do whatever Mydei needed him to! If he could and he got asked, he would move the earth and the sky for him.

“Sure! Anything for you, Mydei,” he beamed, immediately in his face again.

Mydei looked at him with confused eyes, but he placed down his request anyway. “Leave Hephaestion alone and try to be his friend instead. He’s a good person,” he explained, careful about using the right words, “and he knows a lot about me that you absolutely won't hear coming from my mouth.”

That was… true. Phainon may have not liked Hephaestion, but he probably knew Mydei better than anyone else. Forcing himself to be his friend was something new, but he didn't necessarily hate it if it brought more facts and stories about Mydei.

Facing his fears wasn't something he was ecstatic about either, but Mydei was opening up and facing his own now, so who was he to refuse doing that?

Even Astraea now was at home without Mydei– possibly his biggest fear at the moment– and he was pushing through for his father's well-being and happiness… if he was the only one not to do anything and cower away in fear, he would have never forgiven himself.

Besides, it was the first direct request Mydei made. He couldn't just refuse.

“So?” Mydei asked again. The silence probably dragged on a little longer than Phainon thought.

“I’m thinking about it…” Phainon crossed his arms and looked up to him with an insecure smile. “Maybe? If you ask?”

“That is what I'm doing.”

“I’ll try, then! For you.”

He was a little scared. He wanted to make Mydei happy– no matter how or if it ended up being difficult for him– but he was… terrified to say the least. 

Phainon absolutely didn't think Hephaestion was a bad person, but any interaction that he had with him felt so incredibly suffocating. The smallest possibility of not being liked by him or, Gods forbid, Mydei realizing how much worse he was than his ex resulting in being abandoned kick-started his fight or flight immediately.

Even back when Hephaestion visited Mydei, if Astraea didn't notice something was wrong enough to offer him a hug, he didn't know what could have happened.

Despite that, he knew that it was an irrational fear. He knew that he couldn't control it at the moment, but he was confident that he could work on it or be disproven by Mydei in a heartbeat, just like he did when it happened for the first time.

He prayed that Mydei squashed those fears into nothingness once and for all as soon as possible.

While he sat there deep in thought, Mydei leaned in and kissed him on his cheek. It was nothing, just a sweet, thankful kiss on his cheek. “Thank you, Phainon,” he added, basically whispering it into his ear.

Phainon's face was burning so much that he was sure it was about to explode.

He just made out with him, he had his tongue shoved down his throat as he felt him whine and push him down– and what made him blush was a sweet, innocent kiss on his cheek. He might as well propose to him, at that point.

Mydei laughed softly at that reaction, falling back again. He was so beautiful whenever he relaxed and laughed around him. That was all that Phainon was able to think about whenever he saw a smile on his stunning, perfect face. Kissing him still felt unreal.

Phainon tried to lean in again almost on reflex, akin to two magnets attracted to each other, but he stopped himself when he felt the impulse to yawn. Maybe he should have taken a nap, after all…

He wasn’t too tired, but he needed to start to put into account that he needed to sleep during the day more, whether he liked it or not. Probably Mydei would have understood if he told him, but he really, truly didn’t want to miss out on this date. He had been waiting for this for days and he was so excited to go out with him like this–without other people around, just being able to spend time with him and get to know him a little better than the last time.

Mydei, however, still tilted his head and looked at him with worried eyes. “Have you slept?”

His shoulders froze for a second, but he didn't even think about lying to him. He made clear that he didn't like it, and neither did his mother. If he lied to him now– especially after he decided to face his fears– he might as well let him go forever.

“I took a nap,” he answered truthfully, albeit not stating the actual time that one nap took. Hopefully Mydei wouldn't mind that little white lie.

Mydei knitted his eyebrows. “Was it enough?”

“Probably not…” he answered, before turning towards him and leaning forward, almost enough to fall out of the wooden car he was still sitting in. 

Mydei retracted by a few steps, but he held him still all the same, thinking about preventing his fall. Phainon only relatively cared about it. For all he cared, he could have fallen face flat on his chest without complaints. Thinking about it now, it wasn't too bad of an accident.

However, there was something more pressing on his mind. Feelings that he needed to acknowledge and speak into reality. Letting Mydei know his reasons to skip sleep and be there. 

Phainon laid his hands on Mydei's shoulders, looking at him directly in his eyes. He exchanged his stare and let him lean in and whisper, “I really wanted to see you, Mydei.”

“Irresponsible,” he shook his head. “You're supposed to be the oldest one between us, so why do you behave like a child and then run to me for comfort?”

“Because… it's easy to trust you, Mydei. And I want to see you everyday now.”

It wasn't a lie. He knew that he was almost thirty years old and he shouldn't run after someone else so insistently, but it was hard to ignore his feelings regarding Mydei. They were intoxicating and addicting at the same time, and he wished that he could spend all his time with him, instead of going to work.

So, if Mydei was going to suggest an outing, Phainon would have taken that chance, no matter what. Sleep was unimportant to him– but it clearly wasn't the same for Mydei. He looked at him as he caressed his cheek gently, a little hesitantly, but all the care that he showed in his words reflected in that touch.

Phainon couldn't help but lean into it. He closed his eyes and let out a pleased hum as he smiled. He probably looked pathetic, but he didn't care. He could have left a thousand times by now, but he didn't… he wanted to believe that a weird little show of affection wouldn't push him away.

It had been a long time since he last properly trusted someone, but Mydei made it so easy. He just prayed to be right about it.

“Come sleep at my place. You're too tired,” Mydei whispered, retreating his hand. He looked at him with worry too clear in his eyes, but he didn't necessarily press on to that matter much. If he wanted to accept, he would have been glad to welcome him, otherwise… it would have been fine too.

Phainon couldn't help but smile at him upon that request. It meant that he could get some sleep while spending time with Mydei… it was a win-win situation! Of course, Mydei knew what to suggest even now.

He stood up all of a sudden and walked out of the car before looking at Mydei again. The blonde didn't move from his position crouched on the ground and just stared up at him with a surprised expression and curious eyes.

He was so cute. He looked like a confused kitten endearingly watching what kind of stupidity its owner participated in this time.

However, it didn't last long– and Phainon knew that he kept thinking that exact sentence throughout the night, but he felt like it perfectly described what Mydei kept on doing. Surprising him, keeping him entertained, always doing something when he least expected it, like a tide, always changing and morphing every second.

Phainon didn't hate that some things didn't last long– the most precious, treasured things like his smile or a quick pout or a blush– because it made them more special.

A fleeting smile, a momentaneous embarrassment, a microscopic change in his expression… They were the things that Phainon remembered the most because he knew that they wouldn't have lasted long.

But he knew that he would have seen them again.

As a wave changed every second and landed on the shore before retreating, another one would have repeated a similar or identical movement, sooner or later. Mydei expressed this notion in everything that he did, and Phainon noticed. The little smile will come back, the tiniest blush on his cheeks will happen again, the smallest movement of his eyes and eyebrows will repeat itself at some point.

Mydei's entire existence relied on small, special moments in repetition that Phainon was fully planning to remember until his next life, when he will learn and remember them all over again.

His smile got bigger when he thought about being able to see it again, and again, and again. He truly felt like the luckiest man on the planet.

A hand suddenly rested on his head and pet it, almost to congratulate him. Phainon looked forward and saw Mydei, already smiling again.

And he was… petting him? A few moments ago he struggled to touch him and now he was completely fine with petting his head?

It seemed like Mydei was a much more complicated person than Phainon first assumed.

“Look at how happy my puppy is…” he whispered, so casually that Phainon choked on his own saliva. His mind instantly short-circuited at the same time as he started coughing, uselessly trying to make sense of what he just heard.

His puppy… His puppy?

He was definitely going to die tonight. Hyacine will find out that he died because his boyfriend– were they now? They kissed, right? They should have been. Maybe. Technically. He hoped. He had to ask later. And he called him his puppy while he pet his head and smiled at him. Both Hyacine and Castorice would visit his tomb and declare his cause of death was being pathetically in love with a man he met that same month.

Gods, he would never live it down. No matter if he would have died already, Hyacine would somehow remember and laugh at him every time she saw him in their next life.

Phainon shut down his mind, trying to think at an acceptable speed but it seemed impossible. He was now thinking how Mydei would have looked if anyone else tried to hit on him. Would he be possessive? Jealous? Phainon wanted him to. Maybe without fighting them, but telling them off would be… good. Hot. Deadly for him, probably.

His puppy.

He wanted that to stick, somehow. He didn't care if it was just a few instances or if it ended up being a pet name– quite literally– he wanted to keep hearing his voice forming those words and know they were directed at him.

“Phainon?”

Mydei's voice rang in his brain like an alarm urging him to wake up from whatever dream he found himself in. As soon as he looked at him, he saw questioning eyes and his hand back on his side, no longer petting his hair.

His cheeks were still on fire from before, he was sure that Mydei could understand that much at least, so he wasn't bound to be too worried. He seemed to be simply wondering what there was on his mind.

With a deep breath, Phainon mastered the focus to answer him. “I… really like that…” 

Phainon almost forced it out, but it was the truth. He liked it! If it didn't make his brain go into momentary maintenance, he probably would have been explaining in depth all the reasons why he enjoyed it so much as well.

Mydei furrowed his brows together. “Like what? Getting called a puppy?”

“ Your puppy, specifically!”

“Because you are a puppy. And you're the only one in my life, so it's only natural I'd think of you as my puppy.”

Phainon smiled softly, fully knowing that was an excuse. He didn't press on, but he knew that it was. Even if he was the only one in his life– which wasn't true because he called Astraea a puppy as well, apparently– no one would ever call anyone else theirs unless they meant it.

Alternatively, Mydei was so cute and oblivious and adorable that he didn't notice. Both were more than amazing options for Phainon, honestly.

“Astraea told me that you said we're similar,” he mentioned, just to see his first reaction.

To his amusement, Mydei hung his mouth slightly open in something that looked like surprise and confusion, but he didn't ask where he got that from. He was intelligent enough to understand that his son blatantly betrayed him and he had no way out now.

As soon as he closed it, he cleared his throat and explained, “One of the main reasons I asked you out a while ago was because he reminded me of you. He loves you so much too. You're good with kids, hard childhood or not.”

That monologue looked way too much as a list of reasons why Mydei eyed him to parent his son and Phainon desperately prayed for it to be false. He needed it to be his imagination and not what he was actually suggesting, or he would have definitely lost his mind.

“And now you're saying that you want to be his father, so it's only natural for me to think of you two as similar, no?”

He would have died.

He would have died and come back to his apartment in a coffin and Hyacine would have told everyone he died because he was too gay for this one firefighter he met a few weeks ago. That apparently was completely fine with him being his son's father. What the fuck.

“You eyed me with the intentions of mating with m–”

“Don’t end that sentence.” Mydei interrupted him, already stopping his mind to wander further in that direction. Honestly, it was probably for the best. “Hephaestion was the one suggesting it. That nice side to you, though… it was always on the back of my mind. We wouldn't be here if you weren't that good with little kids.”

Phainon couldn’t help but let out a little laugh. “You're not helping your case here.”

“What is that supposed to mean?”

“You keep saying you want me to be your child's father… is that some sort of confession?”

Mydei’s mouth hung open for a few seconds, then he crossed his arms and slightly tilted his head. “You already know I like you, why would I need to confess again?”

Saying that Phainon froze would be a grave understatement. Of course, he knew that kissing someone the way they did meant that they liked each other, at the very least. What surprised him was the smoothness with which he admitted it.

“What?” Phainon asked, a little anxious. Not that he didn't believe him, but he was… cautious. It wasn't bad to doubt those words at first, right? He was just taken aback by the casual tone that Mydei used, he knew that he liked him and he probably suspected that his feelings were reciprocated.

However, Mydei raised an eyebrow with judgmental eyes. “What, what ?” he huffed, maybe a little annoyed, then turned back to him. “Do you think I would be here if I wasn't interested in you? I told you how many times already? If I didn't want anything to do with you, I would have said so.”

Phainon blinked. He expected the huff, he expected the judgment, but he didn’t expect the constant reminder about his unwillingness to leave him all of a sudden. He liked it, he just didn’t expect it and he thought that he was annoying him. Apparently not. Or, well, not enough for him to hate him, leave him or ignore that behavior.

The blonde man in front of him stared at him for a second and shook his head. With a sigh, he repeated more clearly, “Trust me a little more, instead of assuming I'm similar to any other person you might have dated in the past.”

What a fool he was being.

Of course Mydei wasn’t like his past experiences. His first mistake was assuming that he was even remotely similar to them. His every gesture and word diverged from them, gave him more security and confidence, reassured him when he needed him the most… he needed to stop to brace himself for the worst.

He genuinely wanted to trust him, for once. If he hurt him, he had the inkling that his sister and Hyacine would both make him go through hell anyway.

Mydei didn’t even call out his name or interrupt his thoughts, as patient as ever. It was yet another thing he appreciated.

“Is your invitation still valid?” he asked in the end, tilting his head.

“Of course.”

“I'll take it up then!”

Mydei smiled at him just as Phainon reached out to hold his hand excitedly. He noticed another shudder, but his fingers easily intertwined with the white haired man’s. That was another problem for another day. He would have asked, at some point, but not now. Most likely, his goal was going back home both for Astraea and to force Phainon to sleep.

He was fine with it. After all, he was tired and he already kissed Mydei. Anything else that happened until midnight was just a well accepted bonus.

They walked back to where they first had the food as Mydei made some questions about the trees and plants around them– ones that Phainon barely knew how to answer, but he threw out decent enough guesses for the conversation to keep going for quite some time.

Phainon watched as Mydei kept on staring at the leaves around them, trying to figure out which ones they were. “How do you even know so much about plants?” he asked, now morbidly curious about the matter. From what he knew, botanics wasn’t in the curriculum for firefighters, right?

“A friend of mine likes to study them,” he answered, unamused. “His name is Perdikkas. He studied botanics all his life as a hobby, so he taught me a few things.”

Phainon hinted at a laugh, a little amused. Of course, he did his fair share of studying– he needed to keep himself updated too, as a nurse– but studying as a hobby wasn’t something he expected to hear. Especially something as complicated as botanics. It wasn’t gardening, he had to memorize every plant, their organs and tissues, their behavior… it was a full blown science.

“As a hobby?” he asked, slowing his pace to let Mydei look at the leaves he was so interested in with more attention.

Mydei looked at him with a fallen leaf in his hand. “You don’t have a hobby?”

“Yeah, but… studying? Botanics isn’t exactly easy. Where does he work?”

“In a pharmacy.”

Well… at least it was somewhat related. Only somewhat , since most remedies they give off are chemical and made in a lab, but he could see the connection. Still, the fact that he found the time to study botanics while trying to graduate in pharmaceutics was impressive all the same.

He wondered if the entirety of Mydei’s friend group was similar. If they stuck together for such a long time despite the age difference between them, there had to be a catch, or otherwise something that linked them. They probably weren’t his best friends– that role was probably filled by Hephaestion– but they were very present in his life all the same and he did call them friends.

As if he knew what he was thinking about, Mydei started to explain, “Our friend group is full of people that like studying. I enjoy studying history, my friend Leonnius often repeated it to me for his exams and I started liking it. Peucesta likes studying psychology, Perdikkas adores botanics, Ptolemy is an avid reader of almost anything that can catch his attention… Hephaestion just really likes animals. He doesn’t study them, he says it ‘takes away the magic’.”

Phainon let out an amused laugh about the mention of that man for the first time. He had to admit that knowing him through Mydei’s words made him seem quite interesting and fun to hang out with. It was better this way, he thought in the end. Since he promised that he would try to get to know him better and get along with him, the best outcome was finding him amusing, at the very least.

“I kind of… agree with him,” he admitted, now much more relaxed than a few minutes ago. Telling the truth about his feelings was a little easier, and he started to trust Mydei’s words at face value a lot more. As it turned out, having an honest talk about his issues and needs with someone that genuinely cared about him made miracles.

“You would get along,” Mydei mentioned again. Apparently, they were somewhat similar in his eyes? Or he knew both enough to know that. Phainon doubted that he would force it on either of them. The blonde man looked at him and let the leaf fall to the ground again, just to whisper, “Don’t see him as my ex, just see him as a friend. I can guarantee you that he has no interest in me.”

Phainon pouted in a dubious expression. “How do you know?”

“We wouldn’t be here if he didn’t insist so much on us getting together. I’m pretty sure he will start asking about the wedding as soon as he knows we kissed,” Mydei joked, with a deadpan tone.

It was a little funny; the guy seemed like he was personally cheering on them. If he truly was like that, then Phainon should have stopped worrying about him because he clearly had other objectives that solely involved seeing his best friend marry someone else. Honestly, that alone lessened any kind of possessiveness he had regarding Mydei. If he wanted him, they wouldn’t have broken up and he wouldn’t have pushed for him to accept to text him, after all.

As he was thinking, Mydei began to walk slowly again, giving him time to notice and adjust his pace. That kindness and patience that never pressured him or treated him like a hopeless baby was something that Phainon liked to see more and more often, and he kept on hoping that it would never stop.

He looked over to him again, reprising the conversation from before. “And what’s Leonnius's hobby? You didn’t mention it.”

Mydei tilted his head and thought about it for a second. Phainon couldn’t help but notice just how cute he looked, all perplexed like that, like an adorable cat trying to figure out something they didn’t fully understand. “It’s less of a hobby and more of a passion,” he stated in the end. “He teaches soccer to little kids. He has a girls’ team this year.”

“But he teaches history?”

“Yeah, but the principal hates him. See, Leonnius thinks that standard lessons are too boring for students to get everything in their heads. So, he teaches them in the courtyard and puts up little shows for them for whatever they’re studying. He ends up making a lot of noise.”

What a peculiar friendgroup that Mydei had. He pictured him much less extravagant, maybe a little closed off and introverted, but he really wasn’t. It was easy to talk to him and he largely enjoyed how open and honest he was about everything way more than if he had the personality he imagined.

And the fact that he never backed down from a challenge, he kept him on the edge, he was so surprisingly unreadable until recently… He loved to spend every second with him and he yearned to spend even more time at his side in the future.

Phainon smiled warmly at him, gently squeezing his hand just to feel him closer for even just a moment. If Mydei noticed, he had no reaction to it. “He seems fun,” Phainon added, refusing to let that conversation die.

He wasn’t scared of an awkward silence, but he wanted to keep on listening to his voice and what he wanted to talk about. It was clear that he loved his friends, and he couldn’t really hate it even if there was a weird feeling in his chest gradually forming. He ignored it for the time being, hoping that it would quiet down soon enough.

He was happy now– he wanted to trust Mydei and his judgment, no matter what his mind would suggest to him. If Mydei confirmed that he didn’t have to worry about them… he simply wouldn’t.

“He’s the oldest,” Mydei answered him, catching his attention again, “but he still acts in a quite childish manner. You would be insufferable if you ever met him.”

Oh, that was interesting. Mydei thought he would be impossible to stand if he stood next to this guy? Consider him intrigued, interested and fully into trying to absolutely make it happen just to see his reaction. “Now I need to know who this Leonnius is.”

“Get it out of your head.”

“C’mon, Mydei…”

Phainon was entirely prepared to whine and beg to let him meet him just because he was oh-so-curious about why the blonde man would be so against their meeting, but his attention stilled when Mydei stopped walking. He looked over, and noticed that he was staring at the table they abandoned, now clean and with other people sitting in it.

It was clear that there was something that bothered him, but Phainon didn't know which one was it between the seat being stolen or the food being taken away.

“Mydei?” he called out, taking a step closer just in case it would be something where he needed his intervention.

Against all his predictions, Mydei looked back at him and pouted, genuinely distressed. Maybe more sad than upset, but it was a face he had never worn in the past few weeks all the same.

He looked like a starved cat begging for food. He was so cute. If it was a plot to get him to do whatever he asked, it was working amazingly even if he would have done it anyway.

Mydei looked down for a second, before whispering, “They took our food.”

Cute. Cute. Cute. The cutest thing he had ever witnessed. And it came from a giant, built man who dove into the fire on a daily basis. And he was so damn cute all the time.

“We left our table, of course they did,” Phainon answered, with such a soft voice that he barely recognized that it was his own.

He didn't even want for it to be so soft, that was just how it came out. But, maybe, he was just so sad and endeared to Mydei that he instinctively did it.

He shifted position and stood in front of him, holding his free hands too. Mydei didn't react too much to the touch this time, just accepted the support he was given and intertwined his fingers with Phainon's.

Mydei bit his lower lip as he swung his arms forward and backwards, keeping his eyes on that table.

He looked so unconsolable… and Phainon couldn't stand it.

Without letting go of him, Phainon kissed him on his cheek a few times. “Talk to me, Mydei,” he whispered, “what's wrong? Please, let me help.”

Mydei hesitated for a second. He trusted him, that much was obvious, he probably just felt a little embarrassed in front of that request.

Phainon, naturally, took the matters into his own hands yet again.

“Please, Mydei,” he whispered against his skin, moving his head slightly to kiss him on the side of his neck. “I want to help you in whatever you need. You manage to be so cute even now, but I don't like knowing you’re sad…”

He left another kiss on his neck, a little more insistently, enough to push him against the tree behind him.

“Please,” Phainon repeated again, wrapping an arm around his torso as Mydei led his hand to caress his hair. This time, he couldn't help it and sucked on his skin, gaining a soft whine from Mydei.

Such a pretty sound.

Mydei's hand dropped to Phainon's cheek for a second, forcing him to look at him. He was always beautiful, but seeing him blushing and with red marks on the side of his neck made him even more stunning than he usually did.

Slowly, Mydei tilted his head and kissed him, delicately and carefully. It was so gentle that Phainon was sure that he would have passed out if it lasted any longer.

Of course, that was exactly what Mydei was planning. Phainon knew that perfectly. Should he tell him to stop? Maybe. For his well-being. But who was he to deny him a kiss?

No one. If Mydei wanted to kiss him for the next hour, he would have happily obliged.

He felt arms wrapping around his shoulders and his other hand flung to hold him more steadily by his hip. Phainon absolutely wasn't complaining of how the night was turning out to be.

Mydei yanked his head back at some point and, even if Phainon tried to catch it, he couldn't quite reach it again. A pity, but he figured that it wouldn't have lasted forever.

“I didn't want it to go to waste,” Mydei stated, looking at him from where he was standing. Maybe it was a little too close, but neither of them cared. Then, the blonde looked over Phainon's shoulders again and added, “Astraea liked what you ordered too.”

Oh, he didn’t need to add anything else. If Mydei wanted the food they left on the table, he would get it, in one way or another.

Phainon nodded before he grabbed his hand and dragged him along, somehow knowing that he would have followed him. Mydei stumbled at first, but he didn’t fall. Within a couple of steps, he kept up with his pace without Phainon needing to slow down or stop, and whispered, “Phainon.”

“Shh,” Phainon turned and slowed down, “I said I’d help you, right? Let me do my job.”

Mydei stared at him in pure, clear confusion. “What job are you talking about?”

“Being your boyfriend, of course,” Phainon smiled brightly at him as he intertwined their fingers together again. He liked his hands so much. They were big and slender, completely unlike what he had imagined them to be. There were some callouses and scars, but there wasn’t much fat around them and the individual fingers were long and seemingly delicate. 

The duality that Mydei basked in so often was yet another thing that he was discovering to love just as much as him.

“You–” Mydei stuttered, before stopping himself, blushing again. “Fine. Hurry up.”

Phainon smiled, happy with himself and being able to see those reddened cheeks yet again. No matter if his voice was somewhat annoyed and he was looking at him with a deadly glare– he was just very happy about seeing him with a cute little blush on his face because of something he said.

Being embarrassed about being referred to as his boyfriend… It was the cutest thing he’s done so far. Phainon wondered if he would react in the same way if he ever used a pet name, but the sheer thought of being able to do that turned all his gears at full speed for the second that the idea bounced around in his head. Maybe thinking about it would cause his brain to implode on itself. Yeah, he definitely should stop thinking about it.

Instead, Phainon smiled brightly at him and whispered, “Of course. Do you want to stay here?”

All he got in response was an even worse glare.
