He laughed nervously and squeezed his hand almost as a reminder that he didn’t want him to walk away or let go of him. Or, at least, that was what he wanted to communicate. He was unsure whether or not such a simple gesture was able to pass it through. 

“Okay, you don’t,” Phainon answered. He didn’t even wait before dragging him along towards the stand, the same place where they ordered. By that point, he figured that Mydei understood what he wanted to do.

Phainon stopped walking and stood still, not saying anything. He wasn’t waiting for his turn, he just wanted to see how long it took for Mydei to lose his patience. Maybe he shouldn’t have done it when he wanted to lessen his worries and help him after reaching out like a knight in white armour, but it did amuse him. After all, if he was there to know him better, he might as well test that too. 

“Hurry,” came a stern whisper, after just a few seconds.

Impatient.

Phainon laughed for a moment before calling out the waiter and obliging to his boyfriend’s desires. “Excuse me! Can I get another dish of what I ordered an hour ago?”

“Oh, are you still hungry?” the woman across from him asked, evidently recognising them. It wasn’t hard, he was sure that two men like those weren’t the usual people that hung around there, from what he could see. Most people were either families with kids or much older people assisting at the concert.

The thought of Mydei having hobbies akin to the ones of an old man planted itself in his head, and Phainon smiled at it before keeping up his conversation with the woman in front of him.

“We forgot to pack it instead of leaving it there! We wanted to bring it home.”

“Don’t worry, then! We still have your dishes, we usually keep them for half an hour before throwing them away.”

“You’re a lifesaver!” Phainon beamed as he got handed the boxes in a plastic bag. He smiled and thanked her again, glad that they didn’t have to pay for additional two plates. He actually had no idea they had that policy. 

He handed the bag to Mydei with a much gentler smile and added, “Here you go.”

“Thank you,” Mydei answered, grabbing the bag and refusing to let go of his hand. Phainon had no idea whether he liked it or he was forcing himself to keep on holding it, but maybe it didn’t matter.

He clearly wanted to keep holding his hand despite the first difficulties he had with it, and that was everything that should have mattered. Knowing that someone that struggled with being touched suddenly wanted to keep that same touch as close as possible was bound to make him feel a certain type of way, at the very least. Accepted and loved, maybe, but not only that.

There was some kind of trying to overcome each other’s fears in every interaction they had that proved just how much both of them wanted this– whatever it ended up being– to work that warmed Phainon’s heart.

Phainon tilted his head slightly and looked at him with soft, loving eyes. “You sounded so hurt about it… I couldn't stand by and do nothing,” he explained, weirdly reflective with his tone.

Of course, he knew why he did it. He was bothered knowing Mydei was somewhat sad and he didn’t want to repeat the experience. However, during that time… he felt so much lighter than usual. Helping others wasn’t something that came difficult to him, but he often felt some kind of fear of disappointing them, or not reaching the goal that he promised them.

That didn’t happen just then.

Mydei was right next to him and he didn’t feel pressured or judged, he was just happy that he could do something for him, with no secondary feelings dragging him down. He knew that he would have been there afterwards and he knew that he trusted him, and maybe that was the difference.

He perfectly knew that others had a certain idea of him, but Mydei made perfectly clear that he wanted to know him and he liked him , not the person he expected him to be, to the point of asking to get along with the people he cared the most about in his life. That was reason enough to trust his every word and feel calmer around him.

“You care so much about me,” Mydei pointed out almost innocently, just stating something that was as plain as day.

Phainon blinked a few times and smiled, a little confused. “Am I supposed… not to?”

“It’s just baffling,” Mydei answered, right before sighing. “Someone who can barely look after himself is worrying this much about me?”

Now that he thought about it, what kind of impression did Mydei have of him? Sure, he didn’t expect anything from him, but he wasn’t helpless or unable to do a single thing on his own either. Maybe he just had to cook for him to show it to him. He definitely could turn around that thought, right?

It would have been a problem for another day. A day that would have come soon, but right now he had other, more pressing matters to lay out to Mydei and obsessively think about for the next several hours.

“It’s not so difficult to comprehend,” he stated slowly, letting his thoughts fall in the right places. He needed the correct words that properly explained his feelings, and he wasn't willing to fail at that, of all things. He smiled at him, feeling his cheeks blushing from happiness and excitement. “Mydei, you're phenomenal. I want to devote myself to you, no matter how you feel… I want to help you feel better above all else.”

Mydei looked at him as they walked. He didn't look impressed, or embarrassed, or anything other than… observing. He simply seemed to be looking at him while his brain connected all the information he had on him and formed an analysis about him and his behaviour.

It was unnerving.

However, it only lasted a few seconds before he asked with a curious voice, “What about you?”

What about him? He would have been happy just helping Mydei and being allowed to be around him. He didn't need Mydei to worry about him– it would negate everything that he just said.

He wanted to help him, there would be no point in doing that if he ended up giving him more things to worry about.

“Me?” he asked, convinced that Mydei didn't fully understand his words. He knew that he wasn't stupid, but he could doubt how much he understood his intentions.

Of course, he could have worried about him and wanted to help him, but Phainon simply didn't think he needed it. Even if he struggled sometimes, he was able to get back up pretty quickly.

Mydei stopped walking quite abruptly in the middle of the road, still near the entrance of the place of their date, forcing Phainon to do the same.

He looked at him with something that resembled anger and worry, before pulling him to the side and laying the bag he was holding on the concrete, right next to them. His free hand now cupped his cheek, and Phainon immediately melted into the touch. It didn’t really matter whether he wanted to or not, Mydei’s warmth was always something special that he couldn’t help but indulge in.

“You don't take care of yourself, I doubt you care about what you need or what happens to you,” Mydei whispered as he rubbed his thumb against his skin. “Let me help with that.”

Phainon didn’t necessarily disagree, but he was doing that to lessen Mydei’s burden, not make it heavier.

Then again… Mydei could be feeling the same thing and he couldn’t deny it to him either.

“What's the point, then…” he whined, voicing his thoughts before he could stop them. He wasn’t particularly proud of feeling that way, but he said that he would be open with him and stop obfuscating issues or hiding them, so it didn’t have to be so bad, right?

Mydei looked at him and weakly smiled, almost softened by that answer. “The point is that you deserve love as well,” he stated, as if it was a simple fact that he didn’t think he would have to lay out to him. “I appreciate everything that you're doing, but I want to offer the same things to you.”

Phainon could just stare at him without words to offer. He wanted to believe him, he truly did, but he felt disgusting the second he thought about accepting that kind of care from him. Holding hands? Kissing? Touching? Sure, all those things were enjoyable and he didn’t have to think about much about anything whenever he did them. Trusting Mydei? A little harder, but he did nothing but try to gain his trust. Letting himself fall in his arms so directly simply because Mydei thought he deserved to be loved? Almost impossible.

It wasn’t his fault, Phainon inherently believed that he didn’t deserve it. What did he even do for him? Taking him out one night? Staying with his son for a while? Kissing him? None of it made him worthy of such pure feelings.

He heard a sigh right in front of him, and turned his attention to Mydei again. “You don't believe me,” he stated, tilting his head and letting his hand go to cross his arms over his chest.

“No!” Phainon lamented almost immediately. He was sure that he looked almost desperate, but the slight pushback he got right then scared him. Mydei was still there, but he still hated it. “I just… I believe you, Mydei. I don't know if I deserve it.”

He dropped his head in shame almost immediately after that. He didn’t want to admit it, he knew it was selfish and he knew everyone in his life hated it. Hyacine got upset on his behalf, Castorice didn’t know how to approach it and Cyrene’s words didn’t get to him most of the time. However, he didn’t know how Mydei would react to it.

Honestly, if he could, he would have run away instead of waiting long, silent moments between them only fearing Mydei’s reaction every passing second.

“Phainon.”

There it was. He wondered what he would say for a second. Maybe he would yell at him, or tell him that he does, indeed, deserve it with the same talking points everyone always used. You didn’t do anything to not deserve it. I really like you, so why don’t you accept it? Or something like that. 

He loathed it.

So much running around the issue in circles, when the issue had always been about so many others repeating it to him and only getting satisfaction when he was the one sacrificing for others, and he was fully aware of it. Simply put, he was never given a reason to believe anyone claiming that he deserved love because they always proved him wrong. They left, they hurt him, they only searched for him when they needed something out of him.

Mydei looked… different. He wasn’t avoiding the issue, he wanted to talk about it and saying that he deserved love as if it was an objective statement. A fact. There was no explanation for the reasons why he had to accept it, he laid it out as an option he had. A very valid one that Mydei would have liked him to pick because he wanted to offer it to him.

He expected a monologue, even if short. He expected words about how much he liked him, or how much it hurt him to see him refuse his affection like that, but none of it arrived.

Instead, Phainon raised his head to meet Mydei’s amber eyes and barely realized the quickest motion that he had ever seen him do.

All of a sudden, he was hugging him, hands around his torso and shoulders and head right next to his, faintly brushing his cheek with his hair.

It wasn't forceful, he kept him close with a gentle touch and extreme care, almost like a precious, fragile antique passed down for generations that absolutely couldn't break.

Phainon stood still for a second, still a little confused, but he hugged him back soon enough. If that was his reaction to what he told him, he was more than willing to accept it.

“Everyone deserves it, you're not an exception,” he whispered next to his ear, with such a soft and loving voice that Phainon was sure that he would explode. Then, Mydei held him more strongly for a couple of seconds. “If you ever tell me who made you believe you're so inconsequential to not deserve love, I'm going to break their skull.”

Phainon laughed at that. He barely even cared about his hand not being held, or the reaction Mydei could have had to a few of his raw feelings now– the possibility of being abandoned, or his trust being broken, or to be judged were all vanished in the wind.

And it was all because Mydei didn't hesitate in showing him how he thought he deserved to be treated. Whether he was forcing himself to communicate it to him or not, he didn’t know, but he certainly felt it. The amount of care that he gave to him in those few hours was hard to ignore.

He laughed again as he felt Mydei bury his face in the crook of his neck, keeping him close in a somewhat possessive stance. It wasn’t too noticeable, but it felt like it. It wasn’t necessarily jealousy– nothing happened in the last few seconds that would make him jealous of anyone– but he could feel a tint of protectiveness in that hug. It wasn’t too obvious, but it was there, almost as if he was hesitant to show him the full extent of his feelings.

One day, maybe he will.

Phainon gently put aside those thoughts and caressed Mydei’s hair. “That is murder, Mydei,” he joked. Not that he didn’t like hearing that he would kill anyone that deeply hurt him, quite the contrary, but he was unsure whether Mydei was joking or not.

“And?” Mydei asked with a tired tone, too close to Phainon’s ear for him to think clearly.

Somehow, even if he had to close his eyes and take a deep breath to keep his composure, he was able to spit out an answer. “And you would go to jail.”

“And?”

“... And I can't see you every day and you'd be so lonely without me?”

“Ha,” Mydei half laughed, finally raising his head off of his shoulder. He finally looked at Phainon again, nodding. “It would be rather boring without you there, but at least you would believe that guy was an asshole and you deserve more than to believe in the words of someone that clearly doesn’t care about you.”

Phainon couldn’t keep himself from smiling. He wasn’t trying to validate his position in the matter, he didn’t tell him that he could absolutely trust him, but that he should stop the words of people that weren’t in his life anymore.

Mydei was in his life and he was trying to help him, unlike them. He showed him that he cared, that he wanted him in his life, that he wished him to be someone that his son could rely on, that he wanted to trust. Who was Phainon to betray and ignore all those honest feelings that were being poured onto him?

He wanted to accept all of them. He wanted to trust him. And he would have tried harder than ever before, just because he didn’t want Mydei to believe that those feelings were misplaced. His abandonment issues be damned, he found someone that earnestly accepted him and he had full intentions of putting in as much effort as possible to maintain that relationship.

Phainon couldn’t resist the urge to kiss him, after that realization. He wrapped his arms around his torso and held him closer, before diving in to kiss him again. 

At first, he felt Mydei’s body hesitating, his lips freezing and his muscles tensing, but he gave in shockingly quickly. His lips started moving following his lead and his arms shifted to lay on his shoulders, lazily hanging there. Phainon quietly opened his eyes, content with just being able to witness his eyes fluttering close and the slight blush on his cheeks. 

Mydei really was so, so unbelievably cute.

Phainon smiled as he lightly bit on his lower lip, only for Mydei to deepen the kiss for a few seconds. So he liked that. Important information duly noted.

He smiled one last time before letting him go, watching as he opened his eyes again. Phainon couldn’t believe it himself either, but this might be the first time that he found someone just as into him as he was in them. They didn’t even know each other much– sure, they texted all day and called often, other than having gone out two other times, but they didn’t really know each other– and yet, he still liked Phainon like no one else did before.

It was subtle, but he showed it plenty enough for him to accept and embrace it.

Mydei grabbed the bag from the ground, checking inside if the food was still intact and hot, probably to know if it needed a few adjustments and if he could place it in the fridge already. Phainon just stared, patiently waiting for him to finish. Honestly, he was content to just do that. Stand there and witness whatever he did, admiring him as he casually relaxed around him.

He was sure that the warm feeling in his chest would have continued and he would have kept on readily accepting it and craving a little bit more of it every single time.

“Is there still Ptolemy at your place?” he asked, intertwining his fingers with Mydei’s, a motion that seemed natural now. That conversation undid the knots in the back of his mind and incinerated every doubt he had about approaching Mydei. It was as if a lock was turned, and he felt free enough to at least relax around him and earnestly love him.

There was a lot he still felt that he had to think about, communicate and fix, somehow, but it wasn't a problem now. Feeling like being able to openly love him was enough.

Mydei nodded, turning towards him. “Yes. And my child. We aren't fucking tonight, Phainon.”

Phainon whined, much akin to the one of a dog being denied food. “Buuut we will,” he tried his luck, smiling at him with pleading eyes. “At some point? Right, Mydei?”

All he got was the hint of a smile and a huff way too similar to a laugh.  “Let’s go back. Our child awaits.”

Our child? Our child?

Mydei perfectly knew what he was doing. Teasing him by including him to such a level was… unhinged. Not something he would expect from him, from what he knew of him. And yet, he fully knew that it was working. He liked being included in Astraea's life just as much as he did in Mydei's and he was excited about going back and seeing how he was doing.

Maybe, it was partly the nature of his job, but he genuinely cared about that child in a way that he never did with the other children in his care. He had to keep distance with them, he had to keep those feelings on the job without bringing them home, lest one of them tragically died and he couldn't do his job for every other child in his care.

Astraea wasn't his patient and he adored him for seemingly no reason. Sure, part of it was because Mydei liked him, but he seemed to genuinely love him and he couldn't find it in himself to not exchange those same feelings right back to him.

Phainon smiled at Mydei and happily fastened his pace as his arms drew long arches in the air. The blonde man was slightly confused at first, but he easily kept up the pace and followed him with no more hesitation.

“It's so easy to get you riled up,” Mydei observed, with a low whisper.

Phainon fully turned to look at him as he walked backwards. He smiled excitedly and beamed, “Just because it's you!”

Mydei smiled back at him and closed the distance between them, quickly kissing him on the lips. It was just for a moment, but it was so casual that it tugged at Phainon's heart all the same. The simple fact that he was indulging him so often made him feel peaks of happiness that he had never felt before.

A kind warmth spread in his chest as Mydei still refused to let go of his hand even when he was unlocking the door of his apartment. He smiled, happily waiting for the door to open, and followed him after he heard the ‘click’ of the lock.

It was right after they got to his floor that Mydei let go. Phainon understood why– the date was over, they probably had to take care of Astraea, Mydei had to see off his friend– but it still hurt. The touch still lingered on the back of his hand and his skin frizzled for a few seconds.

Ah, that would become a problem. The prospect of having to go through work and the rest of the day without Mydei was already something he didn't even want to think about.

Mydei smiled and nodded at Ptolemy once they were inside the apartment, with him doing the same with him. “Thank you so much, Ptolemy,” he added as well.

“Don’t even mention it!” Ptolemy waved his hand to dismiss such a polite sentence. “Astraea took a few tries, but he’s sleeping now. He wanted to wait up to say hi, at some point. He’s adorable.”

“He is,” Mydei agreed, before accompanying him to the door. “Thank you again.”

With a smile, he left and closed the door behind him, leaving them alone once again.

Phainon looked around him, a little lost in his thoughts. At least, the child did end up sleeping, but it was bothering him that it didn't work as well as he had hoped.

Maybe he was a fool in thinking such deep trauma could be healed just with a plushie.

“The plushie helped a little, at least…” he murmured to himself, still trying to come to terms that they would have had to try something else now.

However, Mydei, ever his saviour, intervened instead of the wires in his brain that he already knew way too much. “It's the first time he has to sleep without me in the house… it's bound to be more difficult,” he explained, before smiling at him. “Your plushie is helping him every day, don't worry about it.”

Phainon let out a sigh of relief that he didn’t know he was holding. Maybe he cared too much about that child, but that plushie was nearly impossible to find anymore! He managed to find one because he wanted to buy it for Astraea because it reminded him of Mydei– and sure, a lot of things now reminded him of Mydei, but he liked it too, so his mission was successful.

He naturally would have been a tiny bit sad if not even that could help him, because that meant that it was something much, much deeper than what either of them thought and he didn’t want him to resort to meds at such a young age. If it could be fixed in other ways, he would have gladly taken the chance.

For now, a plushie and supportive adults around him were enough, and that was the best outcome for him.

Phainon yawned again, suddenly feeling his tiredness back at full force. He just had the strength to thank every deity up there that it was a Saturday and he was about to spend the night in a warm bed with Mydei. Absolutely the best emergency nap he’s ever had.

“What a sight. The child is awake and the adult is about to fall asleep against the wall,” Mydei noted, back from putting away the food they took back home. Phainon knew that he was talking about him and Astraea, but he didn’t care much. He could barely stay upright and the fact that he didn’t fall to the ground yet was a miracle.

He heard a light laugh in front of him, then strong arms pulled him in, carefully letting his head rest against a shoulder. “Take a nap before a date with the guy you want to be partners with, not after,” Mydei whispered, as a way to tease him a little.

Phainon just let out a tired whine, before the cogs in his brain started turning properly and understood what he said earlier. The child was awake meant that…

He immediately squeezed his eyes a couple of times to force himself awake and got up from Mydei’s body. Looking at his right, he saw Astraea, a little tired but very much awake and standing right there, plushie clutched to his chest.

“Mama?” he asked, still gently rubbing his eyes. “Wanna see you and Phai before going to bed…”

Maybe Phainon should stop noticing just how often he mentioned him whenever he brought up Mydei as well. The fact that he already accepted him in his life so earnestly made him so happy. It wasn’t ecstasy, it was different from the bolts and shocks he got from being with Mydei– it was calmer and more subtle, almost like a quiet presence that soothed every muscle in his body. Seeing him made him content and relieved more than anything else.

He watched as Mydei moved towards him and crouched down right in front of him. “Hey,” he whispered, letting him crash on his arms, brushing his head from right to left against his chest. He smiled and left an affectionate kiss on the top of his head. “You did a good job tonight.”

That, he definitely did. Of course, Mydei worked hard to soften the blow for when it would have actually happened, but Astraea definitely put in a lot of effort just so they could have a few dates outside of the house and on their own too. He had to question if he truly knew more than he thought, but he guessed that he had understood that much prior to his meeting with Mydei.

Not that it wasn’t impressive, he knew he was very smart, but most children who were so perceptive had to grow up a little too quickly due to the circumstances around them. Thinking about it after seeing how Mydei treated him was upsetting, but he didn’t speak about it. He doubted any of them needed to hear him ramble about something that they all knew already.

However, that didn’t mean that his desire to be there for him wavered. If anything, it just got more persistent.

“Phai!”

The child’s voice made him blink to reality again, just to witness shiny, excited and happy light brown eyes staring back at him, adorned by the cutest smile he had ever seen. Phainon immediately walked towards him, almost as a reflex. He didn’t blame Mydei for pampering him as much as he did, he was adorable and it had to be almost impossible to tell him no.

“Look at who we have here!” Phainon beamed, crouching down next to Mydei. “It’s way past your bedtime, isn’t it?”

Astraea pressed his lips together, but nodded. Big brown eyes travelled back to him, almost afraid of what he would say next. Did he think he was scolding him? That wasn’t his intention, but he couldn’t really take those words back. So, he decided to do the best out of that situation.

Not that he was planning to go anywhere else– and he certainly didn’t want to scold him, it was just an observation, but it didn’t land as well as he had hoped– but since he was there, he figured that he would offer another solution he had lying in the back of his mind.

Phainon smiled gently at him, relaxing as much as he could to make him understand that he meant no harm. “Have you ever tried taking chamomile before going to bed?” he quietly asked, slightly tilting his head.

The child blinked a couple of times. “Chamo… what?”

He definitely didn’t and he wondered how Mydei didn’t think of it yet. It was pretty easy to make and it often did the job. Maybe he just tried tea and, since it didn’t work, he dropped it entirely.

However, chamomile was special. He knew why, what there was in it and what made it such an effective bedtime beverage, but it was something beyond what he had learned in his studies.

Call him foolish, maybe even stupid, but it reminded him of his childhood. Maybe it wasn't a very happy childhood, sure, but he remembered how relaxed he was after drinking his sister's chamomile.

It was a fond memory, and that beverage helped him go to bed dozens of times as a child, no matter how bad his insomnia got. It had always helped him, at least a little bit and even when he couldn't fall asleep. Maybe it would have worked for Astraea as well.

Phainon smiled at him, then explained, “It’s a magic drink that helps you sleep.”

Of course, it wasn't magic. But for Astraea it would have been, for a little while.

The child looked at him with sheer wonder in his eyes, nearly shining as he registered what he just said. As soon as his brain computed it, he bounced in his place and smiled up at Mydei.

Surely, he will be happy to know that Phainon just solved another problem and Astraea was now going to ask for chamomile every single night and he would have had to say no at some point.

If he had the strength to. A much needed training for when he will ask for more expensive things than just tea or a few toys.

“Mama!” Astraea yelled, his voice full of unrestrained excitement.

Mydei, on the other hand, just sighed and caressed him on the head. “I’ll prepare some.”

Of course he would. The fact that he couldn't say no to his son was an issue, yes, but something that Phainon thoroughly enjoyed seeing.

A father that always put his child on the top of his priorities was something that he always thought of as very attractive. Maybe it was weird, but he genuinely thought that! And he liked Mydei for other things too! Simply put… he liked seeing him parenting Astraea with so much kindness and conviction.

Phainon smiled as he watched him walking away to the kitchen, followed by his child. He gathered the strength to stand up as well and walked after them, stopping by the counter next to where Mydei was preparing what he needed. He wondered for a second why he had everything already, but a quick glance to the kid blasted a brilliant idea in his mind.

“So you know the secret formula too, Mydei? Did the fairies teach it to you?” he asked, tilting his head in obviously fake curiosity.

Astraea didn’t know, though, and he noticed his head suddenly snap towards them, interested in their conversation. He looked like a tiny hare with his ears perked up after hearing a sudden sound around them, a second before running away. That child didn’t even know how cute he was, much like his father. A cute parent and an even cuter child.

However, the reason why he mentioned fairies wasn’t just for Astraea to perceive chamomile as some sort of magic spell– his first objective was teasing Mydei and, judging by the silence, it was working.

“... Yes,” Mydei answered, after a long silence. 

He didn’t add anything else, but it was enough for Astraea to excitedly move his legs as he was sitting on a chair, big eyes focused on Mydei’s figure, impatiently waiting silently for that seemingly magic drink that would have solved his insomnia. 

Phainon smiled and moved to gently caress the top of his head, somehow making him aware of how much he was moving. He slowed down, but he didn’t stop because he was too excited to try out actual magical food, apparently.

Children truly are special little things.

As soon as Mydei gave him the drink, he blew on it a couple of times and gobbled it down as if he didn’t drink water for two weeks. Next to him, a quiet laugh warmed the room and Phainon didn’t even have to turn to know whose it was. 

By that point, if he didn’t know how Mydei’s laugh felt like, whether he remembers its sound properly or not, he didn’t deserve to sit in that same room.

However, he turned anyway to look at him and see how Astraea was doing, just to see the child already asleep on his shoulder. “Out like a light,” he commented, with a slightly amused smile on his face. “Always works.”

“Thank you,” Mydei whispers, faintly smiling at him. “Let’s go to bed.”

Great idea. Honestly, Phainon didn’t even know how he was able to stay up so much in the first place, with his eyes already closing on their own. “Make way.”

He abandoned himself on the bed the second Mydei led him to it, dreading even just the prospect of having to change his clothes. Was it really necessary in the end? Did he really have to? He was so tired that he doubted he even cared where he slept. A mattress and a rock sounded about the same right now.

Phainon noticed Mydei walking in the room after putting Astraea to bed, and he was convinced that the look on his face couldn’t be described in any way other than disgust. In normal circumstances he would have cared about it, but now he couldn’t even be bothered to feel judged for it.

In a daze of his own mind, he smirked and teased, “You can just sleep on me, right?”

“You wish,” Mydei nonchalantly said, pushing him enough to make him roll over to one side.

He laughed lightly, almost like a child playing with a friend. “Mydei–”

“Don’t you dare turn around,” he immediately shut him down, with a voice grave enough that Phainon knew to respect his instructions without playing around it too much. It wasn’t angry, but it seemed serious and almost pleading to listen to him. 

Phainon settled and stood there still, waiting for what he wanted to do. Or say. He knew he had something in mind that he was way too embarrassed to do in front of him, or something along those lines. Maybe it was easier with him turned around, to avoid eye contact during that moment. He seemed to have some issues with that too, sometimes.

“I like you more like this,” he whispered, as his hand rested on Phainon’s shoulder. He was fully turned around, laying on his side, but he could picture a little shy smile decorating his face. “You’re annoying sometimes, but I can tell you’re more relaxed and happier. Don’t run away from yourself too much.”

Phainon’s skin crawled. Was he able to gather all that after a few dates? If Phainon wasn’t extremely scared after hearing that request– because he hated himself and he knew everyone else did too, if he didn’t put up some sort of honey tinted lie all around him– he would have asked him directly.

Instead, he tried to deny it.

“I’m not–”

“I don’t think I need to repeat myself,” Mydei sighed, before calmly getting under the sheets. Phainon figured he quickly changed as he was talking. “You already know what I mean. Just believe me when I say I prefer seeing you and not whatever other personality you carved for yourself. Even if I haven't seen all of it yet, I just need to be patient.”

Somehow, as he gave himself a few seconds to digest what Mydei was saying, Phainon felt almost content. He was the first to make such a request, and he could tell that he was being sincere. Trusting him was a good decision.

The heavy boulder on his chest slowly disappeared, giving him the chance to gather his courage and sit up, looking around him. Beside him, he saw the clothes Mydei prepared for him and lazily started to change, fully aware that he was being watched with interested eyes. Maybe he was embarrassed about it, but the two facts didn’t exclude each other.

He honestly enjoyed knowing that Mydei found him attractive, in more ways than just one.

Phainon threw his clothes on a chair not far from there and stretched before falling on the bed again, tucking himself to sleep right beside Mydei. He smiled at him, a little hesitantly. “What a smooth talker, Mydeimos.”

He only sighed in response. “We’ll see who will win this bet, then.”

“Bet?” Phainon repeated, suddenly interested. “What’s the price?”

Mydei thought for less than a second before confidently suggesting, “Sex.”

Phainon was sure that his brain imploded upon hearing that word.

Sex? He wanted to have sex as a price for… getting to see his unfiltered, real personality? All the ugly things about himself were buried deep within himself and he did promise not to ever speak of them to anyone, but sex with Mydei? He would be lying if he wasn’t considering throwing all those promises out of the window.

His mouth moved slightly to say something in rebuttal, or maybe ask for an explanation, but Mydei acted way more swiftly and turned around, mumbling a little, “Goodnight.”

Phainon was immediately on his shoulder, lightly shaking it with his hands. “Mydei! You can’t just–”

“Sleep or I’ll call Castorice.”

He immediately stopped and laid at his side, unsure on where to keep his hands. Mydei didn’t seem like he managed sudden touches too well, so he thought about keeping them off of him to avoid making him uncomfortable.

Maybe, if he did it slowly…

His hand slowly touched his arm, then his shoulder, then his side, just to make itself known. Mydei only had a reaction to the first touch with just a quick shiver, so Phainon took it as a sign that he didn’t bother as much as he thought. He leaned against him, an arm sliding under his head– and Mydei even lifted it slightly to help him, showing himself happy with his initiative– and the other hanging from his side and laying against his chest. 

From that position, he could feel his smell of honey and pomegranates, intoxicatingly sweet. Phainon didn’t think about much at all right after that, letting the warmth and that extraordinarily nice smell lull him to sleep. He always had issues with it, that was why he kept on skipping naps and not sleeping enough, but it was never as easy as he felt right in that moment. He fell asleep as easily as he used to do when he was younger, in a place that he regarded as safe.

And, for the first time in those past few years, he hoped desperately that he would lose a bet.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

“Are you the kisser type, Mydei?” he asked, giving him a meek smile.
Mydei knit his eyebrows together, almost as if that was a weird question to ask. “Is there something wrong with wanting to greet your boyfriend?”
“This is a greeting?”
“Until you decide to move in.”

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Phainon looked at his switched off phone as he was getting dressed, waiting for… anything, really. Anything to pop up on the black screen. One of Mydei's messages, if he had to choose what he wanted with precision.

It hasn't been a lot since their date, just a few days, but he already missed him. Nothing changed, apart from Mydei searching for him first instead of the contrary every once in a while to ask about his day and asking if he could call him after a long day of work.

He adored those quick moments.

Apparently, Mydei still liked teasing him about being Astraea's father because he kept on telling him about what he did or said, and the little child often asked to talk to him when he could.

Sometimes he really wished to just live at his place, even if he fully knew that the living conditions there weren't optimal. It was already too small for two people, let alone three.

So, he just sat there. Yearning to be there instead. Cuddling with him and playing with his child.

If Astraea ever called him any variation of father at any point in his life, he was sure that he would have certainly died.

However, no message arrived, and Phainon left his room with a sigh. He missed his dates with Mydei and the times he'd play and talk with that little child… maybe he should volunteer to babysit for him every once in a while. He wouldn't die of boredom and he would actually be able to do something about it.

Slowly walking to the living room, he found Castorice and Hyacine dressed properly to go out, maybe a date or an outing. Given how relaxed both of them were, Phainon tended to believe the second option.

Hyacine noticed his presence in the room and smiled at him, kindly and pleased to know he was now keeping them company. “Phai! Do you want to go out with me and Cassie today?”

“I’m going to go from the high of kissing the love of my life to being the third wheel for the most beautiful relationship on the planet?” he jokingly answered, coming closer to hug her. She always smelled of fresh flowers and her clothes were soft and colorful.

If someone told him that she was a walking cloud, he would have believed it.

Castorice smiled at the both of them as she was fixing her hair with her fingers and suggested, “Invite Mydei too, then.”

Phainon froze for a second, enough that Hyacine had to kindly move him from his position leaning on her. He almost didn’t notice, as all his attention was stuck on Castorice’s voice replaying in his head. It was true, he could call Mydei and ask if he wanted to join them, but he didn’t want to forcefully move faster than he should have when the development of their relationship was dangerously quick already.

However, Mydei would have been probably fine with it. He had made it his mission to remind him that he was happy where he was now and that he cared about him being present in his life so, even if Phainon didn’t fully believe it, he could at least respect his wishes.

A sigh escaped from Hyacine’s lips as she took a step back from him. “Invite him,” she said, holding up her open hand. “I’ll give you five minutes!”

He had said it several times by now, but he would absolutely be lost without his best friend by his side.

With a quick nod of his head, Phainon ran in his room again and picked up his phone, quickly sending a message to Mydei and hoping that he was in the mood to go out. Even if they’d be with others, he simply wanted to see him again.

phai☀️: mydei ^-^

phai☀️: do you want to go out today?

phai☀️: with cas and her girlfriend 

mydei🐱: Sure.

mydei🐱: What do you plan on doing?

Oh, he just answered immediately. That had to be a good thing, right? Was he about to text him as well? Did he miss him, even? Every little question that popped in his head could just be explained with the fact that yes, he did miss him and yes, he wanted to go out and talk to him despite how hard work had been lately for him.

Phainon felt so much love from just those two messages, even if they were such a normal way to answer anyone asking if they wanted to go out. It felt something that they were so used to do, and he was in love with the thought that it was going to be their future now.

It was stupid and childish, but it extremely excited him all the same.

phai☀️: probably just buying some things and walking around the city !!!!

mydei🐱: I’m in.

mydei🐱: Can Astraea tag along?

Could his adorable child that Phainon loved and missed dearly as well? If it was up to him, he wouldn’t have even thought about it. However, he wasn’t the only one in that outing, so he had to stop his brain in time, walk over the the living room and ask, “Hyacine, he asks if his son can come too.”

Saying that the girl didn’t jump up with joy and sparkling eyes upon hearing the question would have been an understatement. “Yes! He's such a cute child,” she nodded excitedly, earnestly happy to know she will be seeing him again.

Phainon smiled at that reaction, but he couldn’t say that wasn’t what he felt as well when he did get to see him. That little child was so easy to love, after all.

phai☀️: approved :3

phai☀️: i'll come pick you up !!!

mydei🐱: How nice of you.

mydei🐱: Glad to see you again so soon as well.

Oh… maybe Phainon was just in love with this man.

It was largely irrational, they hadn’t known each other for that long and he wasn’t planning on telling Mydei any time soon, but he was always thinking of him and all his possible thoughts were long past just a crush– hell, he wanted to be his kid’s father, that alone was enough ground to stop using that word.

In the last few days, though, he didn’t think he had ever felt so much affection towards him since he lived with his older sister, and even then Cyrene had a very different kind of way to care for and love him than Mydei. The intensity, however, was similar. Cyrene’s was gentler and Mydei’s was fiercer, but they both felt… steady. Ever-present. Truthful.

That was the kind of presence that Phainon had wished to experience for years, to finally being able to start trusting someone else to the fullest of his abilities. He was beyond happy that it happened to be Mydei.

phai☀️: mydei……

mydei🐱: [Photo attached] Take this as motivation to speed up.

Phainon almost dropped his phone to the ground in disbelief as soon as he saw that picture. It was obviously taken by someone else, but he didn’t even care that another person got to experience that moment instead of him at that moment. It was Mydei kneeling in his apartment and with his firefighter uniform on– which on its own was enough to make him drop his phone, really– and a very happy Astraea standing in between his legs and looking up at him, small hands reaching up to his face and strawberry blonde hair almost touching the ground. Mydei was gently smiling at him and his cheeks were lit up in a content blush as well, as if the rest wasn’t enough.

He knew perfectly that he sent it to tease him, but part of his mind couldn’t help but notice how much love he had for that child. Of course, he was bound to and he already knew that he was ready to sacrifice everything for him, but seeing it in full display like that was, for one, adorable, and it displayed just how much affection he had both for him and his son. He had enough for both of them, and probably even more in store to give to all his friends.

Mydei really was a wonderful person. Even if he might have issues and problems that he would find more about in the future, he had always tried his best with him, and that was all that mattered to him.

He quickly typed an answer, unable to get that picture out of his head. He honestly couldn't believe that he was so lucky to have all his wishes to finally be answered properly.

After greeting his roommates and telling them they'd meet halfway through, he decided to use that time for a quick run to get over to Mydei's house. After all, he asked him to hurry up to get there.

This time, though, he mostly ignored everything around him. He didn't care about much of anything that wasn't Mydei, just because he missed him and getting to see him again was his number one priority. He wouldn't have been mad, however, if Astraea opened the door instead. He missed him just as much and he was beyond happy being able to spend some time with him again.

As soon as he reached the building and noticed that the door was open, maybe Mydei already thinking about it or someone else forgot to close it upon going in or out, but it didn’t matter much. His steps quickened as he walked up the stairs, only abruptly stopping when his body almost slammed into Mydei’s, leaning by the doorframe of his apartment.

He was looking at his phone, but the quick succession of the steps so close to him made him raise his head to look at the man in front of him, no particular expression reflected in his golden eyes. Phainon smiled happily at the sudden attention and he quickly moved to hug him, his heart almost stopping entirely when he felt an arm wrapping itself around his waist, keeping him in place.

Staying time away from Mydei– albeit not too much, but it was still time without him— especially after their last date was obviously killing him. One second seeing him again and he was already feeling so much better than any other day in his life combined.

“That was faster than last time,” Mydei joked, leaving a soft kiss on his forehead, between his silver bangs. Phainon cursed himself for not taking the opportunity to kiss him right there and then instead of a simple hug– he was so excited about seeing him again and he sort of forgot that he could do that now.

For better or worse, though, his boyfriend absolutely didn’t pass on the occasion.

He felt soft, sporadic kisses on his cheeks and jaw, then his neck and chin. Basically anywhere where Mydei could reach from his position, but they weren’t too many, nor forceful in any way. They felt like a nice, sweet reminder of their relationship and the point where they were at now, almost declaring that presence directly on his skin.

Phainon let out a few giggles as he welcomed all the kisses, and his hands wrapped around his unmistakably large shoulders. When he could finally look at him, he leaned in and smiled as he whispered, “You gave me pretty good motivation.”

Mydei immediately closed the distance between them, maybe tired of the dance they've been doing for a few weeks now with some rare exceptions, or maybe just because he was at his limit and he was missing him too much. Either way, they ended up kissing and Phainon didn't want it to stop.

At first, it was a pretty calm kiss– demanding, but secure on its footing. Then, Phainon bit on Mydei's upper lip and forced him to deepen the kiss, letting out a few whimpers in the process, but never slowing down.

Neither of them backed down, seemingly having some kind of challenge over who could resist the most. Phainon absolutely didn't mind kissing Mydei for a bit longer, though.

They changed angles, kissed deeper and slower, faster and more delicately. Phainon was sure that he was in heaven. Even when Mydei broke the kiss and slid to the side of his neck, Phainon was taking it all in, bathing in those kisses all the same.

He even hoped that Mydei would get a little selfish and leave a few marks.

“Ah, Mydei… did you miss me that much?” Phainon managed to say in between the feeling of wet lips leaving little reminders on his skin, without staying too much or too little. Just enough for his body to remember every single place touched by that kind of affection.

“Mhm,” Mydei mumbled against his skin, leaving one last kiss before looking at him again. Phainon was unsure whether he was dissatisfied or relived that he just stopped kissing him and turned to talk to him. “The other night I slept so well that I was about to ask you to come over every evening after that.”

He would have. Anything to stay with Mydei more often, and even better if it involved sleeping with him.

“And why didn't you?” Phainon asked with a slightly hoarse voice, words pronounced with a somewhat teasing tone as well.

Mydei bit his lower lip and smiled, before leaning in again, but kept himself away from his lips enough to tease him back. “Self preservation.”

Phainon smiled as he looked first at his golden eyes, then down to his lips, before rubbing his hand on his shoulder and whispering, “I can stay over tonight. If you want.”

He was teasing him, he expected him to tease him back with something else, but that wasn’t what happened. Instead, Mydei leaned in again and kissed him, holding him a little closer. Phainon whined into the kiss, surprised that it was even happening again so fast and so suddenly, but he accepted the gesture right afterwards.

If Mydei wanted to kiss him, who was he to tell him no? It was nice and he enjoyed knowing that his mere presence and a few attempts at teasing got him so worked up that he couldn’t help but kissing him so often and with so much persistence.

This time, though, the kiss wasn’t as long as the first time, and Phainon found himself off of Mydei after just a few seconds. It wasn’t a problem, he told himself. After all, he could very easily just tease him as a response.

“Are you the kisser type, Mydei?” he asked, giving him a meek smile.

Mydei knit his eyebrows together, almost as if that was a weird question to ask. “Is there something wrong with wanting to greet your boyfriend?”

“This is a greeting?”

“Until you decide to move in.”

Phainon’s saliva got stuck in his throat upon hearing that answer. He coughed a few times, but he barely managed to survive those last two seconds. Living together. After three dates. Maybe he wasn’t the one running too much in this relationship.

What even was his line of thinking? He thought that sleeping at his place was too much and too fast and now he wanted to move in together? With his son? Mydei was going to effectively kill him one of those days.

“And I'm going too fast?” he managed to jokingly ask, nervously hoping that he actually meant it and it wasn’t just something he absent-mindlessly suggested. Even in that case, it made him feel warm and feverish all the same– just the fact that there was a thought around it was enough for him to feel something almost uncomfortably moving inside him.

It wasn’t unwanted, it was just unexpected. However, Phainon liked thinking about that possibility in the near future more than he would have ever admitted to himself.

Mydei let out a soft laugh, finally letting him go as he backed down in a welcoming motion, inviting him in. “We’ll see if you stick around enough to see such a development.”

He said that when they were talking about being together, Phainon noted. Maybe it was just something he was used to saying to a romantic interest of his to push them to take more initiative, but otherwise he liked it. It always sounded like a challenge and Phainon loved it.

There would have been an answer on his part too, if a little familiar redhead appeared in his field of vision. Phainon smiled as the kid’s eyes started shining the second they saw him, and he crouched down to catch him after he sprinted in his arms. Such a cute child.

“Phai!” he beamed, practically yelling next to his ear. Phainon didn’t mind too much, he was happy to know how excited he was to see him again as well.

“Oh, hey, honeybuns!” Phainon smiled, leaving an affectionate kiss on his cheek, getting a somewhat confused giggle in response. “How are you doing?”

Instead of answering as he always did, though, Astraea blinked and slightly tilted his head to the side. “What does that mean?” he asked, obviously referring to the nickname.

It was nothing, really, just something Phainon had been thinking about in the past few days. How much he resembled a bunny and why both he and Mydei were so off track when thinking of him in any other way or why he reminded both of them of each other at the same time. They needed to remind each other that, despite how easy it was to play house and pretend that he was their actual child… he just wasn’t. He grew up with other people and had a specific personality that neither of them had a hand in, for the most part.

“Mh… nothing! Your hair is just like honey and you're as cute as a bunny,” Phainon explained, without going into it more than needed. He was sure that Mydei would have asked him a few more questions, but Astraea only needed to know those few facts.

The child nodded, visibly happy, and ran off to finish whatever it was that he was doing before Phainon arrived, and he luckily didn’t think about it too much past that.

“It’s a cute nickname,” Mydei noted, from behind him.

Phainon turned and saw him just standing there, waiting for him to have his moment with his child, as he was trying to sort out what looked like quite a lot of bags, maybe choosing the one to use for shopping in a few minutes. It felt so domestic and natural that Phainon tried not to think about it.

“I’m glad you like it too!” he just opted to say, showing him a rather satisfied smile. Or, at least, that was what he wanted him to see.

“He is a bunny, now that you point it out,” Mydei reflected, crossing his arms as he swung the empty bag on his shoulder. “He’s very reserved, but energetic and excited whenever he's happy. Bunny describes him well.”

As if that little name summoned him all of a sudden, Astraea appeared from behind the door frame, plushie in hand and fully dressed to go outside, and walked towards Mydei. “Mama, where are we going now?” he asked, golden eyes patient and curious.

They really were so similar to Mydei’s, only a little darker. They were deep honey, while his father’s resembled amber or a beautiful, clear sunset.

Mydei crouched down and smiled, tucking some of his hair behind his ears and otherwise fixing a few stray hairs out of place. “Some shopping with Phainon’s friends.”

“Hyacine will be there too,” Phainon added, figuring they'd both remember her even if they met her just once. Hyacine usually left some kind of impression on others.

Astraea slightly tilted his head. “The doctor?”

Mydei, on his part, sighed as he stood back up instead. “Is she Castorice’s girlfriend?” he asked, not finding it hard to put two and two together.

“Yeah!” Phainon smiled at the mention of his other friend. “They’re honestly really cute.”

His boyfriend just nodded and hummed as a way to signal that he understood, but he didn't do it say much else on the matter. Instead, he chose to focus on letting his son put on a jacket in case it was a little breezy outside.

“Mama,” Astraea called, raising the plushie in his hands, “can he come too?”

“Sure, this can be his first adventure,” Mydei conceded, with the sweetest voice that Phainon had ever heard in his life. “But keep him close, okay? We don’t want him to get lost or feel abandoned, right?”

Astraea shook his head and clutched the plushie close to his chest again, listening to every word that his father said and carrying them close to his heart as much as he could.

Phainon smiled and kneeled next to the child, affectionately petting his head. “Still without a name?” he asked when he saw him look up at him.

He turned and refuged in his arms again, as Phainon accepted him in an embrace. “It’s hard…” he mumbled, a little ashamed of the fact that the little thing still didn't have a name for himself.

Phainon left a kiss on the top of his head and waited for the child to look up to him. Those eyes were always curious and full of wonder, but so trusting in him too. Adorable, intelligent child.

“It’s fine,” Phainon reassured him, running a hand delicately through his hair that he couldn't help but notice that was perfectly taken care of. “Take your time choosing it, it’s very important.”

The child nodded excitedly and pulled his hand towards the door, already opened by Mydei. “Let’s go!”

Phainon laughed, standing up and following him obediently, first down the stairs and then out of the building, Mydei following them closely behind. Luckily for him, Astraea stopped pulling and just held his hand, just keeping up with his pace.

That child was far too excited about him being there for anyone's well-being.

And now, he was alone with Mydei as well… not that they had been with anyone else every time they managed to spend some time together, but he did miss this. Just feeling him close as they hung out was making his head spin and his heart beat faster.

Maybe he should ask a few questions now that he could, though. They've been hammering into his brain for the past few days, and he needed to know the answer.

Maybe it was stupid. Mydei probably wasn't even thinking about it, but he needed some kind of official statement or he will end up thinking that it was his mind playing tricks on him.

“So…” Phainon dramatically started, already noticing Mydei’s nerves tensing as soon as he used that tone of voice. Of course, he knew that he would have had to listen to something absurdly obvious that his dear maybe-boyfriend made up last minute. “Where do we stand now?”

“Are you dumb?” Mydei’s prude answer made Phainon’s head drop in an apologetic motion, already knowing that would have been his reaction. The blonde let out an exhausted sigh. “We’re together, of course.”

“Like… a couple?”

“... Yes, Phainon. I called you my boyfriend earlier.”

Right. He did do that. And Phainon did too, in his head, but he wanted to be sure, since they didn’t officialize anything since they had that kiss.

Maybe the making out on his doorstep could have been an indicator.

Mydei huffed, stopping to walk and grabbing his arm to force him to halt him in his steps and to look at him. He didn’t look upset, just a certain type of disappointed that Phainon couldn’t quite grasp. “You’re always like this. I kissed you for several minutes, asked you to move in with me and sleep with me more often, and you still think I don’t want this to last?”

He was right, he understood his point of view and he caught why he was so annoyed. It was his fault for thinking that he would need any other affirmation for it than all the ones that he got already in the last few days. However, he was thankful that Mydei still gave him what he asked for, even when he didn’t think he even deserved it.

“Phai is going to stay more often?” Astraea asked from below him, looking primarily at Mydei in search for the answer that he was hoping for.

“If he wants to,” he answered, looking back to Phainon with a knowing smile.

He took it all back. Mydei was evil incarnate and he hated him.

“Mydei,” he whined, pouting and putting on a scene to hope that maybe, maybe he would have stopped picking on him like that. All he got was obviously Astraea’s confused stare and Mydei’s impassible eyes. Obviously it didn’t work, so Phainon just kept on whining. “It’s not fair.”

“Is it not? No one is forcing you,” Mydei teased him further, his stance firm and his eyes still as serious as ever. “Just know that Astraea really wants you to.”

The child nodded excitedly and yelled, “Please!”

He was going to die.

He was going to die and it will all be Mydei’s fault. His ghost will definitely haunt him for the rest of his lifetime and then some more after his death just for this.

“Fine! Okay,” Phainon said in exasperation, “I’ll stay after this.”

Astraea happily bobbled his head left to right and bounced on his spot a few times, while Mydei let go of his arm and gave him something similar to a smile. It wasn’t one, his eyes just softened and he had a satisfied expression, but nothing more and Phainon was unsure whether he was picking on him or not.

Either way, he didn’t mention it and he started walking again, in relative silence until Mydei spoke up. All in all, he didn’t hate the quiet and he didn’t feel uncomfortable in the slightest, but he was happy to otherwise talk to Mydei any time.

However, he didn’t expect the impossibly sweet and soft tone that he used. Or the topic he brought up, for that matter, even if it was awfully obvious why he did.

“One day I will ask what happened,” he walked closer to him and whispered, his finger silently brushing against his wrist, right where he could feel his veins. “You don’t look ready to talk about it now, so I won’t force you to.”

Phainon truly, honestly thought that he was dreaming. Apart from his voice— which still felt as if it could disappear in just a few seconds, were he not attentive enough to catch it— his touch lingering there, as if it was a stark reminder of his presence and will to stay close to him, and his words clearly full of care and intent devoted into making him feel wanted were just too much for his poor little heart.

Mydei, however, was worried about something that he didn’t deem as too important to even refrain from answering.

“It’s nothing too big. Many people apparently just don’t like my personality,” he calmly answered, with an apologetic smile. He wasn’t saying the entire truth, but the thing that so many people hated was part of his personality anyway, so what was the harm in phrasing it that way?

They hated his overworking tendencies, how competitive he was, how much he valued his job and his friends above all else, how closed off he truly was instead of the happy-go-lucky guy that everyone liked much, much better. Was that not part of his personality? More than that, was it not who he truly was?

He was used to it being criticized, but after so many years focusing on his studies and how reliant he was on being satisfied because of them, he struggled to completely let go of the need to work so often. His childhood wasn’t the brightest, he didn’t have friends except his sister, and working hard was the only way he could feel some sort of satisfaction.

Unfortunately, stopping that behavior was way harder than he expected, and those were the consequences.

Phainon felt amber eyes falling on him, inspecting his every move after hearing those words. “Explain.”

“They like my body and the first few weeks, but they… back down after they find out what I’m really like,” Phainon explained, slowly. “So, they leave or find someone better for them and I’m kind of left with my thoughts.”
