He noticed the slight blush on his cheeks as well, maybe because they had never really discussed anything sexual between them yet, but he just took it in, satisfied that, based on Mydei’s words and actions, he would be the only one able to see and prompt such a reaction.

If he had a dog’s tail, he’d start wagging happily just about now.

In response, Mydei just sighed, letting go of the clothes he was supposedly looking at and raised his head again, tilting it slightly to look at Phainon. He still had his cheeks slightly darker, but the blush was barely noticeable now and the scowl on his face was tremendously adorable. “It’s not the time or place to discuss something like my tastes–”

“So you like it!” Phainon beamed immediately, taking a step closer and invading his personal space again. He didn’t know why exactly, but what Mydei told him and how he stared at him when he moved his hair out of his vision earlier made him so utterly confident and clingy without even caring anymore about the fact that he might be abandoned. Not at the moment, at the very least.

Maybe he was being a little too hopeful, but Mydei never went back on his words so far, and he had so many reasons and opportunities to drop him in the middle of nowhere and going on with his life– but he didn’t. He was still with him, helping him choose new clothes, sharing his life with him, letting him try and care for his son, kissing him in public so fiercely, being so open with all kinds of affectionate gestures.

There was still the looming danger in the back of his mind, but in that moment he tried to ignore it to the best of his abilities. He promised that he wouldn’t leave him, he demonstrated that he meant every single word he said, he had no other choice than to believe him and hope that he wouldn’t fuck it all up by himself.

Mydei, on his part, was blissfully unaware of what he was thinking at the moment, and he just shoved the pants he found on his chest, slightly pushing him half a step back from where he was standing. “... Try on the clothes.”

Phainon hummed as he caught them, not even questioning his sudden behavior. “Why don’t you help me with–”

Another shove to his shoulder, a little weaker, almost got him off of his feet.

“Message received!” Phainon yelled, running away to disappear with… the rather big amount of clothes that he picked for him. He didn’t realize it before, but he did pick up a lot of them. Enough for a full fit for a night out. If he wanted to pay for them, he would have had to physically stop him.

He looked for a brief moment to what he had there and he quickly started to put them on. Black turtleneck with the half of a sun on the edge of the neck where the fabric ended, a white shirt, a deep blue trench-coat with rather large sleeves and little golden-like chains on the left part of his chest, white jeans, somehow a black thigh garner– of course Mydei was staring at his thighs while he picked up this outfit– with a cute… horned animal made of silver on it.

It all seemed way too expensive for him to spend it in clothes. That wasn’t absolutely something that Phainon would get out of a day out with friends. And his boyfriend. It still felt surreal calling him that.

Regardless, he did put it on and, admittedly, Mydei was right. He did objectively look good in black and blue. It was almost shocking how well he could make up that outfit in the matter of a few minutes.

With a satisfied sigh, he turned and stepped out of the room, just to find Castorice staring at him and Hyacine gasping and covering her mouth with her hands. Now, that seemed a little bit too much. It wasn’t the first time that someone dressed him well enough to make a few heads turn towards him… was it really that different?

“You look… really good, Phainon,” Hyacine said, still a little taken aback. Phainon wasn’t even too sure if that reaction was genuine or if she was still joking around as she had done before so many times.

Castorice, on the other hand, brought her index finger and thumb to her chin, reflecting on the situation. “The problem is that he likes too many vibrant colors,” she explained, as Mydei stepped closer to fix the collar of the trench-coat that definitely didn’t need any kind of fixing. His thoughts and the feeling of his hands against his turtleneck took a backseat temporarily as he listened to what his friend was saying. “He’s a good-looking guy, it’s not hard for him to find clothes that look good on him, he just never wears them.”

From in front of him, Mydei tilted his head and questioned, “I meant to ask, but why do you like those colors so much?”

“Every color is beautiful! They’re meant to tell a story and give certain feelings,” Phainon simply answered, before thinking about how to properly explain it. He understood why others would think he’s just horrid at putting colors together, but there was a reason why he liked them and always put them on. He sighed, looking at him, “And the people close to you do have a favorite color, right? I just like to carry them with me.”

Silence ensued right after that.

It wasn’t something that never happened, he knew that most people dressing in a certain way just don’t care that deeply about what colors they put on past asking themselves if they look good together, but he did like to wear colors that gave him comfort and inspired love. Wearing clothes that had the same colors that his friends adore for a reason or another was one way of doing that. He didn’t care much for matching them, but he did like to know that his friends were with him whenever he went.

Unexpectedly, the first to break that silence was Hyacine. She smiled and walked towards him, hugging him excitedly. Phainon welcomed her with a hug of his own, but he was slightly weirded out by that gesture after the amount of times she beat down on him and his horrible fashion sense.

“Never, ever change,” she muttered against his chest, hugging him for another few seconds. Phainon was still confused about this sudden change in behavior, but he accepted her request anyway. He had no idea why whenever he spoke his mind he got this reaction, but he was glad to see this reaction nevertheless. As Hyacine raised her head and took a step back, she crossed her arms and sighed, “But learn how to style clothes, please.”

Phainon let out a laugh and nodded, a little embarrassed that he still had to be dressed up by his friends at his age. Or boyfriend. That was still standing next to him with his hands on his shoulder, for some reason.

Gods, he didn’t know that he liked to openly show him how much he cared for and loved him in public so much with so little issues. He still had to debate with himself whether he loved or disliked it, but he’d found himself leaning into the touch so often just that day that he feared that his body already made the choice for him.

Mydei looked at his trench-coat when Phainon turned to face him, seeing if he had something to say as well. His hand was tracing the fabric on his shoulder in a calming motion, almost as if he needed to ground himself and offered him a way to relax and unwind himself as well. “It’s really admirable,” he ended up saying, before looking up into his sky blue eyes again. “What you just said. It’s admirable.”

Phainon felt as if all the air in his lungs got taken away from him.

The way Mydei was looking at him felt so honest and loving, almost as if he just poured all his feelings for him right there. Maybe he did. Maybe that was one of those phrases that he said that had an immense value for him and he just didn’t understand why. It sounded like a normal compliment, but it felt so much more intimate and personal that he felt sorry for the girls with them that had to witness them.

A sudden laugh from near him mad both of them turn with curious eyes, just to see Castorice smiling at the both of them. She quickly waved her hand on front of her face, gesturing it wasn’t too important. “It’s nothing,” she excused herself, then smiled again. “You’re a cute couple.”

He blinked a couple of times at that statement. Of course, he knew that they were together and they both wanted it to stay that way, but no one really complimented them for ‘looking good together’ or anything of the sort yet.

There was something about being recognized as an actual, romantic couple and being told they fit together that warmed his heart almost instantly.

“Thank you!” he beamed, smiling as he felt the hand on his shoulder relax further at the admission from him. Maybe it was satisfaction, as he had insisted since they met that day that he wouldn’t have left and Phainon was so stubborn to accept it, but it felt like pleasure to receive that kind of compliment by a friend as well.

Phainon didn’t even have to ask which one was of the two, because Mydei answered him as soon as the girls started talking with Astraea again. With a whisper, only meant for him, he quietly asked, “Did it get into your head at least? That we’re together and I’m not leaving any time soon?”

The tone he used was so affectionate and loving that he struggled to answer him. His voice was lower, his breath was so close to his neck that he could feel it clearly, he whispered so close to his ear that he could hear it over and over in his head, his hand trailed over the edge of his shirt and trench-coat, weakly grabbing it as his other hand rested on his arm, drawing gentle and relaxing movements on top of the fabric.

It honestly felt like a dream, in a way or another. It couldn’t have been real even for a second.

However, he understood what he asked him. Even if he struggled to believe him fully, he didn’t want to pin the fault on him or to say he was a liar. He wasn’t, this was his own issue, but he was starting to think that, maybe, Mydei was just the right person for him to partially let it go.

He smiled and leaned in as he slightly tilted his head, somehow keeping his eyes open and resisting to put his lips over Mydei’s. “Sorry for the wait,” he whispered, while his hands traveled on his hips and his thumbs tentatively massaged his physique over the jacket that he was wearing.

“Mh,” Mydei hummed, staring back at him with loving amber eyes, “I do like a challenge.”

Phainon let out a warm laugh, before closing the distance between them, letting Mydei cup his cheek and give away a couple of kisses. They weren’t too deep because they were both aware of the fact that they weren’t alone, but not too chaste either. They had been trying to get to that point, to trust each other as much as possible, to let go of that useless voice in the back of their minds telling them that it wouldn’t last or that one of them would ruin it.

If it happened, Phainon thought as he backed himself away from Mydei, he would have thought about it then. Right now, he was happy. He wanted to enjoy what he shared with Mydei as much as he possibly could.

Mydei ignored the sudden hesitation and kept his head close, his thumb gently rubbing against his humid lower lip. Phainon stared at him without moving, almost not caring that they were right in the middle of the way to the changing rooms and he was still wearing clothes that he had to yet buy.

His blue eyes almost worriedly wandered around Mydei’s perfect features, before settling on the one thing that he feared for their relationship now that they were on the topic. Better to tank all damage all in one go, right?

“Is it not overwhelming?” he breathed out, careful to not disturb the finger on his lips too much. It was something that effectively destroyed his relationships again and again, and he didn’t want the same to happen to Mydei… especially when he knew that he thought they went a little too fast.

He tilted his head slightly in the opposite direction as he thought of a satisfactory answer. “At first it was, a little,” he confessed, as Phainon’s bright blue eyes followed his every movement he made, without even moving an inch. Mydei sighed, before looking at him with his usual deadpan expression and answering him, “I don’t mind it now.”

“Why?”

“Was it something that others were mad about? I find it cute. Besides, I want the same thing.”

Cute. He found how invasive his behavior was cute.

Or, well, not invasive… Mydei wouldn’t even dare to call it anything negative in the first place. If he knew that was the way he referred to it, he would correct him just about now. Intense would have been a better way to describe it.

It all made him so happy. Mydei merely existing by his side made him so unbelievably happy.

“Thank you,” he whispered one last time, before he felt the hand on his cheek fall down and land on his shoulder as Mydei leaned his head over his shoulder.

“Have a little more faith in this,” he whispered, with a voice so low and barely audible that he feared that it wasn’t even happening. Phainon, however, listened to everything he was saying without knowing why. Probably, because it felt important and he wanted to to drill every single word into his own brain. “I’m not going anywhere. I’m right here and I like how clingy you are and how jealous you are of me.”

His grip immediately grew stronger on his hip, his eyes not moving to meet Mydei’s even when he left an affectionate kiss on the side of his neck. He relaxed, but he was still trying to gather the strength to process everything and answer him. Right now, he was extremely glad that the girls were taking care of Astraea, or he would feel almost too embarrassed to speak to him again after that.

He felt a couple other kisses on his neck, silent and subtle, while his hand rested on the opposite cheek and pushed him towards him in a teasing motion. Phainon almost let out a whine and, if he continued, he was sure that he would have actually lost the balance on his feet.

“Did it get into your head?” Mydei whispered, running his thumb up and down his cheek in a relaxing motion.

Phainon sighed, then nodded as he turned towards him, his face still a little too hot for his own liking. “A little. I really like this,” he lowered his eyes to look at the hands on his sides, before hugging him closer in a fluid motion. “I want it to last.”

Mydei let out a soft laugh, hugging him back and running a hand through his hair to make his presence known. “Then stop trying to run away. None of us wants you out of our life, Phainon.”

Warm, stable whispers he could get lost in. Warmth and love all around him. Softness and acceptance washing over him. He felt every single one of those emotions every time he was with him… how could he not fall for this man? He was the best he could have ever wished for. The fact that he had an adorable child that was turning his world upside down as well was even better.

Regardless, Phainon did love those clothes and he the way Mydei was touching them– not to talk of the fact that he chose those clothes specifically for him. He changed back and checked the price, surprisingly finding out that they weren’t too expensive, after all, so he happily bought them, even if just to own something that his dear boyfriend liked seeing on him.

As soon as they walked out of the fourth or fifth place they ended up visiting, Astraea took Phainon’s hand and looking up to him, light brown eyes shining in hopes that the question on the tip of his tongue would meet the desired answer. “Phai! Can you come back with us later?” he asked in the end, much to the adult’s interior peace.

“Sure!” he promptly answered, now secretly happy that he could spend more time with both he and Mydei. It had been way too long since he last had the opportunity to spend some quality time with them, and his hellish working hours didn’t help him to unwind nor feel less anxious about everything that was happening in his life now.

A night out with Mydei over the weekend was just what he needed.

“Phai,” Hyacine called him, from a few meters ahead of them, “we’re going to go back!”

Phainon left Mydei’s side for a second, sprinting forward to reach them and giving them a hug, greeting them properly. “Don’t you want to grab something to eat before that?” he asked next to Castorice’s ear, a little confused by that sudden decision.

“I think you need the time alone,” she whispered back, stepping back and smiling at him. He stood there as they waved at him and then Mydei and Astraea, right before minding their own business again and walking away.

He stared as they walked, talking excitedly between each other, a few laughs and affectionate smiles shot between them– the same that Mydei often gave him as well and the one that he promised to keep offering him for a very, very long time.

Suddenly, something in his brain lit up. A virtually impossible suggestion to make at that stage of their relationship. An insane question to even think of after just starting to date someone, but it was so functional for everyone involved… and besides, it was among the wishes of both. Maybe it was too soon, but it wasn’t like Mydei didn’t mention it to him already.

“Hey, Mydei,” he called out when he felt him reach his side, then turned to him after a few seconds. Blue eyes met amber, still in a bit of a trance after seeing what he did between his two friends and the idea that just illuminated itself in his head almost without permission. Mydei stared at him, patient, waiting for what he wanted to say. Phainon let out a shaky breath, trying to ignore how that just made him even more eager to hear him accept his suggestion, and his lips finally parted to ask, “Do you want to move in with me?”

Silence.

An expected silence, but a piercing silence nonetheless.

Mydei stared at him and Astraea was almost ignoring the conversation, instead only holding his father’s hand while he was playing with his foot on the ground, bouncing it between the opposite parts of a line on the concrete. Phainon wondered for a second if he usually did it or if he understood that whenever they talked that seriously he wasn’t meant to listen too much to it. He had yet to decide whether he liked it or not.

A shook of Mydei’s head and a feeble “what?” coming out of his mouth effectively moved his focus back to him, even if the thought of that behavior remained still on his mind, almost like a frozen picture in motion with way too many possible meanings– and he didn't like a singular one.

However, that wasn't the right time to think about it. Not when he dropped a nuclear-grade request on Mydei and he was staring at him as if he just revealed him some life-changing epiphany about the physical world that he thought to be false for his entire lifetime.

Well, he couldn't blame him. It was more than just ‘rushing it’. It was like starting a car at full speed in a dead end road. They were meant to crash against a wall sooner rather than later.

Yet, if they could just survive the hit…

“Hyacine and Castorice are going to move out in a few months,” he explained, slowly, then hesitantly smiled and tilted his head, desperately hoping for an affirmative answer that he most likely will never get. Even knowing that, she still asked again, “Do you want to move in?”

Mydei blinked a few times, but he luckily was able to speak this time. “When I said that today—”

“It was a joke, I know,” Phainon interrupted him, stepping closer just to gently grab his arm and looking at him straight in his eyes, without ever being any sort of intense. Instead, he softened, his hand sliding down to hold Mydei's as he spoke. “But I’m serious. I don't want to be alone, and you want a bigger house at a reasonable price… think about it.”

It sounded reasonable like this. He knew that it did, because he was there, suggesting it, when he had an astounding fear of rejection and being pushed away. If he saw it as something positive for both of them enough to get something positive out of it, that had to count for something. Mydei had to see it as well.

He looked at him with still a shimmer of hope, praying that t wouldn't be shut down by him and he actually agreed with him. Even Astraea was looking at him, weirdly interested in the topic that was being discussed.

Mydei let out a drawn out sigh, nodding as he thought about it. “Let’s do this,” he suggested instead, looking back to him. “Babysit Astraea for when I’m at work and sleep at my place. See how we’re going. Then, we can…”

“Decide whether or not going to live together after barely a few days of dating?” Phainon leaned in, finally secure in knowing that he did, in fact, accept his proposition.

“You felt my boobs on our first date, we’ve always moved freakishly fast. If anything, trying things out first is a new thing for both of us.”

“So it’s not a no.”

“It’s a hesitant yes. Eventually.”

He was so happy. Staying away from him for so long was becoming a torture, and now he got to live in the same apartment as him? It was like a dream coming true.

He just prayed that they could survive the fall, if it ever got to a fracture or an intensity so violent that they had to somehow brace for any sort of impact.

But he agreed! That was the important thing right now. He agreed, and they'd live in his apartment, and he'd come back to the arms of his loving boyfriend every single day, and he'd play with his beautiful, kind son so much more often. There wasn't anything more that he could have asked for.

“Phai is going to live with us?” Astraea asked, holding his plushie a little tighter to his chest. Somehow, Phainon didn't like seeing that action too much in that context, but he didn't say anything. Maybe he was thinking about it too much.

Mydei crouched down and welcomed him in his arms, most likely because he noticed the same thing. The child easily leaned in against his chest, searching for heat and some kind of support, almost hiding in that embrace. His father caressed his head gently and he answered, “More or less.”

He looked up with his mouth open in curiosity and wonder, obviously liking the answer with a bit of hesitation. Astraea moved his body rhythmically from left to right and let out a thin whisper that neither of them almost didn't catch it. “I really like Phai…”

“Would you like to live at his place?” Mydei asked with a gentle tone, careful with his every word, most likely with good reason.

Astraea looked around him and shyly backed away from him, bumping against his thigh. “I like it where we are now…”

Phainon really didn’t think this through. Of course Astraea would be scared of losing a comforting and safe place like Mydei’s apartment… if his life with his biological parents was even just half as bad as Mydei described it, it was normal that he wouldn’t be stoked about moving so suddenly.

He didn’t think he would be unreasonable about it, he trusted him enough, but they both had to be careful and introduce it to him slowly and carefully. He trusted Mydei to help with this, he wasn’t too worried, he just felt a guilty for not thinking too deeply about the feelings of the very traumatized kid that was always a part of the deal.

Luckily, his father was very capable at calming him down and trying to find a middle ground between them all. “It would be bigger and Phainon would be always there,” he explained, lightly rubbing his back as he smiled calmly at him. “Nothing else will change, I’d still be there and we’ll move over everything we have at home. How does that sound?”

“Better…” he mumbled, before ending up in his arms again, still whispering against his chest. “I really like seeing Phai, you’re happy when he’s around.”

Mydei smiled and proceeded to kiss him on the top of his head, before looking down to him and asking, “Are you happier with Phai as well?”

The child hesitantly got up from the man’s body, thinking in his place about the question he just asked him. A hand quietly ran through his blonde hair, meant to calm his nerves and giving him an occasion to ground himself and express what he thought without any kind of fear coming his way.

As Astraea looked up to Phainon, he instinctively crouched down, immediately catching the child in his arms. He looked so scared by that point of view. Clenching his plushie to his little chest, slightly trembling, his face stuck against his chest, accepting that hug to soothe all his uncertainties. It was a sight that he didn’t want to see any time soon, but he was glad that he could, at the very least, offer him some sort of consolation and support every time that happened.

All in all, he wasn’t taking too badly, given what he went through for the last few years.

Phainon caressed the back of his head and kept him in his arms, gently stroking his back from time to time. He wasn't crying nor breathing heavily, but it was best for him to know he had the support and there was no need for to panic. “I’m happier with both of you as well, honeybuns,” he whispered, hugging him closer and leaving a sweet kiss on the top of his head.

The child just pushed against his chest more after that sentence, even if he wasn't properly frightened or anxious anymore. Mydei did say he was warmer, so maybe that was what he was gripping on him so firmly, not wanting to let go even just to go back to his father.

He looked at him, tiny in his embrace and searching for heat and comfort, and he could do nothing but hold him close for the moment. It would have resolved itself in due time, but he had to stand by and look at him in that state for a while, for now. He had no idea how Mydei survived on his own with such an aching pain in his chest yelling at him to do something more useful whenever he was sad or scared.

“It's enough,” Mydei's voice suddenly called out from above him. Phainon raised his head slowly, unsure if he should believe those words or keep pitying everyone involved. As he met his amber eyes, all he saw was understanding. “He's very strong, don't underestimate him. You did everything you could to calm him down, it's enough,” he explained, before kneeling down and caressing his child's head. “What do you say, Astraea? Do we say yes to what Phai asked?”

The child turned slightly, cheek still squished against Phainon's chest, hesitant with how he weakly nodded at him, keeping his plushie held safely to his body, almost using it as an anti-stress toy.

Phainon let out a relieved breath that he didn't know he was holding. Almost instantly, he felt a quiet laugh and a kiss on his temple as Mydei pulled him in. Such a simple gesture, and yet it calmed him down almost completely, offering him a safe haven, even just for a few seconds.

“Let's go home to plan things out, come on,” Mydei suggested, both to him and his child. He ruffled Astraea hair and, simple as that, the kid's press on Phainon's chest softened, and his hand reached to grab his father's.

There was no other way to look at it– even in just a few weeks, he made such big progresses, and clung to Mydei like a baby koala to his mother. It was cute, but it was also indicative of how much effort his partner was putting into raising him. Phainon couldn't be any less, if he wanted to keep his promise.

“Mama,” the child's voice, now a bit more distant, made him look up, realizing that they were already a few steps ahead. Standing still, but a bit farther away nevertheless. He was looking at Mydei with hopeful eyes, almost as if there were stars glittering in his irises. “Can I wear my new dress? Please?”

Mydei smiled and nodded, gentle as ever. “When we're at home,” he answered, turning towards Phainon again, “and if Phainon hurries up.”

Of course. Including him again and showing he wanted him in his life again. Warming his heart and soul as he usually did.

He closed his eyes for a second and let out a small laugh, fully recognizing that attempt in keeping his promise. Phainon himself had to honor it as well, no matter what happened.

If not for himself and his own happiness, at least out of respect to all the effort that Mydei was putting in.

Stay with them. Trust Mydei. Try to be happy and feel like deserving that kind of happiness.

It looked a little difficult, but the more they both involved him in their life, the more that included him in their plans, the more they accepted him as who he was… it was starting to get easier.

Those thoughts slipped out of his mind the second they both started chatting and talking to him on the way back to Mydei’s apartment, replaced more and more often with looking forward to feeling new kinds of warmth inside his chest.

Maybe, he could actually allow himself to be happy this time without feeling too guilty about it and maybe– just maybe– he would have been able to love someone as he had always wanted.

He absolutely wanted to give back to Mydei what he kept offering him without take backs. Wholly, unfearing and earnestly, as he had always did.

Chapter End Notes

This took me forever but here we are! Halfway through! Another 100k words of this! I had fun writing this so I hope that it will be just as enjoyable to read ^-^ And yes, the outfit that Mydei tells Phainon to buy is the Luckin collab one because I love it lol

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

“Mydei. It's normal,” Phainon’s voice grew in annoyance and Mydei could find the slightest tint of anger in it as well. “I work there, I know better than to grow attached to children with cancer.”
“Why are you angry?”
“I’m not!”
There it was. The yell that Mydei was looking for.”

Chapter Notes

Content warning: there are heavy themes regarding a child dying due to a terminal illness and hints about mourning her, so please proceed with caution. It will be brought up next chapter as well, but only in passing and I will summarize there the main contents of this chapter if it's too much for some, take care of yourselves first !!

See the end of the chapter for more notes

The feeling of tranquility settled in Mydei’s routine during the past few weeks, especially since he finally understood what it was that Phainon needed and what they had to do now. Before that outing, he wasn’t too sure of it because he could just guess what was on his mind, but he opened up and he finally put those worries to rest.

And then he suggested they’d go live together and Mydei was about to have a stroke right in front of him as soon as he heard those words. Live together, under the same roof, just after a few weeks was more than irresponsible or impulsive– it was insane. There was something deeply wrong with him to even think about it.

Admittedly, though, everything was going well. Astraea was getting used to Phainon’s presence in the house even if he often didn’t sleep there due to his infernal shifts and Mydei’s heart was calming down with each day that passed. Maybe they would have been actually able to live together without crashing and burning, after all.

Even then, sometimes Phainon just wasn’t home. Shifts at the hospital required him to switch between day and night sometimes and it was often because of emergencies, so he couldn’t warn Astraea or Mydei. They simply found out with messages and notes left next to a ready breakfast.

After one or two times of that happening, Mydei grew tired of leaving his son all alone in his apartment. He caught the occasion to drag himself and his son out of his house, walking until the bar near his place. There were kids living there with their parents and, even if they were much older than Astraea, they were certainly better than leaving him home alone or spending the entire time with adults.

As soon as they stepped in, a familiar face greeted him, already drinking some kind of alcohol that early in the morning. Mydei sighed, but he put down his son and pushed him a little to say hi to the kids who turned to smile brightly at him. He wasn’t as shy as he was in the past, but he was still a little insecure of talking to strangers, kids or not.

When he checked whether or not his kid joined those other two kids safely, plushie clenched to his chest as it was a normal occurrence now, he turned towards the adult drinking beside him. Sleepy, golden eyes and a proud, white mane of hair greeted him back, and the familiar voice acknowledged him as well. “Oh? Mydei? What brings you here?”

If he didn’t know better, he would have walked away from anyone who drank that early in the morning. Unfortunately, knowing Jing Yuan meant seeing him drink and sleep quite often during the day.

“I wanted to ask if you could look after my child, since you always laze around here, for some reason,” Mydei huffed as he sat down next to him. He looked at the hour on the display on the wall, keeping track of it. The reason why he had to drop him off here wasn’t for anything else than meeting a dear relative visiting, and he’s rather talk to her on his own before letting her meet his child.

“How rude,” Jing Yuan calmly answered, “I stay here to support my husband’s activities.”

“You’re rich, Jing Yuan. Your husband absolutely doesn’t need you to stay here to stay afloat. Make yourself useful while you stay here, at least.”

“It’s indeed not a problem to keep an eye on your child. Yanqing isn’t going to school either.”

Mydei nodded, before walking over to where Astraea was to greet him. He didn’t want him to think anything bad would have happened, and he preferred to be completely transparent with him whenever he had to drop him off to other people.

As he turned the corner, he noticed his child telling his name to the other two kids, greeted by smiles and kind words. “Are you betting?” he asked, shooting back at her the same energy that she thought he would have suffered from instead. Granted, he would never tell her that he thought about it up until now.

“No, thank you,” she put her hands in front of her body, as if to count herself out, “I care about my money.”

Obviously. Money was important and he had to keep it close. That was one of the first things she had ever told him when his mother and Aglaea moved in together. It was useful advice, but it sounded hollow when the mouth that uttered it kept on telling lie after lie. His opinion on her changed since then, but the memory of those initial thoughts remained.

Another sigh escaped her lips, but this time her eyes stared at Mydei, rather happy. “All things considered… you look happier. I was getting worried about you, but I'll have to thank this guy for saving you.”

Mydei didn’t even think it was that obvious. He wasn’t feeling great before he met Phainon and adopted Astraea, sure, but he thought that the worst was gone for a few years now. Apparently not.

Or, Phainon made him so happy and so visibly more alive than even that time that he looked a completely new and different person from before he ever met him. He was sure a lot of it was thanks to Astraea, but he couldn’t deny that he felt an upward possibility of happiness whenever Phainon was around.

Before he could think of an answer, though, he felt his phone ring. Stupidly, he gave in and looked at the caller, immediately noticing Phainon’s face spread on the screen. Curse himself for caring, he almost immediately picked up before he saw his sister’s devilish smirk.

“You should answer or your boyfriend will get jealous, I don't want any part in that!” she teased, closing an eye and turning her head away, with that satisfied expression still on her face.

Typical Cipher.

Mydei sighed and stood up, phone in hand, and picked up once he was far away enough to have a private chat with his boyfriend. It was mostly for his own momentary peace, he already knew that she would have heard everything, no matter how far away he got.

“Hey,” he greeted him, already feeling like there was something was wrong from the fact that he didn’t immediately speak instead. “Is there a problem?”

A tired voice– barely a whisper– came out of the speakers of his phone. “No, I just… wanted to hear your voice.”

Every alarm in Mydei’s head started ringing the second he heard that toned down, tired, hollow voice speaking back at him. It barely resembled Phainon, the only reason why he recognized him was the timber of his voice being memorized in his brain.

There was definitely something wrong and it either just happened or he hid it from him. He didn’t know which one he preferred.

“Phainon, is everything okay? You don't sound like nothing is happening,” he asked, hesitantly tasting the ground that he was walking in on. He had never heard him so devastated, he had no idea how he could even approach him.

A laugh came from the other hand, same as that voice. Tired. Desperate. Empty. “You can already catch that?”

Mydei bit his lower lip, reminding himself where it was that he worked. Kids permanently in the hospital. A creeping feeling of knowing what happened in the last few hours settled in his chest, but he still suggested the only solution that he could think about. “I can come pick you up.”

He believed in him and in knowing how to handle his job and the intense emotions it brought. He truly, honestly did. However, hearing him in that state hurt him and he wanted him help him, someway.

“A child died,” that creepily hollow voice confirmed for him. “She had lung cancer. She held onto me since she came here. And now…”

Mydei took a deep breath, pushing away thoughts that immediately connected that situation to his own child.

It didn’t happen yet. Stop thinking about it. He’s fine in the care of trustworthy people, healthy and well.

The focus should be on Phainon’s well-being right now.

“I’m picking you up,” Mydei said, still trying to think critically and offer his help. He wanted to be there for him, and the distance he perceived right now was far too great to ignore. “Try not to take your thoughts too seriously in the meantime.”

Not a sound came from the other end for a few moments. Then, a shaky sigh went through his ears, and a much lighter, familiar voice gave him an answer that he wasn’t too keen on accepting. “Mydei… Stay where you are.”

“You can't be serious.”

“Mydei, this is my job. I can't just… leave. Like you can't leave a house on fire if you can't save one person, or if you have to get hurt to save another. There are her parents, her friends here, her siblings… she was one of the oldest kids here, everyone knew her.”

There was hurt in his voice, at least. He wasn’t completely letting it wash over him and he wasn’t letting it take ahold of him. Like he was taught as well when he was on his way to be a firefighter. Maybe their jobs were indeed more similar than he initially thought.

Don’t bring the pain home, don’t detach yourself too much and always look after your well-being after a rescue.

Gnaeus often repeated it to him. He wondered why he pushed him so much to adopt Astraea, if he wasn’t meant to stay close to the people he saved, yet detached at the same time. Maybe he simply thought that giving a child like him to social services would have been too cruel, or he was worried for his health and thought that caring for a child of his own would have helped him.

Either way, he understood Phainon’s point. Not many would have agreed with him and even now knowing that he had to leave him be and just distract him from that situation left a sour taste in his mouth, but it was a way to deal with it without being unprofessional or hurting himself too much for his own good.

“Just tell me about your day,” Phainon requested, interrupting his flow of thoughts. His voice was kind and mellow, unlike the usually bright voice he had, but better than the empty one that he had used when they first started that call.

Mydei tensed his muscles and almost froze, a little taken aback by the sudden request. “I… I'm at a cat café with my sister,” he answered, as calmly as he could. He was trying to ignore the situation and do as Phainon asked, but it proved to be a harder task than he expected it to be.

He didn’t like it one bit. The only reason he was keeping it up was because Phainon asked, and he’d rather help him get his mind off of it for a while than not doing anything.

“Mh,” Phainon hummed in his ear, seemingly interested in it, “how are the kittens?”

“Cute and tiny,” Mydei said, maybe a little too fast. It almost sounded like an answer that he prepared for that occasion, but he genuinely found it hard to ignore the fact that his boyfriend hid his issues from him earlier and now was unwilling to confide in him, instead choosing to bury those feelings.

Even if he had to stay detached, he clearly was hurting and he sounded like he knew the kid personally, maybe even often talked to and played with her. He already failed at staying away from that patient, even if he was supposed to. What was the point in hiding it or pretending as if the hurt wasn’t there then? At the very least he should talk about it.

“Mydei, breathe. Don't let your mind wander too much.”

The voice was kinder now. Almost as if it gradually calmed down and turned into the nice, honey-like voice that he heard every single day. It was gentle and warm, but the words it used didn’t register well in Mydei’s mind. He was supposed to wonder whether or not this was good for either of them and offer support when needed, even if it was normal for him.

He was worried, he wasn’t going to deny it. Was it too much, maybe? Perhaps, but seeing how little he cares about himself was hard to withstand. “How am I supposed to–”

“Mydei. Don’t treat me like a child,” he immediately cut him off, with a tone that bordered anger. Mydei didn’t know how he felt about it yet. “I understand that you never thought about this aspect of my job, but it’s not much different from yours. Just with less flames.”

He was right. He knew he was right, and he didn’t want to overstep or seemingly thinking that he couldn’t do a job that spent his entire life studying for, but he was horribly worried and he couldn’t shake that feeling off of him at the moment.

“Mydei,” Phainon called out again, this time with a soft, yet demanding voice, immediately forcing him to keep his attention on him. “Stop those gears from turning, Mydei. It’s not the first time. I learned to deal with it, but… we all thought that she would win. She had a relapse a few days ago, we gave her our proper goodbyes already. I just thought that it wouldn’t be so soon.”

“You’re talking about it as if–”

“I was talking about my morning routine? Maybe I got too used to it. I promise that it hurts. I feel every bit of pain, but I can’t mourn her because I have a job to do.”

He understood that, and he was starting to accept that it was just the only way he could deal with it while being there for both the kids left and her parents.

He was acting a little too selfishly. He was still worried, but they would have talked about it later, when Phainon would be allowed to relax and release all the frustration and pain that must come with this situation.

He went through something similar with Hephaestion’s time in the hospital, and he hid his feelings too, at first. His mother was the first to force him to talk about them, and everything after that went slightly better on that front. There was still fear, uncertainty, heartache… but at least he talked about those feelings and let out a little of his own frustrations over not being able to help.

Hopefully, it would have been the same for Phainon.

As if his brain summoned him, that voice worked its way into his thoughts once again, as gentle and soft as Mydei remembered whenever his boyfriend whispered worries, opinions, small talk and sweet nothings in the dark of his room right before sleeping. “Mydei, you told me already about Hephaestion, I’m sure that it was traumatizing. But I like my job. I like helping out people however I can, just like you like yours.”

There it was. Their jobs were similar, and he almost intruded too far in his own interests and wishes by implying that he needed to be coddled or picked up for having to deal with a life that they couldn’t save. It happened plenty of times in his career as well and he would get upset if someone close to him would say that he wasn’t able to deal with his own job.

“You’re right. I’m sorry,” Mydei apologized in the end, feeling somewhat calmer now that he reached a conclusion that Phainon supported and that it was satisfactory for him as well. “Talk about it with someone later, will you?”

A humming noise was what he got in response, and for now it had to be enough. He trusted him enough to know what he had to do for his own well-being.

“I’m sorry, I shouldn’t have called you,” Phainon’s voice rang again in his ears, this time full of regret. Mydei was calmer, but he knew that he tended to hide his ugly feelings, unveiling them now was meant to be met with some push-back by his own mind.

However, Mydei wanted him to know that he appreciated it, so that it would have been easier for him to do it more often. He liked being involved, knowing that Phainon trusted him with his troubles, sometimes even searching for refuge or advices from him. “No, it was… I'm glad you told me. Involved me in your life.”

“But you’re sad now.”

“I think anyone would be. But this showed me how serious you are about us. How much you truly want to share your life with me because you like me. Yet again.”

That was all that he had ever wished for since they officially got together. He knew that Phainon liked him, even loved him for quite some time, but he wanted him to trust him with his issues, instead of shielding the both of them from his worse thoughts and hurting himself further.

“Liking you,” Phainon sighed, almost dreamily, “would be a grave understatement.”

Mydei let out a small laugh, smiling to himself. “And what is the correct word, then?”

“Love,” Phainon immediately spat out, almost as if he was waiting for it. “Adore and cherish are pretty fitting alternatives too, if you prefer some other words.”

Being so upfront about his own feelings, speaking so plainly… it wasn’t like Phainon at all, but he knew that every word that came out of his mouth was honest. He heard the slight hesitation and awkwardness, his voice threatening to tremble or break, but he didn’t hold back at all.

It was an admission on his part, maybe, and the recognition of a feeling that intensified so quickly for both of them.

Mydei still didn’t dare to voice it out loud.

Too powerful, too heavy, too many implications for his tongue to even be able to bear it just yet. He knew he loved him. He knew that, realistically, he wouldn’t leave him. He knew that.

And yet, that damned word still felt like sweet poison on his tongue.

“Mydei… I can’t read your mind, you know,” Phainon’s voice faintly echoed in his mind. Mydei listened carefully as that word threatened to be whispered into his ear again. A sigh came in instead. “Spell out what you want to say instead. That’s what you always tell me, right?”

You don’t have to say it back. Just talk to me.

A content, relaxed smile made its way on Mydei’s face, happy that he finally, finally understood what he meant and how openly he expressed his feelings now. There was still fear, but his constant presence in his life in the last few months must have meant something.

His tongue hesitated, a breath caught in his throat, a second of doubt clouded his mind. They all got smashed into a brick by his own brain, already working too fast for him to even come up with any way to stop his mouth from working on its own.

“I want you here.”

Those words felt too heavy on his tongue as soon as he whispered them, almost as if he had to hide them away from the world– despite knowing they were his honest feelings and Phainon wouldn’t reject him. They have been there for a while now and he felt the lack of his presence more in the last few days, but it was still slightly scary to voice them so directly.

It was foolish and selfish probably, but he couldn’t help it. He missed him, he rarely even saw him outside of the weekend due to his stupid night shifts and he hated it. And now he was going through a difficult time and not only he refused to let him help, but he was willing to finish his entire turn with those unresolved feelings gnawing at him.

A warm, content, relaxed laugh drove itself directly into his brain, calming him down almost immediately. How he was able to even be able to do that in such a situation was beyond him.

“Soon enough,” he whispered, in a voice that he rarely used. The only times that Mydei had the pleasure to listen to it was between kisses right before falling asleep or whenever he sensed that there was something amiss in his mood and he needed to relax. A warm, deep, honey-like voice, only for him to hear.

Mydei barely even registered what it was that he actually said, because that deep voice, sounding so close without the contact to back up that sensation, was driving him insane.

“Mydeimos,” came in that voice again, whispering his full name without the slight warning, “I'll kiss you however and how much you'll like as soon as I get there, I swear. I’m sorry if I’ve been so busy lately, I promise that I will get that day shift. And I asked for a free day tomorrow, so I can finally ensure you that we will spend some time together soon… intimate as well, if you want.”

I swear. I promise. I can ensure you.

He didn't even need to say that he loved him. It was just some fancy word that, sure, Mydei enjoyed to hear, but the sheer devotion that he was showing him wasn't something that could be encapsulated in a single word.

Hearing him whisper sweet promises in his ear and knowing that he would have followed up on them warmed his heart more than any love confession that he could ever make.

That was the kind of person Phainon was– showing that he cared with his words and actions, trying to make the people that he cared about as happy as he could.

And whenever Mydei glanced back at it, he saw it. The bottomless abyss of something that he was hiding along with the shining glimmers of adoration that he had for him, akin to a starry sky reflected in his irises.

Mydei was fine with it. If he wanted to stop hiding whatever he didn't want to talk about, he would have opened up someday. In the meantime, knowing just how much he cared was enough.

Then, the request for some intimate time. He was probably hinting at having sex, and Mydei agreed. He was getting handsy, more flirty, sloppier with his kisses. He was more than glad to satisfy his desire.

“I’ll ask my sister if she can keep an eye on Astraea,” he mentioned, with a softer tone than what he meant to use.

It didn't matter. Phainon dreamily sighed all the same. “I’ve been missing you as well… I know these shifts are taxing, we just didn’t have a substitute for my position yet until today.”

“You found it now?”

“Yeah. I wanted to tell you tonight, before...”

“Don’t worry,” Mydei calmly whispered, offering some kind of smile even if he couldn't see it. “Try to get through the day and come back, same as always. Get some sleep, I’ll cook you something warm. We can watch a nice movie after we put Astraea to bed.”

“Sounds so good…”

“Come back in one piece. See you tonight.”

“Have a good day, babe.”

Mydei's breath caught. It was quite stupid to notice it now, but hearing him call him with a pet name was... heartwarming. Almost endearing. It had such a nice ring to it and it felt so natural– he wanted to hear it more often.

He stared at his phone for a few seconds, Phainon’s contact name displayed on the screen, and he immediately chased away the thought of changing it to something cuter, more intimate, like a nickname or, Gods forbid, a pet name.

Have some composure and decency, Mydeimos. You're not a teenager anymore.

Yet, that thought made him feel so good. Almost as if it was meant to be there. As if he wished to hear other pet names– whether it was the same one or different ones, it didn’t matter– just to feel that ecstatic feeling again.

He and Hephaestion never really used them in those situations and he didn’t think that he would like them at all, but Phainon’s attitude in how and when he said it was different. The closeness, the deep voice, the weirdly affectionate and flirty tone… all of it contributed in making it sound better than anything that Hephaestion had ever told him.

It was bad. He was into him way more than he expected and, worst of all, he liked it. He enjoyed the attention, the stupid nicknames, the pet names, the more intimate moments, the casual shows of affection– way more than he did in his relationship with Hephaestion. He didn’t know what it was, he just knew that it was because it was Phainon.

Those thoughts unraveled further inside his head as he turned around and was met with Cipher’s knowing smirk.

It was going to be a long, awfully annoying talk. He didn’t even notice his faint smile as he was thinking about Phainon, and he knew that she was going to bring it up.

Mydei slowly walked to sit down in his place, expecting a question that arrived almost immediately. He almost wanted his days as a single man back.

“You like this dude so much,” Cipher purred, almost to an uncomfortable degree. “Not even Hephy got you so worked up, what the hell is he doing to make you so flustered?”

Mydei looked at the food and drinks in front of him, likely brought there by some waiter while he was on the phone. “I really like him,” he whispered, calm and relaxed, before deciding to just drop the much bigger news on her. “And… we’re moving in together in a few months.”

All in all, the reaction to news like that was pretty underwhelming.

She just stared at him for a few second and mouthed a small “what the fuck”, before going back to stare at him to get some kind of explanation. He honestly expected at least a laugh, or an insult, or a warning for Phainon– but none of those ever arrived. She just couldn't wrap her head around it.

“I’m doing this for Astraea as well,” Mydei added, maybe hoping that some well deserved context would make things better. He didn’t forget when he didn’t tell her that his break-up was agreed on both parts and had to explain to Hephaestion why his dear sister was outside of his window at three in the morning. He would like to avoid that same situation with Phainon. “My apartment isn't built for more than one person… he would have so much more space and the price won't be too big.”

She still stared, before finally blinking and trying to take in all the information that was given to her in those last few minutes. “For fuck's sake, you're in love.”

“I never said that.”

“You didn't have to! It's obvious!”

“If you say so.”

“If I– Little lion, you’re so head over hills that you’re willing to move with him with your son! For how long did you even know him?”

She had a point. He knew that. They’ve been going out together for a couple of months, and they’ve been knowing each other for not much longer. That was a fact, and there was nothing that they could have done to make it amount to the years that usually took before being able to even think about sharing a house.

However, Mydei felt confident in what they could do to avoid a fallout.

As he noticed already, Phainon had a degree of love and devotion that was barely comparable to the aforementioned ‘usual situations’ that other couples went through, and Mydei was more than confident that both of them and Astraea would have survived, if everything went as swimmingly as the last couple of weeks that they spent trying to see how days spent as some kind of family was.

It all went well.

He and Phainon had some arguments, but they both expected it and they weren’t very serious– they were both willing to change their routine to accommodate the other or what they needed– and they didn’t really have an impact on Astraea because they were more akin to requests and working towards solutions than fights or even discussions in the first place.

They worked well together, even in that situation. Phainon even got more handsy and gave and accepted affectionate words and gestures more often, both to him and Astraea.

“Give or take, four months, but I’m not going to move there right away. Castorice and her girlfriend are going to move in a few months, we’re using that time to see how it’s going. He’s been staying at my place most days and babysitting Astraea.” he explained, trying to make it sound as reasonable as he possibly could.

However, he could see her face, unmoved and doubtful.

No matter how much he explained it, she was still about to witness her little brother move in with a man that she had never met nor knew about until that moment. He wouldn’t even have expected her to be supportive.

True to his thoughts, Cipher let out a heavy sigh. “And you think that’s going to be enough?”

“I hope.”

“You hop– Does Gorgo even know?”

“… Not yet. I wanted to tell her once we’re sure that it can work.”

He knew that it sounded horrible, that he seemed like an ungrateful child, that something so big should have been a topic with her already, but he just didn’t know how to bring it up now. He knew that she liked Phainon, but he wanted to be absolutely sure that it would have been fine for him and Astraea before even bringing it up with her.

If she worried for him even now that he was largely feeling well and independent, he would truly be a horrible son.

“Well, it’s your life, little brother!” Cipher nodded, seemingly dropping the argument. Mydei felt grateful for it. “I’ll support you, but–”

“If he pushes his luck, you will kill him, I know. Thank you,” he smiled, finally directing his attention back to the kittens all over him and the food on the table.

There was still a tint of worry for Phainon’s well-being in his mind, but there wasn’t much that he could do now, so he better take this day to be with his sister after so long instead. He would have been fine, returned home and then he could think about do something to help him. He understood having difficulties with not taking his work home regarding not being able to save someone else, it will take a while to digest it either way.

Thinking back at that call while his sister dragged him out of the café as they payed for what they ordered, he felt happy that Phainon could call him out so openly.

Don’t treat me as some fragile thing.

Mydei didn’t even notice that he started doing that, he was just worried about him and felt weirdly possessive and protective towards him. However, he forgot that Phainon can take care of himself and that he chose to do that job.

He knew the risks and what it entailed– he had no right to come in and tell him that he would have solved it, and he knew that he would have gotten mad if Phainon did the same with him when he couldn’t save someone with his own hands.

They are partners, they do live together, but they need to respect each other boundaries. Phainon simply told him he didn’t like that behavior and Mydei would have respected it and thought about it going forward.

Same as always. Talk, make every desire clear, follow it up with solutions that they would work out together. Nothing new, nothing more. It was just calmly walking together towards a future that they could share with each other.

In that fast pace, as every other time, there were so many calm, relaxing, warming moments such as that– of trial and error, understanding, reaching out to each other.

That was what it made him so sure that they could last without the fall out that he had with Hephaestion. It wasn’t youthful attraction, addictive feelings and slowly getting used to the other’s presence with no reaction.

Phainon always had some kind of response, no matter how muted or hidden, and the feelings he had felt grounded in reality, stable, not needing another fix every so often. He knew that Phainon was in the same room and that was enough to feel warmth in his chest.

If he was alone with his own thoughts, he would think more about it, but his sister soon asked him to go to one place or the other until the sun started to set.

He had fun, at least, but he wasn't too ecstatic of going back to pick up his child. Less because it was his child and more for the people around him that knew him enough now to either pick up that something was wrong or pick him up on it.

Respectively, they would have been Sunday and Jing Yuan. He hoped not to see Robin, at the very least, or she would have joined Sunday in letting her know what was wrong with him. Not something that he necessarily wanted to talk about.

Unfortunately for him, Jing Yuan took his title of lazy cat seriously, so he found him at the entrance and he prayed that his sister would save him from that sad, horrible destiny.

The man turned, eyeing Cipher almost immediately and offering a kind smile. “Oh, Cifera. It’s delightful to see you again.”

“You’re still here, Lion King?” she asked, smiling as she sat down next to him.

Mydei took a relived sigh, grateful that his begs have been answered so swiftly. He didn't know what he would have done if he had to wait so long to at least hold his child in his arms again.

“Of course,” he heard Jing Yuan' say in response. “Might I propose a drink for the both of us?”

His sister’s eyes lit up, happily nodding. “Don’t threaten me with a good time!”

That was done. They usually stayed together for enough time, so he could go and search for Astraea because, frankly, if he went one more minute without knowing how he was doing, he was honestly going to break two or three of the tables around him.

“Mama!”

The usual nickname made him react immediately, turning towards the source of the sound and smiling as soon as he saw those honey-colored eyes and white strands in his blonde hair.

Almost instinctively, Mydei crouched down and opened his arms, letting the little child crash in his embrace.

He took a second to kiss him on the top of his head and make sure that he was doing fine, quietly breathing in and out as he caressed his hair.

He missed him so much. Even if it was just one day, all that happened made him feel his absence more than he thought he would.

“How have you been today?” Mydei asked, letting him back a couple of steps to look at him. He looked well, maybe even better than when he left him there– perhaps, spending some time with younger people truly was a better choice for him in some occasions.

Mydei was well aware that he was a little protective of him, but he couldn’t help it. He saw him at his lowest and he didn’t want to have to do it again under any circumstance. Not being able to keep an eye on him just meant that he wasn’t sure how he was doing, and it was a problem that he would have had to face.

Eventually.

Once this situation with moving in with Phainon wrapped up.

His child giggled happily, a sound that he wanted to hear for the past several hours, and it ended up echoing in the back of Mydei’s brain. “Good! Are we going home now?”

He nodded, before looking at the door. Still nothing. “We’re going to wait for Phainon first,” he absentmindedly explained.

Astraea nodded excitedly, before running back off to play with the two younger people in that bar. He was glad that, at least, those two were able to be friendly with him and let him pass some time with people closer to his age.

After all, school was always an option for the future.

He was quickly approaching the age to start elementary school, and Mydei for one would have liked to fall back on someone if he wasn’t able to make many friends in his class. He knew how lonely it would have been for him, and Phainon probably knew too, from the little he knew about his past.

Both of them would have liked to avoid that scenario and, even if he still had a lot of adult people he could rely on, it was different from having friends around his age.

“He’s been playing all day with Yanqing and Yunli.”

The voice from behind him made sure he would turn around, just to see a meek smile behind the counted next to him and a polite stance, much less stiff from the one he remembered. “Sunday,” he greeted him, standing up again. “You don’t have clients today.”

“We’re technically still closed and my sister is on vacation right now,” he explained, leaning on the counter as Mydei walked over to sit down in front of him.

He wasn’t entirely against a talk with him, maybe he could have helped with his mood. After all, from what he knew, he was in Phainon’s place as well in the past. Married early, partner had a child before knowing him, incredible change of personality and hobbies in little time due to dating a single father… he could see most of these traits in Phainon as well.

Sunday smiled, already in his work uniform. They probably had to open soon, if he had to judge by the next question that he posed him. “Can I make you something?”

Maybe he needed it.

“Oh, no, thank you,” he opted for in the end, refusing to listen to those thoughts that would have just worsened the situation. It wouldn’t have been alcohol anyway, but, even in that case, he would rather not take anything other than water at the moment.

However, Sunday did feel something was wrong. Mydei still had to decide whether or not it was a lucky or unlucky situation. “There is something on your mind,” the gray-haired man stated, offering him a glass of water instead of listening to his request. He watched as the blond took the glass and added, “I don’t know you as much as Jing Yuan, but I have learned a few things about you.”

Mydei nodded and bit his lower lip, slowly agreeing with him. It wasn’t in his nature to lie or make up lies about his feelings– he either made things worse or it was so noticeable that there was no point in hiding it in the first place.

“Do you think moving in with someone after less a year of dating is insane?” he asked, maybe with words that were a tad too strong. He just needed an unbiased answer from someone that barely knew him and never met Phainon, because he was sure that was what his sister thought when he first told her a few hours ago.

He just wanted to make sure that it would be the right decision and to not make others worry for him, especially his family. They have been sticking by him and sacrificing so much for his well-being that he didn’t think it as fair to involve them even further in his own issues.

Sunday looked at him with an apologetic smile, but Mydei could tell that it was different from the one that he used with clients. It was less forced, less stiff, more natural. Mydei wondered if it was so different because he was with a friend of his husband, or if his real personality was slightly changing after living with someone like Jing Yuan for as long as he did.

He didn’t think that he would have ever found out, but it was something that he stumbled upon as he observed him. He used to be composed and controlled when he first met him a few years prior, and now he was… looser, more impulsive, relaxed. He wondered if that would have been the case for he and Phainon as well in the future, since they already started growing and changing each other, in a sense.

Mydei remembered when he first met Phainon– he was doubting him and himself, hesitantly approached Astraea and hardly even voiced his needs. Now it wasn’t much different on some aspects, but he started most talks he had with Astraea and he didn’t seem so doubtful about their relationship anymore.

It may not seem like much, but he noticed the difference. Phainon smiled with genuine happiness so much more often now.

“Well, it’s… a little unhinged,” Sunday answered him, crossing his arms. “But I have been living with Jing Yuan since our first anniversary, so I don’t know if I am the best person to ask.”

He was almost stunned at that revelation. He knew that they started living together soon, but he assumed that it happened when they got married– three years into their relationship. He didn’t know them at the time, so he just assumed that was when they started to live together, but apparently he was wrong.

One year of dating… sounded awfully close to what they had too.

“How come?” he asked, now a lot more curious in Sunday’s experience than his own situation.

The other man smiled and nodded, offering him a gentle stare. “Better for the child.”

“Was it?”

“It was more stable. Just a year may seem illogical and impulsive to others, but juggling between raising a child, working and dating is a little different than only dating. I knew I would have stayed with him and Yanqing liked me enough, so there weren’t too many problems when we eventually did start living together. Just do it gradually and sort out your issues as they arise, and you will all be fine.”

Just as they had been doing now, then. Fast pace in what others assumed needed a waiting, and patience in things that others didn’t even think about.

As he thought, he noticed something sliding across the counter and, as he looked downwards, his eyes landed on an origami in the form of a lotus flower. He knew that it meant something akin to rebirth and new beginnings, but he did ask himself why Sunday just had one at arm’s length for the occasion. He couldn’t even tell who made it between him, Jing Yuan and Yanqing.

Regardless, it was a well-meaning gift and, as such, Mydei couldn’t possibly refuse it. “Thank you, Sunday,” he said, carefully taking it in his hand. “I hope it will go as smoothly as it did with you.”

“I trust your judgment on this person. I’m going to cheer you on, trust that things will get better soon,” he nodded, offering yet another meek smile.

Mydei nodded back, finishing his water and waving to him, figuring it was the time to get back on his feet and gather his son again. That talk at least calmed down some of his nerves, and, although he knew that Astraea was having fun with Yanqing and his friend, he wanted to present him to Cipher, before Phainon showed up and occupied half of both of their brains for the rest of the day.

He looked around for a while, noticing that Cipher was missing as well. Jing Yuan was on a call, but he still smiled at him and pointed the way for him, most likely where his sister went off to. It wasn’t what he was looking for, but he might as well check if she went to greet him out of her own volition. After all, it wasn’t hard to understand which one was his kid even if she didn’t see him hug him earlier.

As he walked into the hall that was indicated by his friend, he was greeted by Astraea talking to his sister, smiling and excited, while Cipher smiled back, with a kind of affection that Mydei had hardly ever seen on her face.

At least they got along well.

That exchange didn’t last too long, since Astraea noticed him almost immediately and excitedly squealed an adorable “mama!” and ran towards him, as he often did. Mydei, of course, was ready to take him in his arms, lifting him up and holding him close to his chest in a comfortable position.

“Hey, little star,” he greeted him as well, planting an affectionate kiss on his forehead. “Did you meet your aunt?”

Astraea blinked a few times, a little confused. “She’s my aunt?”

“Yes, she’s my sister and your aunt.”

“She’s like the cute kitten at the park... But she shouts a lot.”

“She does.”

Mydei let out a soft laugh as he answered, fully knowing that Cipher was right there and she could hear pretty much everything that they were saying about her. He was sure that she wouldn’t have gotten offended over it, but it was almost a given that she would pretend to.

Almost as if she heard his thoughts, she jumped right beside him and lightly punched him on his shoulder. “Hey!” she smirked, before looking at the child in his arms. “This kid is pretty cute, I’ll give you that.”

As if he didn’t know.

“I’m well aware,” Mydei smiled as he held him closer, much to the surprised and happy sounds coming from his child. He kissed him on the cheek, causing a pleased, happy sound to echo in the air, and whispered, “Cutest kid on the planet.”

Mydei watched Astraea smile again, right before his expression morphed into a tired yawn.He squeezed the plushie still in his arms and leaned on his father’s shoulder, searching for a warm and nice refuge.

He smiled, starting to slightly move his arms and rock his body to help him sleep faster. He most likely would have fallen asleep, and it was better for him to do so at the earliest possible, or he wouldn’t have slept that night. “Tired? You didn’t take a nap today.”

“It was fun… Fig Stew had fun today too,” he whined, trying to stay awake enough to tell him about his day. As he said already countless times– adorable.

“Yeah? What did you do? Did Yanqing and Yunli teach you anything interesting?”

“Yanqing has a really pretty toy that makes sounds… he played it for a bit too. He’s really good…”

He watched as the child narrated him his day, each word weaker than the previous one, clear enough that sleep was already engulfing him without letting him fight back. Despite being able to sleep during the night, he was still a five year-old that needed to take a nap in the afternoon, no matter how energetic and excited he could be.

“Okay, you should sleep,” he laughed at the third time the child blinked way too slowly, almost as if he tried to wake himself up every time that he opened his eyes. Adorable once again, but it was better if he did close his eyes for a few hours before dinner.

The child, however, whined. He sounded displeased by the offer, but not too mad or upset– just unwilling to like that particular offer. “No…” he whispered, holding his precious plushie to his chest, “I wanna see Phai…”

“Mh,” Mydei agreed with a hum, taking out his phone. He was missing him as well and that shift did seem unnaturally long, so he figured that they could hear from him how it was going. “Let’s call him.”

That alone seemed to give life and energy to the child’s light brown eyes, and his head perked up as soon as Mydei tapped on Phainon’s contact. He even felt him grow restless in his arms, excitedly waiting for the moment when he would be able to talk to him again. Neither of them had seen him that morning and, after the rhythm they set up with him at least sleeping throughout the morning in their same apartment, the lack of his presence for the entire day was meant to be noticeable.

As Mydei heard the phone getting picked up, he didn’t even have enough time to greet him, before Phainon yelled, short of breath, “Mydei! I swear I’m getting there!”

He let out a soft laugh, thinking about his partner quite literally running out of the hospital just to meet him there. “Where are you?” he asked, adjusting the weight of his child on his arm.

“Uh, heading to your place? It was hell to get out of the hospital today, sorry I’m a bit late!”

“It’s not a problem, Astraea needs to sleep and just wanted to see you. We’re at the bar near my place.”

“Anything for the little bunny! Can I talk to him in the meantime?”

Mydei turned to the kid, still intent in understanding what the two adults were talking about, and his eyes held the faintest hope of actually being able to talk or see Phainon more now than ever before. He didn’t really blame him– he completely understood that because he has been dying to see him again for the entire day and he was able to hear his voice, at least.

“Astraea, do you want to talk to Phai?” he finally asked, offering him the phone and immediately seeing the life flowing back into his eyes.

He loved Phainon so much. He was so happy that they adored each other to that extent.

“Phai!” he squealed, before exchanging his plushie for the phone, holding it up with both hands. Mydei laughed, but carefully held the plushie either way while his child chatted with Phainon for a few minutes. His heart almost ached as he watched him smile throughout his entire talk with him, excitedly explaining him what he did the day as Mydei was hanging out with his sister.

He hoped that those quiet, happy moments raised his spirits a little, after the hell of a work shift he just had.

“Mama!” Astraea beamed all of a sudden, raising the phone in the air enough so that Mydei could get it back in his hands again. The child smiled way more restless than before, vibrating in his arms just because Phainon was about to arrive there as well.

He really couldn’t have asked for anything more.

Mydei gave him his plushie back as he returned back to his talk over the phone that, honestly, could have ended right there. They didn’t have much else to talk about, after all, they could simply hang up and–

“I swear I’m almost there, Mydei.”

Of course, Phainon had something else to talk about. Like how sorry he was that he was late and how often he will remind him that he was trying oh so hard to hurry and arrive there as soon as possible and grovel at his feet for forgiveness. It wasn’t like he ever held it against him, but he had a habit of thinking that every wrongdoing towards him was some capital sin that he had to atone for and asking for forgiveness several times was the minimum that he should do.

He didn’t like it especially in these situations– it wasn’t his fault, the circumstances asked for it– but he didn’t want to scold him too much. It was something that he brought up already and he knew that he was working on it, there was no need to be aggressive or angry at him. The same sentiment could be expressed with a calm tone, and it may bring to a swifter instance of change.

He smiled, moving his arm up and down slowly to rock Astraea’s body again, this time with slightly more success. Maybe he would hold it against him because he was forcing him to fall asleep before Phainon could even get there, but they had tomorrow and they would have eaten dinner together anyway. Both of them would have been fine, even better, if they just rested for a few hours while Mydei took care of the rest.

“Take it slow, I’m not going anywhere,” he reminded Phainon, while he felt the weight on his shoulder grow heavier. He stepped out of the hallways he was standing in to lean against the wall in the main hall, next to one of the tables and pretty easy to spot from the main entrance.

He absolutely wasn’t trying to see Phainon hurriedly run towards him. He wasn’t.

… But it wouldn’t have been a bad thing if it ever happened.

Phainon’s voice ringed through the phone, in almost joking tone. “Nope! I’m almost there!”

“I understood that the other two times that you mentioned i–”

Mydei’s sentence got interrupted all of a sudden after the doors of the main entrance slammed against the wall, revealing a familiar silhouette running towards him.

“Mydei!”

He hugged him back on instinct, still unsure whether or not his child was still sleeping or if they got woken up by the sounds around him or the sudden movement against his body. He didn’t even hear a noise and when he looked down he was peacefully sleeping through all of it, so his worries ceased right away.

As soon as he stopped thinking about his child, his mind rewired all his attention on Phainon, who was clinging to him as if he just came back after months on a perilous journey and not less than a day at work. Mydei still leaned into that hug, offering his free shoulder to keep him there, at safety and warmth for as long as he might need it.

“How are you doing?” he asked, while his free hand wandered in his silver white hair in calming motions.

Phainon whined and squeezed him a little closer, careful not to wake up the child. “Not too well, but it’s going to get better now that I’m here.”

Mydei smiled as he felt his boyfriend finally get up from his shoulder to lean in again for a tired, gentle kiss. He did promise to do exactly that, and he knew that he tended to keep his promises.

“We should go home,” he suggested, placing a hand on Phainon's cheek. He leaned into it as he closed his eyes, looking even more exhausted than Mydei expected him to be. He rubbed his thumb against his skin and whispered, “Astraea needs to sleep and you should lay down for a bit.”
