His partner nodded, agreeing with those assessments. When he spoke, his voice finally sounded weak, a far cry from what usually came out of his vocal chords.

“You’re right…” he just whispered, not adding anything else and simply agreeing to following him.

Luckily, his place wasn't too far away, but he noticed just how much today has worn him down. Slower pace, unable to speak, barely able to keep himself awake.

He has never seen him like this.

It was probably just for the long day of work, but he couldn't help but think that he was suffering more than he let on and he purposefully hid it from him. That was something that could make him upset, if he didn't remember what he first thought of him when they met.

Eyes akin to the bottomless ocean and the shining sun reflected on its surface at the same time, almost betting on which one would get to be shown openly to the world.

He wasn't scared of it. He just hated to think that he was shutting him out right when he needed him the most.

With a heavy heart, he walked up to his door, almost dragging Phainon up the stairs, and shut the door behind him. He saw Phainon dive face first into the couch as well, but he didn't mind him too much for the moment. Right now, the first thing he had to do was putting his son to bed and close the door, then he could check on his stupid partner.

It admittedly wasn't too hard– Astraea slept throughout Phainon hanging onto him like a koala, so he didn't wake up even when Mydei put him to bed.

He stopped for a second to look at him, peaceful and content, and that sight single-handedly made him feel better for what kind of conversation he was about to walk into.

There wasn't something even rivaling the peace in his soul that he felt every time that he was sure that his child was safe and sound, happy and healthy. That was who everything he was doing was for. He needed to remember that.

Those thoughts were pushed in the back of his mind slowly, carefully, but that feeling was still present in his heart. It felt like a warm, soft ball of cotton against his ribcage, almost akin to a pillow, as a reminder of how good of a decision it was to adopt him despite all the challenges and struggles that he faced.

He didn't even dare thinking about what it could have happened to him if he didn't take that decision. He doubted that he could be able to live with himself if he ever doomed him to a life even slightly worse that this one.

He shoved those thoughts away right after hearing a loud groan coming from the living room.

If he didn't know that was how Phainon sounded when he was tired and uncomfortable, he would have thought that there was someone else in his apartment.

With a quick pace, he walked back to him and found him sitting on the couch instead of lying down as he thought. His eyes traveled across the room until they met warm orange staring back at him, and his expression slightly changed from slightly annoyed to almost grateful.

If he wasn't still slightly upset over the fact that he was trying to hide his feelings from him, Mydei would call it endearing.

“Lay down,” he commanded, lightly pushing him by the shoulder until he fell down onto the cushions of the couch. He looked a little surprised, but he didn’t fight back nor react negatively– he let him do what he wanted and waited patiently for his next move.

Mydei simply stared. He wanted to make sure that he was only tired, that nothing else happened, that he was at least functional to last for the rest of the day. Tired blue eyes stared back at him, vaguely empty, but that deep ocean that he remembered wasn’t there anymore. His eyes looked like a cloudless sky instead.

A hand suddenly crept closer to Mydei’s cheek and he let it caress his skin, hoping that it would at least help his partner to feel some sense of grounding. “Don’t be too worried,” Phainon whispered, with a quiet smile on his face, “it’s not the first time it happens.”

That wasn’t even the issue anymore.

It stopped being a problem for him once he made him understand that it was the same thing that he did when he had to decide what to do as he was saving people from fires. He perfectly understood that they both had to make peace with the fact that they couldn’t save everyone.

He just wanted him to talk to him about it. Get some of it off of his chest, instead of carrying every burden that he could possibly encounter. Stopping to hide it from him.

“You can still talk about it,” he suggested, trying to keep himself calm. It wasn’t his fault, he was just used to cope like this, it’s new for the both of them. They just had to be clear with each other and everything would have been fine again.

Phainon dropped his hand on his stomach, averting his gaze from Mydei. Maybe he understood what he wanted to do, maybe he didn’t like it, maybe he was too tired. Too soon to tell. “I don’t know. I feel a little… empty.”

“A child in your care died,” Mydei reminded him, noticing immediately the way his muscles tensed for a second. “If anything, you're a little too calm about this.”

He nodded slowly, thinking in silence for a few seconds. When he turned towards Mydei again, his eyes were shining, no longer empty, but with a sea of emotions behind them. Almost as if that reminder and the fact that he was forcing him to face reality and actually talk about his issues gave him back that sunlight and color that Mydei found himself loving.

It almost felt like watching the dawn on the beach. One moment it was deep, dark blue and the next it was full of light and vivid colors, ready to come to life in a matter of seconds.

He didn’t cry or tear up, but he did turn back to him and asked, “Have you ever… failed to save someone?”

That was the issue in the end, wasn’t it?

Even if he gave it his all, and he was sure that the rest of the nurses and doctors did the same, she still died. It happened, Phainon himself admitted that it wasn’t the first time, but it didn’t mean that it didn’t hurt.

Don’t bring the pain home.

It was easier said than done, especially in a field where a professional is meant to work all the time with kids that are fighting for their lives all the time. Even if he did his best not to grow too attached, it was nearly impossible for him not to feel some degree of affection towards a kid that he helped every single day.

With a heavy sigh, Mydei nodded and whispered, “Of course I did. That doesn’t mean that avoiding to talk about it is healthy or helpful in any way.”

Almost instantly, Phainon shifted uncomfortably from his position. He was still looking at him and he didn’t look upset, but he was obviously uncomfortable with those words.

Maybe he did overstep.

It wasn’t his intention, he just wanted to voice his concerns, but he could understand how he could have taken it badly. It was something that he struggled with and he just laid it out bare for him to process it on his own without the need to ask him about it first– it must have been frustrating.

“Don’t treat me as some fragile thing, Mydei, I can deal with it,” he whispered, audibly annoyed. He probably didn’t mean it either, but Mydei didn’t take it personally. Between silence and anger that he could clearly see, he would have taken the second option in a heartbeat. At least, he was showing something.

Mydei tilted his head slightly as he looked down at his from the side of the couch, where he had been kneeling the entire time. “With no need to talk about it?” he casually asked, maybe a little too directly and still insisting on the same topic.

“Mydei. It's normal,” Phainon’s voice grew in annoyance and Mydei could find the slightest tint of anger in it as well. “I work there, I know better than to grow attached to children with cancer.”

“Why are you angry?”

“I’m not!”

There it was. The yell that Mydei was looking for.

Maybe it was cruel. He did push him to shout at him over a newfound anger that he worked up and dragged out of him, but he knew that he needed it desperately. He never cried, never asked for anything, always following him, always smiling and pretending everything was fine until it wasn’t… it was nice to know that he had negative emotions, deep down.

However he felt, Phainon immediately looked at him with a horrified look on his face. “Sorry,” he whispered first, as if he just insulted him. His hand shifted to curl around the fabric of Mydei’s shirt, and he repeated, “Sorry, Mydei. It's not your fault.”

He loathed it.

Being mad at him was an acceptable reaction, and instead he was apologizing for… what, having human emotions? Not being perfect? He already knew he had all sorts of feeling and he never asked him to be prim and proper or even perfect around him. This behavior was starting to piss him off even if it wasn’t entirely his fault.

“It is my fault. I worked you up intentionally,” he explained, surprised by how calm he could still sound despite how upset he was slowly becoming. He took a moment to breathe before continuing. “You do know that keeping those ugly feelings inside won’t do any good, right?”

Phainon exhaled, exhausted. “They’re heavy feelings, Mydei… I didn’t want to involve you in them.”

Stupid.

If he could do it without feeling guilty because he was going through a hard time, he would have hit him on the head.

“I want to get involved in them because you’re feeling like shit and I want to help you, idiot,” he explained plainly, maybe a little harshly, but that attitude was genuinely getting on his nerves. Did he not already told him time and time again that he enjoys having him there with him? That he wants to be with him and nobody else? Was it that hard to believe?

True to himself, Phainon just looked at him and playfully whined, “Ah, my boyfriend hates me…”

At that point, Mydei couldn’t help a light smack on his arm. “It’s not true and you know that.”

He laughed for a second, before pulling himself together again and searching for his hand. Mydei held it and accepted that kind of request, sitting through the slight uncomfortable feeling that it seemed to dissipate and shift every time that they held each other like this. He wondered if Phainon noticed yet, but he was aware of how it must feel for him as well and he could see how it was evolving– slowly becoming pleasing for him as well.

“I’m sorry if I hurt you today,” Phainon whispered, with such a weak, low voice that Mydei feared that it would break. “It’s hard to… open up and believe someone will care or understand anything about me.”

Mydei could tell that he was struggling to even say that to him, his voice was full of shame and he seemed like he didn’t want to be heard. That front that he sensed since the first time he saw him wasn’t completely false, in the end. He just used it to protect himself from everything else, maybe pleasing people with it as much as he could.

He didn’t like it, but he understood that it wasn’t a choice born out of stubbornness or mistrust towards him– it was just how he survived until now. If anything that he told him about his past friends and short-term partners was true, along with being sent between different families with his sister, he understood why that may have looked like a good way to exist.

Except, now he had another choice before him.

Little to none of those tricks and ways to escape others’ perceptions of him worked on Mydei, so he could choose to slowly, step by step, reach out a hand and open his heart to him at the most of his capabilities.

No one was asking him to always be honest about his feelings, no one really was, but to at least ask for help and let himself feel another’s presence in difficult moments could have been… nice. It was just nice to know someone else was there for him in the past, that was all he wanted for Phainon as well, for the moment.

“I can’t guarantee you that I will always understand, but I do care about your well-being, I thought that much was clear,” Mydei answered with a whisper, matching the tone that he set. He didn’t know if it was something that Phainon enjoyed, but he figured that it was an intimate moment and it should be kept as such.

He smiled and turned his body on his side to face him, still gently holding his hand. “What sold me?”

“Your eyes and your voice,” Mydei knitted his eyebrows, warning him with a glare. “This isn’t an invitation on hiding more from me, Phainon. It’s a reminder that I notice and I know you better now.”

“You do,” he laughed, suddenly dragging both of their hands against his forehead, inhaling deeply. Mydei stood silent, waiting for the next request to arrive. “Can you give me a few days to process it? I cried enough today.”

“You cried?”

“Okay, almost cried. I was very sad.”

“Very sad,” Mydei repeated, barely keeping him a giggle. A hundred more ways to describe what was more akin to mourning than anything else, and he chose ‘very sad’. Adorable. “What a vocabulary from our nurse here.”

He made a playfully offended face, before smacking him on his chest. “Mydeimos! Your dear boyfriend is so sad that he had to call you and that’s how you treat him?”

Mydei found himself laughing along with Phainon, still controlled, still just a slight modification from the mood that he had all day, but it was genuine. He wanted to see more of his genuine feelings– his laughs could light up an entire building, if he just started to be honest with himself.

At the very least, he was glad that his attempt at distracting him, even if for just a second, actually worked as well as it did. There was no reason for him to think about it in a spiral right now. He asked for time and space to mourn, and he should grant them to him, but distracting himself for the moment would have done him some good either way.

“You should act your age more,” he scolded him playfully, drowning in the man’s giggles below him. He smiled, feeling almost drawn to that sound, and he leaned in and calmly whispered in his ear, “But I liked knowing I was the first one you thought about.”

It was true, it was how he felt. Loved, wanted, trustworthy. The amount of adoration he was able to detect in the way he spoke to him opened his eyes to think about him in ways he didn’t before.

That made him believe that they could have been able to survive, even at that pace. Even with their issues. Even while they had to yet discover each other’s worlds properly.

Phainon just smiled, his blue eyes shining of a shade that he hadn’t seen up until that moment. “Mydeimos, tell me,” he whispered, caressing his cheek with his free hand, “who else would I call?”

“Hyacine. Castorice. Your sister. Maybe you talked it out with your colleagues.”

“Right. Of course. They exist.”

They exist.

Did he even consider them, or did he instinctively choose to call him? It didn’t even look like it was a choice. He had a problem, he was having a difficult day at work, so he called Mydei. It sounded so natural. Such an easy conclusion.

Maybe he did underestimate how much he loved him.

He laughed again, maybe for his perplexed face while he was waiting for a follow-up question. “Your voice calms me down,” he whispered instead, voice calm and relaxed. “It’s so deep and soft, it rolls right off of your tongue. It’s warm too. It sounds like sweet honey all the time, it’s intoxicating.”

Devoted. Adoring. Loving.

That was all that Phainon had been with him all day, relentlessly showing how much he trusted and loved him. It shouldn't be a surprise that he liked to hear his voice as well.

And yet, Mydei smiled once again. He felt happiness spreading in his chest once again. The warmth around him heated up once again.

“You’re so far gone,” he whispered, leaning in again. He wasn't sure if he wanted a kiss yet or a retort, so he hoovered in front of his face, patient as his brain scrambled to take a decision.

Suddenly, Phainon’s thumb caressed his lips as he looked at him, a calm smile only a few millimeters from Mydei’s lips. “Am I not allowed to compliment you? I thought you wanted me to be more open with you.”

It was true. He was glad that Phainon was being so open now, even if he had to cut out all the ways he could have escaped from it. Even if he was feeling like he was doing it partly to make him happier and because he gave him a clear request, rather than thinking he deserved to express himself freely regarding his attraction to him. Even if he knew that he still didn’t think he deserved any of it.

Mydei took a deep breath, quickly reminding himself that it was a lot to unpack now, especially after the day he just had. Eventually, they would be able to talk about it, slowly and bit by bit– there would have been just push-back if he forced him further and that was the last thing that he wanted.

“Sleep for a bit. I’ll make you that soup with vegetables that you like so much,” he stated in the end, granting him a quick, affectionate kiss that Phainon reciprocated immediately.

So natural, almost like something that he was so used to that he did on reflex.

“Thank you for today, Mydeimos,” Phainon whispered before yawning, stirring a little and slowly closing his eyes as Mydei suggested.

His partner quickly gathered a heavy enough blanket and gently laid it on top of him, making sure that he would be comfortable to sleep for a few hours. It wasn’t too late, but he still needed a while to cook what he promised him and Astraea needed to rest as well. It was best if he rested well for a while before eating and spending time with him again.

Before leaving the room, Mydei glanced back at him, quietly smiling at the peaceful and rested face below him. It wasn’t the first time he found himself staring at it as he slept, but he never grew tired of it– there was a kind of serenity that he doubted he would ever see in him when he was awake.

He wished that he could see it more often, but he knew better than to hope for the impossible too soon. He believed in him and he trusted him more after the time spent testing themselves to live together, he knew that he would have been able to reach impossible goals– with time. Without pushing him too much. By trying to understand him, as Phainon was trying to do with him as well.

Trust that things will get better soon.

Sunday’s words echoed again in his mind, and he couldn’t agree more.

They rushed until now and there was no sign of slowing down, but they could take moments in that frenetic speed to look around and relax, try to understand each other and offer help or a shoulder to lean on. That was something that they had always done, since the start, and they just had to keep doing it until they deemed necessary.

As Mydei stepped into the kitchen, a warm heat spread in his chest, knowing that he was doing this– all this– just for Phainon, and the same was true for him. He couldn’t imagine being so willing to put in all of himself for anyone else now, not even Hephaestion. He loved him, but nothing that he ever felt for him bordered the limits of the amount of devotion and adoration Phainon felt for him.

He feared that, luckily for them, he was starting to feel in the same way.

Maybe not in the same way as Phainon did, but those feelings were strong enough to border simple affection or romantic intent. Adoration was starting to feel like a right term to use for his feelings now.

Those thoughts intensified, as did the warmth in his chest. He never felt so happy to make a meal for someone else, even if it was just a soup with some vegetables, potatoes and beans.

He feared that he was falling in love, and it wouldn’t pass enough time for him to realize his new surroundings before Phainon caught him. Naturally, casually, with his usual warmth, as he always did.

Chapter End Notes

This was kind of a hard chapter to navigate, but I hope that it was enjoyable !! Most of the consequences will happen in the next two chapters and this was inspired from a personal experience on both sides, so I intend on treating it with the complexity and tact that it deserves, thank you for reading ^^

chapters.title: Chapter 9
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

“So you wished she was still here and held onto Mydei instead? And now you… know him better and realized that Dad fits him better? Right?”
Astraea weakly nodded as he lowered his head. “I… just wanted her to be more like him…”
A soft smile appeared on his face as soon as he heard that little admission. When Mydei said that he was intelligent for his age, he was dead serious.

Chapter Notes

cw: mentions of self-harm, childhood trauma and child neglect

See the end of the chapter for more notes

All in all, the past week went by pretty quickly.

Phainon still didn’t cry and felt horrible about it, but he forced himself to mourn Phoebe at the best of his possibilities, helping the children close to her as well. It was a tragedy, but one that he hoped that never happened to any of them, if he could help it– even if he was well aware that there wasn’t much that he could do, apart from his best in staying close to these kids and helping them when he saw fit.

His colleagues were going through the same as well, but most of them overcame it and kept on working as they usually did. Luckily, most kids were already doing well already too.

It was something hard, but he had to look past that, if he wanted not to bring too much of his job in his private life. He basically had a kid now and most of his turns were about to be moved during the day, Mydei’s house hosting different people to keep an eye on Astraea.

Sometimes it was one of Mydei’s friends, then Hyacine or Castorice, then Mydei’s sister when she still was in town, then the owners of the bar down the street. Everyone loved him and wanted to help them.

However, Astraea did happen to have a couple of favorites, and Phainon happened to be one of them.

“Phai!”

The child’s voice caught his attention, until then split between the past week and compiling the usual documents for the payments that he received and how much he used of them that last month. Unsurprisingly, anything that bothered him during that activity was a very welcome distraction and Astraea happened to be his responsibility as well, so that stupid document could be closed and forgotten for a few more hours.

As soon as he turned, though, he noticed that something was wrong.

The excited voice was the same, but the manner that the kid used looked… off. His shoulders were tense, his eyes were darting off to the side, his hands were clasped together, nails almost trying to avoid his skin, his eyes were slightly humid, his mouth restless, munching on the inside of his cheeks.

Slowly, Phainon kneeled on the ground and extended his arms, inviting him for a hug. It wasn’t the first time that he saw him so anxious, nor the first time that he saw what Mydei meant when he said that he hurt himself sometimes, but it never got easier.

When he felt his entire weight against his chest, he held him closer, a hand behind his head and a hand wrapping him in a warm, safe place. Phainon just stroked his back for a while, not pushing him to say anything until he actually wanted to. It was already a miracle if he calmly asked him for help.

Sobs started reaching his ears while little hands pulled his purple hoodie, and that was when Phainon couldn't possibly bear it anymore.

“Baby,” he called out, pushing him back a bit and tilting his head to see just how bad the situation on his face was. Astraea looked at him, but there were tears flowing down his cheeks and his mouth parting unnaturally, so it couldn’t be good. “What’s the matter? Are you hurt?”

Slowly, the child nodded, a little scared. It was nothing that he didn’t expect yet, but it still hurt to have that kind of confirmation.

Regardless, he possibly couldn’t let him wallow in those negative feelings.

Phainon smiled gently and slightly massaged his cheeks before leaving a quiet kiss on his forehead. Hopefully, knowing that he was loved and accepted even in that moment would have helped him a little.

His heart started to rest easy when he saw light brown eyes shining as he looked back at him, his trembling greatly diminished and his anxious demeanor almost completely absent now. His little hands now grasped at his sleeves, his fists opening and closing around that piece of fabric like a cat kneading on a warm, fluffy blanket.

As he felt his breathing go back to normal and his face get relaxed enough for him to close his eyes, Phainon kissed him on the top of the head and lifted him up gently, explicitly to not bother him too much now that he seemingly calmed down. “What hurts, stardust? Do you want to tell me?”

Astraea sucked his bottom lip, right before pulling on his sleeve.

“Can I?” Phainon asked, offering a hand, met immediately with a quick nod and pleading eyes.

Whatever he did, it hurt, but Phainon was still unsure if it was because of the physical damage that he did to himself or the feelings that it brought in his mind. He was sure it was a mix of both, but he wondered if there was something on his mind for him to be so sad and anxious.

Either way, he trusted him, and he didn’t want to betray that trust.

With a swift yet careful movement, he turned around and put Astraea down on the table, leaving a kiss on his cheek to guarantee him that everything would have been fine and he didn’t have any ill intentions. Even if it most likely was just scratches, he was still a five year-old and he was scared– the least he could do as his guardian was reassuring him and making sure he trusted him a decent amount.

He knew it thanks to his profession as well, but it wasn’t what he needed now. He knew the human body after all the endless hours spent in all those boring and tedious internships that almost killed all the passion that he had for his career path, but he didn’t want to bring the nurse home to deal with Astraea too. What he asked for over and over again were his genuine feelings and himself and– even if he didn’t fully believe he was that extraordinary or good of a person– he was willing to do this for him.

As he carefully rolled up his sleeve already expecting the worst, he started seeing a few scars probably caused by burns, along with irritated skin, probably the result that brought this on. It wasn’t a big deal on a medical standpoint, it would just need cream applied for a few days for it to heal completely, but the fact that Astraea did this to himself for whatever reason was what bothered him particularly.

He had to have a clear reason, but nothing he could ever do would justify any kind of harm being made on his body, and he wanted him to remember that.

The boy sniffed up, clearly uncomfortable, yet avoiding to retreat his arm or turn away from him. Strong and brave, just like his father.

“It… wasn't on purpose…” he whispered, avoiding any kind of eye contact.

Phainon let go of his arm and smiled, waiting for him to look back at him. He understood that it wasn’t easy for him and he had to be patient, but he wanted him to feel at ease. It wasn’t his fault, and whatever thing that he did, he was sure that he could be able to talk it out of him.

When light brown eyes stared back at him, hopeful and sincere, Phainon planted a sweet kiss on the top of his head and whispered, “Don’t worry. Let's go treat them, okay? It won’t hurt at all, I promise.”

Astraea nodded as he puffed his cheeks, probably upset with himself. He didn’t talk about it a lot with him and he didn’t know if he did with Mydei, but he recognized that expression– it was the same he had when he put the blame of everything on himself even when others told him that it objectively wasn’t his fault.

Seeing it on that child wasn’t easy, but he had something that Phainon didn’t when he was his age. Stability. Support. A decent family. Even friends, lately.

Naturally, as soon as he extended his little arms towards him in a request to be picked up, he couldn’t deny him. He kept him close to his chest and rocked his body ever so slightly, trying to calm him down as much as he possibly could, but he was glad that he still trusted him and didn’t cry or freak out when he suggested the idea of being the one to medicate his injuries.

As soon as he put him down in the bathroom, on top of the laundry chest, he saw him getting slightly more restless, but he made sure to quickly show him that the only thing he was going to use was cream. It might have burned a little at first, but it was temporary and the fastest way to solve the problem.

Astraea didn’t say a single word since he started applying it on his skin, but he could see that it hurt a little. It was already a little irritated, so it was a given, but he was carefully approaching his tendency not to yell or whine for the pain. If he was a patient, he would commend him for being a good, patient kid, but knowing how scared and anxious he was, he was slightly worried that he would be preventing himself from voicing if he was uncomfortable.

With that thought in his mind, he quickly finished the job and rolled down his sleeve, waiting for him to say anything. He kneeled down in front of the child, barely in time to see him extend his arms towards him asking if he could pick him up.

Phainon smiled before granting his wish, once again walking as he rocked him a little. He still had to take a nap that day, and doing so right after crying his eyes out and reassuring him seemed good enough.

“It burns…”

It was a tiny, minuscule whine, one that Phainon had to be right there to ever hear, but he was glad that he expressed a bit of his issues. It was the bare minimum, but it had to be good for now. Just knowing which feelings he had was already a lot that to work with.

He landed a kiss on his temple, catching his attention enough that he turned around to look at him. Big brown eyes stared, and Phainon couldn’t help but reassure him further with a kind, patient voice. “It will go away if you rest a bit.”

The child sniffled and nodded, hands still gripping at his clothes. He wasn’t stupid and it wasn’t the first time that it happened, so he had to know that there have would been questions at this point. Mydei loved him and he never wanted to put him in a difficult situation, but those moments were ones that he had to ask questions and pry further to ensure his safety.

All in all, Astraea was rather calm. He could feel some anxiety, but he wasn’t crying and his breathing was normal– he even looked at him every now and again, without avoiding his eyes. It was a good thing, considered the situation.

Regardless, he had to approach the situation carefully. “Astraea, can you tell me how you got these scratches?” he asked, as kindly as he could master and still giving him all the space he needed. It was important, but it was fine if he didn’t look at him or just laid his head on his shoulder. As long as he wasn’t scared, it would have been good for him.

Almost immediately, he felt the grip on his clothes become stronger and faster breathing on his neck. He reacted almost on instinct, maybe used from his work and how many crying children he had to calm down, but he knew that right now the last thing he needed was to cry again and believe that he was at fault for those scratches.

“It's okay,” he whispered, caressing his head and rocking his body again, offering his voice and his heartbeat to calm him down. He kissed him on his cheek, trying to make himself known to him again as a trusting person that he could rely on. “I just want to know so we can try to avoid it in the future. So you don't get hurt again.”

A few sobs came out, but it was honestly less than Phainon expected and Astraea lifted his head way faster than he believed he would. There were tears in his eyes, but he wasn’t too scared and he seemed willing to answer.

Or, better yet, he forced himself to answer because he learned that asking for help in those matters will make the pain a little more bearable.

Phainon smiled and kissed him on his forehead, before whispering, “Hey, now… what's the problem, baby?”

He expected him to avert his gaze, look down, play with his hands, do something else to distract him from his eyes, but he didn’t. He simply gathered a bit more of courage and answered him, a little hesitant, but he got his answer in the end.

“I… I think I hurt Mydei…” he whispered, so low that Phainon swore that he misheard what he just said.

Hurt Mydei? There was nothing on the planet that would make Mydei mad, even less if it was Astraea. If he hurt him, he would probably try to talk it out with him, explain him why he was hurt and Astraea would learn that lesson and apply it, like any other time that it happened.

The fact that he called him Mydei too was something that he was curious about, because he never even called him anything other than Mama. To his knowledge, Mydei didn’t hate it, but he was pretty neutral to it, so if that was what Astraea was referring to, he should have rested easy.

Regardless, even if it wasn’t a big deal to him or Mydei himself, it was important to Astraea, so he should still hear him out.

“Mydei?” he asked, morbidly curious about his answer. He thought it was as he imagined, but he would have liked to confirm before doing or assuming anything. He quickly moved to sit on the couch and put the child on his lap, still letting him have the vicinity that he wanted in that moment. Then, he asked, voice kind and gentle, “Why would you think that?”

Astraea averted his gaze then, but he kept answering. “I keep calling him Mama and he said it's fine, but…”

“But?”

“It's… I don't want to.”

Phainon blinked at that statement. He expected Mydei to be the one to not be fine with it, not the child. “You don't want to call him Mama anymore? Why?” he asked, a little confused, but still careful about understanding what was happening.

“It was an accident… I was thinking about Mother when it happened, and…” he trailed off and started playing with his hands, looking down and puffing his cheek. His shoulders tensed a couple of seconds later and he raised his head again, before confessing his reasons. “He's more Dad now.”

That was what it was, then.

He didn’t know the full details to it, but it did look like he was anxious about Mydei’s reaction. Maybe they talked about it before or Mydei had some worries about that nickname.

Care and tact, Phainon. This is still a traumatized child, he reminded himself. He could have complex conversations and knew more than most would expect from an almost six year old child, but it was still rather complicated to approach the topic and he had to do so with simple words that he could understand.

“So,” he weighted his words carefully in his mind before speaking, “you wished she was still here and held onto Mydei instead? And now you… know him better and realized that Dad fits him better? Right?”

Astraea weakly nodded as he lowered his head. “I… just wanted her to be more like him…”

A soft smile appeared on his face as soon as he heard that little admission. When Mydei said that he was intelligent, he was dead serious. The fact that he could understand it on his own instead of asking about it or ignore it to go for the easier path only because he cared that much about Mydei’s feelings was beyond something that he greatly respected. Maybe he was even proud of him, but he was unsure whether he would talk of it in that way just yet.

For the moment, it was just a weirdly warm feeling towards that little child, and the closest description to him was, indeed, pride for what he was able to process on his own.

Maybe he was more introspective than children his age, maybe it was because of his difficult upbringing, maybe he had to grow up faster than he was meant to– but he was just a child. It was almost scary seeing it happen right before his eyes.

His hand landed on the top of his head, gently caressing it. “Do you know that it’s very complicated to understand that even as a grown-up?” he started, fully aware of the curious and bewildered expression of the child on his lap. “You’re really intelligent and responsible, Astraea. I’m sure Mydei would be proud of you instead.”

“But…”

“Honeybuns, you just lost her. Even now, not me or Mydei would ever push you into dealing with that by force. I can guarantee you that Mydei knows that. He just chose to trust your opinion and let you heal at your own pace.”

That seemed to put it to rest.

Astraea pouted and shifted a little on his lap, until he could sit and lay a side against Phainon’s body. He seemed calm now. Fine with the situation. Almost as if his words about Mydei were the same as Mydei directly saying it to him.

The thought of that alone was mind-blowing to him.

He and Mydei are so close to him that any word they said about what the other thought had to be true. To Astraea, at least, it was exactly like that.

“Dad’s too nice sometimes,” the child commented, with the slightest bit of hesitation.

Trying out the name. Slowly letting himself try out how it felt. Getting used to it again.

Phainon doubted he called his biological father like that if he was as horrible as Mydei claimed, but it was another way to address Mydei, and he had to get used to it. He wasn’t even bothered by the fact that he had to yet call him his father, he had plenty of time to spend with him and at the moment he was happier about this than anything else.

“He’s just a good father,” he corrected him, smiling when he saw his head perking up. “He is, isn’t he?”

“The best!”

“Do we call him? Do you miss Dad?”

The child immediately lit up, his honey tinted brown eyes shining at the mere mention of his father after being reassured that he might have been fine with being called what he wished to call him. It was normal that he’d want a definitive answer soon even if he didn’t outwardly asked for it, so they might as well try to see if Mydei would pick up.

He honestly had no idea what firefighters did for a living whenever there weren’t big fires, but he did know that he was doing something at work, so he knew that he might not answer right away.

However, Astraea didn’t know that, because Mydei always tried to pick up if it was him calling. Granted it didn’t happen much, but in his head he was probably available enough to answer the phone.

The child shifted position again, now kneeling up on either side of his thigh, gripping at his hoodie and bouncing slightly in excitement with a big smile on his face.

There really was no competition– he adored Mydei with everything that he had. Even when he was a little scared of an answer, he was so happy to be able to hear his voice in any way after a day of not being able to talk to him.

Phainon let out a happy laugh as he took out his phone from his pocket and dialed Mydei’s number. He stared so much at his contact that by now he knew it by heart, but Astraea was gripping and pulling him out of excitement so much that he opted to call him by tapping on his contact, lest he called a stranger.

Good and intelligent child, but resembling any other child his age whenever Mydei was involved. He doubted it was a coincidence.

“Hello?”

A smile appeared on his face as soon as he heard that beautiful, wonderful voice that lit up every single one of his days. A hand pet Astraea’s hair, implicitly telling him to wait a second. “Mydei! How are you?”

“I’ll be back in a few hours, why did you call?” he asked instead, probably busy with something at the moment.

He was glad that he answered anyway, if that was the case.

“Astraea really wants to tell you something.”

“Astraea?”

“Mhm, it's really important.”

Mydei had to be worried after mentioning something important that Astraea needed to tell him, but it didn’t matter. As long as he listened to him and gave him an answer withing the following minute, they would have all be fine.

With a swift motion of his hand, Phainon gave the phone to the child on his lap, as excited as ever. While he talked, he just caressed his hair and kept him close, just in case he needed it.

“Hi! I really miss you…” The voice he was using was slightly hesitant, but he showed no sign of crying again, so Phainon rested pretty easily as he listened to what Mydei was telling him. “Can Phai do potatoes too? I want both! And… can I call you Dad now?”

So easy and simple. A tint of hesitation, but nothing near what he felt just until a few minutes ago. As he expected from a child who was growing up with Mydei, he was a brave and strong kid.

A smile lit up the room, and his phone was returned into his hands. He wasn’t crying, he was pretty calm and satisfied, his body still crashed in a hug against his body again. Phainon’s hand automatically caressed his hair, slowly realizing that the call on his phone was still going.

He huffed, but continued his call with Mydei. “Accepted it?”

“Of course? It means he sees me as a completely other person that cares about him and not just someone similar to his mother,” Mydei calmly answered, laying out the facts that he already knew, as Phainon suspected.

However, he agreed with Astraea. He missed him.

“When are you coming back?” he asked, with a slightly softer voice, almost immediately feeling the child’s attention on him.

There weren’t known words to describe the admiration he felt towards his father, as there weren’t many to describe the feelings he felt for him. Two different ways to love Mydei, but they both loved him more than anything.

The blond huffed, evidently annoyed by the fact that he had to stay at work instead. “As soon as possible. I want to hug and kiss and hold my child after that.”

“As it’s natural.”

“I need to hang up now. See you later?”

“Yeah, see you later.”

As quickly as the idea bounced in Phainon’s head, so it disappeared, leaving him alone with Astraea again.

It wasn’t bad, he was used to it by now, but it was a little bizarre not having Mydei with them as well.

And they haven’t gone out alone in way too long while Phainon still had stupid fucking night turns and they overlapped with the time when Mydei was free. That may be a reason as well.

Regardless, they couldn’t stay there for the few hours that would have taken Mydei to come back home.

“Let's go do something,” he suggested, turning towards Astraea. “What were you doing earlier?”

The child thought about it for a second, maybe trying to remember anything before everything started happening. It had to have been rather heavy, no matter how fast time went by. “Drawing.”

“Can I join you?”

“Yeah! But I don’t remember what I was drawing…”

“Let’s go check, okay?”

Astraea smiled and nodded, easily jumping off of the couch and leading him to his room. Phainon, on his part, took a deep breath and ran after him– not because he was walking fast, but because he was tired and he needed to hug Mydei or he would have gone insane.

Hang in there for a few more hours, the day can’t possibly get worse than this anyway.

He walked until he stepped into his room, and if he had to describe it in just a few words, he’d use disorganized and cute at the same time. He was well aware that children didn’t put much attention on their rooms’ order in any way, but his was so inherently cute that he was willing to walk past that.

There were colors, pens, pencils, sheets and books on the floor, but the room had so many cute objects that Phainon didn’t even know if he should tell him to tidy it or not. He almost wanted him to keep that untidy angle, since they were going to spend time together anyway.

After he kneeled down, his hands shuffled throughout all the drawings– there weren’t many and the ones laid out weren’t fully understandable to him, but it didn’t matter. He made out some winged figures, so it must have been something regarding fairies, since he knew that he liked them.

Maybe from one of the books that Mydei kept reading to him or took from the library.

“What are these?” he asked when he saw him scoot over to sit next to him. “Something from a book?”

Astraea nodded and picked one of the books near him, on the floor. He showed him a familiar one, about animals, fairies and friendships, from the little that he remembered of it. “Dad read it to me. I tried too, it’s not hard.”

“Ah, I remember this one.” He grabbed it and turned a few pages, skimming through the lines. He remembered most of them, but he had yet to see the illustrations sprinkled in the entire book. He smiled softly and he turned towards him, greeted by an extremely confused expression on the child’s face. “Did you know that my sister wrote it?”

Brown eyes immediately lit up, staring at him almost in disbelief. “Auntie?”

At that point, he didn’t even need to hear him call him his father, if he was treating him as such and called his sister ‘auntie’. He practically covered that role along with Mydei, and he was more than fine waiting further until he was ready. He wouldn’t want him to go through what he went through with Mydei today.

“Her name is Cyrene, but she used another name to write this one,” he explained, closing the book and giving it back to Astraea. “She used to tell me stories too when we were younger, around as old as you. She would make up stories of fairies and magical places, and then we’d act them out whenever we were home alone.”

“Is she a fairy too, then?”

“No, she’s not. If I’d have to describe her… she’d be a cute elf. Do you know what elves are?”

The child shook his head, looking at him with his big curious eyes and the book clutched to his chest, entirely enticed by what Phainon was saying.

With that, Phainon picked up a pencil and a more or less free sheet, then he turned and asked, “Can I show you?”

At the nodding of his head, he started drawing, letting the child lean in and peek at the drawing with curiosity. “Elves usually have long, pointy ears,” he explained, as he drew those same parts, “and long, beautiful hair with a lot of intricate braids.”

Admittedly, he wasn’t an artist, but he remembered his sister enough to draw her properly. He braided her hair more times than he could remember, and he remembered all the annoying remarks on her ears– to the point that she started to take pride in them instead of getting offended.

She liked being an elf, maybe to run away from the harsh reality they had to live as children, maybe because she genuinely liked those magical creatures, but she liked them enough to write children’s books about them.

Turning her pain into happiness for others was something that he will always admire her for.

Astraea straightened up his back, suddenly more interested. “Braids like the one Dad has?”

Phainon smiled and tucked his hair behind his ear, softly looking at him with a kind of kindness that he didn’t even remember feeling ever before. It wasn’t too intense, just different.

“Sometimes he does them on you as well, right?” he asked, with a much quieter and softer voice. “We could ask Cyrene to try and do the same when she stops by.”

“Can she?”

“Mhm, I can ask.”

“Is she as pretty as Castorice and Hyacine?”

He laughed at the mention of both of them. It was nice to know that he liked them, but it was ironic that they were the ones who gave him the opportunity to move in with Mydei when he was the one that let them meet in the first place. Almost as if they were returning the favor.

The child seemed to like dresses, so Hyacine’s cute style and Castorice’s elegant casual outfits entranced him in ways that he had to yet see with other people. Most likely, he will lose his mind once Cyrene will meet him, given just how much she liked dressing up with cute, flowing dresses.

“Let’s see if I have a recent photo…” Phainon took out his phone, smiling at the child. He immediately leaned in to see his phone and, luckily, his sister sent him a photo pretty recently, so he didn’t have to go too far down his gallery. He didn’t remember what he had there and he didn’t want to figure it out with a six year-old looking at it.

He landed on a selfie that she sent him with a friend of hers, something about a fellow writer that she met. He didn’t remember the details, but she seemed to be enjoying her company and she seemed nice, so he didn’t pay too much attention to it. The important thing is that she was well dressed with a light pink and white dress, and Astraea was staring at her.

“Here she is,” he announced, slightly tilting the phone towards him to let him see the entire picture better.

He puffed his cheeks and smiled weakly, almost too in awe to do anything else. “She’s so pretty…”

Phainon smiled, before putting the phone away. That was all he wanted to show him and, since he did it, he didn’t see another reason why he would keep it out. Right now, he wanted to stay with Astraea and answer his questions about this aunt of his, if he had any.

Instead of questions, though, all he felt was Astraea’s head on his thigh. He didn’t take a nap, so he could be tired, that wasn’t what surprised him. What caught his attention was the fact that he dropped the book and gripped on his pants, maybe in an attempt to keep him in that place or to get his attention faster.

Whatever it was that he wanted to do worked perfectly though, because he did neither.

“Astraea?” he asked, a little hesitant about what was going on through his head. He honestly never knew what was the answer to that question and it was a little scary, but he always answered earnestly, so he could just hope that it would have been the same for him now.

The child kneeled up again and turned around, looking at him in his eyes as he asked, “Can you stay?”

Could he stay… of course he could stay.

He wanted to stay with him, spend time with him, help him, if he needed it. Why would he want to go away?

Then again, that was what he thought about Mydei. He wasn’t sure it was completely in the past either– he thought it was in the past many times, but it never was. There were many situations that he looked at through the worst possible lens and ended up ruining a perfectly fine bond.

Just because he was afraid. Just because he couldn’t bear the thought of anyone leaving him. He desperately acted like they wanted, hurt himself as a punishment when he wasn’t able to reflect those expectations and put the blame on himself, over and over again.

He was doing better now, he learned to keep a certain distance lest his feelings became too intense, but it was different with Mydei. He was meant to be close to him, to care deeply for him and to cherish his presence in his life. He wanted to do all of it, both for them and for Astraea.

Everything was going so much better, and he didn’t want his own issues to get in between again. Luckily, Mydei was perceptive, so he knew whenever he felt a little off or anxious, and Astraea’s presence helped as well.

A stable support system. Something that he wished he had since he was a child.

He bit his lower lip as he answered the child, trying to keep those feelings in the back of his head and hearing him out. “I have no intention of leaving,” he stated, fully believing in his own words even if doubts got in the way countless times, promptly followed by Mydei’s reassuring him that he will follow up on what he promised him. “We will all live together soon, try to wait a little more for that, okay?”

Astraea leaned on him by placing his hands on his thigh and tensing his arm, voice calm and hesitant at the same time. Change had to be scary for him too. “Can we go there soon?”

At least, he wasn’t worried in the slightest. He had no doubts that they would have ended up in that house even if he never really took a single step into it.

“Very soon,” he smiled, gently petting his head. “I wanted to show the place to you and Mydei first.”

“Can I bring Fig Stew?”

“We’ll get everything before moving, don’t worry.”

The child smiled in excitement, immediately running off towards his bed and grabbing his dear plushie and sitting next to Phainon again. He raised an arm to welcome him in a half hug, letting him lay his back against his side and play with his hand, along with the plushie.

Such a cute and loving child. He was healing too, slowly and one step at a time, just like him.

It brought him some kind of warmth, knowing that they were helping each other in their own ways, along with Mydei. He was getting better too, Phainon had noticed already in the past few months that he’s known him.

Slowly, carefully, one step at a time. Together. It would have been fine.

Astraea, seemingly unaware of his thoughts, kept on playing with his hand and laughing whenever Phainon covered his face or the plushie’s, but it unfortunately ended pretty soon. Just as the child kneeled up to gain some ground, the bell of the apartment rang, and both of them ran the option through their heads.

It could be Mydei, but he never forgot his keys and it was way too early for him to come back home.

It could be one of his friends, maybe, but they often warned whenever they visited.

It could be someone from the bar down the street or his family, but Mydei would have told them even if they asked to come by last minute.

Either way, there could be no one else. Mydei didn’t have other people that could visit him, so it had to be his friends or family, maybe coming unannounced because they knew that he or Astraea were home.

Phainon still smiled at the child, given how on edge he was for the unexpected visit. “I don’t think it’s Dad, but let’s see.”

He nodded too, taking Phainon’s hand as he followed him to the door. As soon as he stopped, he noticed Astraea’s hand gripping his hoodie, barely lessening his hold on the hand that he was already holding. It was probably nothing, but it made him aware of the trust he had in him– almost blind and complete trust.

He doubted he was like that with anyone else besides Mydei, and that alone made him smile slightly, genuinely happy of his newfound discovery.

As soon as he opened the door, though, part of that happiness disappeared.

In front of him stood Hephaestion with a book in his hand, and he already felt his head spinning. He wasn’t jealous of him anymore after everything that he and Mydei shared and talked about regarding their relationship, but he wasn’t ready to meet him alone, on his own, and absolutely not at Mydei’s place.

This was a nightmare.

“Phainon, right?” he kindly asked, hinting at a smile.

He was so nice that he couldn’t even hate the guy. Handsome, pretty, nice, well-kept, absolutely a delight to be around. He wasn’t surprised that Mydei was in a relationship with him as much as he did.

Phainon huffed, but nodded anyway. “You must be Hephaestion.”

Short. Concise. Gentle.

Please leave.

“Hi, Hephaestion,” Astraea waved behind him, in a weirdly respectful tone. Almost as if he had never seen him and his father wasn’t one of his closest friend.

Did he actually not visit that much here? Was that the case?

If that was what was happening, then he wasn’t surprised he visited without any warning. Maybe, after everything, he and Mydei didn’t talk as much as before. Even if they were still pretty close friends, he didn’t want to force himself on him or left him alone out of respect.

Honestly, he couldn’t bear it if that was the case. It was so disgustingly altruistic that he would end up respecting him instead, and he didn’t even know if he was fine with it.

“Hey, Astraea, happy to see you!” he smiled in response, slightly waving a hand. He turned back to Phainon almost immediately, handing him the book he had in his hands. “I was just dropping by for this book that Mydei lent to me a few months ago.”

Right. That time he visited Mydei. When he was in the house as well. When he was about to run away. When Astraea helped him control his breathing and Mydei sat on his lap to prevent him from leaving.

That time.

And he never came back since then, apparently.

“I'll make sure of giving it to him,” Phainon answered, taking the book in his hands.

He added nothing else, instead choosing to drop the conversation there. He would have left soon enough, so there was no point in putting himself through this torture, especially when Astraea seemed uncomfortable with him as well, and–

“Become his friend.”

Mydei’s words rang in his head again, almost like an annoying house alarm that the neighbors forgot to turn off. The last thing he wanted was become his friend, but he did promise Mydei because he cared about that type of things.

He sighed, took another breath and sighed again. He felt Hephaestion’s eyes on him, probably bewildered for that reaction, but he didn’t have enough energy to care, at that point. “Do you want to come in?” he asked in the end, obviously annoyed.

Hephaestion, on his part, didn’t comment on it. He just smiled and nodded, agreeing with the proposal. “If you insist.”

Astraea still hung onto his hand and slightly squeezed it when their guest passed by them, heading to the table in the living room. Phainon let out another sigh, maybe a tad too annoyed by his presence.

He should probably tone it down. That man wouldn’t have left Mydei’s life anyway.

“Phai…”

The sudden whisper shifted his attention to the child again, and he found him looking at him with worried eyes. He probably thought that he needed help to deal with Hephaestion, but, honestly, he felt more possessive over his peace and space than worried about Mydei leaving him to go back to his ex.

There was a big splash of it in his brain, worrying about the fact that he was way too handsome and nice to the point that he felt nauseous about it– but it annoyed having to spend time with him, rather than being scared of the thousands possibility about his future with Mydei.

If he thought about it, there was absolutely no way that he would go back with him. He knew that. Mydei himself repeated it to him a billion times, other than showing him the choice that he made over the course of the few months they went out with each other.

His heart belonged to him, or he wouldn’t have left him with Astraea, nor accepted to living with him so soon.

That voice telling him that it was his fault and that he didn’t want anything to do with him was still there and it was pretty loud, but now he could believe his memories and what Mydei promised him because he went out of his way to show him that he genuinely cared.

Use logic. Take a step back and analyze the situation. Ask the right questions to yourself and assess if that voice is right or wrong.

That suggestion was told to him countless times from different people in his life, but he could never believe their words because his brain was always right. Everyone still left. They all still abandoned him, even after saying that they wouldn’t.

Mydei was the exception– he showed it to him constantly, even when he didn’t have to. He trusted him more than anyone else he has ever been with. On top of it, he suggested to treat those voices as someone trying to make him fail, and that was the best way he found to handle it.

“Maybe you should actually fight those voices, if they’re so bothersome. They’re getting in the way, so just treat them as an enemy. Like… if you find a virus, you would like to kill it, right? Just shut them down. They’re not the ones living your life. Spite and anger aren’t always bad, it depends on how you use them.”

That was what he said, and it has proven to be useful.

If he treated it as some external entity that wanted to see him fail, he wanted to do the exact contrary of what they implied. If they told him that Mydei would have left him, he just didn’t believe them out of pure spite and checked up with him later if he was right or not.

For now, he was always ended up being right, so he would have kept using this strategy until something more useful came up. Maybe it was the wrong way to accept it, maybe he should have embraced the entirety of his issues, but Mydei was right. Those voices brought him pain and nothing else. Thinking he had to prove them wrong felt better than having to blame it on himself.

Obviously, he wasn’t a master at it yet, but it was a way to properly shoulder his everyday life and he gladly took the opportunity to try it out.

He was still working on the rest, but Mydei was rather patient and perceptive, so he didn’t worry too much about it yet.

Phainon’s attention returned to the worrying child when he felt his hoodie being pulled again, asking for an answer.

“Shh, it's okay,” he reassured him, pulling him in for a quick hug. His hand pet his head slightly, hoping that it would have been enough for him to calm his nerves. “Leave it to me. Go get Fig Stew, or he will feel all alone today, don’t you think?”

Astraea nodded left his side to sprint to his room to get it, while Phainon stayed there to seem courteous enough and not wanting to kick Hephaestion out of the house as soon as possible.

He should try at least, now that he welcomed him in.

“Sorry, do you want something to drink or eat?” he asked, with an obviously fake smile on his face. After all, he just had to be friendly with him– it was not much different from his usual job whenever difficult patients asked for his help.

Hephaestion nodded after reflecting for a few seconds. “If you have some wine, I’d gladly take it. I know Mydeimos doesn’t drink alcohol, however…”

“The best I can offer you is orange juice. Or tea.”

“Tea it is, thank you.”

Disgustingly nice, yet again.

He still didn’t let anything come through, but it was still rather annoying to head to the kitchen to prepare tea for him. Especially since Astraea seemed so worried and had all his walls up whenever Hephaestion was involved.

He honestly didn’t know if something happened, if he didn’t like him for other reasons or if he was scared of him, but he was on edge and he didn’t like seeing him like that when minutes ago he was excitedly asking him questions and playing with him.

Almost as if he summoned him, the full weight of the child crushed against him, a hand gripping at his hoodie and the other keeping his plushie close to his chest. Phainon’s hand instinctively caressed his head and pulled him in, almost promising protection and shelter in case he needed it.

The water for the tea was still boiling, so he could direct his attention to the little child and picked him up, as he was seemingly asking him. “Are you scared of Hephaestion, baby?” he asked, without proper warning.

At least, he would know before starting to actually talk to him, trying to understand what was the problem. He didn’t want to put him in further difficulties, he has had enough to last for an entire lifetime as it was already.

“You and Dad act weird around him… I don’t know if I can trust him,” he explained, a little scared to voice his thoughts. He kept the plushie as close as possible, but it still came out, so he didn’t mind if he needed that plushie as an external helper.

“He’s not a bad guy. Dad just has… a complicated history with him.”

Astraea stared at him. “You don’t like him.”

It was obvious, then. Great. Most likely, he probably destroyed his every possibility of reaching out to him in a friendly manner, but he didn’t think it was too important.

“I don’t. For the moment,” he confessed, before turning back to check on the boiling water on the stove. “But he won’t harm you, or Dad wouldn’t keep seeing him and I wouldn’t let him in. Don’t be too scared. You talked to him already, right?”

He turned to see his answer right after he was finishing preparing the tea, leaving the fragrance to get absorbed and mixed in the hot water, and a shy nodding greeted him. “He seemed nice.”

“Exactly,” he agreed, putting down Astraea again and handed him the boiling tea, momentarily taking away his dear plushie. “Let’s try this. Do you want to bring him his tea and report back what he says?”

The child looked down at the red tinted water, before slowly nodding. Brave and strong, as always.

Phainon kept an eye on him all the same, just because he was carrying scorching hot water in his hands and he didn’t want him to fall or get burned. Luckily, Hephaestion saw the situation and was careful as well, properly thanking him after he got a hold of the tea.

So, Astraea returned back safely, with a satisfied smile on his face and already asking for the plushie back. Phainon gave it back to him with a smile on his face and picked him up again, looking around the kitchen to prepare a few biscuits to eat with the tea.

“Well?” he asked, expecting already a positive answer. Maybe it wasn’t much, but even just a smile and a ‘thank you’ could move mountains for a scared child.

The child smiled and refuged in his body further, dragging the plushie with him. “He was nice.”

“There you go,” Phainon smiled, satisfied of the outcome as well. He left an affectionate kiss on his forehead, before figuring that the child in his arms would have stayed there regardless. The most amount of movement would have been to sit at the same table with him and Hephaestion.

He spent too much time with adults. He should have a friend’s place to go to, but he lived inside of Mydei’s apartment most days, so he barely had any other options now. All he could hope was that he would have found some friends when he started going to school, at least.

Either way, he pushed that thought out of his head and asked him, “Do you want something too?”

He nodded, even if a little hesitant. “That soft bread Dad bought the other day.”

“Mhm, do you want something in it? Jam, chocolate, something else?”

“Cherries!”

Which meant jam that tasted like cherries. He spent a lot of time with adults, but he had those moments where he just sounded like a child and nothing else. Cute and complicated to understand unless there was an adult that understood him enough around him.

Phainon wasn’t always able to do that, the development was pretty recent. Babysitting him for Mydei was pretty taxing, but it also brought them close enough for him to be able to do something like that.

Maybe he understood why Mydei went so out of his way to parent him now. There was so much satisfaction after all the fatigue, every single day.

He smiled as he completed Astraea’s snack and handed it to him. “Here you go.”

His body immediately moved to prepare tea for himself from the water that was left from Hephaestion’s drink, choosing another type of flavor. Just to differentiate. And he didn’t like peach, much to his sister’s dismay.

“Drink?” he turned to ask his child, still with the plate in his hands. Attentive as ever, he perked up his head, almost looking like he was an antennae just receiving a message. Phainon laughed at the reaction, then asked, “Water or juice?”

“You won’t eat anything?”

“I’ll drink tea and eat some cookies, don’t worry. Water or juice?”

“Water is okay.”

Phainon nodded and filled a glass with fresh water, then took the plate from the child’s hands and gave him the glass instead, just so he could carry more easily Fig Stew as well. Nothing happened again, luckily, even if Phainon had to go back to the kitchen to get the biscuits for both him and Hephaestion before finally sitting down.

After he placed them at the center of the table along with some sugar in case it would be needed, he smiled at Hephaestion. The man smiled back at him.

It was such an uncomfortable situation that Phainon didn’t even know how he could get out of it alive and unscathed.

As long as he didn’t talk, though, he wouldn’t see the end of it and he wanted to accelerate the process instead.

“So, did you want to talk about something in particular?” he asked, without even looking at him. His voice was nice enough, so he prayed that it would have been enough because, as it was now, he didn’t want to have a heart-to-heart conversation with him, if that was what he wanted.

Once he knew what he was looking for, he could adapt himself to the situation.

Hephaestion hummed, right before taking a sip out of his tea. “Not really.”

Great. Just great. He had to entertain him now. No topic to talk about, no Mydei in sight, plenty of voices telling him to jump out of the window and even more hatred for them to shut them all down.

Phainon was hoping that the conversation would end there at least, but unfortunately, Hephaestion continued with something that he had to yet decide if it was good or bad. “I just wanted to let you know that Mydeimos is all yours.”

He could only stare wordlessly at him after that.

Was he there to… make sure that he wouldn't get doubts about the state of his and Mydei's relationship? Did Mydei even talk to him, if he didn't visit for months? Or maybe he just hinted at it once in their discussions?

Regardless, he kept being nice to him, despite knowing his exact feelings towards him. He felt the voices dissipate slightly, and so did his anger.

It was a valid and useful method to counter what his mind made him believe about himself, but he had to measure it. Too much hate and spite would have made things end just as badly as if it was completely absent.

Right now, all he could do was hear him out and consider not to completely hate him.

He was gentle, nice, considerate, other than having Mydei’s well-being clear in his mind. He would have liked to find anything to hate him for, but there truly weren't any.

An amused laugh erupted in front of him. “You seem surprised!” Hephaestion looked at him again, then looked down towards the red hue of hot tea reflecting his face on its surface. “I broke up with him for a reason. I’m glad that he found someone like you.”

Phainon blinked, trying to understand better what that was hinting at, without finding a clear answer. “What does that mean?”

“Someone that genuinely cherishes every part of him. He’s really happy right now. The happiest I’ve ever seen him since his father’s passing, probably.”

“And that was…”

“Ten years ago, more or less.”

A decade… most of which he spent in a relationship with Hephaestion. And he was still happier with Phainon.

Just how bad was this fallout between them? And was Mydei's father so important to him? He mentioned what happened, but he thought that he made peace with it a long time ago.

Might as well ask, at that point.

“Was he that close with him? He never talked much about him,” he pointed out, before crunching on one of the biscuits and moving his mug in a circular motion, between playing with it and mixing more of the sugar that he put in it.

Hephaestion sighed, with an attitude that Phainon didn’t like too much, but he had to yet understand the reason of something like that. “You should ask him. It’s a rather sensitive subject, but I’m sure that he will open up to you about it soon enough.”

Phainon blinked for what felt the millionth time in the last ten minutes. Was he that concerned with their relationship? With Mydei’s happiness and agency in what he got to tell him?

Sure, he knew that he still had to talk to Mydei for several years to properly know him as he wished to, but the fact that the one person that knew him the best– probably outside of his mother, from what he understood– was actively trying to give them the opportunity to talk it out was… nice.

Absurdly nice, up until that point. Maybe Phainon was wrong this time.

He took a deep breath, almost looking defeated. “Maybe we started off with the wrong foot,” he whispered, both to himself and the man in front of him. As he raised his head again, he tended a hand and give him an apologetic smile. “I’m Phainon.”

In response, Hephaestion smiled as well leaning in a little to shake his hand. “Hephaestion.”

His heart and mind calmed down almost immediately. Apparently, he was no danger– as Mydei told him– and he genuinely wanted to be his friend– as Mydei suggested him. Maybe he should listen to him more often than what his brain made him believe, he seemed to be right more often that it did anyway.

Now, though, he had to make conversation with someone that he didn’t know in the slightest and the only topic he had was pretty heavy. It wasn’t like he had any other options, so he just tried his luck. “I saw you with Mydei when we first met in the hospital. May I ask what happened?”

“Leukemia,” he answered promptly, not looking too depressed about it. “I didn’t have the heart to put him through it when we were already falling out of love with each other, so I broke up with him. He still visited often, but I could see how much it still weighed on him. I’m just glad that his mother, sister and uncle distracted from it well enough. His boss did his best as well to give him something else to do and think about. It wasn’t ideal, but we both survived.”

Phainon imagined it was something of the sort, but it had to be difficult to get through it right after breaking up with his long-term boyfriend. They still saw each other, Mydei still visited and probably brought presents or flowers, or just talked to him while he was in the hospital, but it had to be hard for both of them. He wasn’t surprised that Mydei ended up having a few one night stands after that.

“Phai,” Astraea called out, curiously looking at him, “what does that word mean?”

The white-haired adult let out a tiny laugh upon seeing him with all the jam around the corners of his lips, seemingly still having difficulties eating. He was glad that he could still see him acting like a child his age, unable to get himself dirty whenever he ate something that could end up on his face.

He quickly stood up in front of him, using the paper handkerchiefs that he brought along to tidy his face enough to avoid the jam from making his clothes dirty as well. He was used to it because either he or Mydei often did it whenever he was eating something, but he still didn’t like it too much.

They were far from being able to hear him lament about it, but Phainon was beyond happy that he was relaxed enough to do that and let them look after him whenever it was necessary.

“What word? Leukemia?” Astraea nodded innocently, still munching on his piece of bread. “It’s a really bad illness that attacks your blood. Sometimes, people die from it.”

Maybe, thinking more about it, he shouldn’t have explained him what it was. He was familiar with death from the little he knew about his life before Mydei took him in, but he wasn’t sure how he approached illnesses, especially those who affected younger people as well and particularly when it was people close to him.

Evidently, he wasn’t, because he looked at Hephaestion with the saddest face that Phainon had ever seen him wear. He smiled and pet his head, not shying away when he leaned into his stomach for support and to feel his touch. He was probably a little scared by the revelation, but there was more worry than anything else in his eyes.

“Don’t look at me like that!” Hephaestion beamed, a little embarrassed. For the first time an emotion that wasn’t just being courteous, at least. “It was just another fight I had to win, no more and no less. Luckily, the doctors were able to help me recover.”

Astraea, however, still looked to Phainon. He believed Hephaestion’s words, but he searched for his approval anyway, almost as if he had to ask him to be completely sure of what was in front of him.

Phainon smiled and gently ruffled his hair. “It’s not something that everyone gets, don’t worry. You went through a lot of tests when you first started living with Dad, right?”

“Hyacine took my blood too.”

“Then you’re fine. Like I said, it’s not contagious and not everyone has it, it’s rare among children too.”

The child looked up to him with big, questioning eyes, but he eventually nodded. He still didn’t go of his hoodie, but he did understand, at least. He doubted he was going to leave him any time soon and he knew what those eyes wanted to say, but he still waited for him to make an actual request.

“Papa, up.”

Phainon froze.

Papa. Papa? Really? Now? With Hephaestion right in front of him who immediately realized the situation and covered his mouth with his hand? Waiting for them to figure things out? Sipping on his tea?

He did seem a demon now. Mydei was right– he was, indeed, a menace. Not in the way Phainon expected, but a menace all the same.

“Papa…”

Phainon blinked again, waking himself from his trance and finding Astraea whining and pulling on his hoodie, requesting the same thing again without voicing it properly this time.

He took him up in his arms, almost absentmindedly, still stuck on how he called him. Mydei was certainly less catatonic when he was called any semblance of that name, but he cared only relatively. He almost gave up on the possibility of getting called anything close to Papa even if that child already recognized him as such, and then he hit him with–

A kiss on his cheek pushed his every thought out of the window, just to turn and see Astraea giggling. “Papa is so funny sometimes,” he whispered, keeping on giggling as if he just saw the funniest expression on his face.

Astraea was a traumatized child.

He had to keep reminding it to himself.

In his arms there was a young child who yearned for parents he could trust, a slow, secure, normal life and friends he could spend time with. And he was trying really hard to focus on the present as well– he shouldn’t be surprised that he started calling him like that, after all the promises of living together, his constant presence in the house and his open affections for Mydei.

The child already loved him, he had to be thrilled about seeing him so often and Mydei being in a romantic relationship with him.

So, Phainon didn’t even comment on it, responding with just a smile and a playful kiss under his chin. The child giggled a little louder, and kept on smiling until he sat down and let him stay on his lap. “Do you want to finish your snacks here?” the adult asked, while Astraea seemed happy and restless on his thighs, throwing his head back to look up at him and laughing happily.

“Yes!” he giggled again, turning around now to hug him. “You’re always so hot.”

Phainon laughed softly, right before correcting him. “Warm.”

“Warm! Papa is so warm all the time!”

“Why, thank you, Astraea!”

There was a special kind of warmth that came whenever he talked with that little child, completely different from the one that Mydeimos gave him. It grew in his chest, warm and stable, quietly and calmly spreading in the rest of his body, but never violent. Never strong or forceful. Never intense. Just like calm waves by the beach during a sunny day.

They should bring him to the beach someday. He may like it, and it would be a good opportunity for them to spend a nice few days.

“I understand why Mydeimos likes you so much. You’re so radiant and gentle, other than being good with children.”

Hephaestion’s voice echoed through his ears, as if his brain already erased his presence from his surroundings to focus on feelings that he deemed more important. He wasn’t properly sorry, but it wasn’t very kind of him, given he had been nothing but nice and understanding since he stepped foot into the apartment.

As he was about to ask forgiveness, Hephaestion talked again, echoing his feelings from earlier. “Please, don’t hold back and don’t worry for me. I accepted we were better off as friends long ago. Love him fiercely as he deserves, and don’t hold doubts for me anymore.”

So nice. Disgustingly nice, he still thought. But supportive as well.

He understood why Mydei liked him as well– strong and gentle, trusting and independent, sensitive and able to joke and pick on anyone he wanted. A man of contradictions, just like Mydei himself, full of the qualities that he repeated he liked about Phainon.

Maybe that was why he said that they’d get along well… and he was probably right. He just had to believe him and actually try to talk to him, curse his own mind.

A soft laugh came out of Hephaestion’s mouth again, before he put down his now empty mug. “Well, it’s better if I go. Thank Mydeimos again for the book and don’t do anything weird,” he stated, as he stood up.
