He looked over to Phainon with a smile painted on his face, right before winking at him. “I’m rooting for you guys and I have a bet about this, don’t let me down.”

He had a what now?

“Uh, sorry?” Phainon tried, not believing his own ears.

“See you soon, Phainon, Astraea!” he quickly waved instead, seeing himself out and already opening the door for himself. Phainon didn’t even know what to say to anything that came out of his mouth, but Hephaestion seemingly didn’t care because he just smiled at them and said, “Thanks for the cookies and tea!”

The slam of the door was the last thing that he heard before he could be left by himself, Astraea still finishing his bread.

After meeting all of Mydei’s friends, Phainon could state with confidence that Hephaestion was definitely the weirdest and most interesting one. No wonder Mydei liked him.

“Dad has weird friends,” Astraea commented as well from his lap, with some food still in his mouth.

Phainon laughed softly, before wiping out all the scarlet red jam from his mouth again, hopefully for the last time. “You like Ptolemy.”

“Ptolemy brings me books and he reads them like Dad. And he’s really nice.”

“Is he your favorite?”

“Always after you and Dad.”

He would lie if he said that his heart didn’t bathe in warm light yet again. He was so happy that he called him Papa, that he saw him as Mydei’s lover, that he loved him so much. He was such a brilliant, wholesome, adorable child. He didn’t even mind the added difficulties that came with his complicated past, as long as he could feel better in the future.

When Mydei told him that he took him in almost on a whim, he didn’t understand him to the fullest, but now he did. He truly was a special child. The fact that he had the slightest hint of Phainon’s same hair color in a sea of Mydei was almost a bonus to an already winning lottery.

This got him the best partner he has ever had and the most beautiful child on the planet. He had to be in some Gods’ good graces.

“Shall we go back?” Phainon asked as he handed him the half glass of water that he had left, watching as he obediently drank it all in one breath. “You can read that story to me so I can understand your drawings too.”

The child excitedly nodded, leaving everything as it was on the table for him to tidy, and Phainon shook his head with a half laugh leaving his lips. They really had to teach him how not to leave so many things hanging around the place.

He ultimately didn’t mind to put them back where they had to be put since he was still pretty young and didn’t want to dim his excitement about narrating his favorite stories to him, but knowing where his things are without losing them would be a good future goal that didn’t take too much out of him.

The story was familiar, some things that his sister took from what she narrated when they were children, and weaved it in a beautiful story for others to immerse all of themselves into, so that they wouldn’t feel alone anymore.

She’s always been a bit of a dreamer, always talking about mystical places and romantic stories, but it was impressive how she was able to live off of her passion so early in life and to dedicate herself to let other people live through her fantasy and give them a chance to dream with her.

The fact that Astraea was one of the people that dreamed with her and that he reasoned so much with her stories just made him even prouder of his older sister and the type of life that he started to embrace after he met Mydei.

A few hours went by with just Phainon listening to Astraea talk about his favorite books or reading some to him– because the little child claimed that he wanted to hear his reading voice, since Mydei and Ptolemy were different readers– but as soon as he heard keys turning and a lock opening, he perked up and look towards the entrance.

Phainon smiled softly, watching as the little child stood up and peeked from behind the doorframe, excited and a bit anxious, but overall happy to see Mydei again.

“Dad's back?” he asked, waiting with anticipation to see if he was right.

He nodded, standing up as well. “I think it’s him. Shall we go and greet him?”

Astraea didn’t even wait to answer, sprinting in the direction of the door unprompted and immediately hugging Mydei as soon as he stepped foot inside the apartment. Phainon limited himself to watch the scene, his shoulder leaning against the doorframe of Astraea’s room, beyond pleased to see the smiles on both of their faces after so much turmoil happening in the last few hours.

“Hey, were you waiting here?” Mydei asked, welcoming him in an embrace that he probably wanted to give him since he knew of what was going on.

“I missed you lots,” the little child confessed, clutching his arms around his shoulders as his father hugged him, just for a couple of seconds before getting go. With a shy expression, he looked up to him and tried to mutter another apology, but he didn’t even have the time to speak that he was pulled into another hug.

“Don't be sorry, it's not your fault,” Mydei whispered, caressing the back of his child’s head for a few seconds. They didn’t stay in that hug for long, since Astraea’s worries were already subsided and Mydei’s need to check on his son’s well-being was already met, but it seemed that both of them wanted it anyway.

Phainon sighed and walked slowly towards them, still keeping his distance. Astraea did start seeing him as a parental figure and Mydei probably already deemed him a vital part of his life, but he still didn’t want to step into a moment he didn’t belong in.

After all, even when they will start living together, they will need alone time sometimes. As he and Mydei or he and Astraea will as well. It was normal.

Somehow, repeating it in his head made it seem normal and something acceptable. Seeing them being happy without worrying whether or not they would abandon him was actually very nice, and he didn’t want to give up on that feeling now that he understood how to get there.

Mydei cupped Astraea’s face with his hands, smiling brightly at him. “I do prefer Dad, don’t worry.”

The child just smiled, probably finding himself in the exact place where he wanted to be since his doubts started swarming his mind. “So is Phai Papa now?” he asked eventually, as innocently as ever.

He had to get used to it.

Dad and Papa. Wow.

Phainon watched as Mydei laughed softly and dared to suggest, “Hasn't he always been?”

Mydeimos and his need to tease him was probably something that Phainon would never escape as long as he lived and he was perfectly fine with it. Besides, he could do the same to him any time.

“I like Papa!” Astraea smiled, moving to hug Phainon’s side. “Don’t change him, please.”

He stepped closer to him, taking his partner’s chin with his thumb and index finger, looking at him for a second before giving him a gentle kiss. Phainon urged himself to kiss back, but he didn’t turn even when Mydei moved his head back to talk with his son again. “I won’t, there’s no need to worry.”

Blue eyes lingered on that face, smiling at his– maybe theirs now– son, brightly smiling back without letting go of the fabric that hung against Phainon’s upper body. A hand moved to pat his head again, right before the child flew off again to his room, seemingly unprompted.

“Astraea,” Phainon yelled, calling out to him without really needing him to look at him and just listening to him, “tidy your room a little, or Dad will have a heart attack!”

The child still peeked with a big smile on his face, but the only thing he muttered was a loud “okay”, before disappearing again behind the doorframe. Sounds of sheets being moved around and shuffled could be heard from where they stood, so Phainon assumed that he listened to him and actually took his time to finally tidy his room.

His gaze lingered a little on the entrance of the room, until Mydei forcefully hugged him, almost making him lose his balance. He promptly hugged him back and did all he could to stand up without falling down on the floor because, honestly, landing on the hard, cold floor with a man as heavy as him on top of him was the last thing that he wanted to experience right now.

Maybe there was no need to be afraid, since Mydei seemingly kept his hand behind his back to keep him upright– almost as if he wanted to surprise him with that sudden affection knowing how Phainon would react. As if he knew him enough to predict that already.

Yet another warm feeling settled in his chest, even as he just escaped landing butt-first into the ground.

“You have no idea how happy I am right now,” Mydei whispered against his ear, tone soft and warm. “Being greeted home by my son and my boyfriend that somehow got him to use both Dad and Papa over the course of a few hours is a sight that I won’t forget easily.”

Phainon let out a soft laugh, accepting the eventual kiss that followed that sentence. He agreed with him, the happiness sitting in his chest was so concrete that he could almost physically feel it with his hands if he just put them over his heart.

He wasn’t even sure it was what they had been trying to do when they got together– he just liked Mydei more than anyone else that he had ever approached, but he didn’t mind the son that came with him as part of the deal. Now, though, he would sacrifice himself for his happiness.

Mydei let out a sigh against his cheek, catching his attention again. “I was getting worried… I had no problems getting called Mama, but he did seem restless for a few days and I was praying that it was nothing serious.”

“You said you prefer Dad.”

“I do, but I never mentioned it to him. It’s something that he thought about on his own and he ended up realizing that he was projecting heavily his feelings for his dead mother onto me, so he wanted to right that wrong. I’m proud of him.”

It was impressive. He was about to turn six years old– even if he kept saying that he already was for as long as he could remember– and it was incredible that he understood Mydei’s feelings and his own trauma shaping how he viewed him.

Not even some fully matured adults knew how to spot it, but that just proved how reflective he was of anything around him, especially if it concerned either of them.

Phainon sighed as well, offering an open hand when he noticed Mydei trying to intertwine his fingers on his own accord. It didn’t happen often, so he let him do whatever he wanted, keeping himself up while his partner’s free arm wrapped around his right shoulder as well. There were often easy, domestic moments such as that one, and he grew awfully used to them.

“How did he even figure that out… he’s six years old,” Phainon lamented, still incredulous about that piece of information.

It hadn’t been too long from his parents’ death, but he already stepped away from unhealthy coping mechanisms too. Either Mydei’s parenting was miraculous or he was an incredibly self-reflecting kid– or both, honestly. He could definitely believe the first to be true, if he thought about it.

“I put the doubt in him when he started calling me that,” Mydei whispered, aware of the vicinity between his mouth and Phainon’s ear, much to his relief. “I asked him if he was confusing me with her and he told me that he wasn’t, but a few months went by, he got to know me better and effectively realized that I was completely different from her. Luckily, he tends to overthink and puts importance on my feelings as well. That’s probably why he was scared.”

So, both. Mydei was just that good with children.

Even when that was the case, though, he didn’t let himself forget about the scratches on his body that he still had to figure out how got there in the first place. They weren’t many and luckily there wasn’t any blood, but they were clearly self-inflicted. That was what disturbed him the most.

“He hurt himself before he told me,” he confessed, trying to focus on the relaxing movements of Mydei’s hand on his. “He was afraid to hurt you and he couldn’t bear it. There was no blood and he just scratched his arms, but I medicated them already.”

Mydei let out a steady breath. “He’s getting better, then.”

Better.

It was getting better now. Phainon was even more afraid to ask about any scars or cuts that Mydei found on him again.

He still dared to ask out of concern. “Was it worse before?”

“He didn’t ask for help before.” Mydei shifted his position slightly, turning his head to properly look at him before letting go of his shoulder to rest a gentle hand on his cheek. Probably, he just wanted to make sure he wasn’t overthinking, but that gesture alone made his nerves dissipate significantly instead. “Or, he did, but in rare cases and I had to pry out of him what was the reason. It’s normal for him to relapse sometimes, but as long as he asks for help, it’s going to be fine.”

He was right. It was difficult to get out of that mindset, but they couldn’t do much more than offering love, stability and support.

Maybe, Phainon himself would have ended up in a difference place as a child if he ever got a parent like Mydei is for Astraea. It was a little too late to think about it, but he did make himself those kind of questions even if he ended up being pretty well-adjusted and lived a relatively happy life.

It just meant that Astraea would get what he did, at the very least.

“Slowly. He’s intelligent and hardworking, he will get there,” he muttered, before turning towards Mydei with a proud half-smile. “Besides, he has two fathers, a few aunts and several other adults that all love him.”

He let out a soft laugh, nodding to himself and leaving an affectionate kiss on his cheek. “I'm going to take a shower, do you have to go to work later or I can take my time with preparing dinner?”

“No, they’re forcing me to take a few days at home to adjust to the new shift. And I can make dinner, you just came home from work.”

“The kitchen is at your disposal, then. Astraea wants potatoes.”

Phainon let out a loud groan, leaning his head on Mydei’s shoulder. His partner softly laughed at the reaction, but all he did was letting go of his hand and gently stroke his back, as if to tell him to find strength after the news. “Potatoes again... I don’t think I’ve ever eaten so many potatoes in my entire life.”

“Prepare something else for us and add some meat for Astraea,” Mydei suggested, well aware that he was right. Potatoes weren’t in the plans and it was a food that the child fixated on lately, so they were just standing as victims for the time being, but Phainon knew he was right– they couldn’t eat them three times a week if they valued their own mental well-being. Mydei huffed, caressing his hair briefly. “He asked about it and he had a hard day, but season the meat properly, Phainon. Salt isn’t seasoning.”

Again bringing up that accident… Phainon couldn’t help but let out a heavy sigh, even if he knew that he was right. He just didn’t know where his seasoning was nor knew the correct one to put in, so Mydei had to tell him and has picked up on him ever since.

It wasn’t something that bothered him, but the fact that Mydei was willing to give him full control of the food that they all were about to eat spoke volumes about how he actually felt about it.

Phainon learned that he didn’t say outright what he felt and trusted his actions and intentions to speak for him, and that was what made easier to calm his nerves when it came to their relationship. Everything that Mydei did was clear, he always knew what he was trying to say and he recognized that it was something that he needed.

“I’m going to drag that into my grave, aren’t I?” he asked in the end, keeping up the joking attitude. He liked it and it kept everything more playful and interesting– he adored teasing him and getting teased back, almost like a back and forth challenge between them.

Mydei smiled and let go of him, forcing him to raise his head again. As soon as he looked at him, he found his lips against his cheek again for a split second, while his hand kept his chin still. “But I trust you for the rest as always, and I’ll come help you in a while,” he whispered, before letting go and disappearing in the bathroom without another word.

On his part, Phainon stood there, still and albeit a little thrown aback by that last sudden gesture. His hand traveled to his chin, caressing the skin that was held by Mydei until a few seconds prior, shocked of that last conversation.

He didn’t even mention Hephaestion visiting, but he could tell him later. He must be tired now.

Regardless, he noticed just how happy he was.

Of course, he didn’t know if it was because Astraea called him Dad, or if he called Phainon Papa, or if he asked for help when he needed it. Maybe all three.

Phainon was certain of something else now, even if he suspected it for quite a few weeks now. He honestly, truly, didn’t want to leave. He spent all his life searching for a place he could turn to, and now that he found it, he absolutely didn’t want to let it go.

His few months with Mydei quickly turned to more than just dating a single father and he started realizing it just now– it was grander than that. The time he spent with him and Astraea started to heal something that he didn’t know needed the right space to breathe properly.

Home. That was what it felt like.

Maybe it was stupid and childish, and maybe a little arrogant given how much his sister sacrificed for him, but he couldn’t help but describe it like that. Cyrene was living her own life, chasing her own dreams, and so was Phainon. He just so happened to yearn and look for something resembling a home to go back to and to lean on, rather than anything revolving around his career like his sister was doing.

He was obviously happy for her, but he needed this. He needed Mydei, and Astraea, and stability, for once in his life.

For once, he wasn’t forced to light his own sun to keep himself warm. For once, he could let himself feel warmth from someone else holding his hand or leaving him a kiss or simply talking to him. For once, he wanted to try and desire something for himself without being forced to let go, and he knew that same wish was made for him as well.

Maybe a little star would look down on them and keep things the way they were now, but for the time being, he was more than happy to treasure that time with the two people that barged into his life and changed it for the better in so little time.

Chapter End Notes

Kind of short update, but I wanted to write the Hephaestion and Phainon meeting so here we are ^^ the change of name for Mydei was meant to be for chapter 11, but since it was hinted in the last chapter and the two separated would have been half the length of this, I just merged them, but I still hope it was enjoyable !! And Cyrene will appear soon so I figured I'd start talking about her a little more :]

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei rolled his eyes and leaned into his shoulder, without quite resting his head on it. “What’s the problem now? Still too sleepy?”
It was meant to just be a slight teasing, but Phainon kept his hand close, just shifting it to properly hold it. Then, as he leaned in his ear, he whispered, “Did I hallucinate that you searched for my hand without flinching in front of everyone for the first time?”

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“Why did you stay up that much last night? You knew we'd have gone out today.”

Phainon groaned loudly, the annoyed sound quickly transforming into a yawn mid-sentence. “Just… got zoomies.”

Mydei huffed, shaking his head as he finished fixing the cloth on the ground, trying to keep it as spread out as he possibly could to cover the area they would need for lying down or sitting above the grass. Astraea quickly carried a bag with food and a few games they brought, handing it to his father that he used it to pin the cloth to the ground.

“Phainon,” he sighed, finally looking up to him, “you can't get zoomies.”

“Why not? It's real!” he whined, handing him another bag, meant to be yet another weight to keep that long cloth still. “I just had the need to really look into the layout of my apartment, just so we would know what we should move around! Astraea wants all his room like it is now and we surely want something nice for ours, and then some more spaces to play and—”

“Calm down. You drank too much coffee today, you know how fast you talk when you do that.”

“I need to stay awake in a way or another! I wanted to finish it and today it's Astraea’s birthday and my sister is visiting—”

“Calm. Down.” Mydei moved the rest of the bags away and took off his jacket, adding it to change clothes that they brought with them just in case. It was a picnic, but they didn’t want to risk anything– and not it will be used as a pillow for Phainon. “No zoomies. Yes napping.”

He nodded as he thought about it, taking the semblance of a pillow that Mydei just put together. “Napping sounds nice,” he agreed, sliding down to follow that suggestion.

With another sigh, Mydei finally nodded and sat facing away from him, finally calm about the fact that he would rest a little. He seriously felt like a whining child sometimes. Not even Astraea ever whined or refused to take care of himself as much as he did.

“Dad?”

The quiet call made him turn and smile at his child, extending an arm to invite him in a hug. “Shh, Papa is really tired,” he explained, waiting as he walked closer and sat on his lap.

“Papa is tired so often…” Astraea commented, lowering his voice as a response.

“People at work kept him there a little too much until recently and it's hard for him to adapt to another schedule again. He needs to sleep a little more today, I'm sorry, pumpkin.”

“As long as he's fine.”

“Exactly, his health is the most important thing.”

Astraea nodded, before looking over his father’s shoulder, without stepping away from the safe embrace that he was being offered. “He always says that too but then he needs to sleep…” He looked back at Mydei, slightly tilting his head to the side. “Papa is that long word you said the other day.”

If there was one difficult thing about understanding his son, it was whenever he mentioned a word that was long or difficult for him, but completely normal for Mydei himself, so he had to take a wild guess. ‘Long word’ didn’t really cut it down and it being applied to Phainon didn’t help either.

“Mh… Stratospheric?” he hesitantly asked, trying to remember what he was talking about.

Unsurprisingly, the kid shook his head. “No, no! The hippo one.”

“The hippo… Oh, hypocritical. Yes, he is hypocritical.”

“Hypocritical, hypocritical!”

Mydei smiled as soon as he saw the smile on his son’s face, excitedly repeating a word that he probably won’t use for the next decade. He often did it to remember it for the future, but some words were too complicated and complex to even fit into anything he could ever say in his everyday life.

He still let him, watching as Astraea rolled to the side and leaned on his thigh with his hands while he kneeled down next to him, his eyes sparkling as he looked at him. “Today Auntie Cyrene is coming. Dad, she's really really pretty.”

Of course, he knew. They were there for Astraea’s birthday, and Phainon’s sister immediately asked if she could come over since she was free and she expressed her wish to meet both Mydei and Astraea. It was just a good opportunity to make it happen and make the child happy, since he seemed to like her so much.

“Oh, is she?” Mydei asked, smiling at the child next to him. “Did Papa show you a photo of her?”

“Yes, yes! I wanna ask her where she gets all those pretty clothes!”

“I’m sure she can tell you.”

The child smiled and nodded, before standing up again and falling right back in his father’s arms, resting his cheek on his shoulder as some sort of refuge.

It would never stop making Mydei the happiest man on the planet. Seeing how much his son trusted and loved him even after such a short period of time made him unapologetically happy.

His hand rubbed on the child’s back, smiling at him as he kept him close and safe in that position. “Are you happy, stardust?” he asked, with a soft, mindful voice.

A small nod sat itself in motion over his shoulder. “Thanks for saving me, Dad. And not giving up on me.”

Mydei pulled him a little closer, squeezing his body against his chest. He didn’t even have to mention it, he would have been physically unable to leave him to social services anyway, but he was glad that he was doing something good for him, at least.

“I would have never been able to abandon you there.” He kissed his head, keeping him in that embrace, but he still kept his arms loose enough in case he wanted to roll away. “It was the best decision of my life. Both I and Phainon love you more than you can imagine.”

Maybe it was too much of an admission, but he should have known that little, truthful fact, at the very least. Even just thinking that he could feel even remotely unloved or ignored was something that bothered him.

If he knew that, maybe he wouldn’t have been so preoccupied with calling him in another way just a few weeks prior. He wanted it to be clear, so, perhaps, he could have avoided feeling like that ever again. Even if it was impossible erasing his memories, he wanted to offer new ones that he could rely on, and he had to know how much he was cared for in order for him and Phainon to offer him a happier life.

The child pushed back a little, falling on his lap and leaning back. Mydei’s arm instinctively protected him from a fall, while his tiny, little hands came closer to his face, his curious expression analyzing every inch of his face.

Mydei wasn’t too sure if there was a facade or not, or if it looked as melancholic as he was feeling, but he figured that it wasn’t too important. His child had already figured out what was going on in head several times, one more time wouldn’t be surprising.

“Don't be sad, Dad…” he whispered, a little confused on his own words. He probably didn’t know the exact word, but he understood that there was something wrong either way. “Papa would be sad if you’re not happy even if he’s sleeping now.”

He laughed, nodding to himself. “Your father gets sad about the littlest things.”

“It means he cares lots. I like a Papa who cares lots rather than someone so strong that he doesn't show emotions.” He sat back up and smiled, seemingly happy to even just talk about him. Mydei’s hand traveled to his head as he spoke, offering the amount of affection he deemed necessary. Astraea looked up and smiled with his tongue in between his teeth and stated, “I like Papa like he is, even if he's sad about little things.”

Mydei couldn’t help but smile back. “Me too,” he agreed, before turning around and noticing just how much his belongings were spread outside of the cloth that he laid down. “Come on, help me a little.”

Astraea nodded excitedly and, sure enough, he did help him. He couldn’t move anything too heavy, but he did help him for how little he could do, all while leaving Phainon alone and letting him sleep peacefully. Listening to Mydei wasn’t something new for him, really, but it was almost exciting to see how happy he was to just be involved in whatever they did, whether it was boring or not.

It most likely meant something that Mydei and Phainon didn’t like to think about, but it mattered less than they probably thought anyway because it was in his past and not something that reflected his life now that he lived with them.

As always, little Fig Stew ended in the child’s hands without no one noticing and, before Mydei realized, he rested his head on his father’s thigh and used it as a pillow, completely focused on the plushie in his hands.

Mydei just left him there, knowing that he wanted his alone, silent time whenever he brought out that plushie whenever he was out with him. He was doing so much better now, but he still needed some time for himself whenever he was in an unfamiliar environment, without people he knew and trusted or both.

Maybe going out on a picnic wasn’t the best decision for his birthday, but he wanted him to just try it and see if he liked it. He was almost completely sure that he never tried it with his former parents, so he offered it to him without thinking too much about it and Astraea looked quite excited about it, so he didn’t even question it.

Hopefully, he just needed a while to recharge his batteries and enjoy this day.

“Excuse me, is this free?”

The nice, gentle voice accompanied by a few laughs and some yells in the background that he couldn’t fully catch made Mydei’s attention shift towards its source, just to see an elegant woman with long, red fiery hair smiling at him with three children with shorter hair of the same color. Probably relatives in some way.

He felt Astraea getting back up from morbid curiosity, which maybe was going to be a rather positive thing for the rest of the day. He didn’t do well with new people in his face, but he was curious and kind, at least enough to get excited about knowing them.

“Oh, yeah, we don't mind,” Mydei hurriedly said, still keeping an eye on his son.

Just observant. Looking at these new people and that was it. Curious as usual.

The children with the woman, however, weren't quite as calm as he was. One in particular, with a side braid and a little mischievous face, looked way too excited to see him.

“Woah! Your hair!” she exclaimed, pointing a finger at him. He didn't move, but he did tense his muscles as the girl ran closer. “It’s so pretty!”

Mydei decided not to interfere, however. He knew that Astraea asked for help whenever he needed it and, right now, he didn't look like he did. He was a little weirded out, but he just hugged his plushie and stared back at the girl in front of him, as silent as before.

Gathering courage and not running away even if it slightly scared him. Good.

“Trianne, let him breathe,” the woman with them scolded the child, before turning towards Mydei with a worried and mortified expression. “I'm sorry, they're a bit energetic… we can move.”

Mydei smiled and shook his head, hopefully being able to interpret his son's wishes. He looked more sure of himself and curious, more than scared. “No, it's fine. Do you mind, Astraea?”

The kid shook his head, staring at all three of them instead. “I like the flowers in their hair,” he commented, rather innocently.

Curious, curious child.

He could be the most introverted kid on the face of the planet, but he would take arduous paths on socializing with new people in the name of curiosity alone.

The girl in front of him beamed, a little too happy that this kid that she just met complimented all of them. “Oh, I know! Come play with us! I’m Trianne, that's Trinnon and that's Tribbie!”

Astraea was a little confused. It was obvious to anyone that he was, and with good reason. Three girls that he had never met in his life were pulling him along just to play with him for a few hours– that was probably the nightmare of any introverted kid.

He retracted into his own little body, leaning on Mydei's arm, his plushie still clutched close to his chest. He still wasn't quite scared, but he started to feel slightly uncomfortable.

“Astraea,” Mydei calmly called out, offering a gentle caress on the top of his head, “why don't you give it a try? If you don't like it you can run here again.”

The child looked up to him a little worried. “And we can read a story?”

“And we can read a story.” Mydei tilted his head, still letting him to be as close to him as he wanted. “So?”

Astraea looked at his plushie, then at the girls, then back at his father, and nodded, already standing up from the ground.

When Phainon told him that he was brave and strong, he was beyond proud of him. He knew that he could do anything that he set his mind into, no matter what it was, but others rarely caught it.

He was glad that Phainon was the one who saw it as well.

“See you later, Dad,” the child greeted him, giving him a kiss on the cheek, maybe more for himself than Mydei.

His father smiled back at him, affectionately ruffling his golden hair. “See you, stardust. Be careful and step away if you feel too scared.”

The child hummed an acknowledgement before tensing his shoulders and following the already excited group of girls into whatever they wanted to do with him.

Mydei watched as they walked not too far away, seemingly just talking or getting to know him. They didn’t seem bad kids and the adult with them looked beyond responsible, even just for how quickly she scolded them for making Astraea uncomfortable.

Turning around, he checked whether or not Phainon was still sleeping and, much like he expected, he didn’t even stir. He doubted that it was just a sleepless night, but it was something that he would need to check it up with him sometime in the future. Not on the day of their child’s birthday, at least.

It was still hard to see him as their child, but not something that either of them necessarily hated. Astraea was their child, it was a matter of fact at this point, it just felt too good to be true, even if the child himself chose it and they were hoping for it constantly for months.

It was hard now, but it will feel familiar in due time. Just like Phainon’s presence slowly started to feel normal, the fact that now Phainon was as much of a father to Astraea as Mydei was will eventually start to feel normal as well. Expected. Natural.

His attention diverted to the woman in front of him, intent in keeping an eye on the kids as well. They weren’t even that far away and no one else was in that area of the park, but he understood feeling a little on edge without dropping an eye on them every now and then.

She turned around and smiled warmly at him, her long, red hair dropping on her shoulder as she moved her head. “My name is Tribios. I’m their older sister,” she explained, figuring that, since those kids started to play together, it would have been better to present themselves.

Mydei nodded and extended a hand. “Mydeimos, I’m his father.”

As she took his hand, she smiled again. “He's the spitting image of you.”

“He’s adopted. But I get it quite a lot.”

“I can understand that. My sisters and I actually have different fathers, but Mom's genes are simply too strong, so we all look pretty similar.”

It sounded… pretty weird, honestly, but not impossible. Everyone always told him how similar he was to his mother, never to his father and he did question himself if it would have been the same in case he had ever had a biological sibling. It wasn’t something that he had ever brought up with his mother, however, because of the difficult situation they were both in, and Cipher was a good older sister– no matter if she was biological or not, she will always be his sister despite everything.

He nodded in acknowledgment, ready to say something about it as well, but he stopped in his tracks when he felt Phainon moving behind him.

Admittedly, he didn’t really expect him to sleep throughout all their time there, but he at least wanted him to rest for a few hours, not barely thirty minutes.

“Go back to sleep,” Mydei immediately warned him, already feeling a hand on his shoulder. Clingy and stubborn, as always.

Phainon groaned way louder than he would have liked. “Mydei, I can’t sleep now.”

“Why not?”

“Too much sunlight.”

“You were sleeping just a second ago.”

He knew that he was. He was sleeping peacefully, and then suddenly woke up for who know what reason.

As a response, Phainon stirred and sat up slightly behind him, with his eyes still closed and his head unable to stand up straight on its own. “Doesn’t matter. I’ll push through until we get home.”

Mydei finally turned around after letting out an exhausted sigh, looking straight into his eyes. “You will get sick if you keep this up,” he whispered, almost as a warning.

He didn’t want him to get sick for his well-being, but he couldn’t lie and say that their child wasn’t in his mind too. Phainon was pretty useful for him to keep a saner lifestyle between work and the care he had to give to the child, and he didn’t want Astraea too worry too much. Especially if his father didn’t seemingly know when it was time to rest and that it wasn’t good for his health to force himself to stay awake so much when he was tired.

Maybe using wasn’t the right word, but it was what he essentially did, so there was nothing wrong for him to describe it like that. It reflected badly on him, probably, but it was why having Phainon at home lately helped him and Astraea so much.

It will eventually sink in with another verb. Maybe just taking care of their child, maybe parenting the child, even.

It was true that they both were happy to be seen as parent by Astraea, but they needed a little more to get used to this new arrangement.

“I’ll get sick when it’s not Astraea’s birthday,” Phainon settled on, way too decisively for Mydei’s liking. “I really can get through the day, believe me. I can’t miss my sister’s visiting either…”

At some point while he was narrating, his head dropped on Mydei’s shoulder, his eyes still closed shut.

What a liar. He couldn’t even open his eyes and he wanted to greet his sister in those conditions? If he didn’t know him, he would have never guessed that his job was taking care of sick people in hospitals.

He couldn’t even recognize when it was being too hard on himself and his son had to go and get worried for him. A fool and a liar.

Mydei let out an annoyed sigh. “If you can’t even open your eyes, go back to sleep.”

All that greeted him in response was a loud groan, maybe ever louder than the last one that he produced.

A child. He was dealing with an overgrown child.

“Sleep,” he almost hissed, forcing him down again. Luckily, he let him do it, perhaps because he was way too tired to oppose himself to him. “Astraea isn’t here anyway, he’s playing with some kids.”

“Figures… Fine. Just because you asked.”

“It shouldn’t be just because of that.”

“Doesn’t matter! Night!”

“Rest well.”

Mydei watched as he let himself down on the cloth again, head resting against the pillow they prepared, and this time he put a few more jackets on top of him to try and keep him from wake himself up again.

He let out a sigh as he turned around again, only to find the woman with them– Tribios, if he remembered correctly– smiling at them.

“You’re a cute couple,” she whispered, warm smiles flying in his direction.

“Thank you,” Mydei nodded, a little embarrassed that she had to witness it. He was unsure whether or not anyone else ever stared at them like that while they talked as they just did. Most times they were alone, free to do whatever they wanted to safe from other people’s eyes. It was somehow weird having a stranger stare at them like that and fishing compliments out about how cute they looked.

Regardless, she had no ill intentions. She just called them a cute couple, something that a number of people expressed already in many different ways. It wasn’t her fault she happened to be there and witness all of it.

As he looked back at her, he noticed that her quiet blue eyes dropped to the ground, looking at her jointed hands. “Mydeimos,” she called out again, “this might sound weird, but do you… perhaps know of someone named Aglaea?”

“Aglaea? She's my mother's girlfriend,” Mydei simply answered, guessing that was who she was referring to. Maybe it was a friend of hers.

At that answer, life suddenly flew back in her eyes. “Oh, you're Gorgo’s son! Of course, you look so much like her!”

Did he just walk on in another friend of his mother’s? It honestly wasn’t a rare occurrence since she used to live here and just moved to live with Aglaea and offering him a more stable lifestyle before he could decide on his future job, but it still baffled him whenever it happened.

“How do you know Aglaea?” he asked, tilting his head slightly to the side, now morbidly curious. He didn’t know much of Aglaea’s private life, and if he could know more via her friends– or, at least he thought that she was her friend– then so be it. She didn’t speak much about herself and he didn’t want to intrude too much, so he never asked her directly.

Tribios smiled proudly, placing a hand on her chest. “I’m her teacher!”

Mydei stared at her, speechless.

He surely misheard. That woman didn’t look a day older than thirty years old, if he had to be generous. She was forty? Maybe more?

“Her teacher?” he repeated, just to be sure that he heard her correctly.

Upon seeing her nod, Mydei looked at her with lost, unbelieving eyes.

“That's how she calls me,” she explained slowly, offering yet another smile. “She says that it doesn't matter if I'm a little younger, she always learns things from me. So, I'm her teacher.”

Honestly, that sounded like Aglaea.

Not putting too much weight on a person’s status or age was something that she did quite often, even if she was extremely respectful with everyone, at first glance. She was the kind of person that was able to insult others without them even noticing, or trapping them in her praises.

It was one of the reasons why their relationship was rocky at the start, after all.

He was happy that his mother found someone to love again and that loved her back, but he couldn’t trust Aglaea because he kept picking on little, minuscule things that would tick him off about her real intentions. His only mistake was not noticing that she only did them with people that she didn’t like and, when he realized that his mother wasn’t one of them, he accepted her into the family.

Mydei respected her, she was an intelligent, respectful, elegant woman, and she knew enough about the world to know what words to use and when it was useful to do so. He saw her protect his mother and sister already, besides offering her support whenever Mydei himself was in trouble.

Maybe she wasn’t his mother and he will never see her as such, but she was a woman that she deeply respected in more ways than one and for many more reasons than he initially thought. Even when he was unsure on how to read her or her intentions. She was complicated to understand, but she wasn’t evil. Like Tribios, she meant well, and that was enough for him.

Sometimes, however, she seemed so easy to understand as well. Maybe it was the way she was raised, or some past situation in her life, but she had that double identity about her that Mydei appreciated seeing every now and then.

“I guess it makes sense,” he muttered, thinking back to her behavior and what he thought of the woman in front of him.

They were essentially different– Tribios was warmer and seemed more responsible, while Aglaea had something regal and detached from reality about her, while sometimes acting childlike– but he guessed that they were similar in some things.

Tribios laughed, then raised her head towards the sky. “Aglaea has always been a very peculiar woman, right? She's so wise, but so childish at times.” She turned towards him again, tilting her head. “Is that what Gorgo saw in her?”

“No, not at first. She just… enjoyed what she was seeing,” he tried to recall that time, now almost ten years ago. “Her beauty, her stance, her strength, her confidence, her kindness. She found out later how childish she could be.”

“She's a woman full of virtues,” she nodded, happily smiling again.

Mydei nodded, internally agreeing with her. He wanted to keep up with the conversation because she looked like a kind woman that was easy to talk to, but a rapid tap on his shoulder shifted his attention.

When his head moved to the side, he saw Astraea holding Fig Stew, eyes uncertain and vaguely anxious.

His brain immediately made up a million different scenarios, ranging from just being slightly upset to having fought with the other three kids already. He didn't seem too shaken, so it shouldn't be something too grave.

“What's the matter?” he asked, with a gentle voice, his hand almost instinctively going to rub the child's back.

Astraea came closer, gluing his body to his father's and biting his lower lip. After a few seconds of patiently waiting for him to speak, he whispered, “Don't wanna get Fig Stew dirty.”

Mydei smiled, already feeling the light brown eyes innocently looking up at him. It was such a silly reason to get anxious, but he understood that the plushie right now was such a safe object for him that leaving it behind was upsetting.

“Alright.” Mydei smiled and gently caressed his head, trying to reassure him. “We'll keep him company until you're back, yeah? So later we can eat all together.”

The kid nodded, a smile appearing and fading rhythmically on his face. “Thanks, Dad,” he said, before he offered a kiss on his cheek and left the plushie with him, running back to play with his new friends.

Mydei followed him with his eyes as the plushie stood in his hands, a mental note already forming about having to wash it at some point, given how much he used it. He saw him smile and immediately starting to talk with them, so he finally rested easily.

“He really doesn't look adopted,” Tribios commented, facing the same way. She smiled at him as she turned around, seemingly curious about them. “How did you end up with him?”

“I work as a firefighter. I found him after rescuing him from a building on fire and he’s been staying with me ever since,” Mydei quickly explained, not giving her too many details. She would have known eventually if she and her sisters kept hanging out with them, but it was way too heavy to just tell her outright.

She nodded initially, then pointed between him and Phainon. “So you two… weren't a thing back then?”

“I adopted him less than a year ago, me and Phainon have been… a thing for the last five months.”

“Many new things then!”

“I’m happier. I don't mind.”

It was true. Everything that happened in the last year or so made him infinitely happier, he won’t deny it. The relationship with Phainon was the best he’s ever experienced and he adored his son, not to count how closer he felt with both Sunday and Jing Yuan now that he shared their experiences. His sister kept on calling him every few days since she visited and his mother already invited all of them to visit for her birthday. Even Aglaea wished him well and often reminded him to do one thing or the other for the child.

In general, compared to a few years ago, he was happier, felt more peaceful with himself and got closer with a lot of people already in his life– except Hephaestion, but it was inevitable. They would have started talking consistently again soon enough, when both of them would be ready to.

Tribios moved her legs and ruffled the white dress that she was wearing, until her arms wrapped around the fabric, her legs almost touching her chest. Her gaze traveled to Phainon, still peacefully sleeping behind Mydei.

He turned as well to look at him or if he woke up again, since she turned so suddenly towards him. However, he was still deep in his sleep, his usually perfect hair falling gracefully on a side of his face, partially hiding it, his mouth was slightly open and he rested on his side as he usually did, with the palm of one hand facing the sky and the other against the cloth below him.

Mydei could bet that he would whine to him about how he couldn’t feel his arm as soon as he woke up, as he did most mornings.

Unconsciously, he moved to sit slightly closer to him, crossing his legs in the process. He saw him like that plenty other times, but every time it felt like watching an ethereal being that miraculously fell right in front of him, so trusting of him that he let him see him and get closer on that basis alone.

An angel.

Phainon oftentimes looked handsome or cute depending on the moment, but whenever he let all his walls down, once he was completely trusting and honest with him with nothing between them as he started to do just recently, he truly felt like a mysterious, ethereal being that happened to meet him in this life.

That was true even more whenever he felt distant, almost scary, like he did on the phone several weeks prior. Mysterious, ethereal being– beautiful, sweet and scary.

However, he was never scared that he would do anything dangerous to him or Astraea. All his reactions so far seemed to be based on how much he cared about others or out of personal defense. It was slightly creepy, but he easily softened whenever Mydei would calmly talk to him, almost like he was a scared animal in a defensive stance.

Suddenly, Tribios cleared her voice, catching his attention again and forcing his mind to let go of those thoughts.

Less intense thinking when he was with other people. Right.

“How come he's so tired?” the woman asked, not completely changing topic, but enough to let him focus on something else.

Mydei sighed, recalling everything that had been happening for a while now. “Shitty shifts at the hospital, readjusting his schedule is a bit hard and he suffered a recent loss. Child died of lung cancer, she was in his care.”

“Oh, I’m terribly sorry.”

“It happens. It's his job. We can’t save everyone.”

“Right.”

He immediately caught how uncomfortable she was as soon as he said that sentence.

It wasn’t something that most people would say or expect when someone talked about a recent loss, especially a child they took care of. The truth was that going into the jobs they were into wasn’t an easy choice because they fully knew that, despite how much they wanted to save everyone, they had to come to terms that they would have had to see some of them die in varying degree of cruelty.

They were two different ways of saving others, but neither of them was valued more or less than the other. Or, that was not how Mydei saw it at all. Especially since that child died, he opened his eyes about how similar those two jobs were and how much they could understand each other’s struggles about their own careers.

Mydei’s eyes moved to look at Tribios again, still a little lost about what he just said. With a sigh, he asked, just to shift the topic again, “What’s your job?”

She immediately beamed brightly again. “I’m a photographer!” She shrugged, explaining it further. “Or, well, I write a few articles on various things happening in the area and I take my own photos.”

“Really?” Mydei asked, genuinely interested. He didn’t know anyone that was a journalist or a photographer, so knowing more about it as someone that enjoyed reading any sort of thing was interesting.

She nodded excitedly. “I wrote a piece about this alien turtle species, they're very cute and I had so much fun trying to find good photos!” Tribios suddenly raised a finger before searching something in the bag right next to her, changing position again to stand on her knees. She held a phone in her hands, and leaned forward to let Mydei see as well. “See, they're the ones with the red mark near their ear.”

Mydei stared at the picture that she was showing him, of a particular water turtle with, effectively, a red mark on their ear. They weren’t rare, he had seen them already, but he had no idea that they were an invasive species from the sheer amount of them that anyone could find near a fountain or even some cities.

“Oh, I have seen them,” he commented, nodding. “They're not supposed to be from around here?”

“No, unfortunately… and the local species are having a bit of a problem with keeping up with them.”

“I understand. It’s a pity, I don’t see many of the local variety.”

“It is. They are protected now, but many don’t know, so I hope I can help a few people with it.”

“I didn’t, so thank you for telling me.”

She smiled, seemingly already proud of herself. He wondered again how she could possibly be Aglaea’s teacher, as she called herself, but he understood why she liked her. She was wise in a weird way, maybe mixed with maturity and knowledge, while still feeling like a woman her age. He liked talking to her.

So, he did.

They talked for a few hours about anything on their mind, time going by more quickly now that they had something to converse about and they knew each other better. Mydei still dropped an eye in Astraea’s direction, just in case, but he always saw him laughing or playing, so he didn’t worry too much about him anymore.

“Ah!” Tribios exclaimed all of a sudden, after mentioning that it was probably time to eat lunch. “I know you're good at making food!”

“Oh, yeah… it's nothing special, but I like cooking.” Mydei took out the little boxes he prepared that morning for all three of them, hearing out what they wanted that day and mentally taking note of what kind of food they ate in the last few weeks. Luckily, he categorically banned potatoes because they were too complicated to bring around in lunch boxes, for everyone’s well-being. “Usually, Phainon helps me as well, so I can’t take all the praise. He doesn’t look like it, but he’s good at it as well, even if he doesn’t like it much.”

“So you help each other in the house already as well?” Tribios asked, already fascinated with the food that he brought out. “Unfortunately, I can’t cook that well, so I can’t make anything too complicated.”

Mydei wasn’t too sure, but he caught a glimpse of sadness in those deep blue eyes. He figured that being an older sister with such a big gap wasn’t easy, especially when young children relied on her as one of the adults in their life. He didn’t know how old their mother or how much she could take care of them, so it was normal for her to care about things like that, especially when presented home-made food that looked better than her own.

“I can help you, if you’d like,” he suggested, putting the lunch box away. “Astraea seems to get along very well with your sisters, would it be trouble for you if he kept seeing them? I can teach you something about cooking while they play around.”

She stared at him mindlessly, before smiling brightly and letting warm red color her cheeks. “Of course! Thank you, Mydeimos, you’re very nice.” She sat back on the cloth she put down next to his, nodding. “To be frank, my sisters have a hard time making friends. Trianne is always very energetic and loud, so most kids find her annoying. Trinnon is blind and quiet, so she can’t play every kind of games and prefers staying on her own. Tribbie is the one that others find the most approachable, but she can’t stand her sisters being made fun of by all these kids, so she often just stays with them.”

Turning his head in their direction, Mydei did notice that Astraea was next to who he thought had to be Trinnon, talking to her while the other two ran around in the grass, never invading other people’s space.

He probably didn’t know she was blind, but he sensed that something was wrong, or she couldn’t do something, so he kept her company. Something like that from a stranger must have gone a long way, if that was their history with other kids.

“I understand,” he nodded, turning back to Tribios. “You must have issues raising them all on your own.”

“There’s my mother too, so I’m not alone!” she explained, before lowering her eyes again. Her hand traveled to tuck her hair behind her ear, before continuing. “But it’s not easy, you aren’t wrong. Having a friend that they all like and that is sensitive enough to understand them and be so excited to play with them means a lot, so I’m glad we met by chance today, Mydeimos.”

Mydei nodded, offering her a slight smile. “I do like talking to you, and I’m sure that Phainon will as well. I’m happy if we can keep seeing each other in the future.”

She smiled brightly back at him, now maybe a little more relaxed in her posture as well.

He was about to add something to it, but he felt Phainon stir behind him again, followed by the stare of the woman in front of him travel in the same direction.

With a swift movement, Mydei extended an arm towards him, lightly caressing his hair. He didn’t say anything, but he didn’t believe it was necessary. Phainon just muttered gibberish and kept sleeping after brushing his head against the pillow made for him.

Mydei looked at him for a second, deciding whether or not he wanted to run a hand through his hair or if he should just leave it alone– letting the portrait of that ethereal being beyond his eyes take life once again, erecting up half of his walls again, or leaving him to sleep, as an opportunity for him to look at him slightly longer.

He bit his lip and retracted his hand in the end, sitting back up in the same position as before, facing Tribios.

A soft laugh reached his ears, the woman in front of him genuinely entertained by how cautious he was being with his boyfriend.

“You really don't want him to wake up,” she commented, with a rather light tone.

Mydei didn’t really mind answering. Maybe it would help him figure things out and put everything that he thought in last few hours into the proper perspective, after all. “I don't think he slept at all in the last few days. He's usually much more energetic, but if he sleeps so soundly…”

“Did he go back to his old turns?”

“No, I just think he's not used to relaxing. Even before we started dating, I found him at the hospital often and his friends often told me that he avoided sleeping. One of our first dates ended up with him taking an afternoon nap because of this, actually.”

“Oh,” she straightened her back, “that's… worrying.”

He nodded, only agreeing with her. “We'll figure it out,” he said, so convinced of it that he wouldn’t be surprised if there were further questions about it.

Luckily, one of the three triplets– Trinnon, he believed– walked up to her sister while another one helped her and calmly sat down next to her, followed by her sister. Mydei turned his head to see the loudest of the triplets still play around with Astraea not too far away, mentally noting which one was Trianne and which was Tribbie.

“Is it eating time?” Trinnon asked, with a quiet, monotonous voice.

It probably was.

Mydei watched as Tribios nodded and handed her and her sister lunch boxes of their own, while they both happily smiled. In a moment’s notice. the third twin arrived too and Astraea plopped in his lap a couple of seconds after, immediately reaching for his plushie.

A hand traveled on his head, gently caressing his hair, before he noticed that he hesitated on getting his food. He usually liked to eat, especially food that he or Phainon prepared, and he looked joyful and happy until a second ago. There was something wrong going on in his mind, but he couldn’t pinpoint it for the life of him.

So, as he often did, he simply asked him.

“Hey,” he whispered, tucking his hair behind his ear. “Is there a problem?”

Astraea joined his hands and sucked briefly on his bottom lip. “Is Auntie Cyrene not coming?”

“She is, she's just a little late.”

“And Papa?”

“Papa's tired. I'm sorry, I know you expected a little more.”

He could have planned things a little bit better. He did want him to have fun during his birthday of all days, but he understood that he looked forward talking to this aunt that he only knew through his father’s stories and playing with both of his parents. Instead, one of them was so tired that he needed to sleep and his aunt wasn’t there yet.

It was disappointing, but he doubted he was as sad as Mydei’s brain made him to be. He did find new friends that he enjoyed spending time with, and he chose the food he would eat for once. With all probability, he was just frustrated with the situation.

“It's okay,” the child ultimately said, finally rising his head to look at him. “You're both here, so I'm not alone. It's fine.”

There was no smile nor any other reassuring gesture on his part, but what he said particularly sounded like trying to look at the positives. As if that was actually how all his birthdays went in the past and the fact that they were having a day out for his birthday was something worthy of being highlighted.

Mydei looked around, before raising a hand to excuse himself with Tribios and stepping away a few meters from his position, with his child in his arms. Astraea was a little surprised of the sudden movement, but he just clutched his plushie a little closer and trusted his father throughout this new motion.

Once he stood by a tree not too far from where Phainon was resting, Mydei sighed and looked at Astraea again, already waiting for a question or an explanation. Whatever came first would have been fine, but he was unsure whether or not his father wanted one or the other.

Nodding, Mydei finally questioned,“Is that how you spent the last birthday?”

“I read,” the child answered, before lowering his head slightly. He bit and sucked his lower lip, his mouth moving in motions that suggested a forced smile morphing into a regretful expression, morphing yet again into a pensive face. “Father came home angry. Mother… I don't remember. She wasn’t happy either. I didn’t see her until the morning and she never made me birthday wishes.”

Knowing more about his biological parents just hurt him every single time that it happened. His mother seemed to be the most decent one out of the two, but he didn’t even know if she was at the mercy of her horrible husband or if she had enough. Astraea rarely talked about both of them unless Mydei made direct questions about them, and he didn’t blame him.

Leaving a kid at home reading books unfit for his age to the point that he didn’t want to read anything out of fear he would get something wrong for the entirety of his 5th birthday, just for then come back angry and avoidant must have been horrid to go through for him.

Regardless of the situation, he hoped that she would at least wish him happy birthday, but apparently she didn’t even in the following days. He understood why he started calling him Mama, knowing what he knew. Having a decent mother that would love him, since his father was so angry and violent all the time, was an understandable desire.

“But, Dad,” the child called him again, his head still hung low, “this is different. You're here, and we're doing something fun, and you care lots.” As he raised his head, a small smile started to appear on his face, easing the worry that Mydei started to feel in the last dozen of minutes. “It's the best birthday ever.”

It was enough for him to smile back and hug him, as close as he could.

That day wasn’t supposed to be perfect, nor did Mydei have the intention of making sure it would be, but he definitely wanted him to have the best time he possibly could and he felt horrible when he saw that disappointed expression. The sentiment was probably there already, he just learned to be happy in what he could and trust him whenever it came to his well-being.

He still wanted to do better, but there was time for that. Phainon would wake up soon and–

“Auntie Cyrene.”

The little voice next to his ear made sure he would shift his attention to the child again, instead of his own feelings. “Astraea, she will arrive–”

“There!” he yelled, with a face so surprised that Mydei hardly believed to have seen it in any other occasion. “Auntie Cyrene is there!”

Mydei turned around with curiosity clear in his eyes, looking at the direction in which his child was pointing at. Sure enough, there was someone that fit the vague descriptions that Phainon gave of her.

Either way, Mydei was hardly believing someone like her was allowed to simply exist among mortals. Saying she looked like an otherworldly being would have been an insult to the kind of presence she carried with her.

She’s more like a little elf.

That was what Phainon told Astraea recently, apparently something that he used to describe his sister over and over again with their son. He saw the resemblance and why he chose those words to describe her, and she fit that regal, fantasy-like description perfectly.

Long pink hair with blue tips gathered in intricate braids, glowing pink eyes, white lace patterns on her arms and legs, an elegant, yet simple, white dress with pink, blue and purple accents, transparent and shining earrings, elegant white ballerina shoes while she kept a pair of heels in her hands.

Calling her a Goddess wouldn’t have been too off the mark.

Despite everything that he noticed and how surprised he was– because, unlike her brother, she knew way too well how to dress– he still found similarities she had with Phainon. The same gentleness in her eyes, the same breathtaking beauty, the same confident way they carried themselves with, the same kind of immediate adoration they got from Astraea.

They surely were siblings, there was no doubt about it.

After a little bit of hesitation, Mydei raised a hand and tried to get her attention. “This way!” he yelled, while Astraea waved an arm to help in the mission to get her to come their way.

Luckily, she noticed both of them and smiled, running towards them. Probably, Phainon told her that they’d be having a picnic-like day and she brought shoes that matched her dress and wouldn’t get too much in the way of her walking in places like that.

“Sorry I’m late!” she explained, her breath a little heavy because she probably ran after realizing just how late she was. “My editor called about a book and I couldn't refuse that kind of call, I didn't think we would stay on the phone that long… but I found you!”

“Don't worry about it. I’m Mydeimos,” he extended a hand, bracing for the skin contact ahead of time.

She promptly nodded and smiled, grabbing it with confidence. “Phai’s boyfriend… I’m Cyrene, glad to meet you!” She turned to look at the child in his arms with a smile, raising a hand to greet him. “And this must be little Astraea, right?”

He excitedly nodded, so clearly happier than before that Mydei almost took a deep sigh of relief. He didn’t just out of respect for both of them.

“You're so cute!” she stated with a smile, still keeping her distance from him. Mydei guessed that it was because they just met and didn’t want to make him uncomfortable, which was something that he could respect as well.

“He's been rather excited to meet you,” Mydei informed her. “He really likes some of your books and the way you dress.”

She made a surprised face– way too similar to Phainon’s– and her bright, pink eyes relaxed just a second later. She turned to Astraea, gentle and kind. “Really? Do you like fairies? Phai mentioned that to me.”

“Lots and lots!” Astraea smiled, looking at her with a kind of excitement that he only showed with Castorice so far, and multiplied by tens at that. “And… you're really pretty. I really like your hair… Papa is sleeping, though.”

Jumping from a topic to the other was something that he did when he was embarrassed, but everything he said was genuine and truthful to his feelings. He did it with him a couple of times already, and it was always cute. This time wasn’t an exception.

Cyrene, however, raised an eyebrow and looked at Mydei with a questioning stare.

“Papa is Phainon. He's been overworking and he fell asleep from exhaustion today,” he quickly explained, setting the child down on the grass. He immediately ran towards Phainon, almost as if staying away from him for too long would harm him.

Simultaneously, a warm feelings pervades his chest again, by far not the first time it happened, especially ever since Phainon started living with them. Coming home to see both of them preparing dinner, playing, talking or sleeping was always another reason for him to keep being happy day after day, without regrets in what they were about to walk into or for his past decisions.

If anything, he was glad that his past experiences and decisions led to this.

Seeing the two people he cared for the most getting along and trusting each other while reserving a lot of love and care for him as well was all that he had ever wished for.

His thoughts were abruptly interrupted by Cyrene sighing next to him, in a rather annoyed way. “Classic Phai, he will never learn,” she whispered, looking in his direction for a second before turning to Mydei again. “You need to keep an eye on him at all times, or he will start working when he should be resting and his sleeping schedule will be completely fucked up! He needed to work so often even when we were children too and I had to drag him away from books in the middle of the night so many times…”

Mydei let out a small laugh, less for the fact that Phainon didn’t change and more for the fact that Cyrene swore so openly. Somehow, it didn’t fit at all with the way she presented herself, but he didn’t mind. Those two siblings kept on surprising him, he found it rather exciting by now.

“But it doesn't matter!” Cyrene beamed, fixing the white and black bag on her shoulder. She took a peek behind his shoulder, towards the place they decided to sit down just a few hours ago. “You're over here, right?”

Mydei nodded. “Yeah, I prepared something for you to eat as well. I asked Phainon what you liked, I hope you don't mind.”

“Absolutely not! He always brags about your food, so I want to try it.”

“No promises.”

It was said in a joking tone, but he hoped that she would like the food he prepared. Phainon was sure about what she liked, but a lot of it were sweets, and he had to work with something else entirely to prepare a decent lunch for all of them. On top of it, all of them ate a cake already that morning, since it coupled well with breakfast.

Cyrene didn’t wake up Phainon, even if she sounded quite appalled by the fact that he was sleeping that day. Probably Astraea would have taken care of it, given how tentatively he was looking at him.

Instead, she just sat down and took a bite of her lunch, without the full intention of eating it all until Phainon woke up. Even then, she cupped her cheek and let out a pleasured sound as soon as she could taste it properly. “Oh, it's so good!” She turned towards Mydei, pointing at him with a fork. “Phai really hit the jackpot. I haven't eaten real food in months and this is heavenly.”

Mydei let out a soft laugh, a little embarrassed. He didn’t make it a habit of proudly saying he cooked well, but everyone kept making him way too many compliments about it. Especially Phainon and Cyrene… he wondered what kind of food they ate when they were growing up. From what he knew, neither of them had a simple nor stable childhood and Phainon offered to go and learn how to cook to help his older sister.

That statement from her didn’t surprise him, if that was the case.

“Papa… Papa, it's time to eat. You will feel worse if you don’t eat…” Astraea said behind him, gently shaking the man by his shoulder. He probably wanted him awake and he was using the food to get to stay with him for a while, but saying it was hard to wake him when he was so deeply as he was would have been an understatement.

Miraculously, though, he let out a half-asleep noise and stirred before finally opening his eyes, as everyone was looking at him with interest. Mydei noticed that even the triplets were either listening in or looking at whatever was going on with morbid curiosity.

Phainon, on his part, just zeroed on the child and caressed his shoulder. “Astraea?” he managed to as well, with a consistently tired tone.

Astraea nodded, then pointed towards Cyrene. “Auntie Cyrene is here too.”

He turned around too, just to stare at his sister, sticking out her tongue and winking at him, almost as if it was some sort of secret greeting between them. Her brother, however, just nodded and weakly waved at her, before his attention returned to his child. “I’m so sorry I feel asleep today. Did I ruin your birthday?”

He shook his head, a little hesitant in his next actions and words. So, Phainon waited, as he often did whenever he noticed he was having some issues in communicating properly.

After biting his lower lip again, the child laid next to him to hug him, immediately receiving a hug back from his father. “I always feel better when you and Dad hug me… Does it feel better now?”

“Lots better,” Phainon said, before his head lowered to kiss him between his hair. “Thank you, baby.”

Astraea suddenly sat up, full of life again. He waited for Phainon to sit up– who struggled a bit, but ultimately was able to– and dragged himself over to Mydei again, looking up straight in his eyes.

He looked like a lost baby deer, waiting for some food.

Mydei laughed, tilting his head. “Astraea, you know where your food is.” He handed him the bag where he kept every single one of them, only taking out water and plastic glasses. “Remember the colors? Which one is yours and which one is Papa’s?”

“This is mine,” he said, grabbing a pink colored box, before eyeing a blue one, “and… that is Papa's.”

“Exactly.” Mydei turned towards Cyrene, already with a slightly lighter pink than the child’s box. “That’s all yours, Cyrene.”

She smiled, happily nodding with her fork and food ready to be eaten already. “Thank you, Mydei.”

He smiled at her, going back to his own food, but without checking on Phainon first.

The man stretched his arms behind his head, food ready on his thigh and Astraea looking at him on the other side, with big, excited eyes.

Maybe he underestimated the amount of love and admiration he had for his boyfriend. He had the impression that he just accepted him so readily because Mydei clearly liked him, but he might have just enjoyed his presence around the apartment because of deeper, more honest feelings than he initially imagined.

It was probably better this way. He was still surprised because he didn’t see it coming, but, given how often the child was left alone with Phainon at home, it had to be expected at some point.

His eyes fell on Phainon’s face, finding him smiling back at him once he realized he was staring while he was stretching.

Mydei immediately averted his eyes, in a believable enough manner that most didn’t notice. By all chances, Phainon did, but he wasn’t worried about it too much. The most he would get afterwards would have been teasing and maybe a few kisses, so it really was a win-win situation all around.

Cyrene joined her hands all of a sudden, almost as if she had to catch their attention. She was looking at her brother, so it was absolutely possible that, even after Mydei moved his face, he could have been staring right in his direction. “And how is my little brother doing?” she asked, tilting her head.

“Fine, for the most part,” he answered, mindlessly letting Astraea finally sit on his lap. “I asked for a shifts change.”

“It was about time! Day shifts will be easier, you'll see.”

“I hope! It’s hard to even stay awake now, as you noticed.”

Liar.

Bold, charming, good with words, but a liar.

It was a little white lie, one that was meant to calm down his sister, but it was still something untrue that he spouted to her face.

Cyrene herself seemed to understand it, but she didn’t say anything about it. Maybe she was used to it and he always lied to her to prevent her from being too worried about her. It was a noble thing to do in certain occasions, but she already knew the truth.

Maybe Mydei had to question himself more whenever Phainon tried to lie to him. He didn’t do it much and he could understand when he tried to lie about something or avoid the topic, but that reaction settled something uncomfortable in his chest.

It wasn’t quite doubt, and different from anger or disappointment.

He gritted his teeth as he found the answer, trying to put it behind him. He wasn’t supposed to have any feelings about something that didn’t regard him– and that exchange didn’t– but he couldn’t help but feel worry and curiosity.

His eyes suddenly left Phainon again, focusing more on his food, listening to the chatter around him; Tribios greeting everyone, Phainon talking to Astraea and Cyrene, the triplets chiming in every once in a while. It was nice and relaxing, easy to follow and a great way to spend his time there.

His solitary peace ended soon, with both Phainon and Astraea coming closer to him. He moved his head towards his boyfriend, who replied with a regretful and confused smile.

Help, please.

Startled, his eyes traveled lower, to Astraea’s sad eyes as he looked at Tribios and the triplets, playing around as siblings often did.

Remembering what he told him earlier, he nodded and quickly finished what he had in his mouth, before gesturing Phainon to get up with the child. Astraea didn’t say anything about it, opting to just follow along whatever they suggested him to do.

“Sorry, we’ll come back soon,” Phainon excused all of them as he kept Astraea in his arms, his eyes still fixated on the sisters.

Mydei probably knew what he was thinking about. He knew, because he did as well, especially when he and his mother left his father and before everything else would eventually settle back to its rightful place.

If he had siblings, would it have been different? If there was someone else, would he have suffered less, more, or would it have been no difference?

It was a stupid question, but it was something that he asked himself a couple of times and, if Astraea was looking so intently at them, he was probably thinking about it as well. He just hoped that it wouldn’t end up being jealousy. It was a rather insidious beast to eradicate, especially for someone that spent most of his life feeling alone and abandoned, and was just now starting to have friends his age.

Quickly enough, they found a proper place to talk to their child, now just confused, hidden away from most of the eyes that could be looking at them.

“Hey,” Mydei asked, leaving him with Phainon, just trying to converse with him. “Something wrong? What were you talking about?”

The child blinked a couple of times before tensing his shoulders. He felt under pressure, but it wasn’t something they could avoid now. With all chances, he was thinking about it since the day started.

He nodded, without keeping the eye contact. “It's a little… weird. So many people…” he trailed off, not sure how to continue.

“All the people here want to be here,” Phainon offered, still not completely understanding what it was happening.

Astraea just pressed his lips together, almost as if he had to decide whether or not he was telling the truth.

At that point, Mydei felt like he understood what was going on.

He bended over a bit, enough so he could force his child to look at him and smiled at him to calm him down. “It's real. It's all real and you are very loved, Astraea.” He just spelled it out to him to make sure that he knew that he wasn’t seeing things, but his eyes were already as lucid and honest as he expected them to be. “I know you don't like big crowds, so I didn't want to invite many people, but Grandma and Auntie Cipher already asked if they could call you tonight to wish you a happy birthday. Auntie Cyrene is here, and Castorice and Hyacine said they'd visit later. Even Jing Yuan, Sunday and Yanqing said happy birthday this morning, right?”

Astraea nodded, closing a timid fist around the fabric of his own shirt. “Yanqing said that Yunli couldn't be there, but she enjoyed staying with me.”

“I know your past birthdays weren't the best, but I promise that none of us will forget it, leave you alone or abandon you. I promise.”

He meant it, as he always did.

He didn’t want to know how he would look if he ever felt that horrible during another birthday of his. Honestly, it would have been too much and a statement about how much of a failure he had been as his father.

Truthfully, all he wanted was to make him feel wanted, loved and worthy of happiness. Nothing more and nothing less.

As he expected, though, he did start crying– quietly and with just a few sobs– and Phainon intervened immediately, keeping him closer and quietly rocking his body to attempt to ground him and calm him down.

Mydei just smiled quietly, only daring to give him a light caress on his head to let him know that he was still there and accepting the requests of a few hugs.
