They both waited until they saw him dry his tears and request to be put down a few minutes later to head back to their place with the others.

At least, that was settled as well. It looked like he understood everything he was told, so he had nothing more to be worried about for the moment. All that happened now would have been about Astraea having fun and getting to know Tribios and Cyrene, hopefully.

Phainon had to yet talk to Tribios or the triplets after all, so they both could look forward to that, hoping that she would have given him a good impression as well.

Before they could even sit down, however, they saw one of the sisters– Trianne, Mydei remembered– run towards them, followed by another one trying to stop her, for whatever reason.

Neither Mydei or Phainon seemed too phased and Astraea just looked a little surprised of the sudden movement, but didn’t back down in the slightest when she approached him again.

“Astraea!” she yelled in his face, met only by the child closing an eye. She suddenly grabbed his hands, maybe trying to make him believe her, and that was when his muscles started tensing, but without many more complications. “We won't leave you either! We had a lot of fun with you!”

Mydei noticed Phainon letting out a soft laugh, and he had to agree with that reaction. The girl was intense, but she had the right intentions. She must have overheard them or understood what was going on, and she wanted to reassure him.

Good first friends, he found himself thinking.

Shortly after, he noticed Tribios standing up and approach them as well, smiling at the both of them as Trianne dragged Astraea away. Mydei followed him for a couple of seconds, but relaxed when he finally started eating while listening to the triplets bicker about what just happened.

Maybe it would have been alright. Detaching himself a little from his fathers would have been healthy for him, especially since he would have had to start going to school in less than a year’s time.

“How about we exchange numbers?” Tribios suggested, bringing Mydei’s mind back to where he was. “Obviously my girls like your son and you seem lovely people to be around.”

Phainon stood silent, evidently letting Mydei make the call. He didn’t know Tribios, but he trusted him and he knew that he would have taken the best decision for them and their child.

It was appreciated, but he hoped that he would stay awake enough to talk to her next time. He would probably like her.

“Thank you,” Mydei thanks her, handing her his phone to memorize her number.

If anything, she looked more ecstatic for her sister than they did for their child, or the children in question altogether. Anyone could tell that she cared deeply about her little sisters, despite the trouble that she claimed they brought.

It was normal, he had the same relationship with Cipher and he guessed that it didn’t disappear for them despite the age difference. Maybe it was different, but the knowledge of only having each other until the end and knowing how much her little sisters relied on her didn’t change.

He wondered for a split second if Cipher felt even remotely the same way, despite the nonchalant air she had about her, before the phone was handled back to him.

Another thought for another time, he decided.

Tribios brightly smiled at him, clearly thankful for how willing they were to try and be friends with both her and her siblings. “Thank you! They had a difficult time making friends… but Trinnon and Trianne seem to like him quite a lot. I'm sure Tribbie likes him too, she just keeps things to herself a little more.”

“Of course, Tribios. Thank you again.”

“Let’s go to sit back and finish eating, what do the both of you say? We will have enough time to get to know each other.”

True. They cut their lunch short to help Astraea since he looked in distress and, even if Mydei didn’t voice it, he greatly appreciated how quickly Phainon asked for his help. He didn’t do it often, maybe due to pride or because he didn’t need it, but he was glad that he decided to lean on him this time.

With a swift motion, he intertwined their pinky fingers for a second, much to Phainon’s surprise. As he turned his head, Phainon was looking at him with a little surprised face and a hint of a blush across his cheeks, but he refused to let his finger go just yet.

If he had to make a guess, his heart was probably beating out of his chest as it often did whenever they even just shared a kiss in the privacy of their apartment.

Still so cute and surprised of any and every gesture of affection. Still looking so much like a lost puppy after months and, especially, after claiming he wanted to be his partner at their first date.

Honestly, Mydei had to let his mind wander about whether or not he was utterly and hopelessly in love with him later or if Phainon simply was just like that and it was impossible for him to differentiate the two.

Later. When they’d be alone, he told himself. Too many people around here and too much of a public space to have any thought regarding that now.

However, Phainon hung on his finger way more than he expected, refusing to let go of it even when they settled down again, as if they never held hands before– which they did already. They kissed in public too, that was just Phainon both being his puppy self and acting way too attached.

Mydei rolled his eyes and leaned into his shoulder, without quite resting his head on it. “What’s the problem now? Still too sleepy?”

It was meant to just be a slight teasing, but Phainon kept his hand close, just shifting it to properly hold it. Then, as he leaned in his ear, he whispered, “Did I hallucinate that you searched for my hand without flinching in front of everyone for the first time?”

He didn’t even realize he wasn’t averse to it. He always was, only being able to hold it when he forced himself to. It happened with Hephaestion as well, he was never able to properly start any kind of public gesture of affection, especially if it was holding hands. He didn’t know why it was so difficult for him, given how easy kissing is, or the little issues he has with hugging in private.

Maybe it was just because he knew that it was coming, but even then, he always braced himself for that feeling. This time, it didn’t hurt. It barely brought any feeling at all, except heat and affection.

“No,” Mydei whispered back, shifting the hand Phainon was trying to hold, to let him complete the motion. “You didn’t.”

Phainon hummed as he slid his fingers in between Mydei’s until their palms touched. “You kept insisting that I was scared of affectionate gestures a few months ago, but you’re scared of someone else touching you when there’s heavy intent behind it,” he explained further, just loud enough for him and him alone to hear it. “And now you do it without even noticing… you’re really–”

“Phai!”

“Cyrene!”

Mydei let out a relieved, shaky breath as soon as his head snapped towards his sister, squeezing the hand that started that… whatever it was. It was teasing, flirting, belittling, menacing all at once.

The worst part probably was that he liked it. He would have liked it to continue instead of being stopped by Cyrene, but he was glad she stopped him, or he didn’t know what else Phainon would have said right in front of everyone.

While the siblings talked about having missed each other, how Cyrene’s tour for her books went and how much she’d have liked to have her brother there too, since there were a lot of activities and stands that he could have liked too, Mydei’s eyes dropped to his hand, mindlessly intertwined with Phainon’s. His thumb brushed against his skin, sensing the way his muscles tensed next to him.

A thought raised in his head, unsure whether or not if he wanted to listen to it right now. They were in front of everyone and Phainon was talking to his sister– that he hadn’t seen in a long time, he reminded himself. It wasn’t the right time or place to act on that impulsive thought.

And yet, his head still flopped on Phainon’s shoulder.

Against his will, maybe, but he couldn’t help it.

He heard Tribios let out a soft laugh not too far away from them and the children chatter, but none of them was Astraea. So, none of it was a matter that important to him.

With a nod, Phainon decided to lean his head against Mydei’s, letting his muscles relax. He talked for a while about something that he didn’t care enough to understand, before his attention was caught by a familiar weight on his thighs.

“Dad?” Astraea called, from below him.

Mydei smiled, giving him the attention that he wished for. “Don’t worry about me, I’m fine. Phainon can take care of me to ask forgiveness for having zoomies last night.”

He heard a sound of disapproval and surprise from Mydei, but he didn’t pay attention to it, and neither did their child. Instead, he nodded and agreed with him.

“Papa’s really too active at night,” he said, the plushie ever present in his arms, pushing him under the train as if he didn’t know what was going on.

In those moments, he remembered how young he was. If he knew a little better, he would have refused to mention anything about it to avoid a punishment or a reprimand about it, but he didn’t because he had fun with him.

He would know, since he heard them talking at some point of the night.

“Like father like son,” he commented, slowly turning his head towards Phainon, who was already averting his gaze, fully knowing what he was hinting at. Mydei still huffed, smirking as he looked his way. “Right?”

“Ah, busted!” Phainon turned to Astraea, smiling apologetically. “Sorry, honeybuns. Dad is too intelligent.”

The child puffed his cheek, almost as if he was sad about the situation. “We almost made it though…”

That was what he got for leaving alone two people who had trouble sleeping and liked to spend their nights in any way except sleeping. Useless plans about fooling him even if they didn’t even make the slightest attempt at lowering their voices.

Mydei shook his head and let out a quiet laugh. “Stop plotting with your father and go play with your friends.”

Phainon laughed too besides him, nodding, still holding his hand. Even if the strength that he used so far to hold it got weaker, he refused to let it go, maybe hoping in a miracle that would leave them alone and able to talk.

They did need it, Mydei knew that too, but they were still in a situation where they couldn’t spare time for it.

And yet, he refused to let go of his hand as well.

There was some kind of ecstasy he felt about the knowledge that he purposefully held his hand to express affection and intimacy that he couldn’t scroll off of himself. The way Phainon reacted was burned in his brain as well, both embarrassed and excited at the same time.

Cute. It was really cute, like an excited puppy welcoming him home.

“I have a better idea!” Cyrene beamed, distracting him from his own thoughts. He followed her movements, crouching down in front of Astraea and smiling at him. “How about I tell you a story?”

His eyes shone at the sheer mention of those words, and Mydei found himself smiling at that too. He didn’t think he could even laugh so much and so often in one single day.

The triplets chimed in too, quickly scrambling to put away what they had in their hands and running there too.

“Yes, yes!” one of them said, followed by a mellow, quiet and monotone voice adding, “About what?”

Cyrene smiled brightly at all of them, without answering at first. Then, with a greatly proud stance, she surprisingly stood up and motioned them to follow her. “We’ll figure it out! Let’s see if other kids want to hear it too first, come on!”

The children looked at each other, a little confused, but certainly interested in the proposal. Astraea looked back at his parents, and Mydei nodded a silent permission, seeing stars suddenly lighting up in his light brown eyes.

At least this birthday ended up being something that he would remember with more than just tears and regret for the past. He was spending it doing one of the things he loved the most and with the aunt that he had been wanting to know the most, along with friends that it was overdue time for him to meet.

His heart could rest easy for this year. Everything sorted itself out, in the end.

“I’ll come too,” Tribios announced, shooting a quick glace at Mydei and Phainon as well. “I haven’t heard a story from a proper writer in forever.”

Cyrene smiled brightly at her and nodded, extending an inviting arm towards her. “We’ll gladly welcome you too, Lady Tribios!”

So, as soon as those proclamations started, they ended, accompanied away from the presence of just about everyone that was around them, leaving them alone.

That was probably her objective.

They weren’t exactly subtle about the fact that there was something left unsaid between them, thanks to that hand-holding and little whispers between each other. If anything, it was a miracle it took her for everyone else to notice and so fast for the kids to follow along with her suggestions.

He mentally took note to thank her and Tribios later.

“Mh, I like your sister,” he commented, fully knowing that Phainon was thinking more or less the same thing, maybe still trying to figure out what just happened.

“She happens to be amazing.” He turned towards him, a little slower than he would have normally done if there wasn’t something that he wanted to ask him. He finally did only when Mydei let out a sigh, sign that he was waiting and he had to hurry up already. “You’re clingy today,” he commented, averting his eyes.

Mydei nodded, feeling the mood strain already. For some reason, it was hard to pronounce those feelings, even if he scolded Phainon for it a few times and he was fully aware of which ones he held in his heart.

He wanted to talk about them out loud now that they were alone and on the topic, but, as much as he hated to admit it, he might still need a little help.

“I might have found out a few things about us while you were sleeping,” he confessed, unsure where to go from there. His voice didn’t waver, but he hoped that Phainon would have grasped the tiny ask for help that he laid out for him.

Usually, he wasn’t right often, but he read him perfectly whenever he needed him to. That time must be one of those times.

“Such as?” Phainon smiled, tilting his head to look at him. Mydei could feel the teasing tone, and he prayed that he was thinking about what he wanted to say. “Might this dear prince have fallen in love with me?”

Classic Phainon, but on the right track.

Or, better yet, he already centered the core issue.

Mydei, however, was curious about another part of the phrase that he just used. “Prince? Where did you get that?”

“You carry yourself with a certain… oomph.”

“You need to work on your vocabulary.”

“You’re elegant and you carry yourself like an important man that actually matters? That’s what I was referring to.”

The ‘oomph’ that Phainon referred to wasn’t the first time that others mentioned it to him. Gnaeus himself asked him if he came from a wealthy family when he first met him, before he could break the news that he was Gorgo’s son that he just heard a rumor of two decades prior. He didn’t even realize he moved as if he was something important, nor that he still did it.

He almost hoped that living with a child and working in a field as demanding and physical as part of the firefight department would have diminished those traits, but it apparently didn’t. Still walking like a prince, still being mistaken as some wealthy prince.

Whether he liked it or not when Phainon said it was something that he had to decide yet.

Phainon tilted his head as he looked at him, trying to meet his eyes again, like a curious child. As soon as Mydei noticed it, their eyes finally locked, gentle blue eyes accompanying him to finally talk about what he wished to. “Well, did you?”

A moment of silence.

Mydei took a deep breath, before nodding. “Yes.”

Not mentioning it himself helped. The words were still heavy on his tongue, but he wanted him to know, in a way or another, that his intense feelings were reciprocated and he had no reason to doubt himself or thinking he was being too much.

It was a problem in the past that made him hesitate. He didn’t want him to anymore.

He met his eyes again with a smile, as happy as Mydei was expecting him to be, even if he silently looked at him without moving a muscle. He wasn’t anxious, but he wanted to observe his reaction first. Being in love with him wasn’t something new and neither was feeling all the affection the other had for him, but admitting it was a completely different story.

Seeing his genuine reaction was the most important thing to him right now. It was rare, and he wanted to see him genuinely, uselessly happy because of something he said and laid out for him.

It was selfish, maybe, but he wanted something like that this time. Just one time, he wanted to see genuine, instant happiness on his face without intermissions.

Phainon smiled often, but the kind of smile that Mydei was looking for was one that he liked the most– and the same one that he refused to show the most as well. So, he wanted to imprint it in his mind now that he could.

It was a hesitant smile at first, still indecisive on how much he could show, if it was too much for just a tiny, three-lettered word, but Mydei could see that he could barely hold it in. It was a matter of a couple of seconds before the full smile made its way on his face, the happiness shared by the glitter in his crystal clear blue eyes.

This time, it was just a calm, controlled laugh, but it was genuine. It wasn’t born from courtesy like the ones he often wore at work, it wasn’t to reassure him or Astraea, it wasn’t fake to shield himself from something that he struggled with. It was a genuine, happy laugh.

Mydei almost played to be able to keep seeing them.

“I’m way less scared of moving now,” Phainon confessed, almost ecstatic. “You– I mean, that means that we’re a thing, right?”

That hopeful and incredulous voice just made Mydei finally crack. He softly laughed, adoringly looking at how happy he was hearing him laying out his feelings. “We’ve been a thing for months, Phainon.”

“Yeah, but… this feels different.” He leaned into him, resting his free hand against his thigh. It didn’t cup it or squeeze it, opting to just keep it there, hovering over his pants as a reminder that he was there and that he was asking a question that he deemed as urgent,

Mydei slowly stuck his tongue out, thinking about what he could answer for a couple of seconds. No lies and no mention of the phrase they were talking about, but explaining his own feelings about what Phainon must feel as well now.

“I don’t want you to doubt about being too much or not enough,” he stated, keeping his amber eyes locked with his. “I want you here just the way you are.”

That seemed to do the job. There wasn’t urgency anymore, just relief and happiness reflected in a smile that Mydei hoped to see more often and not just in his memories.

With a swift movement, Phainon leaned in again, this time to kiss him, and he let his hand finally go when Mydei raised it to cup his cheek as he reciprocated the gesture. It was a quick, sweet kiss, nothing out of the ordinary by now, but it did carry heavier meaning than the ones they exchanged on a daily basis.

It felt like a lock, something Phainon used to both thank him and make him a promise that Mydei hoped that he could keep, after all the times that he reassured him and made his wishes clear to him.

Even when they let go of each other, their lips still grazed against each other, Mydei menacingly offering a second kiss to that first one. He didn’t even know what he wanted from it or how it could have been, since his head was starting to spin after just one, almost completely innocent kiss, but he wanted to kiss him again.

He knew that Phainon would have been completely fine with it too if he asked– or not, honestly, if the way he looked at him was any indication of what he wanted– but they could do it later too.

Later, later, later. Always later.

That was what it meant to compromise to raise a small child, and Mydei was fine with it, but sometimes he did feel envy for those who didn’t have to do it.

Maybe that was why he always felt as if they got so close so fast thanks to Astraea as well– if he hadn’t been there, Mydei would have never accepted Phainon’s advances, and Phainon wouldn’t have learned to stay with him so quickly, not to mention moving in together after just a few months.

They had to wait for certain things about their relationships to make sure to take care of him, but he gave them time to grow closer together while they cared for him. It almost felt like that time alone was done thanks to him as well.

Perhaps, he even understood what he was thinking and deeming as an important thing to tell Phainon, while the direct object of his thoughts didn’t even think about it.

“You should have figured out I liked you that much,” Mydei blurted out, practically against his lips. “I wasn’t hiding it, were you not convinced of it?”

Maybe it was too accusatory.

Phainon can’t read minds– it was normal for him not being able to grasp everything that went around in his head.

Too reflective, too stone-faced, too intimidating, too aggressive.

He got told any one of those things a million times, since when he was a child. Even if his mother told him that it wasn’t who he was, did it matter, if everyone else thought of him that way? He couldn’t help it, and others refused to let him help them because they were too scared by his ability of observing and reading a lot of their actions that they believed to be unreadable by a stranger.

There was a reason why Hephaestion was the only one of his age that he was able to call a friend.

He didn’t want to push all of it on Phainon’s shoulders, but he wanted him to be able to understand him as he did with everyone else more than he initially believed. Was it really so hard to understand his actions and gestures? He always made sure to make them as clear as possible, but the only people able to understand them were his mother and sister, with Hephaestion close behind just because he had seen them a thousand times.

But he wasn’t in his life anymore. Not as much as a few years ago. And he wanted Phainon to pick them up as well.

Mydei looked at him nod, thinking of an answer, falling back to sit on the cloth below them. Amber eyes followed him, desperately asking for an answer. “It’s true, you did,” Phainon answered with a whisper, almost as if it was a silent promise between them. “I noticed you were more considerate, and the fault is on me for not grasping what you meant.”

It sounded like an apology, but that wasn’t what Mydei wanted in the slightest.

He heard them way too often just because his actions were too confusing.

Sorry for not understanding.

Sorry if I offended you.

Sorry that you always have to explain yourself.

Those apologies were empty. His actions were perfectly clear, there was no need to apologize. Especially Phainon who often grasped the meaning of everything that he said and did. He didn’t need those useless apologies.

“I don’t need your apologies. I always make myself as clear as I can, especially with you.” He let out a loud, exhausted sigh that he kept hidden for way too long. He didn’t know when he started feeling so aware of the way Phainon in particular answered him, nor why he snapped so suddenly. Maybe it was just the stress piling on him.

He needed some support again, even if Phainon had already given him a lot of it in the past few months. They trusted each other, but they both found hard to communicate some feelings and thoughts and, on top of the sudden change in both of their schedules due to Phainon getting a bit of vacation before moving departments, it evidently shook him more than he expected.

Usually, he wouldn’t even hint at some of the things others said about him because, largely, he didn’t care anymore, but the thought of Phainon sharing those same thoughts destabilized him. The last thing he wanted was knowing that Phainon thought of him with pity or confusion, as if he was a robot or an alien.

Anyone else could think of him that way and it wouldn’t have mattered, but he needed to know Phainon didn’t. At least Phainon didn’t have to think of him that way.

“Why are you apologizing?” Mydei asked again, his gentle, monotone voice masking everything that he was thinking about. Maybe it wasn’t the right way to face the situation when he felt more like a petulant child, not being able to help himself from being mad at himself and Phainon, even if he didn’t do anything.

As long as he didn’t notice, it didn’t matter. He didn’t want to hurt him, but those feelings harbored in his heart anyway, even if he hated himself for it.

Phainon finally let out a heavy sigh, before looking at him with shining eyes. “I meant, Mydei, that I didn’t believe what was right in front of me.” He cautiously took both of his hands in his, looking down to them as if they were some precious jewel that he shouldn’t be able to hold. “I’m sorry that I didn’t believe your actions, you were perfectly clear on your end. I’m glad you told me how you feel about me. I… I do too.”

Mydei observed him for a few seconds, lowering his head as well. He did feel guilty, but he enjoyed hearing that explanation. It was honest, he could fully grasp the feelings he had for him and he appreciated the clarity that he adopted.

He even validated his feelings afterwards, telling him that he felt the same towards him. It was more than he expected, and exactly what he asked for, with too much aggressiveness and pride.

A hand traveled to Phainon’s cheek, caressing it tenderly to catch his attention. “Thank you for clarifying,” he whispered, watching as Phainon’s eyes focused entirely on him, a mid-way between an hungry wolf and a kicked puppy.

Cute. He has always liked how different he could be in different situations.

With a sigh, Phainon squeezed his hands and dropped his head, before letting him go and sitting back, in front of him. “And… I really am sorry about last night.” He raised his head, attempting at a smile. “I’ll work on it.”

“You don’t need to work on it,” Mydei stopped him immediately with the sweetest voice he could master. “Just wake me up and tell me what’s the problem. I am quite confident I can convince you to go back to sleep.”

“Oh? Really now?”

“I did it many other times already whenever you were worried about something, why shouldn’t I be able to do it now?”

Phainon stared at him for a while, speechless, his moth moving without causing any sound. With a few other movements, it finally formed a smile, his head rhythmically nodding at the proposal. “We’ll see.”

Another challenge. It was fine, it kept the relationship interesting. It was something that Mydei thoroughly enjoyed.

Seeing him so happy, laughing to himself about the fact that Mydei would have helped him to sleep if he needed it pushed him to finally listen to the thoughts that plagued him just a few minutes prior.

With a faint smile, he got up on his knees, never taking his eyes off of Phainon, until he sat back on his lap, legs spread across the other man’s ridiculously big thighs. One day he should probably do something about it.

Phainon straightened up his back, his eyes hovering on his face, while his hands settled on Mydei’s thighs, gentle and hesitant. He didn’t grab anything, he wasn’t holding onto them, he was just resting them on them to let him know that he was comfortable with the situation and the way he was sitting.

It was similar to how they started, but this time Phainon was more trusting and Mydei felt the stability they finally reached, step by step. The hesitation in his hands wasn’t because he didn’t think if he could touch him, it was because they could have very well be seen and he didn’t know if he could allow himself to do more than that. The way they rested, though, had never been steadier.

He knew his place, and he liked being there. He trusted in Mydei enough to know that he could feel like he could belong there without many explanations.

Slowly, Mydei allowed himself to reach down, almost instinctively trapping Phainon’s lips with his, with a familiar soft, plush feeling greeting him as he dived in to properly kiss his boyfriend.

This time, after everything they've just told each other, Mydei wanted to be anything but subtle or quick with that kiss as they often did. He took his sweet time, exploring Phainon’s soft lips, hot mouth, eager tongue, timidly asking permission to take matters further.

Mydei gave it to him, opening his mouth as fingers moved slowly up to his hips, squeezing the meat around them and the wet feeling of an external entity invading his mouth.

He was so eager now.

It was uncomfortable at first, like any other time they did it so suddenly, but he was amused by how much Phainon himself seemed to hold back until he was given the signal to do anything. He was pushing much more than he expected, but he was gentle in his own way, as if he was caressing one of those horridly ugly vases that he liked so much.

He felt as if it was something to be cared for and, unexpectedly, he fell in love with him a little bit more.

They only took a step back when they needed to breathe again, but Mydei didn’t move his head away, instead opting to rest his forehead on Phainon’s as he caught his breath again. “Needy mutt,” he whispered, almost acting offended.

Phainon let out a soft laugh, planting a quick kiss on his lips. “A needy mutt you seem to like quite a bit.”

That got another smile from Mydei, who nodded as an acknowledgment. “Unfortunately.”

It would have been completely fine to stay like that. It was comfortable and both of them liked it and clearly they didn’t want to move from that position, but Mydei still sighed loudly.

Son. Composure. Be a decent father.

His brain was banging those singular thoughts in the enclosure of his skull, effectively making it impossible to ignore them.

So, with a groan and a light whine from below him, he rolled to Phainon’s side and sat back again, just in time for their son to run to them with his hair collected in overly complicated braids.

“Dad!” he yelled, diving in his arms, uncerimoniously and completely trusting of him. Mydei, of course, caught him, calmly looking at the work of art that was created with his already ridiculously beautiful hair. “Auntie Cyrene made these!”

Right. A lot of people were in the same park. They probably saw them.

It probably mattered by the way Phainon’s head snapped towards his sister’s direction, but he couldn’t care about it now. It happened, they saw them, they hopefully enjoyed the sight. As long as he got to properly kiss his boyfriend after months, he couldn’t care less about the rest.

“Do you like them?” he asked, holding up a side of his hair to observe how well the white and strawberry blonde hair intertwined.

Their son. It did look like something ordained by fate now.

The child nodded excitedly, rolling on the side and throwing himself back on Mydei’s chest, as if staying too much time away from him personally harmed him. “Lots and lots! Can we do this more often?”

“If you turn around, I can take a picture and see if I can make them for you too when Auntie isn’t here.”

“Okay!”

Promptly, the kid turned around for a few seconds, letting his father snap a picture of the hair that Cyrene put her miraculous hands into, working her magic to create a hairstyle that Mydei didn’t even know existed. He would have probably ended up asking her for tips, but it didn’t matter. If it made his son happy, he would have gladly done it.

As he leaned in against his father again, greeted with a welcoming hug, Phainon took out his phone, taking a picture of both with a speed that Mydei rarely ever saw him do. He often was more subtle about it too, but it was understandable, It was Astraea’s birthday, and he wanted a memory of both he and his boyfriend during that day.

The child seemed not to mind, maybe because he didn’t notice or because he was more preoccupied for how Phainon was feeling. Instead of asking anything about it, in fact, he looked at him with his concerned brown eyes and just asked, “Are you still tired?”

“No,” Phainon sighed, before looking at Mydei, “we can come too.”

Mydei inadvertently smiled at the suggestion, letting the child clap quickly before he pulled on his arm to get him to stand up. He could see how Phainon positively impacted him and why he was less timid now– stability with two parents that valued him and his thoughts could make miracles.

As they both stood up, Astraea pointed at where they settled, and Mydei found himself feeling relief knowing that it was completely shielded from where he and Phainon were. No one saw them, and they had enough privacy from their friends to feel comfortable about doing everything that they did, despite being still in a public space.

Mydei still reached out for Phainon’s hand and dragged him along, following their son. “I like the heat of your hand,” he just mentioned, to avoid any further questions about it.

The only thing that he heard in return was a little laugh and a fastening pace. “As you wish.”

Another smile crept on his face, even if lasting for a few seconds, as did the slight squeeze that Phainon gave his hand when he noticed.

Incredibly, just that quick conversation ended giving him the confidence he needed to stop hoping for their future.

He knew that they would have lasted. He knew that Astraea would have grown up with a stable family who loved him. He knew that everything would have been better when they moved in Phainon’s apartment now.

For the first time since he started worrying about it, he found peace in knowing that it would have just meant they would grow closer as they did today until time let them, and it was more than enough to keep hanging on that warm hand that was now within reach.

Chapter End Notes

Finally putting in Tribios and Cyrene ^^ There will be mostly Phainon's POV chapters now that will still have focus on Mydei as well and!!! Gnaeus and Gorgo will come back next chapter!!!! Really hope this was enjoyable as well :]

chapters.title: Chapter 11
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

“You two are the most important thing right now,” he whispered, just adding fuel to a fire that Phainon doubted he could ever stop now. Mydei’s hand brushed his own gently, both giving him time and reassurance. “And I'm sorry that I made you worry so much.”
That was all he needed.

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

It turned out that switching turns to the day was surprisingly doing miracles to Phainon’s well-being, just like Cyrene suggested. He got to relax in the evening, either bickering with Mydei or spending time with Astraea while he was at work if there was some sort of emergency, or even both sometimes. Since they moved him from his previous department, he mostly dealt with older people or people around his age without a heavy emotional toll on his health, but he still visited the kids when he could.

He liked seeing how happy they were, asking how he was doing and showing him all sorts of books and drawings, other than telling him what was going on when he wasn’t there. It was nice, he was happy to see them again, but he did feel better knowing he wasn’t putting in danger Mydei or Astraea with what he might bring home from that place.

That night wasn’t different from the usual– Astraea was sleeping and he was getting ready too, having been notified already that Mydei was called to proved help to an emergency. For some reason, he didn’t fear for his well-being whenever it happened because he had always been responsible about it, other than being more than capable to do his job.

In a way, he understood it.

It wasn’t the same as his time with the children at the hospital, but they were both putting their well-being on the line in order to save others. If he wanted to keep on doing it, albeit by risking his own life and keeping in mind that he had people waiting for him at home, Phainon had no qualms about it.

Sometimes these things could get astonishingly long, so he didn’t bother try to sleep in the meantime, even if the worry was still there in the back of his mind. However, just like he asked Mydei to trust him, he wanted to trust Mydei. It was his job, he knew what he had to do to get back home in one piece.

However, it was infinitely harder to ignore the tiny, scared voice of the six year-old living with him that often couldn’t sleep all too well on his own whenever Mydei wasn’t home.

“Papa…” Astraea weakly called out to him from behind the door of the room, as he held Fig Stew with a hand, most of its body on the floor, and rubbed his left eye. “Where's Daddy?”

Phainon stood up and walked to him almost on instinct, crouching down to let him crash in his arms. “He had an emergency at work. I'm sure he will come home before morning,” he whispered, hugging him close to his chest as soon as the little child leaned against it.

Astraea raised his head, big brown eyes pleading him. “It’s late… he’s always home sooner, right?”

It was true. It was two in the morning and he left four or five hours prior, shortly after dinner.

He honestly didn’t know what he could say to calm him down at this point. He didn’t know if he was doing fine or not, even if he desperately wanted to refuse the worst options popping up in his head, and he wasn’t in a condition to lie to Astraea. Not about Mydei and not this time.

Luckily for him, his phone ringing saved him.

His hand struggled to grab it from his pocket at first, his darker thoughts still swarming his mind, and those didn’t disappear when he saw that it was Hyacine. She mentioned that she worked until late, since she was asked by their former professor to follow some sort of paid internship at the hospital, but there was no reason for her to call him.

Unless, of course, Mydei was admitted to the hospital and she happened to think to warn him.

Phainon just prayed that it wouldn’t be the case.

“Hello?” he asked, unsure of what to expect. His words died in his throat after that, letting her speak for the both of them.

“Hello, Phainon?” Hyacine asked from the other side of the phone, with an admittedly worried voice.

Every new information was a direct strike to his heart, no matter how much he wanted to believe that Mydei was fine.

“Hey, Hyacine,” he pushed himself to say, his free hand mindlessly stroking Astraea’s golden hair. “What’s the matter?”

There was a patient pause before she gave him yet another stab to his heart. “Mydei is, uh… here. At the hospital. You might want to come.”

Phainon almost felt his heart stop.

Maybe it wasn’t something too serious, but knowing what kind of job Mydei did and how high his tolerance to pain was, if he was hurried to the hospital, it had to be something that was heavy for him too.

“Papa?”

He thanked every deity up there that the child was still next to him, or he wouldn’t know if he have had moved from his current position, let alone drive the both of them to the hospital. The steady grip on his clothes was perhaps the only thing that kept him from screaming.

“I'm on my way,” he just muttered to Hyacine before putting his phone down.

He let his attention go back to his surroundings, his eyes almost instantly on the child next to him, undoubtedly scared and worried about the situation as well. He was probably searching for some sort of reassurance, but Phainon honestly had no idea how he could do that.

Mydei was the strong willed one that could think properly about everyone else around him as the world shattered his every bone against the ground, not him. What was he even supposed to do when even breathing looked impossible?

He let out a small breath, trying to figure out something– anything– to calm down both himself and Astraea, but, unfortunately for him, that child was far too smart for him to ever catch up to him.

“What happened?” he pushed out, clearly hesitant on whether or not he wanted to know the answer.

Phainon drew a heavy breath, sorting out his options. Lying to him about Mydei’s well-being or leaving him home when he knew that he was prone on hurting himself from anxiety was a big, fat no, and telling him about all the worst thoughts in his head wasn’t ideal either– he would just spiral when he might not need to. In both cases he would just put him through a kind of torture that was far too cruel to him.

“… I don't know yet,” he decided to say, the back of his index finger gently trailing down the child’s cheek. With a heavy heart, he suggested, “Dress up.”

Any other information about it felt far too difficult to get out or deliver to that little kid that was so attached to Mydei and, luckily, he didn’t ask anything more. Apparently, what was said to him was enough for him to accept the situation. For the moment, at least.

A shaky breath pushed past Phainon’s lips, before he could stand up and watch as Astraea hesitatingly walked back to his room, readily following his instructions. Good kid.

He hurriedly did the same, packing some of Mydei’s clothes in a bag easy to carry over to the hospital. If he knew anything about these cases, it was that the stay at the hospital is either in a coffin or from two to seven days, unless there are complications. Thinking about it in those terms and not that Mydei could be on the verge of death made it so much easier– if he was at the hospital as a firefighter and not as an average citizen, it meant that they were already treating him and he had more possibilities to survive whatever happened in that building on fire.

It wasn’t like he didn’t care either, but thinking about it in medical terms like any other patient made sure that he didn’t lose his mind to other, much more horrifying scenarios.

As he walked out of the room, he noticed Astraea already by the door, fully dressed to go outside, holding Fig Stew close to his chest while he waited for him. Phainon smiled weakly and brought over his own jacket to put in on, then the keys and swung the bag over his shoulders before going out of the apartment.

Astraea followed closely, reaching out a hand for him to hold and using the other one to keep his plushie close to him. Before they could even start walking down the stairs, the child asked, with a weak voice, “Where are we going?”

It made Phainon stop immediately, still stunted on what he should actually tell him. His mind was a mess, the only thing that made him hold onto a sliver of hope was his knowledge in how hospitals worked and he didn’t know how to even comprehend it himself, let alone explain it to a six year-old.

Hesitantly, he crouched down and rested his hands on his shoulders, trying to ignore the hopeful brown eyes that were looking at him. “Astraea, I know you're confused. But Papa is struggling with talking right now,” he calmly explained, “but I promise that if you don't talk or make questions for a while, I will answer to all of them, okay?”

The child nodded, pressing his lips together for a second. “Can I take Fig Stew and a book?”

Phainon nodded, opening the door again. “A small one.”

He hurriedly went in the apartment, coming back after a few seconds with a small book in his hand that he gave to the adult with him. Phainon quickly fished it inside the bag with Mydei’s clothes, before he locked the door and headed down with Astraea following him and holding his hand.

He had to tell himself to calm down and walk slower so that he could keep up with him, along with remembering to drive responsibly. There was no point in panicking now at the wheel, if he ended up in an accident before he actually reached the hospital– and, as promised, Astraea didn’t utter a word the entire ride. He was unsure about what he thought, but he doubted it was anything positive, given the situation.

As soon as they were able to get into the hospital, Phainon picked up Astraea, just in case he wanted to sleep a little. If he knew the hospital timings well enough, he doubted they’d be able to see Mydei any time soon and it was way past his bed time. It wouldn’t have been a wild assumption to expect him to fall asleep quite soon.

Phainon headed to the waiting room he knew far too well, right in front of an emergency care unit, and found Hyacine alone, waiting for him.

“Hey, Hyacine,” he hummed weakly, maybe for the tiredness. “Where is he?”

She offered the both of them a kind smile. “They're running some tests. He had a few burns, but the harsh part is his arm. Apparently, they found some broken bones.”

“You think I can see him?”

“You live with him and you have his son in your arms. I'm pretty sure they will let you come in.”

With a weak nod, Phainon headed to a nurse near the door to the emergency room, just so he could ask some more information. What Hyacine said already settled his heart, but he wanted to be sure that there wouldn’t be any other sudden news. He felt Astraea straighten up, probably knowing what they were about to do, given how often he visited points similar to that in his several visits at the hospital throughout the past year or so.

The woman that he approached turned with a few papers in her hands and kindly smiled at him. He didn’t know if he caught a sight of her yet, but it wasn’t important right now. He wasn’t there as a nurse, after all.

“Sir?” she asked, maybe a little confused.

“Sorry, I… I'm Mydeimos’s boyfriend. He should have been taken in the emergency room recently,” Phainon quickly explained, tilting his head to the side. “What happened?”

“Oh, you’re Phainon!” she beamed, suddenly more relaxed. “He asked of you a few times, we were about to call you. He got a few bad burns and we found a few broken bones, but he should be finished soon. You can wait here if you want, we’ll call you when we’re done.”

“Who did you call as his emergency number?”

“His mother, but she suggested to call you as well since you were closer.”

“Okay, thank you. I’ll wait here for when we can visit.”

“Of course,” she smiled again, before tucking a hand in her pocket and handing out a sweet to the child in his arms. “For you, while you wait with your father. Don’t worry, your dad is fine.”

Astraea blinked, probably tired beyond explanation. When he processed what was happening, he looked up at Phainon and waited for his nod as permission, and took the sweet in his hands. “Thank you!” he smiled, immediately focusing on it.

Phainon smiled and left a kind kiss on his temple as he munched on the sweet, gently taking the wrapping when Astraea started playing with it. It wouldn’t have been a problem if he wasn’t exhausted, but the lesser things in his hands, the best it would be in case he suddenly fell asleep.

Both gestures caught his attention, resulting in a movement of his head towards him. “Is it bad?” he asked, already visibly calmer as well. He probably knew the answer, but he wanted to be entirely sure before relaxing completely.

“Not too bad. He will be fine with a bit of rest,” Phainon answered, rocking him back and forth a little, trying to get him to sleep. He wasn’t bothering him, but he wanted him to sleep as soon as possible, now that they knew more about how Mydei was doing.

“Papa…” he whined, already struggling to keep his eyes open even after his recent sugar intake, “does he really have to do that every day?”

It was a fair question. It was probably the first time Astraea came to terms about the risks of his father’s job– the same one that let them meet might take him away forever someday.

This was too much of a heavy subject to discuss with a child so late into the night, and far more than Phainon was ready to handle. “We’ll talk about this later, baby. With him too, so we can know what he thinks.”

A little whine escaped his mouth as he rested a cheek on Phainon’s shoulder, now probably completely unable to stay up any further, even if he wanted to. “Papa…”

“Shh, sleep if you need,” Phainon whispered, walking in circles as he lulled him to sleep, feeling the grip of his tiny hand on his shoulder tightening and loosening rhythmically. He smiled and left a gentle kiss between his golden hair, leaning his own head on his. “It’s really late for you.”

“I wanna see Dad first…”

“I’ll wake you up when we can talk to him, rest for a while. That’s what Dad wants too, right? He tells you all the time.”

“True… Night, Papa.”

“Night, honeybuns.”

He fell asleep immediately, without even giving Phainon the time to turn around and head against to the waiting room, breathing peacefully and holding his plushie like every other night.

Phainon smiled, at least glad that he was at peace, even in the middle of the hospital and just outside of an emergency room with his father inside. He couldn’t blame him, really, especially after fearing to see him as a corpse instead of just a few broken bones needing repairing.

As he walked back, Hyacine ran towards him, just as worried. “Did they not let you in?” she asked, maybe bothered for the possibility that he didn’t qualify enough or that Mydei didn’t change his emergency contacts– which Phainon wasn’t worried about, since he did it right in front of him and showed it to him in a dramatic fashion that he never thought he would see coming from him.

At the time, he thought that it was a little over the top and not as necessary when the started narrating every single step he was doing, but he was glad now. At least, his issues on that front were non-existent.

“He’s still getting treated, but from what I heard it’s not too bad,” Phainon answered, not missing the way her stare relaxed slightly. “What are you doing here at this hour?”

“Professor Anaxa called me here for a sudden crash course. I left Cassie home for her own well-being.”

“Ah, his crash courses… You’ve always been his favorite.”

“Sometimes I wish I wasn’t, but it was the same as always. He sounded a little unhinged when he was trying to explain it, but it was interesting!”

Interesting wouldn’t be the word he would use for any of those ‘crash courses’ as they liked to call them. They all understood the basic concepts behind them, but the conversation derailed into fields and hypothesis that none of them could ever dream of. Phainon knew to be glad that Hyacine was his favorite and the only one he ever called for his rants when he somehow linked a sprained ankle with black holes.

No more of that. His brain was begging him to get out of the room and go home. Hyacine always had this inherent nature of trying to understand him even by thinking in ways that Phainon wouldn’t figure out in a million years, and she had fun with it. He was happy that both of them liked those little moments, at the very least.

Hyacine tilted her head slightly, offering a small smile that Phainon was far too grateful for. “Are you anxious?”

Maybe he still was. Even if he knew that he was doing fine now, he felt a little anxious for the future, and maybe a little guilty for never thinking about this outcome.

“I didn’t even think of the possibility of this happening, Hyacine… I thought that as long as I didn’t think about it, nothing bad would happen to him because I trusted him and I knew he was good at his job,” he confessed, wholeheartedly praying that Astraea was actually asleep and he wouldn’t hear anything. “He cares about Astraea so much too, I hoped that he would never put himself in harm’s way for his well-being as well.”

“Phainon, that’s not what his job description says. In situations like that, hesitation takes lives that could have been saved,” Hyacine almost scolded him, but always with an understanding and sweet voice. He was glad to know that she was always this gentle with him, even when he did say things that he shouldn’t.

However, that didn’t seem fair. Not to him, not to Astraea and not even to Mydei.

“Can’t I even wish for my boyfriend not to die on the job? Or at least take precautions?” he snapped almost immediately, already on the defensive. He didn’t mean to put it down like that, but it was so terribly frustrating.

Mydei saved people, but he couldn’t think about his family or his own well-being? And they were all supposed to sacrifice what they had built in all those months, what they went through and what they gave each other just because Mydei’s job description required him to sacrifice everything?

At that point, Hyacine let out a heavy sigh, looking at Phainon with a knowing impression– which usually meant that he overlooked a big part of his argument. It was never a good feeling, no matter how often he saw it happen.

“Isn’t this what he lamented with you a few months back?” she reminded him with a quiet smile. “You both risk a lot for your jobs, Phainon. You can’t ask him to sacrifice his entire career if he doesn’t want to or he likes his job, even if it is for his well-being.”

It was true. He even asked him to let him do it when Phoebe died, without the need to worry for him. It was hypocritical for him to ask Mydei to let it all go just for their well-being, since it was clear that he genuinely liked his job despite the dangers.

Then again, he did change his shift and department after that conversation precisely because he didn’t want to hear Mydei so worried and genuinely scared for him. Even Astraea noticed it and stood closer to him in case he needed more support in that period.

No matter what either of them thought, they couldn’t do such heavy jobs and expect not to drag home something ugly that Astraea would have noticed at some point. They could do it perfectly before living together and caring for a little child together, but not anymore. If not for each other or their own health, they had to think about Astraea now.

As Phainon was about to say something to answer Hyacine and say that, yes, she was right, but he still wanted to talk about it with Mydei, a deep, imposing voice beat him to it.

“It won’t be necessary,” the man next to them said, complete in a firefighter uniform and with a few bandages over his hand. With his free hand, he reached out to both of them to introduce himself. “Gnaeus, Mydeimos’s boss.”

Phainon looked at him for a second, before grabbing it and doing the same. “Ah, Phainon. His–”

“Boyfriend. I know.” He greeted Hyacine properly as well, even if it was obvious that he was here to communicate something to Mydei’s family relating to work, than just a friendly visit. When he moved his stare back to Phainon, he announced, “I will pull him back from on-field work.”

He blinked in shock, maybe expressing too much of a reaction for news that was, quite frankly, pretty positive.

It wasn’t like Phainon was sad with the new– he wasn’t at all, really– but he wondered about the reason. Usually, people who were well qualified for their job as much as Mydei was would be more likely to get away with mistakes with a slap on the wrist or a reprimand. There weren’t many other options left to explain that decision.

“Why? Did he behave badly?” he asked in the end, just asking the strictly needed questions, since he clearly wasn’t the type he could sweet talk to.

He nodded slightly. “Somewhat. He acted on instinct to save two twins, but he risked several lives in the process. Luckily no one died, but, due to some past facts happening, I am forced to keep him back.”

“Past facts?”

“You can ask Gorgo about it when she gets here. It’s related to his father.”

His father. The one he barely even tells him about and that he deeply hates. And now he got pulled back from what he liked doing for a living for something that his father did.

Phainon didn’t know if he was relieved by this decision anymore, if he had to be honest.

“Okay,” he breathed out, finally opting not to say anything of the thoughts circulating in his head. It probably wasn’t his fault anyway and he didn’t want to ruin the relationship Mydei had with the superior who had the decency of informing his family about his future safety. “Thank you for telling me.”

He pat him on his free shoulder a couple of times, careful not to whisper too loudly that Hyacine would hear him: “Take proper care of him.”

Astraea stirred a little on his shoulder, but Phainon’s eyes were occupied with following the figure of the only co-worker of Mydei’s that he had ever met that was already walking away from him, probably heading home.

It wasn’t rude– or, at least, Phainon didn’t take it as such. After speaking with him for just a few moments, it was clear that he wasn’t a person that spent many words with strangers, even if it was the family of someone working under him.

“Happy?”

His attention shifted to Hyacine as soon as he heard her voice, only to see her happily smiling at him as she leaned forward with her arms behind her back.

Phainon could only sigh. “Relieved,” he corrected her, before suddenly changing topic. If he had to think more about how much more difficult the immediate future was going to be for Mydei especially was causing his head to spin way too much for his liking. “How is living with Castorice alone?”

“Oh, so much better! We don’t have a whiny puppy refusing to rest, for starters,” she beamed, happily putting him down as she often did.

“I did rest!”

“After I menaced you of throwing away all your antiques!”

“Mydei hates them too…”

“They are quite ugly. And probably fake.”

“They’re not.”

“You got scammed so many times, Phai…”

He puffed his cheek in dissatisfaction, but he didn’t rebut immediately, simply because he knew that she was right. He found out most of what he owned was the result of scamming, but he would never openly admit it– partly because he took pride in that collection, even if they were fakes, and partly because he enjoyed the banter with Hyacine too much to let it go with a simple admission of guilt.

Although he wanted to push it to continue, their discussion was interrupted suddenly by a nurse approaching them, the same that Phainon spoke with earlier. “Phainon?” she asked, trying to get his attention. As soon as he looked at her, she smiled kindly at him. “You can see him if you want now.”

Phainon drew out a heavy sigh, nodding to her. With a movement of his head, he silently thanks Hyacine, both for calling him and staying with him until he was able to see him, met with a kind smile and a wave of her hand.

Without a word, he followed that woman until he crossed the door of a room rather far away from the waiting room, grateful that the nurse immediately walked out and closed the door. He didn’t know if she had to be somewhere else, since she took the time to accompany him too, but he was glad that he was alone with Mydei, at last.

As he glanced at the bed, he noticed that he was fast asleep, snoring lightly, bandages around his shoulder, neck and part of his head, going over his left eye and ear. That was probably the part that was burned and, obviously, it just extended from the arm that was probably broken, given the different type of bandages on that arm. Maybe it was better not to wake him up or let Astraea rest on top of him, just in case those wounds still hurt.

He pressed his lips in a smile, nodding his head at the information he had now. His heart wasn’t heavy anymore, Astraea was still peacefully sleeping and Mydei was fine, all things considered. All the wounds would have healed with time.

Luckily, he knew how these rooms were structured and where to get what he needed to properly put to sleep the child in his arms. For the moment, Mydei’s clothes would have made a decent bed for him and he was small enough to fit in his lap as he sat on what looked like an extremely uncomfortable sofa.

He had always wondered how horrible would be to sleep in a place like that, but that thought wouldn’t have had to wait too much more before being addressed and lived through, at least for the rest of the night.

It didn’t matter much, since it was just one day, but he still wasn’t sure he wanted to try and go to sleep right away. However, he still settled Astraea down on the sofa, using Mydei’s hoodie as a softer, better pillow and the cover he didn’t realize was still in that bag since their picnic to offer him a little warmth on top of his body. For the moment, it would have had to make do.

Since he was still restless, he took his time walking around the room, unsure that was even a standard room for patients like that in the first place. It was a room with only one patient, for starters, and, after observing further, he noticed a hidden bed next to where Mydei lied. All this was something that was either in rooms of long-term patients– namely children– or some intensive care units. Definitely not emergency rooms, that were often stuffed with five or six people and with doctors and nurses going back and forth.

Phainon even doubted that Mydei was a code red in the first place, if most of the damages that he got caught into were solved in a few hours with no surgeries or heavy operations. The burns might have been the most pressing matter and he didn’t know how grave they were, but he was glad that they gave him this room.

As he tried to get the bed out, he suddenly remembered one of the doctors in his department mentioning that they were adding an emergency room that they still had to renovate, so maybe it was that one. It was still bizarre that they’d give this to Mydei in particular, but he tried to just be grateful, without asking himself too many questions for the moment.

It was better for them, even if it was a little confusing either way.

“Phainon?”

The sudden whisper calling out his name made him snap his head right after finally being able to set up the hidden bed. His eyes met Mydei’s slightly open, tired ones, barely able to keep them focused on him, a bit of a ragged breathing resounding in the room.

Phainon was next to his bed, holding his hand and looking at him with lucid eyes, in a heartbeat. “Hey,” he breathed out, eyes darting all over his body and his fingers trembling slightly. “How are you feeling?”

“It hurts a little, but better than I thought,” Mydei answered, holding his hand and caressing the back of it, maybe trying to calm him down as much as he could.

He fully knew that he was out of danger right now, but he couldn’t help but worry for him until he got out of that hospital bed and sat on their couch. At home. Safe. In a place where he could do something for him.

Mydei let his hands go for a second to use that hand to sit up, letting out a few groans as he settled. Phainon immediately snapped his body towards him, ready to act if anything out of the ordinary happened and needed his personal intervention.

“Don't push it,” Phainon whispered, with a voice once again full of pain and worry. Maybe he should give him more space now, but he couldn’t help it– he went through so many scenarios where he would have never seen him open his eyes ever again, and he was still scared. It still felt unreal, maybe for how tired he was.

“It's okay,” Mydei sighed when he finally sat up. “I'm fine, you don’t have to worry anymore. I told them to call you, but they said that the family had priority, so they called my mother even if she was farther away. Did they call you?”

“Hyacine did after she saw you around two in the morning,” Phainon answered, unconsciously searching for his hand again to ground him in reality again. “They told me your mother told them to call me as well, but I think I was already on the way here… I barely even checked my phone because I was too worried.”

Mydei smiled, reaching his hand out to caress Phainon’s cheek. “I’m fine now. And I’m here, you aren’t dreaming anything.”

Phainon grabbed his hand and kept it there, dropping on his knees on the ground. He didn’t even care if it was dirty, he just needed to feel him as close as possible and be sure that he didn’t push himself too much. His fingers intertwined with Mydei’s as he pressed the back of that hand to his cheek, before ordering his thoughts and sorting them in case there was something that he needed to know.

With a low whine, he finally whispered, “Gnaeus said that he would pull you back from direct, on-field operations.”

He didn’t know how he would take it, but he didn’t know how much he cared either way. He was exhausted, he just wanted to talk to him and see him doing well– it didn’t matter to him how he would take that news at the moment. As long as he got to listen to him, they would have been able to fix it, eventually.

Mydei sighed, but he nodded quietly. “It’s a pity, but the right choice. I would have asked him to anyway.”

“Really?”

“Phainon, you're terrified of abandonment and I have a deeply traumatized child that lost two parents already. I don't want him to lose a third one yet.”

“Wouldn't that hurt your career?”

“Who the fuck cares about my career?” Mydei groaned, sounding almost annoyed. Phainon just hummed at it, rubbing his thumb on the back of his hand, waiting until his boyfriend looked at him again. “I do that job so that I can actively help people and pay my taxes. Not directly saving people doesn't mean that I'm done with my job, just that I won't be moving up in the ranks, which I have never even tried to do.”

In his defense, Phainon didn’t even think about that possibility.

Of course, Mydei cared more about his family than career, there was no doubt about that, but he didn't think he wouldn't care or even ask to be pulled back from on-field work. He knew that he personally wouldn't have asked to ever get pulled out of treating difficult patients or someone with a grave or terminal illness. If anything, those people were the ones who needed him the most.

However, Mydei's life was in direct danger. It wasn't about his mental well-being that could be fixed later on, it was his actual life. If he sacrificed himself to save others, there was no fixing later on in any way.

He would be dead, or suffer for the rest of his life, or something worse could happen to him that the doctors wouldn't be able to help with.

This time he was lucky. Just burns and a few broken bones were nothing to all these other scenarios that could very well occur if he kept operating as he did until now.

Then, there was the fact of Astraea. He was his primary caretaker, that child was able to heal thanks to him, and he lost his parents in a fire already. Losing the one that saved him in the same way would have been a sure-fire way to launch him in a darker place that neither of them wanted to see any time soon.

Mydei squeezed his hand, maybe noticing how lost in his own thoughts he became in the last few seconds, and smiled warmly at him. For some reason, the fact that he was being so understanding and giving that hand to anchor him to something was shattering his heart– not in a bad way, he was just relieved that this was still his Mydei and he was alive and well, still trying to get his mood off of the depths of the ocean.

For some reason, for the first time in years, he felt like crying of happiness. He was so relieved. He was so happy to see him move and talk and look at him like he was the most precious thing on the planet.

He looked so in love. He didn't even mention Astraea or asked how he was doing, because he knew that Phainon took care of it at the best of his abilities. There was so much trust and affection in those amber eyes that it was moving him to tears.

“You two are the most important thing right now,” he whispered, just adding fuel to a fire that Phainon doubted he could ever stop now. Mydei’s hand brushed his own gently, both giving him time and reassurance. “And I'm sorry that I made you worry so much.”

That was all he needed.

Hot, heavy tears slid down his cheeks and broken whimpers left his lips, as his breathing struggled to keep itself at bay. He didn’t even have his surroundings completely clear, everything was glassy and blurred by the tears welling up in his eyes as they burned and his mouth was trying to get more and more air into his lugs without much success.

He wasn’t sure why those words made him lose his composure so violently, since everything was generally going better than just a few minutes ago. Having Mydei there, ready to comfort him and looking at him with that much love reflected in his eyes was doing things to his heart, and on top of it the scare he got when he learned of the situation was still brewing in his mind.

His head fell against the mattress as he let out choked sobs, gripping Mydei’s hand so strongly that he nearly left marks on it. He didn’t even care how he looked right now, he needed to cry in his presence if he wanted to avoid to explode in a thousand pieces.

“You big baby,” Mydei whispered, gently moving his hand until Phainon let it go, immediately complying with his wishes. The hand slowly traveled to the top of his head, kindly brushing against his hair, moving from left to right, causing a needy whine to come out from the other man’s throat. “You came here to support me and now you're crying out of exhaustion and acting all cute pleading me to comfort you… I did give you quite the scare this time.”

He wanted to say it. He did, he was terrified, he needed an entire week off of his job to cuddle with him all day and make sure that it was real and he didn’t lose him without even noticing or making many thoughts about his safety because he told him that he didn’t need to, and he trusted him.

And now he was in a hospital bed with half of his body covered in bandages and broken bones while he was weeping out of the fear of losing him.

Mydei let out a soft laugh and moved his hand on his cheek, caressing it a couple of times with the back of his fingers, until Phainon raised his head again. He was sure he was a mess and the mattress was drenched wet by then, but neither of them cared in the slightest, focusing instead on the way one’s hand rested on the other’s chin, as if taking pity on a sad, whining puppy.

“It's fine,” Mydei said, softly and caring, caressing him under his chin. “It's all over. I'm not going anywhere now.”

Phainon violently nodded, before Mydei could caress him on his cheek again. “I… Mydei, I really…” he attempted to say, unsuccessful.

It was so easy. It was just three words, and yet, they always got stuck in his throat, unable to travel past his lips.

He loved him, he knew he did– hell, he was so deeply in love with him that the prospect of living the rest of his life without him and seeing him looking at him with nothing but love into his eyes sent him spiraling so much that he bursted out crying for the first time after a decade and a half– but he was so difficult to say it out loud, for some reason.

Maybe it was part of his abandonment issues, but he genuinely wanted this. For him and for Mydei. For Astraea too, he wanted all of them to keep living in a place full of love and care for one another, albeit with the issues they might end up having.

And he couldn’t even say it. Cursing himself wouldn’t have been nearly enough as punishment for his inability to something that simple.

Mydei just stared for a while before speaking again. “You don't have to say it, I know already,” he smiled, tilting his head to the side in an adorable motion. “I love you too.”

Somehow, that just made it worse and better at the same time.

His fingers moved on their own for a few seconds and his breathing refused to stabilize, even after everything that Mydei did to try and calm him down. He was really ungrateful, wasn’t he? His boyfriend was on a hospital bed trying desperately to lull him back to sanity, and he was unable to catch that hint and calm himself down. For fuck’s sake, he was almost thirty years old and he stood there crying like a baby in a situation where he should have been the composed one.

A stare was all Mydei needed to slightly change the situation, despite the late hour and the fact that he was dealing with something more akin to a breakdown than anything else. “Hey, sit down,” he murmured, moving his hand to give a few pat on the mattress, next to him. “Sit. Clearly saying on the floor will change nothing.”

Phainon reluctantly agreed, sting up briefly to sit in the spot he was told to. His arms were still shaking lightly and his breathing wasn’t regular, but it was slightly calmer since Mydei started talking to him so softly.

Mydei rested his hand on Phainon’s thigh, lazily brushing his thumb against it. “Hey.” He tried to catch his gaze again, even in those blue eyes kept darting away from him. His voice was soft, understanding, gentle, barely more than a whisper. So full of love. “What are you so scared about? I'm here, Astraea is safely sleeping over there, you’re safe and sound. Why are you trembling like a leaf?”

He drew a ragged breath. “Just…”

With a smile, Mydei pulled on his wrist, telling him to get down, maybe lay on top of him. He did it sometimes, when he realized that Phainon was tired or needed a little bit of comfort without him needing to say anything. This time, it was to calm him down and ground him, almost as a reassurance about his well-being.

Slowly, Phainon complied. It was hard resisting to Mydei’s suggestions and he had no intention to in that situation. He knew that he would feel better and he knew that he needed it, he had no reason to refuse that offer in any way.

A grunt made its way to his ears, but he didn’t pay much attention to it– he knew that it might have hurt him, but he told himself not to worry too much, or Mydei would have smacked his head for worrying about him instead when he could barely sit still.

“Breathe,” Mydei whispered, as he pressed his head against the shoulder free of the bandages, letting him bury his head into it. Phainon whined at the contact, inhaling deeply whatever kind of smell there could be around that spot. A lot of it had something to do with the medicines they used to treat him, but the distinct perfume of cinnamon was still noticeable, enough for him to find it comforting and feel his heartbeat starting to slow down.

Another whine escaped his lips as he found enough peace to breathe normally again and enough heat around him to lay there for a longer while, almost able to fall asleep. It was easy now, knowing that Mydei was right there gently caressing his head to lull him to sleep, while the sweet cinnamon and a tinge of pomegranate reminded him of that same fact– Mydei was alive and well, right there where he was, and they would have gone home soon.

“Go to sleep, Phainon,” he heard before completely losing himself and jolting himself awake as a consequence. After a quick laugh, Mydei pointed behind him and reminded him of where they were. “You can’t sleep on me yet, but there should be another bed here, take Astraea too.”

Phainon didn’t move immediately. He pondered his options first, then processed his words and ultimately did as suggested, even if he wasn’t thrilled about it. It was better that Mydei’s wounds would heal as soon as possible, as it was that Astraea needed to sleep on a decent surface.

After scooping up the child and carefully taking off both of their shoes, he sat on the bed and laid down, resting the child right next to him before he could tuck in the both of them. To no one’s surprise, Astraea instinctively reached out to his body in his sleep, quickly being taken into a hug, as he still held close his little plushie.

As soon as his head hit the pillow, his eyes suddenly grew heavier and heavier, only leaving space for the darkness engulfing him, but he had never felt lighter than in that moment. He didn’t even have the time to tell Mydei goodnight, but he didn’t know how much strength he had for it either– he felt so at peace and accepted, loved… even if they were in a difficult situation, he knew that it would have passed. Mydei would have healed, Astraea would have grown a little bit more and he would still have all that warmth and love that he grew to adore and almost depend on, even through the darkness.

He didn’t fear closing his eyes and slip into his sleep with Astraea’s soft breathing reminding him what he built over the past several months and how deeply they both loved him in their own ways. He wished to never see them go, holding the child a little closer, further allowing his slumber to claim him until he had no recollection of being awake, finally letting his brain and eyes rest peacefully after far too long.

The first thing Phainon felt again when he woke up was a sense of peace, maybe due to resting decently after staying up until so late and feeling exhausted after everything that happened to Mydei and that required too much of his energies, both physically and mentally. Shortly after opening his eyes, he heard a few giggles as well not too far from him, probably from Astraea either talking or playing with Mydei.

He was glad that, at least, he wasn’t completely lost with his surroundings after how quickly he fell asleep the night prior. Everything was pretty clear, he remembered most of what happened and he was relatively calm after the difficult situation that they all had to face just a handful hours ago.

With only a sigh, he made sure that the rest of his family– which was still hard to believe as a word that could be applied to them, but there was no better word to describe it anyway– knew that he was conscious again.

“Papa!” Astraea beamed, hopping off of the bed to go and hug him. Phainon smiled, hugging him back and kissing him on the top of his head as he decided to sit up.

Looking at his side, he noticed Mydei, both more rested and slightly calmer than the previous night. He smiled at him as soon as blue eyes landed on his body, almost as if he was reassuring him. “Good morning, Phainon.”

“Morning…” he answered, letting the child in his arms hop off of his lap. “What hour is it?”

“11 AM. I take it you slept well.”

He did, honestly.

Thinking about it again, though, that didn’t cut it.

He slept so well that he was barely able to notice that he had a breakdown at three in the morning and experienced almost watching his boyfriend die on the job. Not only that, he felt refreshed, as if he went through a complete factory reset.

Saying he slept well wasn’t enough because he felt as if that cry and subsequent rest almost made him go through a fresh, smooth rebirth. He had never felt so good, so awake, so present.

Phainon slightly tilted his head after he let his eyes wander a little between new, fresh bandages over his skin and the calm expression on Mydei’s face. “Did a medic update you?”

“I need to rest for a few months for my arm and the burns are most likely going to scar,” he promptly answered, with an almost neutral voice. He probably expected that something like that could happen at some point given the nature of his job, but it was still a little scary, in Phainon’s humble opinion.

However, it didn’t matter much anymore. He was fine and he would take care of other matters in his unit after he recovered, along with keeping on being by his side and taking care of his child– who felt more theirs than just Mydei’s these days, Phainon corrected himself briefly.

“What happened in there? Can you talk about it?” he ended up asking, a little worried about getting to know such information. He knew it wasn’t too bad, but he wondered if it was light enough to tell Astraea too.

Almost as if he felt the mood of the room get heavier, the child walked back to Phainon to sit next to him, leaning a little on his side, silently requesting him a hug with the corresponding arm. He complied, letting him take refuge between his arm and side of his body.
