“My arm just got trapped under some furniture while I was saving a couple of twins who got stuck in a particularly difficult spot to reach,” Mydei explained, trying to recall the clearest details he remembered. “It wasn’t the first time someone in my team did it, but the difference with this time is that they never got stuck. Luckily, Gnaeus noticed and helped me getting out with the children.”

Gnaeus. Phainon made a mental note to thank him later for more than just pulling out Mydei from on-field work.

Astraea leaned over to look at Mydei, holding Phainon’s arm as a support. “That’s how you helped me too.”

“Yeah,” Mydei softly laughed. “I avoided the falling objects, though.”

Thinking about it now that they mentioned it, Phainon never asked Mydei about how he was able to save Astraea, nor how his biological parents died. There were hints throughout those past few months whenever he would refer to that night, but nothing too explicit, maybe to preserve the minuscule amount of dignity they had left.

They did end up raising that child for five years and his mother brought him upon this world, he probably gave them a little amount of respect for that very reason. Even if they were horrible parents, his mother did something for him– maybe not too much or what she had to, but not even Astraea seemed to be hating her nor be afraid of her like he used to be of his biological father.

“Did your mother come by?” Phainon asked all of a sudden, after his thoughts made him remember about something so important about Mydei and his private life, along the current situation he was in.

Mydei nodded slightly, a little reflective on that topic. “They went home to prepare lunch, since you were exhausted. Cipher and Aglaea are there as well, they wanted to help.”

“Were you dismissed?”

“We just need to sign a few papers and I’m free to go home.”

“Let me take care of it.”

Phainon stood up, only to stop not even two steps later because the child next to him lightly pulled his arm and refused to let go. When he turned around, he was looking at him with big, pleading brown eyes, trying to get him to stay.

It was a child, after all.

With a smile, Phainon crouched down and held his hands, slightly rubbing his thumbs over the back of his little fists. “Astraea, can you help Dad put on the clothes in the bag I brought? I won’t be gone for long, but he needs a little bit of help now, can I count on you to take care of him?”

The child blinked once, then turned his head towards Mydei and nodded, most likely understanding just then what the issue was. “I’ll do my best!” he beamed, finally smiling brightly at Phainon.

“Good boy.” He stood up and ruffled his hair, satisfied of the answer, before finally walking towards the door of the room. “See you soon.”

The entire ordeal was much, much faster that he initially expected. Apparently, they just needed him to sign and bring a few papers home about the treatment of the burns, other than a new appointment for the broken bones in a few days, just to check how Mydei was doing. Luckily, it wasn’t the first time he had dealt with severe burns, but those sheets could be useful either way.

Mydei somehow managed to get into his clothes, ready to walk to their car and finally go home. Phainon didn’t speak much, but he liked to listen to what they were saying– for once, he enjoyed just answering some questions and bathing in the atmosphere with Astraea asking Mydei a thousand questions about the book he brought and they evidently read while he was still sleeping.

When they rushed to the hospital he didn’t have the time to check which one he took, but it was apparently much, much harder than the ones he usually read and Mydei had to explain a number of words to him, and now he ended up memorizing all of them and ask for synonyms. Which he probably will remember, so good luck to them when he starts reciting those in front of a teacher after he started school in just a few months.

They hadn’t talked about it yet, but it was March, the school would have started after the summer and they already completed the subscription for him without doing much more to get him ready for it.

From the looks of it, Astraea didn’t attend school in any way, shape or form yet, so they both hoped that it would have gone well, with a bit of catch up. Nothing fancy, just something about reading and counting– after all, they couldn’t do much for the socializing with other children his age part that they didn’t already try. Hopefully, it would have been enough.

Besides those thoughts, the ride was nice. Pretty normal, even. When Mydei got off of the car, Astraea even carried the bag with barely something inside thinking that he needed help with it, probably taking Phainon’s words from earlier to heart. What a cute child.

Phainon let them go in, nodding towards Mydei when he turned around to see what he was doing, as if to say to lean on him for the time being. It was absurdly obvious he wasn’t used to getting taken care of, no matter if and how much he thought that he didn’t notice.

As soon as the door opened, Phainon noticed Gorgo helping set the table with Cipher for just a split second, before she would hurriedly walk towards Mydei. Astraea moved out of the way quickly, letting mother and son crash in a hug that they both probably needed.

“Mydeimos,” she whispered, before cupping his face with both of her hands and look at him with worry, observing his entire body from top to bottom, trying to assess if there was something wrong with her son that the doctors somehow didn’t catch.

Mydei let her, only smiling when she looked all over at him, just like a child would when they kept reassuring their mother that they were fine, but their mother insisted on being careful for a few hours over how they moved. “Mom, I’m fine, don’t worry.”

It was refreshing and fascinating for Phainon to see it like that. It was so obvious that they loved each other, but he couldn’t help feeling too much in those moments, almost as if he wasn’t allowed to be there– like he was an accessory that didn’t fit with the others colors of the room.

His mother died when he was a child, he barely remembered her. All he had of her were a photo album, her name and some memories that Cyrene would share with him every once in a while. Every other person that he was compelled to call ‘mother’ wasn’t really one, and they barely saw him as their son. He wasn’t sure they even saw him as a child, sometimes.

They changed, but their behavior was always the same. Cold, absent, superficial. Sometimes they could get more interesting by insulting him openly, but they mostly didn’t care what he did or didn’t to.

After all, it wasn’t as if he was their child. He was just a child living under their same room, no more and no less.

What Mydei had with his mother, he had with his sister. It had always been them against the world, until she left to chase her dreams and Phainon found a safe haven in Hyacine and Castorice.

He didn’t blame her for it.

If anything, he was happy that his sister, the person he wanted the most to be happy, finally started to live for herself after Phainon himself told her that he was old enough to fend for himself. Even if it was a lie and he would end up suffering trying to mend that kind of relationship with a romantic partner that was nearly impossible to find, it didn’t matter.

She deserved to be happy more than anything else. He remembered how much she had to pretend to be fine with so many harsh words, how red her fingers were and how tired her eyes looked after writing throughout the night.

If catching her dreams would have made her smile more often, Phainon was willing to lose her presence in his life. It was terrifying, but his sister was so much more important than anything he might feel after her departure.

They were both fine now– Cyrene with her novels and children’s books and Phainon with the family that he had always longed for and doing a job that he loved. That misery looked ineffable, but they somehow escaped it, settling somewhere of their own choosing.

He didn’t really wish for anything more for himself now. The closest thing to a wish were prayers for his loved ones, the ones that were still in his life.

Prayers for Mydei to always be loved and supported by his family.

Prayers for Hyacine and Castorice to always be content, happily living together and sharing their moments of joy and sorrow together.

Prayers for Cyrene to always write, brightening everyone’s day with her smile and uplift and inspire countless others like she did with him.

Prayers for Astraea to choose his path like he did and to always be loved by everyone around him like Mydei was.

He found himself thinking about the last one almost on a daily basis. He didn’t have any particular dream anymore, but that was the closest to it without a doubt.

He took a heavy breath and walked over towards the kitchen, leaving Mydei to have his moment with his mother and Astraea to play with Cipher. Apparently, he loved all his aunts and he was glad it was the case– it was both reliving and easier to handle him whenever he or Mydei couldn’t keep their eyes on him.

In front of some boiling water was Aglaea, most likely waiting for the food to get ready, working just as he remembered her. Cautious, patient, but sure of herself and what she was doing.

“Do you need some help, Aglaea?” he asked, only offering it because he knew that she was the one who needed it the most, since the table was being taken care of by other two people already. He guessed that a tiny help would have been welcomed.

“Mh,” she nodded without looking at him, “give me the plates if you can.”

“On my way!”

Luckily, they were basically done with the food already, because Mydei stepped into the kitchen trying to help, as he often did. Phainon couldn’t say that he didn’t expect it, but he didn’t need him to get involved in something that didn’t need his presence right after such a traumatic event for his body, whether he wanted to admit it or not.

Phainon lightly pushed him out of the room, until he was able to make him sit on a chair around the table. Promptly, Astraea ran to them and sat on the chair next to his, hugging his father’s arm. “Mydei, stay here, you were just dismissed.” He ran his fingers through his hair and tucked them behind his ear, noticing immediately how easily he leaned into it. Not the right time, but he kept it vivid in his mind. “We're enough to serve the dishes.”

Mydei looked like he was about to retort, but he just resorted to what he often told him around midday. “Remember that–”

“I know, Astraea doesn't like these vegetables unless they’re hidden in something else, I'll take care of it,” Phainon finished his sentence, placing his hands on his shoulders. “Sit and relax, we’ll eat soon.”

In all honesty, he didn’t know how much that worked, but he trusted Astraea to do his magic. It wasn’t like Mydei wouldn’t bend over backwards to make him happy or do whatever he asked him anyway.

Going back to the kitchen, he just did what Mydei asked of him and took Astraea’s plain pasta plate and mixed a bunch of broccoli until they formed an acceptable sauce, topping it off with some cheese. It won’t be perfect, but it was something that he could eat without problems.

As soon as he brought it over and sat next to Mydei, on the opposite side to Astraea, he sensed immediately a somewhat tense air all around him.

Obviously, Mydei was pretending to be fine and his mother was worried, but it seemed as if there was another layer to it that neither of them was telling. If Phainon had to guess from their unspoken words, it probably had something to do with his father.

Fortunately, Aglaea thought it was time to break that awkward silence.

“How are you feeling, Mydeimos?” she asked kindly, resting a hand on her chest. “I apologize for not greeting you right away, but I wanted the food to be good, after the night you must have had.”

Mydei hinted at a smile, catching his mother’s attention again. “Don’t worry, Aglaea, thank you for coming either way. I feel… good? The burns don't hurt much and my arm is doing fine, all things considered.”

He was lying.

Phainon was accustomed to his behaviors by now, and he tended to focus too much on looking at the other person if he was lying in their face. However, he didn’t say anything. He knew that the white lie he just told was mostly to get them to stop worrying about him, but, if he noticed it, he was convinced that his mother did too.

In fact, there was an audible sigh at the table coming from her direction almost immediately. “Mydeimos…” she almost reprimanded him, but she didn’t add much.

“Mom, I'm fine, really,” Mydei replied. “It was a slight mistake on my part, but everyone is safe now. That's what matters, right?”

To that, Cipher groaned loudly. “Come on, look a little more under the surface, little lion!”

“Cifera,” Aglaea immediately followed to scold her.

“What? As if it wasn't obvious already!”

“I get it,” Mydei immediately broke the little fight that was starting to develop, maybe out of consideration for Astraea as well. Phainon reached out at the same time to caress his hair and give him some sort of reassurance, given how uncharacteristically silent he was being. “I won't do his same mistakes, if that's your worry. I wanted to ask to keep me out of direct danger already, for the well-being of Phainon and my child.”

So it was about that man again.

Phainon didn’t ask of him directly yet, mostly because Mydei clearly didn’t want to talk about it and he respected his space, trusting that he would have opened up when he felt the time was right, but it felt like this father of his did some horrible things, enough to make Gorgo worry about him repeating them.

Maybe it was just a mother’s useless worrying, but he couldn’t say he had never seen Mydei entertain himself in little care for his well-being, even if he was trying to tone it down since they started living together. Burning himself accidentally, throwing himself into fire at work, refusing to take the car whenever he went out to work in the evening and walked alone in the dead of night.

They weren’t deadly situations, but Phainon did worry at times. It probably was what was going on with Gorgo now too.

However, she didn’t press too much. She just smiled and nodded before muttering, “I’m relieved, then.”

The rest of the lunch went smoothly, tending to go on other topics and without going back to the one of Mydei’s father or his trip to the hospital. Astraea talked as well when he was asked something and sat when Aglaea and Gorgo told him a few stories about their own childhoods or, occasionally, Mydei’s or Cipher’s, much to their groans of embarrassment. In that moment, he almost felt glad that there wasn’t Cyrene with them too.

He laughed whenever they would say something embarrassing or when Mydei groaned, or even when Astraea asked more questions and subsequently ran to his father to ask apologies in case it was too much.

It was a nice atmosphere, but he noticed Mydei tiring himself out after a couple of hours. He barely answered anymore and scooted over to be closer to Phainon, ultimately resting his head on his shoulder, struggling to keep his eyes open.

Phainon smiled softly, gently caressing his hair and accepting the timid request of holding his hand too after a few attempts at slightly brushing against his fingers. He figured that he probably didn’t sleep as much as he should have, so he let him take a nap there, in the middle of the chatter all around them. He was always quite the heavy sleeper, so he was sure that he didn’t mind too much.

However, it didn’t last much longer.

Gorgo noticed the state her son was in, desperately needing to rest, and stood up, gathering her things and getting ready to go. “Thank you for the hospitality, Phainon,” she said as she put on her coat, ready to go home. “Please, take care of Mydeimos and don’t hesitate to call us if you need anything.”

He nodded, thankful to feel somewhat included now. “Don’t worry, I’ll put my years as a nurse to bear some fruit. After all, Mydei tends to push himself too much.”

It was something he did as well, and Mydei scolded him for it several times, even putting his foot down and refusing to let him do it any more than he felt necessary. Since he had to rest now, it was Phainon’s turn of doing so.

“That, he does,” Gorgo agreed. “I give you the best of wishes for your life together here, it looks like a lovely accommodation. Keep on cherishing my son and little Astraea as well, I can tell there is a lot of love and happiness in these four walls.”

“I will. Thank you, Gorgo.”

“Anytime. You’re always welcome to visit too, Phainon.”

With a hint of a bow– because he couldn’t move much with Mydei sleeping on his shoulder– he watched them go as they waved, some more enthusiastically than others.

It was nice.

The feeling of being included like that was rather nice, besides the feelings of not belonging flaring up whenever he had to sit by and witness Mydei and his mother having the most beautiful relationship he could witness and couldn’t possibly reach since his mother was… well, dead.

He could, however, try to have a good relationship with Gorgo, since she clearly liked him and approved of him enough to ask him to take care of Mydei– and that had to count for something. Besides that, Aglaea had always treated him well too, despite the little time they talked, so it might not be a long shot to say that, perhaps, he could find himself included in that concept of family as well.

A low whine coming from his shoulder distracted him from his thoughts enough to drop them there, turning his attention to his boyfriend instead. “Mydei?” he asked, brushing his lips against his hair, only gaining another tired sound as a response.

Then, a quiet sniffle. A light squeeze of his hand immediately followed, along with his cheek brushing against his shoulder.

Worry crept in on him, immediately moving to raise his head with his fingers under his chin. Mydei wasn’t caught by surprise, but he didn’t look at him either. Instead, he just stood there with his head turned away, a trail of tears down his cheeks clearly visible.

He drew a heavy, shaky breath before speaking. “I don't want to be like him. My mother saying that to me hurt much more than anything I felt last night. I spent all my life trying not to be like him, to fix his mistakes, and it was all for nothing. I did one thing similar to him and my mother looked at me with a worried expression that I have never seen on her and my superior demoted me because I dared to act a little too much like my father.”

Phainon froze at those words.

He didn’t know what to say, but he felt the weight that had on him. Maybe he was told he was similar to his father and he worked on himself to fight it and prove them wrong, maybe his father was a firefighter as well and he got told that he had to stay in line, not to act like his father, or there would have been consequences.

It wasn’t the act in itself that bothered him– he said he was going to ask his boss to get him out of on-field operations anyway– it was the reason. It wasn’t just the burns or the broken arm, it was because he acted with the thought of saving someone as he was required to do, and everyone around him pointed at the fact that he made the same mistakes of his father instead, punishing him for it.

He had no doubt that his father was nowhere in his mind when he acted to save children, so hearing so many people that he trusted to underline that fact had to hurt. Especially since he knew all too well how much he loathed that man and how afraid he was to repeat his mistakes with Astraea or Phainon himself.

“You’re not him,” he mumbled, slowly letting his chin go and hold his hand with both of his. “I don't need to know his entire life to say this– Mydeimos, you're absolutely not like your father. You refuse to drink to avoid the possibility of ever treating badly me or Astraea, you always put us before anything else, you worry for both of our well-being, you allow yourself to be honest with me, you sacrificed so much for this family… you’re wonderful, Mydei. Whether or not you happen to make similar mistakes to his.”

Phainon watched as he let out another heavy exhale, clearly taken aback from his words, but he didn’t say anything. Instead, he closed his eyes as a quiet, small tear slid under his cheek again.

Mydei’s hand curled around his own with a decisive grip, only opening his eyes again when Astraea approached him and opened his arms towards him. “Daddy, do you wanna hug?” he asked, with a gentle smile on his face.

Slowly, Mydei smiled and slid off of the couch, sitting on the floor to let the little child throw himself at him. “Thank you, honey,” he whispered as he wrapped his free arm around Astraea, loud enough for Phainon to hear as well.

He looked at them with a soft smile on his face for a second, before he followed Mydei in the same motion, sitting on the floor as well, next to the both of them. He sat there silently, offering his shoulder again if Mydei needed it again, but otherwise just glad to be around them, as it had been for several months when they started getting to know each other.

Now it was different, but both the offer and feelings were still there.

“I missed you,” Mydei whispered right next to his ear, and, as soon as Phainon turned, he noticed that he had his chin resting on his shoulder, his lips just a short breath away from his own.

Phainon nervously laughed, a little taken aback by the sudden admission. “For what? A night out?”

“Shut up and take the compliment.”

“That's not a compliment…”

Mydei groaned as he dropped his head, brushing his forehead against his shoulder. “I like your smell and how warm you are so much that I could die right here and I would be the happiest man alive.” He raised his head again, looking almost annoyed. “Happy?”

Happy didn’t even begin to encompass what he was feeling after that compliment– not that he never mentioned it or showed it, but he never said out loud in that way. He always went out of his way to reassure him that he wouldn’t leave him and he wanted him in his life, but that was the one that might hold up in his head for the next few years.

It made him think that he wanted no one else, and he probably didn’t, his mind was just having a hard time to fully understand it until then.

Before cursing himself out for how much difficulty he had in believing his past genuine feelings conveyed just as confidently, he wrapped him in a hug, smiling when he caught a hint of a giggle from the child on his lap. If he couldn’t only believe Mydei, he should believe Astraea, who had always vouched for him, be it with Mydei or… anyone else, really. That child adored him and loved where he ended up in the last year or so.

“Shall we go rest?” Phainon finally asked, giving Mydei a way out and, above all, an opportunity to rest a few more hours. He could hide it, but he was clearly still tired from what happened a day prior.

Mydei only turned his head towards him. “You slept eight full hours.”

“Mh,” he hummed as he pretended to think about it, “I can't leave you alone without your human pillow, can I?”

His boyfriend let out a choked laugh before nodding, accepting immediately a soft kiss on his cheek. After that, Phainon opted to let him go so that he could change to get to bed again after nagging him for the last few hours. He knew far too well that, although he liked staying with others, he valued a few moments alone too.

Promptly, Astraea crawled on his lap, looking up at him with big, pleading eyes.

Oh, no.

Whatever he wanted to ask, Phainon was bound to say yes. If he requested to bring him to some impossible place to look at something that didn’t exist, may he be damned if he didn’t bend over backwards to make it happen now.

Instead of anything that Phainon’s head conjured, Astraea just blinked cutely as he asked, “Can I come too?”

Of course. Napping. Six year-olds tended to do that.

“You absolutely need your nap,” Phainon quickly smiled at him, taking him in his arms as he stood up. With a giggle, the little kid settled in the embrace, swinging his tiny arms around his broad shoulders, and Phainon felt the need to give him a gentle kiss on his forehead, turning serious for a second. “Good job taking care of Daddy today, Astraea.”

He tilted his head and blinked a few times, slightly confused. “But he always does it too when I need it, so it’s not super special?”

“Good job either way. It’s hard to take care of someone else, you know?”

“Can I do it when you’re sick too? I don’t wanna leave all the work to you all the time…”

Phainon let out a soft chuckle, both entertained by those silly requests and enamored by how much that child seemed to be wanting to help the both of them. “If you want, we’re both grateful. But remember that you don’t need to do it, nor is it your job.”

Once again, he looked confused upon hearing that statement. He tilted his head further, puffing his cheek in an absurdly adorable way and asked, “Why?”

“Because you’re a child, Astraea. We’re supposed to care about you, not the other way around.” He thought about his next words, making sure that he would understand them properly. “You’re still young, but when you will be older, you can take care of us. You will have time to make it up to us for all this time, so don’t worry too much for now. Enjoy your childhood and just offer up a hand every once in a while.”

“Can’t I enjoy my childhood later?”

“It is called childhood because you’re a child. Every age is different and we won’t live forever, right? Your father and I didn’t have great ones, so we want you to enjoy it to the fullest.”

He wasn't sure if he wanted to mention it, but he didn't want to lie to him, even if it was to supposedly protect him.

Maybe, he thought, it wasn't necessary. He clearly had enough intelligence to understand very complex situations and proved to have enough maturity to understand things that he would have never expected him to realize at that age.

Maybe he underestimated him in the past, but he didn't want it to happen again– not in the same way it happened to him with adults in his life always treating him as some stupid, fragile thing.

Astraea wasn't stupid or fragile either. He was just a child, but he understood everything that they ever explained him, if they used words and concepts that he had a grasp on.

He knew about Mydei's family history, why his grandfather wasn't in the picture anymore, when either of his parents was feeling a little down and what they needed, and he listened and trusted them for everything else that he didn't know or comprehended.

And it would have been fine if he had questions. It was better, even. In that way, he would have gained more of an understanding to many topics and that mentality would have probably helped him in the future.

Astraea lowered his eyes to think for a second, puffing both of his cheeks. When he looked at Phainon again, there was some hesitation, but he still kept up the conversation, maybe out of trust. “Why?” he asked again, a little shyly. “I know Dad’s reasons… but you?”

Phainon’s gaze softened, almost happy about the innocently curious question. He just wanted to know more about him, and it made his heart flutter with happiness. “My parents died when I was very young, and me and your aunt weren’t lucky enough to be adopted. We jumped from place to place, often not making friends or having a family to take care of us.” He sighed, thinking back to those hard times, almost bittersweet. “We started enjoying our lives pretty recently.”

They weren’t good memories, but they were the ones he shared with his sister, and she did everything in her power to make them better– the least he could do was remember those moments. However, he didn’t want Astraea to go through what he did. If he could only give him the best of the world he knew, he would have.

The child didn’t speak, instead staring at him with an almost confused expression. He was thinking, Phainon could see his gears turning and stopping, before functioning again.

All of a sudden, he raised his head and emitted a confused sound as he thought. “You have a family now, though,” he stated, before staring at him again with a tiny smile on his face. “I promise you won’t be alone again, Papa. And I won’t worry too much. I didn’t understand why… but you said it’s better, so I’ll try.”

Phainon was sure that this child was sent from some sort of God to look over him and Mydei. He was a blessing that he could never believe to ever have in this life. Even in hard days like that… he lit up the room and showed him new hues that he had yet to witness out of the same circle of colors that he had at disposal his entire life.

The fact that he included him in his family felt another confirmation of something that he yearned for way too long. He already thought of them as such, but hearing him calling it such too was something that he desperately needed.

Mydei and Astraea did carve a place in his heart so quickly that he barely had the time to register it, but he was ready to let their place expand and make sure their presence is even more engraved into his soul.

But telling him anything similar in that moment would have been too heavy. He barely understood what he told him and he was tired. It was far better to accept those words and open up further if he ever asked in the future.

Phainon relaxed his muscles and looked disinterested as he looked up. “But how do I know you mean it…” he hummed, teasing him a little.

Astraea immediately pulled on his shirt lightly, making a cross on his heart with his other hand. “Cross on my heart! Look!”

“Okay, okay,” he laughed, amused. “I believe you, baby.”

The child only let out a little chuckle, genuinely happy about that answer.

Cutest little thing. That child was a bright ray of sunshine in the dull, boring, miserable life he was leading– along with Mydei, of course, but they brought different kind of lights. Astraea’s was bright and white, while Mydei’s was more of a beautiful sunset with all kinds of pink, orange and red hues.

One was shining in the dark, the other was a steady, calming, warm presence. Regardless, they both brought new, wonderful colors to his life that he doubted he would have had the pleasure to even see without them.

His thoughts got abruptly interrupted by Astraea yawning, his head popping back on his shoulder. Phainon laughed softly, planting a kiss between his hair before heading for the bedroom, as the time to put him to bed clearly dawned on them.

Upon crawling on his bed, he noticed Mydei with his eyes slightly open, maybe because he heard him getting into the room. Phainon didn't say anything, instead opting for a soft kiss as a greeting and lying next to him with their son in between them, already fast asleep.

Judging by the way they were both so tired, they probably didn't sleep much the night before, unlike him.

Even then, Phainon didn't mind a little nap next to them. Silently cuddling, watching over them, while they tested and recuperated energy.

Mydei's free arm swung over his head, careful not to hit Astraea, before he could leave a gentle kiss on his shoulder, over his shirt. “Are you happy there?”

It was a sleepy voice, one that Phainon was glad to be the only one able to hear.

With a smile, he leaned over, stealing a more thorough kiss, immediately matched by Mydei.

Everything was in the right place now. Just a few months, and it would be permanent– he just had to wait until then, already bathing in pure bliss.

Was he happy?

He wasn't sure. He didn't really know how happiness felt like yet, but the way his heart beat in that moment was close enough to what he imagined it was.

Phainon smiled, kissing Mydei one last time on his forehead, affectionately and as a way to ensure him a promise.

“I’m right where I want to be.”

Chapter End Notes

There will be just two other chapters and an epilogue to wrap it up and hopefully all of it will be out before next month ^-^ I really hope this was worth the quite long wait and thank you for reading as per usual :]
