chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei reached out with his hand to fix the mess that his hair was in, pleasantly watching his face as it morphed into a confusing expression. “You never had a stable environment to grow up in, nor a stable family, right?”
“Perhaps.”
“You don't have to worry about it anymore.”

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Insomnia wasn’t something that Mydei was familiar with on most days, but there were some nights in which he just could not sleep, no matter how much he tried. During those nights, he found quite refreshing to wake up, careful not to wake up Phainon, grab his boyfriend’s sweater to fend off the imminent cold as soon as he got out of the bed and walk over the window to stare out of it.

It was… relaxing. Not much mattered in that moment, and he could just slow down and feel his heart almost still in front of that sight.

All in all, things were going swiftly and steadily. His arm was healing, the scars from his burns would be permanent, but it was a miracle that he was able to get out of that fire in the first place. He was even able to partly go back to work soon enough, despite everything.

And that family of his was… the usual. Nothing changed. Maybe that was the best news amidst it all.

Astraea helped him, but he didn’t push himself too much, while Phainon started taking leaves and days off more often to be more present at home in the first month or so of his recovery. He always stared at him with those stupid puppy eyes, afraid that any touch would magically break his bones again or put his scars on fire.

He hated it, but the thing he loathed even more than being treated like a piece of precious porcelain that would break if anyone would just brush against it was how worried he made Phainon the night of the accident, and how much of that fear carried over in the last month.

The last thing he wanted was making him worry for no reason and when he already had abandonment issues. He was supposed to help him with it, not make it worse.

“Mydei?”

Phainon’s feeble, hesitant voice made Mydei turn his head towards him, just in time to see him sleepily hug him from behind. He knew that he liked seeing him taking comfort in wearing his sweaters and anything else that smelled like him, as a faint reminder of his presence even when they were apart.

He turned around and left a tender kiss on Phainon’s cheek. “Did I wake you up?” he whispered, as not to wake up Astraea too.

“No, don’t worry.” He wrapped his arms around his waist and rested his chin on his shoulder. “Can’t sleep?”

Mydei inhaled before leaning back against his body, trusting that he would sustain him. It had been so much easier since Astraea’s birthday to get himself lost in his touch specifically. He knew what to expect, Phainon always gave him a couple of seconds to act if he didn’t want his hands on him, he even searched for support from him in that way.

His hand wrapped around the ones on his stomach as he looked at him again, without moving much more than that. Phainon understood almost instantly– he slowly moved his head and trapped his lips in a sweet, quick kiss, then immediately repeated the same action a few times, pushing a little more each time that their lips met.

He was growing impatient and more confident in what they had now, and Mydei couldn’t be happier. All he had to give him was kindness, love and stability, even if he could still feel a little layer of worry. He guessed that it would all dissipate in a few months, when he’s be out of danger and fully reprise his job, away from immediate danger.

The kisses continued, this time with Phainon pressing on. It was obvious he wanted something more than that at the time, but he knew the rules that Mydei put down as soon as they started dating and living together as well: no sex until Astraea was present in the house. It was the only rule that Mydei wouldn’t budge on, and he long abandoned the idea to make him give in to his ideas when he was a tad bit far gone from reason.

Mydei felt his body turning around, unsure if it was him deciding to move or Phainon manhandling him into a more comfortable position for both, until he felt the window against the back of his head. Neither of them stopped catching and searching again the other’s lips, maybe in an attempt of anchoring themselves to something after that hellish month.

All of a sudden, Phainon let out a low whine, and Mydei stopped himself, mere millimeters away from his lips. “There’s something on your mind, I can tell,” he whispered, throat hoarse maybe from having recently woken up and the effort put into those kisses. He dived his head lower, planting affectionate kisses on the base of his neck and accepting the caresses offered on his cheek. “It’s fine if you aren’t ready to tell me, but I’m all ears if you need some help.”

The fact that he noticed was honestly a relief.

He was glad to know that he understood him without the need of him speaking his mind all the time, even if he still misread or didn’t understand certain situations.

As Mydei closed his eyes for a couple of seconds, he felt a couple of quick kisses on his cheek, maybe trying to comfort him enough that he’d feel fine with answering his question. “I thought I would feel worse, but I don’t,” he confessed, letting Phainon gently brush a finger on his lips, catching his attention again. “It’s frustrating more than anything, but even that will fade once I’ll end up getting used to it.”

His boyfriend let out an a breath that sounded like an amused laugh. “And you feel like shit because you aren’t miserable?”

“This feels like something that would change my life, stepping out of what I wished to do for my entire life. At least partly. But I’m not… I don’t care as much as I should.”

“Well… you already almost died. Maybe that's why you don't feel that bad about it.”

He wasn’t wrong, the accident he had as a child did put into perspective how easy it was to die… and the subsequent lack of care he sometimes had in life or death situations. Almost as if it made him desensitized to his own well-being.

Mydei shifted slightly in his place, going on to look at his plastered arm. “Have I ever told you what happened regarding my accident when I was younger?”

“You told me you didn't remember much.”

“I don't, but I recently asked my mother. Apparently, I got involved in a car accident to save a cat. It sounds stupid, but luckily the car wasn't going too fast… I still hit my head against the ground and they rushed me to the hospital.”

There was no recollection of any of this in his head. The last thing he remembered was playing with Hephaestion and then a white flash blinding his vision, only to wake up a few months later to both of his parents hugging him and crying, causing him to shove them away and starting to yell in a panic. If both of them didn’t calm him down immediately, he was sure that he would have started bawling as well.

Phainon, however, was preoccupied with something else.

He moved closer, clearly worried, and asked, “Was it bleeding? Did you have no broken bones? Your skull didn't–”

“Turn off the nurse mode, Phainon.”

“Right,” he sighed, taking a step back, but still close enough for his hands to rest on Mydei’s waist. “What were you saying?”

With a movement of his head towards the ceiling, Mydei recollected what it was that his mother told him a few days prior. “They checked me up, I had a couple of fractured vertebrae and a concussion, but it didn't seem too dangerous. They suspected the coma derived from the trauma, but even they didn't have a certain answer.”

“How long was this coma?”

“A few months.”

“And your father ruined his entire family in just a few months?”

That was the real question, wasn’t it?

His mother never talked about his father too much, maybe because she didn’t want him to get reminded of the fact that they abandoned him, or maybe because it hurt far too greatly to utter a word about him. They had been together for almost fifteen years before they split up, Mydei imagined that it had to be hard for her.

And yet, she didn’t hesitate. She believed that her son’s well-being would have been away from him and she acted on instinct. Because her precious son was more important than herself or the feelings she had for a man that she didn’t recognize anymore.

It was the same reason that drove Mydei himself to adopt Astraea so fast and to put him first so easily– he didn’t have anyone else to sacrifice and he was raised with that same idea. It was how his mother saved him, and he wanted to save that child in the same way.

His father, however, wasn’t evil. He was just a ridiculously, stupidly, embarrassingly weak that refused to admit it and ask for help by his loved ones, and ended up with the wrong people at the wrong time.

“That's what I asked my mother too,” Mydei started to answer. “Apparently, it wasn't the coma that kick-started everything directly. He was worried for me, of course, but that worry inadvertently reflected on his job and he was fired.”

Phainon slightly tilted his head, like a cute, confused puppy. “What kind of job needed him to–”

“Firefighter,” he spat out, without even letting him finish. “My father was a firefighter at the time.”

Silence suddenly filled the air while Phainon got a grasp of the situation. His fingers didn’t move, his breathing didn’t stop or alter, but Mydei could feel the gears in his brain whirring almost uncontrollably, putting every information he knew in the right order now.

Mydei just looked at him, completely available for whatever gesture he could possibly need, as well as questions he wanted to ask. When his mother explained all of it to him, he kept her there for what felt like ages, trying to understand fully the order of the facts.

After what felt like hours of just Phainon staring into the void, Mydei decided to adapt a content smile and slightly tilt his head to the side. “Do you understand why Gnaeus moved me back and why I was scared to end up like him now?”

He took a moment to think further about the situation, genuinely trying to understand both his father’s reasons and his own feelings. Mydei greatly appreciated it. “So… just being fired made him turn into a horrible human being?” he asked, his blue eyes traveling back to his boyfriend’s face.

“No, not at first. My mother said he was just devastated, but he still did his utmost to find a new job, pay everything, look over me when she couldn't,” Mydei explained calmly. “Everything started to fall apart when he started hanging out with despicable individuals that filled his head with nonsense.”

At this point, he didn’t even know whose fault all that mess was.

Was it his father’s for believing them? Was it these people clearly targeting a man at his lowest to fool him or get something out of him? How did he live his last moments, knowing that he and his mother would never come back?

His mother told him that he sent letters after starting proper therapy and he was recuperating, but that apparently wasn’t enough. He still died, for a reason or another. She never opened all the letters and she categorically refused to show them to him, citing personal reasons and not ruining the little respect and love he still had for that man.

Maybe it was for the best.

He trusted his mother, but he hoped that it wouldn’t have come to this.

With a heavy sigh, he completed the short story that he did know. “They told him that finding a new job was useless, that the doctors were lying to him, that the superior that fired him was complicit in some kind of conspiracy. My father has always been soft-willed, so much that my mother called him weak quite often, albeit in an affectionate way.”

“So he just… started treating you badly?” Phainon asked, stepping closer. Maybe he felt the need to comfort him while he talked, or maybe he notices how lost in his head he was starting to get as he remembered those times. Either way, he appreciated the gesture.

Mydei controlled his breathing more cautiously, knowing he was about to step in his own feelings and he didn’t want Phainon to get worried further. “When I woke up, he was happy at first. It didn't look like he changed much either. Then, he was absent from home more often, came back drunk, yelled more often. When he almost hit me, my mother and I left with no notice. The next time I saw him, he lied dead in a coffin.”

His voice was controlled, calm, almost monotone. He still whispered, but there was no crack, no breath hitching, no hint of maliciousness. It was as if he was explaining something in an extremely encyclopedic way.

However, Phainon didn’t move, unless it was to gently grab his hand or nuzzle his nose along the side of his neck and leaving a sweet kiss on its base. He enjoyed it, and it almost made him forget all those years he spent loathing and being terrified of what his father represented in his head.

Almost, but it was enough for him to wrap up his thoughts.

“It felt like someone took my father away from me and placed some other person with his face, his voice and his mannerisms as a part of some sick joke,” he finally spat out, a sentence that always lied in the back of his mind taking shape only in Phainon’s presence.

He hugged him and offered him a shoulder to lean on, probably understanding how hard it was for him to even just mutter that phrase.

Mydei buried his face in the crook of his neck, allowing himself to accept that hug and those offerings of affection, feeling his heartbeat, initially drumming incessantly against his ribcage, slow down to an acceptable pace again. He brushed his face in that comfortable heat, feeling the sudden, gentle caress between his golden locks making itself more insistent.

Maybe a few months ago he would have slapped it away, but, for the moment, he simply let it exist, alongside everything else.

“I’m sorry, Mydei,” came Phainon’s soft whispers, full of promises and apologies that he knew were sincere. “But now I can say with certainty that you're not like your father. Not one bit.”

With a sigh, he straightened his back and leaned against the wall, refusing to let go of Phainon’s shoulder with the only hand he had at disposal. “I don't completely hate him. I just… I don't want Astraea to go through what I did,” he answered, voice calm and rather relaxed.

Another sweet, feather-like kiss made its way below his jaw, then another couple on his cheeks, a little more strongly pushing on his skin. A soft, quick giggle left Mydei’s lips at the repeated gestures of affection, and Phainon caught the opportunity to ask for a proper kiss, soft and tender, almost as if it had to show his complete devotion with that action alone.

Mydei felt his entire body melt the moment their lips touched– and even more when Phainon gently caressed his cheek with his hand. They raced each other’s lips around for a couple of minutes, maybe a little too slow for the kind of kiss that it was gearing up to be, until his boyfriend let go, only slowly brushing his forehead against his own.

“And he won't go through it,” he whispered, “because I know that you would rather throw yourself in a fire, rather than condemning a child to a life of loneliness and fear.”

Quite literally.

Mydei laughed softly and leaned his head against the window again, letting Phainon snatch a few more kisses along his neck. He was well aware that he liked to kiss him there after a couple of times trying to explore what they actually enjoyed doing together, specifically because he was a little ticklish, so it was a fire-sure way to see and hear him giggle and laugh.

And Phainon knew that he would let him, no matter how horrible he was feeling– because he was trying so desperately to make him feel better, and he didn’t have it in him to avoid leaning on him whenever he offered it.

“Now that we're talking about traumatic childhoods, do you want to share a bit of yours?” Mydei asked, almost backed up to sit on the window if they just opened it. He only decided against it because he wasn’t entirely sure that his boyfriend would be able to restrain himself enough to avoid a fall or anything along those lines.

His head tilted against the ceiling as a pout formed on his face, unsure of what to answer. “Not much to say… our parents died when we were children and we bounced back and forth between different foster families. Never settled in a place, never had friends until university, always had to watch my sister work since she was a child to protect me and grant me a gentler future.”

Amber eyes softened at the mention of Cyrene working so hard for him. He could tell she was a hard-worker and she loved his little brother very much, but it was still admirable that she easily discarded herself for Phainon’s well-being. He knew it was something that happened since their first date, but he would have had to thank her immensely the next time he saw her.

“That puts a lot of context to you.” Mydei reached out with his hand to fix the mess that his hair was in, pleasantly watching his face as it morphed into a confusing expression. “You're afraid of being abandoned, you reflect your bad thoughts on yourself, you get defensive quite often, you made up a fake mask to move through life… it makes sense now. You never had a stable environment to grow up in, nor a stable family, right?”

“Perhaps.”

“You don't have to worry about it anymore.”

Mydei was determined to make sure that statement would be valid for as long as Phainon let him. He could tell he wanted to belong somewhere, and he was dead set on drilling into his head that he did already.

Astraea loved him. Mydei loved him. They both saw him as family already. All he wanted was for him to accept it.

Phainon stared at him for a few seconds, trying to understand properly what he told him, before making the cutest smile Mydei had ever seen– not big or bright, just similar to a child happy that he got a lollipop on the way home. Flushed cheeks, cheeky smile, content eyes. Adorable.

“I thought this would have been much harder,” he commented, still half laughing.

“It’s not,” Mydei whispered, taking it as his sign to step forward and wrap his arm around Phainon waist, leaving a little bite on the side of his neck. “You just took forever how much you’re wanted here.”

“I get it! I get it, Mydei,” he yelped, not expecting that kind of gesture. It wasn’t the first time they did it, but he didn’t expect so much motion when it was so late and after they bathed in each other’s presence so lazily and slowly.

Mydei could honestly do it every single day.

He liked how domestic and slow his life turned out to be since they moved in together, especially since they had to yet officially do so. They just fit together– both of them were willing to change enough for the other to feel comfortable about something that bothered him, and take their time on other things that they liked doing.

It was nice.

More than that, it was easy to slip into the routine. Now, every time he had to go out he counted down the people he had to kiss goodbye, and hug again when he came back.

That was something that he wasn’t willing to trade with anything else, no matter how precious it was. It would have been nothing like this.

“Daddy?”

Astraea’s voice resounded in the room, loud and clear, although sleepy. It was quite close, but Mydei couldn’t look at him until he stepped closer, hugging him with his little hands grabbing both sides of his shirt. He was getting taller, but he doubted he would ever stop running towards him like that.

Phainon smiled and crouched down, affectionately ruffling his hair. “Hey, honey,” he whispered, gaining a hug as well. Even if there was still a clear preference for Mydei, both of them were good options for him whenever he wanted to ask anything, and he did it quite often now.

Maybe Phainon truly came through his head, with how attached to him Astraea became and how far more cheerful and child-like he had been since their trip to the hospital. He would have had to ask.

“I'm hot,” the child whined. “It's too hot.”

Mydei stepped closer, getting down to his level. When he saw Astraea turn around, he noticed just how flushed his face was. “Come here, let me check,” he whispered, extending a hand.

“Check what?”

“Your temperature. I can see how hot you are from here, baby, no need to convince me or Papa.”

Astraea moved closer, letting Mydei move his bangs away and rest his hand on his forehead, then his lips. It was warm, but it seemed to be a normal warm temperature with no kind of illness or flu in sight. However, that wasn’t what caught his attention.

“He’s sweaty,” he whispers, looking up to Phainon, hopeful. “I doubt it’s a flu, but what do you think?”

“Mh… he’s probably just hot, Mydei.” Phainon smiled, trying to reassure him as much as possible. It wasn’t something dangerous, worrying uselessly wasn’t going to do any of them any good—especially given the hour. “The season is changing, he probably just need a clothing change and lighter sheets.”

It made sense, since summer was coming again.

Last year around this time, he adopted Astraea too, if he remembered correctly. It was towards the end of it, but it had almost been a year already, and he couldn’t believe how much of a turn he experienced in his life since then: first Astraea, then Phainon and now they basically lived together as a family like any other would.

It wasn’t something that he expected to experience any time soon, but it was easy with the people in his life now, both the ones that he already knew and the ones that he met in the past year. Especially Phainon.

The child suddenly pulled his shirt, trying to catch his attention again, pleading eyes asking for something that he wasn’t aware of just yet. With a slight whine, he whispered a tiny, “Daddy…”

Mydei immediately hurried to raise his fringe up, before turning to Phainon again. “Can you keep his hair up?”

He nodded as he kneeled down, gathering his long hair in some kind of bun and keeping it against his head with no force put into it. He just rested it against his head, just enough to let him feel something along his neck.

“Is this any better?” Mydei asked, smiling down at him. Maybe it wasn’t the best they could do at the moment, but they never cut his hair and now it was too voluminous and too long to keep it as it was.

Astraea nodded weakly, evidently tired out of his mind. Phainon noticed it too, moving his head to check the hour on the clock on the wall and lightly brushing his hand on his shoulder. “A little…”

He was right, then. Just the season getting warmer, nothing else.

“It’s just summer coming,” Phainon repeated his thoughts, offering a sweet, calm voice for Astraea too. The child raised his head to look at the man behind him, probably not wanting to move from that position because he knew of the weight that he was keeping up against his head. “How about we change your pajamas and think about cutting your hair?”

“Can I have it like yours?”

“Why?”

“I look a lot like Dad… not like you. I wanna look like you too, Papa.”

Mydei couldn’t help the soft smile appearing on his face. He knew that Astraea and Phainon bonded quickly in the last few months, especially since they put the idea of living together on the table, but he didn’t believe he would make such a request so soon.

Normally, when they’d walk around, strangers would tell Mydei how much his son resembles him, but no one says anything regarding Phainon, even if he was clearly his parent as well. He knew that it was just a matter of others assuming that Mydei’s girlfriend or wife passing away or leaving him with their child, but he noticed pretty soon that Astraea liked it. Letting himself think that people talked about Mydei as his actual father was something that always made him smile, maybe for his background or maybe for something else that he wasn’t ready to share with him yet.

He wondered how he felt whenever so many asked Phainon if he was babysitting, or if he looked much more like his mother whenever Mydei wasn’t out with them—he knew that his boyfriend wasn’t too happy with it, but he never said anything to Astraea. They were just confessions before going to bed or when Astraea was napping or spending time with the triplets.

So this was something that their child wanted for himself. He wanted to look like both now, and not just like one of them.

“Okay,” Mydei sighed, looking at Phainon. “Can you cut it?”

Phainon nodded with a smile. “Yeah, don’t worry.” He stood up with him, planting a kiss on his cheek. “Go to sleep.”

He really should. He was tired, he knew that he had to rest a little more now that it took more strength and energy out of him to move and do generally anything that he did more easily before. Even if it was frustrating at first, he had always accepted Phainon’s help and cutting Astraea’s hair like his wasn’t different.

There was something more pressing that he was worried about, however.

He shifted his gaze to look at his child with a soft, warm, gentle expression. “That's a lot of hair gone, are you sure?”

“I wanna be like Papa…” Astraea whined, convincing enough for Mydei to concede him his faith. “He's never ever hot and his hair is really pretty and soft and it looks like a fluffy cloud.”

“Okay, like Papa it is. Be good and do whatever Papa says, okay?”

“Okay! Night, Daddy!”

He waved at him, before insistently pulling on Phainon’s sleeve, dragging him away. Mydei giggled, amused by how easily that little kid pulled along a man as built and tall as his father—even if he most likely gave into Astraea’s little request out of excitement.

All in all, perhaps Phainon looked cheery and extroverted most of the time and, to his defense, he actually was, but he kept his most precious feelings and desires close to his chest, hardly expressing it at all, even to Mydei. Unfortunately for him, though, he learned how to read him properly now, and he could say with full certainty that he was over the moon knowing that Astraea wanted to look more like him.

Well, it was better to leave them alone. Phainon would be able to take care of it and he could sleep.

Honestly, if he thought about it now, he had no idea how he could be able to take care of Astraea as comfortably as he did without Phainon’s aid. The money was more than enough now and Mydei could comfortably rest, leaving his child in capable and trusted hands. Especially now that he needed more rest than usual, it was nice knowing that Astraea was getting taken care of properly while he could sleep peacefully.

And those days made him way more tired and prone to taking a nap—which just made him even more tired. The fact that he woke up suddenly in the middle of the night just made it worse.

Closing his eyes wasn’t hard at all as soon as his back hit the mattress of the empty bed, instantly falling asleep without a single issue. No time to even think about w hard it was, how many giggles he heard coming from the bathroom, how cold the bed was without Phainon. He was too tired for any of it.

Unfortunately, that little nap was short-lived.

Maybe half an hour later, something landed next to him and shook his shoulder lightly, tiny pleas resounding next to his ear: “Dad, dad, dad…”

Mydei smiled, weakly opening his eyes. “Hey, honeybuns,” he whispered, still not completely able to process properly who sat right in front of him.

It wasn’t rare for him to wake up either out of worry for him or because he had nightmares or simply wanted to sleep with him. It was rare now, but he still got used himself to it—there was no malice in it, he was just a scared child looking for safety and comfort, he couldn’t be mad at him even if he did wake him up in moments like that.

He squeezed his eyes to wake himself up properly and look at him, but he felt him throw himself in his arms while he was still trying to get his brain to work. He caught him, of course, but he didn't expect him to fall down like that so suddenly.

“Sorry I woke you up, Daddy,” Astraea said, voice muffled against Mydei’s shirt. “I was excited…”

His hand instinctively went to caress his child's hair, sensing something was wrong. “I know. I'm not angry at you, let me see what Phainon did.”

“Papa said not to wake you up…”

“He isn't mad at you either.”

“What if he is?”

It was a legitimate question and, unfortunately, Mydei already thought of the answer. He loved Phainon with all his heart, but so did his mother with his father, and tragedy still caught up to them.

He didn't want them to suffer that same fate. He wanted Astraea to live happily and healthily, surrounded by love and affection. However, if Phainon ever harmed him, he was well aware of the decision that Mydei would take. His mother did it once already, he wasn't scared to repeat it, if it meant keeping his child safe.

“Then I'll save you,” Mydei answered. “Papa is here just because he showed me that he cares and loves you, Astraea. If he ever shows the contrary, it's you and me against the world. Okay?”

Astraea finally raised his head to look at him, red eyes and tears running down his cheeks. Poor child. He truly loved Phainon so much now, the thought of being hurt by him for any reason was probably unbearable.

Mydei kindly wiped them out, but that just made things worse.

Astraea loudly sobbed, hot tears running down faster than before, and Mydei instinctively hugged him, letting him move in any way he wanted. He didn't mind kicks, pulling and pushing with his hands or shaking his head. It hurt seeing him so desperate.

Maybe it was too soon. Maybe he was just tired. Or, maybe, he was just far too cruel.

“I don't wanna leave Papa,” Astraea sobbed, pulling on his shirt.

“Me neither, and he won't do anything to put you in danger.” Mydei caressed his hair, watching as his child looked at him again with lucid eyes and tears gracefully sliding down his cheeks. “But, if anything happens between us, I want you to know that you're my priority. Not Phainon. You. I’m not going to leave you. Ever.”

The little kid nodded, seemingly understanding what he was trying to say. “Promise?”

“Promise,” he repeated, bopping his nose. A tiny laugh resounded in the room, finally replacing the little sobs that his father inadvertently started, and the child hugged him and buried his face in his chest again, accepting a few caresses on his hair. Mydei’s happy expression fell, thinking about what he said and his kid’s reaction. “I’m sorry for talking about something like this now, but you don’t have to worry for being excited about something. You light up my and Phainon’s day whenever you smile, we’re never going to get mad at you for this.”

Astraea slowly sat up and tilted his head, maybe worried that he mistook what Mydei said earlier. “So Papa can stay?” he asked, with a voice more curious than afraid.

“Of course he can,” Mydei laughed. “That’s not what I said, and I think you know what I meant.”

“I don’t wanna see Papa be a bad person.”

“Mhm, I’ll bring him back to reason. Don’t worry, leaving is just the most desperate measure.”

He honestly didn’t believe Phainon would ever touch a hair on that little child’s head, but, then again, his mother thought the same of his father. She thought that she could bring him back too, and yet there they were—Mydei grew up without his father past the age of ten years old and that same man put other things above his family.

The only reason why he grew up as well as he did was thanks to his mother’s promptly taking both of them out of his father’s reach and, if things ever led there, Mydei would have done whatever it took to protect his child and bring him to safety.

His child suddenly fell down on the mattress again, looking at the ceiling in the dark room, only lit up from the dim light coming from outside the door. With a sigh, he commented, “I really hope Papa won’t be so stupid…”

Mydei let out a soft laugh. “He’s strong and intelligent, right? We’re just talking hypotheticals here.”

“Hypo… what?”

“Hypotheticals. It’s something that may happen, but there’s no indication of it actually happening.”

“Ah… so we’re not leaving?”

All in all, he was taking it quite well after Mydei explained it properly to him. He knew that he couldn’t force someone else to treat him well and that leaving them might make his life much better even if he loved them—which was what happened when he took him in. He perfectly knew that staying in a violent house wasn’t nice and, as much as he feared abandonment and how much he loved Phainon, he adored Mydei. He probably saw him as some sort of savior, given just how attached he was, and he blindly trusted his judgment.

If Mydei thought that Phainon was hurting him and properly explained it to him, he would probably follow him.

Then again, it wasn’t happening now and Mydei didn’t want it to happen at all.

“It’s just something to let you know that we both love you too much to get mad at you for being happy about something, even if you do wake us up in the middle of the night,” Mydei explained further. “And if one of us does get mad at you for some reason, the other will get you to safety. You’ve always been my priority, baby. It’s something I told Phainon as well, he knows his place here.”

It was true. The first reason why they took a while to get together despite the instant spark of interest for each other was because Mydei wanted to be sure that Phainon would treat his son well and that he knew that, in extreme cases, Astraea came first. He agreed to those terms, and now Astraea had a second father, a new home and newfound happiness, but those same conditions wouldn’t have expired anyway. If Phainon put him in danger, he would face the consequences.

“Okay,” Astraea quietly agreed, before smiling at him. “Thank you, Daddy.”

Mydei smiled back at him. “Do you want to show me how you look now?”

Just as he said those words, the child jumped back on his seat, all excited and extremely happy they went back to that topic. “How is it?” he asked, with a huge smile on his face.

He hummed as he observed his hair again, mentally thanking Phainon for knowing how to exactly replicate his hairstyle, even with slight tweaks upon the child’s request. After all, Cyrene was his older sister and she probably taught him how to both take care of his hair and how to style hers—and both were pretty complicated, if he didn’t know what he had to do, especially his sister’s.

He always discovered something new about him.

The back of his finger grazed against the side braid that Phainon left him with, probably the only difference from his own hair, pinned with a cute, bright red pin with a ribbon attached of a slightly darker shade of the same color—probably something to keep to still resemble Mydei. Now the way his hair parted made sure that blonde locks fell on a side of his face, just making him look even more adorable. Just like a curious little bunny.

“You’re really pretty,” Mydei finally said, with a soft smile on his face. “You look like Papa more now, don’t you think?”

Astraea energetically nodded, obviously excited about the prospect that now people might call him the son of both because he looked like both. It was clear he liked it, and it only filled Mydei’s heart with happiness and pride for what both he and Phainon were able to do, despite the difficult circumstances.

“Do we tell him he did a good job?” he hummed, putting there the possibility to be excited about it a little longer to make up for the sense of guilt from earlier and taking the opportunity to tease his boyfriend a little bit.

They were all tired, but he was sure that seeing a bit of a flustered face on Phainon would make his mood even better.

As if that statement awoken something in Astraea, he jumped up and ran across the bed, easily jumping off of it and landing safely on the floor, right before running to Phainon. Mydei laughed, partly endeared by it and partly anticipating the chaos that was about about to unfold, which he was fully intending on witnessing.

With a slow push he sat up, taking a moment to communicate to his very tired brain what he was going to do. He didn’t wait too much for an answer, using his only free arm to sustain himself in the first few seconds upon walking. He heard the excited sounds coming from Astraea, immediately followed by sweet, indulging questions from Phainon that calmly warmed his heart, even if he didn’t entirely understand what he was saying.

“He’s still awake?”

Somehow he understood that as he walked closer, and the mild worry in his boyfriend’s voice didn’t get past him. He laughed about it for a few seconds, until Astraea chimed in for him.

“He wasn’t!” he said, puffing his chest as if he was proud of waking him up. “But he's not mad! And he said you aren’t mad too!”

A light, soft giggle escaped his lips, more than just amused at just how the child was retelling their conversation. He knew well enough to leave out the abandoning Phainon in case something bad enough happened part, but, for the rest, the meaning of what he told him was kept and repeated, albeit in an extremely funny way.

“Isn’t our child just so pretty?” Mydei said, well aware of the fact that Phainon was looking at him now. “You took care of it perfectly, Phainon, his looks could rival the ones of a prince.”

He knew what his praises did to him. It wasn’t being horny or embarrassed, more-so like a shot of serotonin directly into his veins and he would become clingy and ask for cuddles for the next two hours, just like a big puppy after giving him a little prize after he did something good.

Mydei was still unsure whether or not it was the fact that he referred to Astraea as their child—and his little requests of having a child with him were nothing secret, he noticed a long time ago that he got excited every time Mydei would mention him being Astraea’s father—or if he praised him for doing a good job.

Even in that moment, he stepped towards him, eyes fixed on his face, and he crashed their lips together. That gesture wasn’t unexpected, but Mydei was far from being able to sustain a movement so sudden and so full of strength without falling. Luckily, Phainon wasn’t completely gone and kept him up by sustaining him from his back as he kept on kissing him.

He didn’t know when he pulled back, but he hoped that his son didn’t see too much of it. Not that he hated seeing them kiss or be in love, he had always been their first supporter, but he was a child that tended to get disgusted over adults kissing, especially when it was exceptionally late.

His eyes traveled to his position, but all he could see was him tilting his head and looking confused over the entire ruse. “What’s so special about it?” he asked, golden locks falling in front of his eyes. “I’ve always been your child too, Papa. Since… that time Hephaestion came over!”

Funnily enough, that didn’t narrow it down at all. Hephaestion came often in the last few months, some times just came over to chat with them prior to Mydei’s accident and even came before they were together. His visits should be last meter that Astraea should use.

“Was I present?” Mydei asked then, trying to aid him.

He nodded excitedly. “Yeah! He had a book he had to give back to you, I think…”

Both of them fell into a religious silent, staring at their kid. That was maybe the second time they went out, neither of them even knew how far that was going to go– and Astraea was already convinced that Phainon was going to be his father? It couldn’t be. It was impossible, he was thinking of some other time.

Sure, he had always liked Phainon, he was the second person besides Mydei that he trusted almost right away, but from that to wanting to live with him and be his son there was an ocean and a half in between.

“Astraea, that’s almost a full year ago,” Phainon mentioned, maybe as lost as Mydei was.

Astraea pondered on it for a couple of seconds. “You took a while.” He smiled at the both of them, probably with the biggest, most honest smile he had ever shown them. “But I wanted Phai from the start! I didn’t want anyone else!”

Phainon, on his part, only let out an amused laugh. “Thank you, Astraea! I’m glad to be here now.”

The child ran over to him, as he instinctively crouched down and welcomed him in his arms. Mydei watched with a soft smile on his face, leaning against the wall for support.

“I love you!” Astraea beamed, happier than either of them had ever seen him.

“I love you too, baby,” Phainon answered, ruffling his hair. “But it's late. Really late. And you're tired, right?”

He nodded slowly, as if those words suddenly reminded him what his body needed now. If he woke up, however, there had to be another problem besides how warm his bed was, and Mydei keenly suspected nightmares.

Getting him a plushie did help a lot, but nightmares weren't something just a fluffy stuffed animal could solve, especially for someone who lived through a never-ending nightmare for years.

Regardless, all they could do was lighten the weight that he carried and sustaining him however they could. Nothing more and nothing less.

“Daddy…” he whined, before walking toward him, landing with an exhausted thud of his head against his leg.

With a smile, Mydei picked him up, letting him rest on his functioning shoulder. “Still hot?” he asked, only moving forward when he felt his head nodding on his shoulder. “Let’s try changing your covers, okay? And take off those socks too, they do a lot here.”

He nodded, already half asleep. “‘Kay.”

As if he saw a sign telling him it was time to move, Phainon quickly walked to Astraea’s room, doing exactly what Mydei said. He genuinely didn’t believe they would have ended up like his parents, he made sure of it, but he was more and more convinced every day that passed. What he said earlier was mostly to reassure their child, but he was sure that, luckily, there wouldn’t be any need for it.

Phainon was so dedicated to him and his happiness, his tranquility that he highly doubted he would be able to purposefully hurt either of them.

Mydei followed his boyfriend, walking in the room upon him finishing to silently change his bed. Despite how chatty he normally was, he noticed how quiet he could get when there was something serious or when he was tired., only focusing his energy on the task at hand. After all, he used to work night shifts, he was used to work at this hour and to focus properly on different tasks even when his brain was slowly shutting down.

These weren’t too difficult at least, so Mydei quickly thanked how prone he was to overworking at night and placed Astraea on his newly changed bed, then took off his socks and tucked him in. “Better?” he asked, gently caressing his head.

“Dad…” he whispered instead, offering a tired smile. “I’m really, really happy now. Thank you…”

A light, breathy laugh escaped from his lips, endeared by how often he seemed to repeat that to him. He knew it already, but he still let him say it, just in case he kept it in for a little too long or he needed it.

He heard a few sobs coming from him, but he doubted it was anything serious, more akin to overflowing happiness and gratefulness rather than any kind of sadness.

“Hey,” Phainon whispered, hurrying at Mydei’s side, eyes focused on the child. “Everything is fine, right? We’re all here. No one is going anywhere.”

Mydei smiled, warmed by just how much he took the reigns of the situation after he realized how tired both he and Astraea were. “Papa’s right,” he added. “You won’t lose this, I promise. We won’t switch you out, we won’t leave you, all this won’t disappear. You will wake up every single morning and you will find me and Papa right here.”

The child looked a little shy after that reassurance, but he still nodded weakly, hugging tightly his plushie until he could hide part of his face. Mydei looked at it for a second, putting in the back of his mind a note about having to wash it at some point, given how much he used that little cat-like stuffed creature.

“Come on, hug Fig Stew and off to bed.” Phainon stood up, giving him one last smile. “It’s way past your bed time and you need to go listen to that book reading at the library tomorrow, right?”

Astraea nodded, but he still turned his head toward Mydei with a questioning stare. “Can I sleep with you?”

“If you can’t sleep, yes,” he answered, without the strength to completely refuse that request. “But try first, okay?”

He didn’t look like he was in the mood to do any of it, probably due to that nightmare that Mydei had already suspected. However, he would like him to try and fall asleep on his own and with the tools that they gave him.

“Do you want some fairies’ nectar?” Phainon hummed, offering yet another way to help him.

A smile finally made its way on his face, excitedly nodding. “A spell too.”

“Nectar and spell on the way.”

Phainon left the room, ready to fulfill that request. Even if Mydei doubted it was anything more than sending him off to sleep with a peaceful mind and subsequently letting them go to rest as well for what remained of the night.

The covers beside him shifted for a second, revealing Astraea sitting up while he looked at his stuffed friend, without saying a word. His brain was probably chaotic at this time of the night, focusing on something might simply help him stay awake enough to drink the chamomile that his father was preparing for him.

Mydei’s hand instead traveled to his son’s hair, lightly caressing it. “How does it feel?” he asked, maybe correctly guessing what was swarming in his mind in that moment.

“Weird,” he answered, after a moment of thinking about the question. “But lighter. And…”

He tilted his head. “And?”

“It’s your gift. Your and Papa.”

“Do you want to talk about it?”

“It’s… I wanna be your son. Not the son of the parents I had before. They never cut my hair, or changed my bed when I was hot, or made me nectar. I wanna be… more like this.”

How cute. They picked up a really cute and intelligent boy.

Mydei had never pushed him to ever recognize him and Phainon as parents above his biological ones, even if it was easy to understand why the little child would prefer his current situation to what he had to go through in the past. Regardless, looking like them and calling them the way he did was his decision and his alone– all that Mydei did and had the intention to do was be his parent in the most fitting way he could. Everything else was in Astraea’s hands, whether either of them liked it or not.

“You’re the only one getting to choose that.” He moved the bangs in front of his hair, flopping right back to that position. “If you want to be like me and Papa, we’ll be more than happy, and if you want to be more like your other parents that’s okay too.”

He nodded, more confident in himself. “I wanna be pretty like Auntie Cassie and Auntie Reney.”

“And you will be. You already are.”

“And strong like you and Papa! So I can help more. Not now, but…”

“With time, baby, I’m sure you will be all of that. You’re strong and intelligent, you will be able to reach those goals.”

Astraea nodded again, a little on edge, but Mydei understood that he genuinely believed in what he was saying and hearing from him. It was probably just a little too much for the hour.

“Does it hurt?” the child then asked, before turning his head toward him. “You’re a bit different with them on now, but do they hurt?”

Ah. He meant the burn scars.

They didn’t, but he was mostly unaware of the way he looked like now and he would often look confused by the different way people would look at him. Some had pity, others disgust, a few fear, but he always had to think about it and reach that conclusion a few minutes later.

It was probably just a matter of getting used to it, but it was a bit of an obstacle at the moment.

“Nothing hurts now,” he answered with a smile, letting him touch a couple of them. “And I’ll be able to use my arm again in one or two months anyway.”

Astraea smiled as soon as he got reminded of it, visibly happy about knowing that, after all, his father was nursing himself back to health at a much faster pace than he thought. Then, an inevitable yawn came, prompting an annoyed whine that swiftly followed it.

Mydei huffed in an amused tone, finding cute just how frustrated he was about wanting to fall asleep, but thinking about Phainon currently finishing to prepare something to help him sleep peacefully.

His hand moved to boop the tip of the child’s nose with his knuckles, affectionately and softly. “You’re tired, I told you.”

He nodded slowly, his head already dropping rhythmically, unable to keep himself awake. Each time he felt himself slip away, however, he woke himself up, rubbing his eyes to do the most he could to resist for a few more minutes.

“Nectar on the way!”

Phainon’s voice bolted him awake, suddenly attentive about his surroundings. With a quick motion he grabbed the mug with chamomile in it and drank it happily, smiling and with his cheeks tinted of a pleasing darker shade. It was slight, but Mydei noticed his legs moving in happiness as he drank it as well.

Both of the adults waited patiently until Astraea handed the mug back to Phainon, looking even more tired than before.

“Off to bed, come on,” Phainon suggested as Mydei tucked him in again. “The fairies want to talk to you again, you’ve made them wait for a while today.”

“Night…”

They watched as he closed his eyes with his plushie held tight in his chest, then they slowly walked away, switched off the light and closed the door enough for the light not to breach into the room.

“I didn’t think he would ever go to bed today…” Phainon commented, visibly exhausted.

Mydei kept up the pace to reach their room, thinking back to what happened after Astraea woke him up again. He bit his lower lip. “It might be partly my fault.”

“How come?” he asked, with a voice that sounded a middle way between curiosity and tiredness.

“When he came to show me his new hair, he was scared that either of us would make him feel unwanted for being excited and I told him that if something ever happened between us, I would have chosen him.”

“You don’t have to make a choice.”

“It was an hypothetical, extreme situation.” He huffed, leaning against the closed door of their room and looking right at his boyfriend. Before speaking again, he made sure to keep his tone understanding and soft. “I have to keep it in the back of my mind, Phainon. Don’t give me a tangible, valid reason to fear for the well-being of our child and I won’t step away from you.”

Instead of the reaction he expected, however– a rebuttal or further questioning– Phainon looked at him with satisfaction and happiness, almost like a puppy who just received a snack after behaving well.

Mydei took a couple of seconds before understanding what was the issue. “Phainon… how many times have I said that it’s your child as well now?”

It was endearing, really, but his expression never ceased being hilarious. He liked it so much that Mydei had started to question whether or not he had some sort of kink around it or if he genuinely liked Astraea to that extent– he had always had it, but he thought that it disappeared after they got to live together for months. Now he wasn’t sure if he would ever grow past it.

“It’s still nice to hear!” he exclaimed. “And if I ever hurt you or Astraea, I’d prefer to be beat to a pulp until I go back to my senses.”

He snorted out a tiny laugh. “That’s also a possibility. But he got sad at the idea of leaving you, he started crying… After explaining what I meant to say a little better, he calmed down, but I doubt it completely left his head.”

“I think you did the right thing, actually. He’s always feared abandonment, it’s nice to know someone would go to that length for him.”

“And you would know.”

“I’m an expert in the fear of abandonment department, you can absolutely trust me.”

He did, honestly. He never thought he couldn’t trust him with anything, including taking care of Astraea and understanding the feelings that Mydei couldn’t grasp as well.

His fingers held his chin in place, planting a kiss on his cheek. “Let’s sleep.”

With a light nod and a yawn, Phainon nodded, following him into the room. Luckily, they still had the clothes from earlier that night and they didn’t have to change them, but Mydei felt forced to take off the jacket that he took earlier when he first woke up. He liked the smell, but he knew that it would have been difficult to keep it with the braced arm too, so he put it down after he reluctantly took it off.

“Mydei…”

At the whine, Mydei rolled into bed almost on instinct to offer a hug or heat to his partner, but Phainon crawled on top of him instead as soon as he saw him lying down.

Mydei could just let out an exhausted whine. “I’m sorry,” he warned, resting his hand on his shirt, at the height of his chest. “Really, Phainon, I’m too tired for this, but I swear we’ll do it when my arm can move safely again.”

And when we talk more seriously about how we want to do this, he added in his brain. It wasn’t lost on him just how often lately Phainon had tried to ask him for a more intimate time, but it had been hard to say yes, both for his physical condition and for the fact that it was rare for them to be able to drop off Astraea some place else to indulge in more… adult activities.

Phainon, however, never insisted, and often he was fine with cuddles or quality time together. Mydei doubted he didn’t at least got himself off on his own, but he was glad that he was respecting his requests, despite the continuous rejections.

He honestly wanted to have that with him too, but, as a matter of fact, they couldn’t do anything surrounding that sphere at the moment. They never even talked about it, he didn’t know what position he preferred or what would make him happy in that scenario. He was going to, but not now. Not when their circumstances were less than favorable for something like that.

Above all, he wanted both of them to enjoy it and he knew for a fact that he himself would be too tired to even think about being pleasured or pleasing him in that way.

As if his instinct wasn’t enough to tell him that Phainon was being difficult over it because he wanted to fuck after almost a year of relationship, he looked at him as if there was no particular issue at hand. After all, Mydei only ever thought of his reasons, he never openly shared them. “You can just prettily lay there?” Phainon asked in a low whine, trying to reassure him and convince him a little.

Mydei couldn’t even blame him. He didn’t know why Mydei kept refusing it or if he was the problem, so of course he would ask for clarifications or offer him a more comfortable way to do it instead.

His hand closed itself in a punch and lightly knocked on his chest, playing with that movement to both keep his attention and avoid his own brain from shutting down. “That’s not the problem. I need to move more and I tend to get more tired if I have to avoid moving my arm. And sleeping with this isn’t ideal either, so I have trouble sleeping too. Wait a couple of months and you will get what you want. I made up my mind anyway.”

“You made up your mind on what?” Phainon asked as he rolled over, lying down incredibly close to him.

It was better now. More cuddles, closer kisses, the possibility of lulling each other to sleep was more achievable.

A soft laugh escaped his lips. “On ending up fucking with the right person for my child to call his father.”

Hopefully it was clear enough. Phainon had nothing to worry about, Mydei fully intended on crossing that line eventually– hopefully in no more than two months, or he would start making unwise decisions too.

Phainon hummed, a question bolting in his mind. “What if… you were with–”

“Hephaestion sucks with children,” Mydei laughed, thinking back to some of the time that he did try to converse with some of them. “They’re all scared of him and he has no idea how to talk to them.”

“That explains it…”

“He’ll settle for a dog maybe. A couple of cats.”

“You’re so mean.”

“Cry me a river. You two ganged up on me for months.”

“It’s fun to pick up on you!”

A finger poked Mydei’s side, and received a little, playful push in response. “Do you want to sleep here or do I send you to sleep on the couch?” he asked with a serious tone, but he knew that Phainon would gather enough from it to understand that he was joking.

“Sorry!” he immediately apologized, before he hugged him a little closer. “Sorry, Mydei. Yes, please, I would like to sleep here.”

Mydei smiled, accepting that position, warm and comfortable enough for him to feel the exhaustion come back instantly. He fell asleep in seconds, listening to the soft, relaxed breathing next to him and letting that warmth envelop him. He could only formulate a tiny thought with no follow-up before sleep could take him, a confession that had been ever present in all the moments he shared with Phainon.

I love you.

Chapter End Notes

I intend on pushing out the last two chapters over the next two weeks, you can expect this amount of words for those as well and treat them as epilogues for both Phainon and Mydei ^^ Huge thank you to the people still sticking with this fic as well, I hope you will enjoy this as well !!

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

With a push of his feet, Mydei stood on his own again, walking past him. “You’re cute when you act like that,” he whispered when he knew he would hear him, before walking toward the food he was cooking again.
How cruel. His boyfriend truly hated him sometimes.

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Phainon shifted in his seat, staring at the phone in front of him, opened on a website that he didn’t think he would even think about opening before a couple more years.

The marriage rings category of a jewelry store.

It didn’t last long, however, as Phainon’s finger shut down the device as soon as his brain couldn’t process the information anymore. Too soon, he reminded himself. It was far too soon for anything even slightly resembling a marriage.

It was already a miracle that they flawlessly moved after Mydei was able to use his arm freely again, thanks to the fact that… he just didn’t have much left in his house. He had always been someone that bought only the absolute minimum for himself, and everything that Astraea needed was already in the apartment.

However, now he had something else to do that didn’t involve engagement rings or moving places again.

With a forced input from his brain, he stood up, peeking out of the room. “Astraea, we have to go!”

“Already?” the boy asked, from his place on the couch while he was reading a book upside down.

Maybe reading was too strong of a word, but he had a book in his hands as he spoke, looking at his father with big, curious brown eyes. He already dressed himself accordingly to go out, and Phainon perfectly knew why. He would never skip an opportunity to hang out with the triplets and Cyrene, given how little she visited due to how turbulent her job had been in the last few months.

Phainon smiled at him. “Do you want to make Auntie Reney wait?”

The response was immediate. Without thinking twice, Astraea rolled off of the couch and went to put on his shoes, then ran in front of Phainon with nothing but excitement. “We can go!”

Another smile appeared on Phainon’s face as he lightly caressed him on the top of his head. He tended to be more relaxed and happier now, and he hadn’t cried or hurt himself since that night when Mydei consoled him, so, maybe, things would start to look up for all of them.

The walk to get there wasn’t long or complicated, Tribios’ house was pretty close all things considered, but the little kid wouldn’t stop making happy noises of excitement. Phainon noticed just how happy he was to get out of the house and he took him to the nearby park or just strolling around whenever he could, but he wished it would be more often.

At least things will change in a few months when he will start going to school. He will meet new people, go out more often, have new friends, enjoy his free time more. He was already extremely happy every time he got to meet the triplets or Yanqing and Yunli, the rare times in which he or Mydei would go there to meet Sunday or Jing Yuan and they were there as well.

With him in school they would have had an easier time too, without the need to worry about leaving him home alone or ask someone else to watch him for a few hours– often to that same couple that worked at the bar near Mydei’s old place, since one of them stayed there to take care of a few things before opening and the other spent his days there because he seemingly had nothing better to do.

And yet, they were the only ones in their same situation and the ones they would ask anything regarding their relationship. It was comforting knowing that there was someone that moved as quickly as they did and for similar reasons.

“Auntie Reney!”

Astraea’s excited yell resounded in the street, making sure Phainon would wake up to reality again. In front of him stood a smiling Cyrene, most likely stepping out just to take a breath of fresh air.

“Little bunny!” she beamed, welcoming Astraea in a hug and a few pats on the top of his head. “And Phai! I hoped you could make it even with the short notice.”

He hugged her after his child stepped aside, peeking into the door behind them. “It’s not a problem, I just didn’t know you knew each other.”

“Oh, you mean me and Tribios? We just met that time with you and Mydei, then we started talking over the phone and we found out we had fun, so I said I’d pass by the next time I could greet you.”

“I didn’t know you liked older women, Cyrene…”

She lightly hit him on the shoulder. “As friends, Phai!” she huffed, before crossing her arms. “Tell me, did you and Mydei do the deed?”

Of course she would ask. It had been almost a year and he did nothing to hide how much he liked him and, with the fact that they were stable and living together with their son, it was normal to ask something like that.

However, Phainon raised his hands in defeat. “I can’t confirm nor deny that question. Orders from above.”

Alas, Mydei would skin him alive if Astraea even caught a syllable of anything about their sexual life. He wasn’t too eager to do it either, but he was far more scared of his partner’s very concrete menaces than anything else.

Unfortunately for him, though, as soon as they stepped into the house and after Cyrene already stopped asking anything about it, one of the twins showed up, probably hearing them coming in. After all, Astraea was there just so he could place with kids closer to his age, not to stay with another couple of adults for the next couple of hours.

He was always excited to go there because he did have more fun with them, whether any of them wanted to admit it or not– the kind of fun he had with him and Mydei was completely different from the one he had with the triplets and it had to be fine, at the end of the day.

“Go play with your friends, both I and Auntie Reney will be right here,” Phainon pushed him from the table of the kitchen, where Cyrene was already preparing some tea to talk over.

If he thought about how happy she was whenever they were able to meet for so long, he would have started crying. He didn’t, but he greatly appreciated all the thoughts she put into their encounters.

As he watched his child nodding and following his friend and disappeared behind a corner, excited words already echoed through the house. If anything, he was happy that he could sit there with his sister while Astraea could take a breather as well.

“They get along so well,” Cyrene commented, handing him a mug with boiling tea. “Tribios told me that all of them always look forward to play with Astraea.”

Phainon rested it on the table, letting it cool a little. He was well aware of the habit his sister had of overheating everything she cooked, and he took precautions as he grew up with her. Yet another reason why he learned how to cook. “Now that we’re on the topic, where’s Tribios?” he asked, resting his cheek on the palm of his hand.

“They called her in at work, she said that they found an interesting article, but who knows where she will have to go for it...” she sighed, before smiling at him again. “But do tell me about what you and Mydei have been doing lately!”

He clicked his tongue and let out a laugh, already knowing what she meant. “We did. Best sex in my life.”

“I’m happy for you!” she beamed as she joined her hands in a satisfied clap. “When’s the marriage?”

That was when his face fell the tiniest little bit, but enough for Cyrene to notice. He didn’t want to talk about it now, it was an idea that he had yet to process, but it had been buzzing in his head for a few weeks now. It was enough to start making decisions about it, probably, but he was still hesitant.

He had no idea if Mydei was on board with it, he didn’t know how to bring it up to him and he had no guarantee that told him that it would work.

It was a scary change, he didn’t want to drop it on Mydei or Astraea suddenly either.

Now, though, Cyrene stood in front of him and she was looking at him as if he just dropped the most shocking news he could ever think of. He could just give her an apologetic smile and rub the back of his neck, trying to explain everything to her. “Ah, well…”

“Phai.”

“Yes?”

“Did you actually propose and told me nothing about it?”

“No!” he immediately yelled, maybe a little too panicked. He took a step back and he drew a sigh, putting his thoughts in order again. “I was… thinking about it.”

Cyrene tilted her head in confusion. “I don’t think Mydei would tell you no. I mean, I don’t know him well, but he looked in love with you… the kind of impossible love that you would read in romantic books.”

Phainon knew perfectly that Mydei loved him. He was well aware that he was honest with his feelings and he often repeated it to him when he needed it the most. That wasn’t his problem– if Mydei didn’t want anything to do with it, they would have never reached a point where he would think about engagement rings.

He let out a heavy, shaky breath. “Isn’t it soon?” he asked, looking towards the surface of his drink. There was less steam coming up from it, probably at a normal temperature now.

“Phai, you moved in with him after less than a year of dating,” Cyrene mentioned. “Too soon is kind of your thing, and Mydei doesn’t look against it.”

His eyes relaxed as his fingers move toward the handle of the mug. “Maybe you’re right.”

That answer was more akin to a mutter, but he genuinely believed it. He knew that she was right, and it was the same thing that Sunday and Jing Yuan said when he asked them about their situation at home and for an advice.

“I am always right!” she smiled, finally taking it as a sign to sit across from him. “Now, do you have some other news?”

He was glad she switched topics, but he had no idea what kind of big news he could have for her. Days went by smoothly, Mydei was going to work again, Astraea was doing better in general and he was much less worried about everything. Things were going pretty well, there just weren’t particularly special days.

After raising his mug to drink the tea– still too hot for his liking, but drinkable– he remembered a detail that could fit what his sister asked him. “We subscribed Astraea to elementary school.”

Her face immediately started glowing, full of both happiness and excitement. “That’s amazing! How is that going?”

“Not too good… he hates math.”

“Phai, I hate to break it to you, but you and Cinny are the only ones who like math.”

Phainon hinted at a laugh, fully aware of how much she hated math too back in the day. After all, there was a reason why she got into writing books and he got into nursing school– it wasn’t only because of it, but there was a zero tolerance of that subject for Cyrene, even if she wasn’t bad at it. She simply didn’t like it, on Phainon’s contrary.

Astraea couldn’t decide it now, though. He would have had to deal with numbers for a very long time and Mydei wanted him to learn how to count and know the basics, so the fact that he wasn’t properly able to teach it to him was wearing him down a little.

“That’s not the issue… Mydei wants me to help him with basic math, since he’s pretty good with reading now and he can somewhat write already, but… he really, really hates it.” He sighed, taking another sip of his tea. “I haven’t seen him hate anything as much as math.”

Cyrene thought about his words for a few seconds. “Maybe he doesn’t understand how it can be useful to him?” she suggested, catching Phainon’s attention with that new possibility. “You know, Phai, Astraea is a pretty easy kid to teach, but he is still a six year old child. They don’t do well with abstract concepts. Maybe you can make up a story that he can see and touch as a reference to understand basic math?”

He couldn’t believe he didn’t think about it, but it definitely could work.

Astraea loved stories, any time Mydei needed to explain something a little too complicated he used some sort of story in a way he would understand what he was trying to say. Even if he rarely needed it, sometimes it was necessary and Phainon somehow never picked up on it.

Mydei was still way ahead of him in his understanding of that little child, but maybe it was natural. After all, he had been taking care of him for a little longer than him and he perfectly knew how to approach him. “I’ll need to ask for Mydei’s assistance then,” he thought out loud.

His sister smiled. “You seem awfully happy about that.”

“I am!” he beamed, showing her a happy, shining smile. After all, it was true. He liked working with Mydei, and even more if it was something for their son.

A loud groan filled the room after a few seconds, taking Phainon completely by surprise. It wasn’t rare for Cyrene to do it, she was human and she got annoyed and frustrated, of course, but he didn’t expect that answer to how excited he was about something regarding Mydei.

“It’s frustrating! All of you are finding eternal love and I’m not!” she whined, puffing her cheek. She relaxed almost immediately, smiling at him again. “But I’m happy for you, Mydei, Cinny and Cas. You deserve all of it.”

Phainon obviously didn’t forget that his own sister didn’t have a girlfriend, he just didn’t think she would care this much. If he thought about it for more than two seconds, though, it was more than normal– she had always been a romantic woman at heart, after all.

He thought about it as he kept on sipping on his tea, right before something lit up in his brain.

“What if I told you that I know a beautiful woman that is very much into women working as a singer, composer and lyricist near Mydei’s old apartment?” he asked, hopeful eyes looking at her.

As soon as she heard that question, Cyrene’s bright blue eyes shone in an expression that could only be described as a cute bunny begging for a pat on its head. “You have to be my wingman, Phai!” she whined, leaning over to taking his hand in both of hers. “Please? What’s her name?”

He laughed, amused by the situation. “Robin. Mydei’s sister tried to flirt with her once but it went nowhere.”

“Ah, we could beat Mydei and his sister, I get it now.” Her face got slightly more interested and her eyes a little more intense. “Do you have pictures?”

Pictures… might be a problem. He was almost completely sure that there were some pictures on her SNS accounts, but he didn’t know if he should show them to her. He trusted his sister blindly, but he wondered whether Robin had a girlfriend or not or if she wanted one in the first place.

She was objectively ethereal with the least amount of make-up or effort put into her appearance, after all. If she rejected Cipher, there had to be a reason for it.

However, they were adult women. They could ask that to each other before starting to flirt or take steps forward.

“I can check,” he stated, flinging out his phone. He remembered her username, so he just searched her up and scrolled through her profile, until he found an acceptable, clear picture of her and Sunday right before a performance. “This is her with her brother.”

Cyrene groaned. “Oh, she’s so beautiful.” She stood up all of a sudden, making her brother jump on his chair. “Phai! Please, put in a good word for me? Let her know I exist? Pretty please?”

He hinted at a laugh, happily leaning into her request. After all, he didn’t get to see his sister so excited about something so mundane. Usually, they either didn’t meet at all or Cyrene was so much more mature than he was that he barely believed that they only had a two years gap.

She was always ready to say the right thing at the right moment, keeping herself detached enough to be seen as much older since they were children, but cheerful enough for him to recognize his own sister.

That thought almost disturbed him.

How much did she have to grow in such a situation, without parents and with a younger brother to take care of? It wasn’t the first time he asked it to himself, but he hadn’t quite put it into perspective to that extent.

If it had such a bad effect on him, he couldn’t imagine how much his dear sister lost during those years.

That, however, was what the rest of their lives was for.

Phainon himself learned how to start and pick himself up again, working on his issues while letting the joys and tribulations of a family life affect him in all the best and worst ways possible. They may have gone fast for everyone's standards, but he was way more relaxed and happier than in the past.

It was easier to let himself feel happiness, thanks to the presence of Mydei and Astraea in his life and he wanted the same for his dearest sister too.

His eyes traveled to hers, still glittering with gratefulness and hope. “I can organize an outing for you two while I catch up with Hyacine and Cas and you can casually sneak out with her?” he suggested.

“Please!” she smiled with a bit of her tongue in between her teeth. Phainon wondered for a split second how did no one ever even try to get with someone as cute and reliable as her, but maybe he was extremely biased.

“You’re so excited about this.”

“Of course I am. Were you not excited when Mydei started answering to your texts? And don’t lie to me, I perfectly know how much of a good mood you were in back then, I remember!”

It was true, he was excited at the time.

Maybe Mydei was being a little cold at the time, but he could feel the genuine care after just a couple of conversations. He was genuine while not coddling him too much, and he liked it more than he may admit out loud, despite the seemingly detached texts he received.

Perhaps it was because they met pretty soon again after they started texting, but he started to quickly tell apart what he said and the way he said it. Initially, it all looked like reading his answer was like reading lines for a book– precise, definitive, confident. There was room for another interpretation, but it was difficult for it to cross his mind, especially after their first date and witnessing what kind of person he was truly like.

If he said that he wanted to challenge him while Phainon pursued him, it was exactly what he meant. He didn’t sugarcoat or hide any kind of secret or double meaning, and it was comforting. He was aware even now that he meant exactly what he said, he never had to ask himself if he meant something else.

Cyrene let out a light laugh. “We have a pretty good life now, Phai,” she said, with a melancholic voice. “Mom and Dad would be proud of both of us, I hope that you know that.”

Phainon stared at her for a second. “I know.”

She looked at him for a while to make sure he would have been fine and didn’t need a bit more of support, before clapping her hands a couple of times to catch his attention again. “Good! Help me make something for those four scoundrels now.”

He snorted, but he easily stood up and agreed, following her instructions. It was nothing too complicated, just a few snacks and drinks for the kids in the other room to wait for them as soon as they finished playing or Phainon decided that it was time to go back home, which happened in another couple of hours.

Unluckily, Tribios was still outside when they greeted the triplets and Cyrene, but Astraea looked and sounded absolutely gleeful over the time he spent there playing with other children his age, for once. It was good that he could have something like that and that both he and the three sisters genuinely liked each other enough to spend time together.

“I had fun!” he beamed, as soon as they headed out, still holding a snack in one hand and a little bag full of food to bring home. Phainon asked if he wanted to hand it over to him, but he staunchly refused, claiming that he would have been the one giving it to Mydei.

Phainon could only smile to that statement, letting him give him Fig Stew to hold, at least. “I did too,” he said. “How do you think Dad is doing?”

“Well!”

“How can you be so sure?”

“Dad’s strong and nothing can make him unwell?”

He was so convinced of that fact, that Mydei could always overcome anything being thrown at him, that Phainon couldn’t help but snort. His big brown eyes looked at him full of wonder, searching for an answer that he didn’t grasp completely yet.

In his head, Phainon knew that Astraea was fully aware of the fact that Mydei was just human and he just got badly hurt in a way that his strength couldn’t fight against it, but now he was at home with no danger and he stopped being put in a dangerous position at work. Both of them made sure to tell him so he wouldn’t be worried about it, so of course he would believe that Mydei was doing as well as they were.

Even if they already knew that he was quite intelligent, sometimes he would have some thoughts that only a child could come up with– and it always brought a smile to his face. It warmed his heart to know that he let himself be a child with the parenting and support finally being provided for him.

However, he knew that he was just following what he told him about letting them do the heavy lifting and not worrying himself too much about them. He still meant those words, but he wanted Astraea to know that he could still hug them and miss them and be worried for them without taking on a role that was just too big for his age.

“Nothing nothing?” he asked, trying to make him realize it. “Not even a bad day at work?”

The little child blinked in confusion. “You said it’s not something I have to think about.”

As expected.

Phainon hummed in thought, putting on a convincing enough show for him to think that it was something worth giving a little more time to. “I meant… you can think about it a little bit. Not too much.” He turned to suggest him something. “A hug would do.”

Astraea puffed his cheek in slight annoyance. “But I always hug him.”

That… was also true. He did hug him pretty often, regardless whether Mydei needed it or asked for it. It wasn’t the entire point of the discussion, though.

“Hug him more often when he’s not feeling well,” Phainon suggested again, trying to make himself clear enough.

“Okay!”

The child stepped closed to his side, almost making him trip over, but, luckily, Phainon was able to save himself, instead reaching out a hand to let him hold it in case he wanted to stay close to him, given the late hour. They stepped out of the house during the afternoon, so it was already starting to get dark and Phainon greatly preferred to have his son as close as possible.

They weren’t far from home, but Phainon preferred him to be safe, rather than anything happening to him even mere seconds away from entering in the apartment.
