He glanced at the hour, thinking immediately about the kind of food he would have eaten today after a nice shower, and, suddenly, nothing else mattered more.

“You’re happier.”

Phainon instantly turned his head around, looking at his child. Astraea’s eyes, however, weren’t on his face, busy trying to make out the road ahead, and he didn’t dare to distract him unless absolutely necessary. “Am I?” he asked, mildly confused. “If that’s the case, it’s thanks to you and Dad.”

A satisfied laugh resounded in the space next to him. “Dad makes people happy.”

He truly, honestly did. He didn’t look like the person to lift a person’s mood with a smile or some jokes, but he made sure to get their mind off of what was bothering them and that alone often helped to lift anyone’s mood– other than just how caring and attentive ot anyone’s desires and needs he was, of course.

Phainon suddenly crouched down to pick up the little child, immediately hearing happy laughs and acute yells in between. Lately he laughed more, he enjoyed his time more and his cries were almost nonexistent. He was especially free-spirited since Mydei’s arm got taken care of and they officially moved in his apartment.

Obviously, he didn’t believe for a second that he didn’t have issues anymore, that the ghosts of the past or his traumatic experiences didn’t follow him whenever he went anymore, but he was… lighter. He found some ways to cope with all the hurt that was caused to him and he had a steady and solid support system in him and Mydei.

He was happier, just like Phainon was.

A smile appeared on his face as he left a kiss between his hair, catching the whiff of his smell for half a second. “You need to take a bath later too, don’t you think?” he asked, a little playfully.

The child put his tongue in between his lips while he stroke an amused smile. “You too?”

“Do you want to do the bath with me?”

“It’s fun!”

Phainon smiled back at him, quietly accepting that request. He honestly didn’t expect him to ever ask, but not out of sadness or fear. He just didn't think he would be comfortable to be put in that position yet.

He usually did it with Mydei, and even in that case he took several months to ask him. He was always being given trust and privacy whenever he needed it, so he was sure that it was an honest, genuine request.

At the lack of an answer, however, Astraea continued to illustrate him his plan. “Dad can prepare the food and you can tell me a story and then we can eat together and–”

“And you go straight to bed because you skipped your nap,” Phainon intervened with a smile on his face.

The child immediately puffed his cheeks. “No!”

“Yes,” he rebutted, insisting on the matter. “You know how important sleeping is.”

“Fine…”

It was a relief, he thought. Seeing him so eager to refuse a direct suggestion made by him or Mydei was comforting, after everything that he went through and how obedient of a child he was.

There was no problem with him listening what they told him, but he treated them as rules, absolute truths that he couldn't whine against, or something bad would have happened to him. It was something that Phainon absolutely didn't want him to think. Not now and not ever.

He could whine, be annoying, yell, make his life a living hell for a few minutes– the last thing that he wanted was knowing that he was scared of an answer that they might give him or a punishment that he didn't deserve.

Lately he saw so many positive developments in that little child as well. He hadn’t been harming himself for a few months now, he was more relaxed, he tried new things even if he was scared of them, he talked with strangers with a little less fear into his eyes, he whined on some occasions. He was genuinely getting better as time passed. Slowly, at his own pace, trying to adapt to his new conditions, but he was working very hard to march toward that goal.

Phainon couldn’t be happier to be able to witness that transformation.

The walk home wasn’t too long, and Astraea instantly flew across the living room to the kitchen, only to crash against his father’s legs.

“Dad! Papa said I need to give you more hugs when you’re unwell,” he mentioned, repeating what Phainon told him mere hours before.

It was what he meant, but it wasn’t absoutely how he meant for the little thing to tell his father about it.

Obviously, Mydei looked at him a little confused, then back to Phainon. “I’m fine?”

“Just in case,” he answered. He stepped slowly in his personal space, daring to smack a loud kiss to his cheek from behind his back. “How have you been?”

“In peace.” He turned his head in Astraea’s direction and his hand moved to pet him on the top of his head, flaming rebel hair fuffy and soft to the touch. “How was your day?”

“Fun!”

“Yeah? You had fun with your friends?”

The child energetically nodded. “And Auntie Reney and Papa made us snacks!”

Phainon smiled when he heard him mentioning it. He didn’t know if he appreciated them to such an extent or if he just mindlessly ate them while he listened to the triplets argue while Cyrene tried not to laugh at the very intense discussion they were having about whether or not they could sneak in a cat in ways that none of them thought were possible.

They settled with hiding it in a spaceship and traveling there with a teletrasport button so they could stay with their older sister and the cat, in the end. They sure had imagination.

Mydei brought him back to reality by giving him a light flick on his forehead. It wasn’t hard and it didn’t leave a mark, but it was enough to leave him baffled, even with the smirk on his partner’s face. “Go wash yourself, you stink.”

“What’s all this violence, Mydei…” he whined, giving him an apologetic smile as he rubbed the back of his head with his hand. “Is that the way you should welcome your husband home?”

There was no harm in trying, right?

He just wanted to see his reaction to that word, how he would take that joke or if he would feel somehow endangered or frightened by it.

Of course, all that he wished for them was getting married and live the rest of their days together, raising Astraea, watching him go through all the joys and sorrows that life itself had to offer… but if Mydei didn’t want it or if he wasn’t ready for that yet, he would have stepped back immediately.

Well, almost immediately. He would sulk for a while first.

His eyes looked at Mydei with insistence, waiting for an answer, his fingers restless and his irises shining in anticipation. He probably looked like a madman, but he couldn’t care less at the moment.

However, no matter how much he looked and waited, Mydei didn’t react at all.

“Stop fooling around and go wash yourself,” he only said, giving him a light push on his right shoulder. “Dinner is almost ready.”

Phainon smiled, happily letting him play around like that. Honestly, it wasn’t the reaction he was looking for, but not the one he feared to see either. They still had time to think about it, but, maybe, he could already get that ring… after all, he opened that store in the first place because there were some sales on it.

So what if he would gather the courage of asking him such an important question in one or two years, or even five or ten? The ring would be the same either way.

“I can start going to fill the bath,” he answered him, while his mind was someplace else entirely. “Both of us need to take a bath, but we’ll be quick, don’t worry about dinner going cold either.”

That was when Astraea twirled away from Mydei, almost as if it was a sign for him to speak up. “I can do it!” he exclaimed, voice full of confidence.

He didn’t even wait before running away to the bathroom either, leaving his parents standing in the kitchen, baffled and at a momentary loss of words. It was only after a few seconds that Mydei registered what just happened and what their son just said.

Hurriedly, he walked aver the door and warned, “Don’t put too much water!”

Phainon let out a small, amused snicker of a laugh. “I’ll check in a few minutes, don’t worry.”

Mydei nodded, a little exhausted. “How was your day?” He huffed, then laid against the wall to rest with his arms crossed over his chest. “Astraea answered me, you didn’t.”

“Oh, normal. My sister wants to end up in bed with Robin,” he mentioned offhandedly, not mentioning… everything else that they talked about. Especially his plans for their future that now Cyrene was aware of as well.

“She’s probably the only person that could bypass Sunday,” he sighed, getting a light giggle from Phainon. “I’ll take care of dinner, go see what our son is doing to our water bill.”

He should have done that, he knew that a little child couldn’t be trusted with the amount of water he should put in a bath, but his eyes couldn’t leave from Mydei just yet.

Instead, he stepped forward, only stopping when he was as close as possible to him, keeping him as pinned to the wall as possible. “You know, Mydei,” he whispered, “I really like how we ended up.”

Mydei initially didn’t move a single muscle nor particularly reacted to those actions. When he made up his mind on what to answer, he spelled clearly every single word he said to him. “And you know that I share those feelings, my love, but if our son manages to flood our apartment–”

“Got it! I’ll take care of it, don’t worry,” Phainon immediately stepped back, rising his hands as he gave up. He wasn’t scared of him, not seriously, but he perfectly knew what a request to step back from him looked like.

With a push of his feet, Mydei stood on his own again, walking past him. “You’re cute when you act like that,” he whispered when he knew he would hear him, before walking toward the food he was cooking again.

How cruel. His boyfriend truly hated him sometimes.

“Mydei…” he whined as he struggled to keep his muscles still. All that he wanted to do was dash to him and hug him, kiss him, answer to that teasing with words that would keep that conversation going and, if only Mydei didn’t look at him with warning eyes, he would have.

It wasn’t the right time for something like that. He was asked of something and he promised Astraea a bath, so he better keep his word.

With a sigh his body turned around and walked out of the room, heading to the bathroom, where his son was already waiting for him. Phainon looked at him as soon as he waltzed through the door, kneeling on the floor and waiting for the water to get to an acceptable level for the both of them. Phainon didn’t know if he was aware of what that exactly meant, but he was trying, and that was all that he expected from him.

“Did Dad send you?” he asked, tilting his head and causing a few golden bangs to end up in front of his brown eyes. Phainon smiled at how effortlessly cute he was even now.

Phainon kneeled down next to him, giving a quick glance to the water level. It wasn’t enough yet, but he had an activity in mind for this time, so he turned it off anyway. “You know your father worries.” He moved his head impercettably in the bath’s direction. “Do you know where to stop it?”

A sincere, confused shake of his head answered him.

His legs moved to let him sit down on the floor, subsequentially crossing over to leave a place where Astraea could sit if he so wished. “Do you know what’s a half of something?” he asked, seemingly derailing the discussion.

Another shake of his head. “Do you know?”

He looked around him, trying to find something to explain that concept to his child. He knew that he heard it already, but it was always something that adults would do for him, so he never bothered to ask– or he simply didn’t think it involved him. It wouldn’t be too hard, but he was still young, he needed to explain it in terms he would understand.

Luckily, he finally caught the object he had in mind: a little metallic sphere that Hyacine left there to ‘remember her by’ kept in a plastic cube that can be opened if the occasion required it. It was nothing special really, just a sphere that she had bought when they all went out for the first time when they were still at university, and since Phainon was the one to pay for it, she insisted that he would keep it for her too.

“It got paid with your money, Phai!” she had said back then. “You should keep it for me and Cassie too, maybe it will bring you even more luck now that you go into a phase of your life that won’t have us as present as before.”

He remembered how much it saddened him.

Of course he was happy to begin this new chapter of his life with Astraea and Mydei, that was what he had worked toward for the past year or so, but it was still disheartening to know that they would grow apart now. Not only that, he hated it so much that his boyfriend and son had to boost his morale for weeks after that fact happened and the guilt and frustration that he felt in those few days was immesuarable.

His issues related to abandonment did get better as Mydei reassured him, but his life wasn’t perfect by any means yet, mood swings still happened, he still secretly hated others all of a sudden, he still felt betrayed whenever his friends moved on with their life without even cutting him out, and it all left him exhausted at the end of every single day.

He could just act what was expected of him because his job let him focus on others that didn’t know him personally and it was much easier that way, but it was nice having a partner that understood his struggles– even if not intimately, he just knew he needed cuddles or a few minutes of due care– and acted accordingly to make him feel better and relaxed.

His hand stretched enough to grab the plastic box and bring it over to show Astraea what he wanted him to understand as those thoughts swirled in his mind, recalling all those late afternoon and evenings where Mydei would spend a decent amount of his time to convince him to just lay down and take a nap, or offered cuddles while they were watching something on TV, whether it was a series or a movie or something else.

He couldn’t believe that was his life now.

“This is Auntie’s pink ball,” Astraea mumbled, crawling closer to look at it a little better. It was nothing special, really, but the little child liked how shiny and pink it was, even if it was just a cheap metallic sphere.

That, however, wasn’t what Phainon had been searching for. Instead, he gave it to Astraea to hold as he showed him the plastic cube. “This is half, for example. It’s when one thing is divided in identical two things,” he said, then united them as a whole cube again. “Two halves make a whole.”

Astraea sat there, looking at both him and the box, the shiny sphere rolling between his palm and fingers, while his brain thought about what he was being presented with. “But… you can’t divide water,” he finally pointed out.

Smart.

“No, you’re right,” Phainon laughed. “What we need to divide is the thing we put water in. So, take the bath, for example. What are the two identical parts?”

Maybe this was too hard. He knew that he was intelligent, but this was a little too much for him too.

“Nothing?” he predictably said, a little confused by that question. The bath was big, it was understandable for him to not know where the half was simply basing himself on the fact that, realistically, he couldn’t cut it in half.

“Okay,” Phainon breathed out, pointing at a straight parallelepiped-like structure on the corner of the bath. “Let’s take that piece as the whole. If we needed to cut it in half, where would the right point be?”

At least, even if Astraea hated math, he liked these activities with his parents. He liked thinking abut how he could solve the problems that they expressively asked him and he didn’t hate being made to think further even on things that he didn’t fully comprehend yet. So, when he moved to sit in front of that structure and study it, he wasn’t surprised at all.

When he noticed that he was having a particularly hard time with it, he quietly chimed in, giving a few suggestions on how he could see the problem better in his head. “Just imagine you could cut it like this to have two equal parts,” he said, moving his hand horizontally to mimic a cut.

Astraea looked at him for a few seconds, lost in his thoughts. He knew what cutting meant and he grasped what halves were, he just needed to put it in practice, and it was fine for him to think about his own way on how to go about it.

He turned to the structure of the bath again, touching it with the hand that wasn’t holding Hyacine’s little sphere. A couple of minutes passed by, not a single sound emitting from that room, with the only one in the air being whatever Mydei was cooking in the kitchen. “Here?” Astraea finally asked, tracing a finger horizontally around what was, indeed, the half that Phainon was hinting at.

“Mhm, exactly!” he smiled. Moving his hand, he shifted his son’s finger a little higher on the parallelepiped. “Then, you need to fill in a bit more. Put your index finger here.”

He tilted his head. “Up to there?”

“Yeah, exactly.”

Phainon just watched as he filled the bath with water up to the half point they agreed upon, and gave him a pat on the head when he stopped adding it in the precise point that he told him. He already noticed in the past few months, but he learned quickly and he made sure to be as precise as possible… just like Mydei, even if it wouldn’t initially look that way.

“Like this?” he asked again, making sure that he was doing what Phainon wanted him to.

Another thing that he noticed was the fear of doing something wrong, no matter how small, but it was quite normal after the childhood he had. After all, they had time, and these things won’t come to pass nearly as easily as getting him to call them with ‘Dad’ or ‘Papa’. They were deeply intertwined in his mind and he would have needed years to understand and overcome them.

“Exactly, up there is fine.” Phainon watched him as he stared at the water, a proud expression decorating his face. “So you know how much you have to put in for next time too.”

He turned around with a bright, shining smile, genuinely happy that he was able to do something that it seemingly was too complicated for him to understand. “Thank you, Papa!”

Getting those smiles even just once a month made it worth everything that he had ever done in his life. Those excited smiles for him and Mydei above anyone else filled his heart with joy and it made him realize just how much he just won at the lottery of life. Not only was he with the best, most gorgeous man he had ever met, he had a wonderful son that he adored with every cell of his being.

Just knowing that they were there was worth all the trouble that he went through for his entire life.

With a smile, he moved his head towards the bath. “Ready?”

“Yes!”

“Let’s wash first.”

As they both got inside the bath, Phainon thanked every other deity that Astraea decided to cut his hair, faintly remembering just how difficult it was to wrap it up and avoiding it from getting wet when it was much, much longer. Now he didn’t need any of it, and he could play and talk with no issues whenever he did do a bath, either alone or with one of them to aid him.

Unluckily, they needed to hurry up to go to eat dinner, so Phainon had to put a bit of a hurry on him. He understood, but he was clearly looking forward to having this as a time to spend with his father regardless.

Phainon made a mental note of playing with him more after dinner to make up for it.

“Papa,” Astraea called as he was finishing to wash his body, “how do you know all those things that Dad doesn’t know?”

“Mh… I studied them! Your father and I studied very different things, but it’s a good thing for you. Now you can learn a lot of different stuff,” he answered, silently standing up and helping the child to get out of the bath too.

Something about that action felt… overwhelmingly trusting.

It went without saying, but it was indeed the first time that Phainon assisted him in a bath in the last year or so. Usually it was Mydei’s job, because Astraea trusted him more and he was comfortable with seeing him at his most vulnerable. So the fact that now he was doing the same with Phainon spoke volumes about how much more he trusted him and how quickly their relationship developed and in which direction.

A calm smile appeared on his face as he helped him dry up and handed over the body cream that he often applied after any kind of bath, then he ran to get his own clothes.

Phainon's eyes followed him for a couple of seconds, only until he disappeared from his line of sight, covered by the corner of his own room. A small, breathy laugh escaped his lips, slightly moving the air in the otherwise silent atmosphere of the bathroom.

He truly did enjoy that tranquil life, full of joy that left him in precious, faint moments where he could hear his mind and think by himself. Short instants spent with his head was something that he liked far more than the hours he used to spend with it before he met Mydei.

Before long, he sighed as he headed to his bedroom to grab clothes of his own too, only to meet Astraea in the bathroom again as they reunited again to wash their hair.

Phainon flushed down a decent amount of the water in it, getting ready to do Astraea's first. Since they both had short hair, it wouldn't take long.

His child walked up to him, kneeling down, of the right height to barely be able to glance at the water still in the bath. “Papa,” he finally spoke, “is school scary?”

He had to expect such a question. After all, he had never gone to school before.

Phainon dragged out a ragged sigh, unsure on what to answer. Unsure if he should have reassured him with little white lies or tell him his awful experience with school, bouncing from place to place and switching classmates and bullies more times than he was able to count. Astraea wouldn’t go through that, but he had no other reference for what should have been a normal experience at school.

“It’s hard sometimes,” he settled on, “but you learn a lot of things and you meet a lot of people.”

Astraea nodded in silence, lowering his head over the edge of the bath once the water in it almost entirely disappeared going down the drain. Phainon took a long, tense sigh, proceeding with the hair washing, despite the heavy boulder on his heart.

He leaned his head with his hand, pushing a little bit forward, noticing that he had closed his eyes already. A smile crept on his face, before he could grab the shampoo and turning the knob in front of him to start the water and wash his hair properly.

As soon as the hot water hit Astraea’s head, a whine spread in the room, maybe out of surprise, but he didn’t move, just holding a little more strongly onto the edge of the bath for a couple of seconds.

Phainon kept on washing his hair, carefully applying shampoo whenever he could reach, until he heard his voice again.

“You and Dad didn’t meet anyone there, though.”

He was really scared, and he could tell.

Going to school wasn’t just a new space for him, a new experience full of unknown factors that he would have to face without the adults or older kids that he leaned on for the least year or so. In some aspects, this could feel like a betrayal and somewhat of a death sentence.

Furthermore, he and Mydei didn’t have many friends they met there and no one he knew had a friend from elementary or middle school, and Yanli and Yanquing met in high school for the first time– eight years after the class he had to start with.

There was one, though.

“Dad met Hephaestion there,” Phainon reminded him. They met more so because they were neighbors rather than classmates, but it had to be enough of an example for the moment, since he had no one else.

Blue eyes observed the child in front of him, noticing again his hands curling more strongly around the edge of the bath. He sighed, the weight on his heart worsening for a second.

He quickly finished his job and he stepped away just to brush a white towel against his hair to dry it properly, thinking about that silence over and over again, trying desperately to find some kind of loophole that would grant him that his son wasn’t feeling horribly about having to go to school.

He couldn’t find one. All he could think about was the fear that infused every single sentence hesitantly coming out of his mouth.

Then, that fear settled in his chest like a heavy presence, neither creepy nor comforting. It was simply there, reminding him of that truth. He couldn’t protect him from going to school, feeling the first fears again, having to face that kind of environment, but he could sustain him and protect him in other ways, before and after it.

Whether it was enough or not, he wasn’t sure, but it was the best that he could do for him.

“Astraea,” he called out again, letting him grab the towel to dry his hair a little more. He turned, looking at him father with big, curious brow eyes– a gesture that was returned with a warm smile. “Try it a little and give it time. Have fun. If there’s something that needs our intervention, we will intervene, don’t worry.”

The tiny child in front of him slowly closed his fists in the towel now around his shoulders, and his brown eyes started shining all of a sudden. Phainon didn’t need to see him start crying out of the blue to hug him close to him, carefully caressing him on the back of his head.

Poor thing.

He was terrified, and yet, he tried to hide it because they were moving and Mydei was still having some issues with his arm until recently. He just didn't want to to add another problem to their worries, even if he promised them that he would lean on them more.

Obviously, he was still just a child. He would have had to take a few years to fully distance himself from that kind of behavior.

Somehow, by that point, it was something that Phainon knew that he or Mydei had to prevent, but there wasn't much that could be done in that direction now. All he could do was trying to calm him down.

“Hey, it’s fine to be scared,” he whispered, catching his attention almost immediately. Astraea looked up with frightened eyes, face decorated with the trail left by his tears hope written all over his face. Phainon only smiled and caressed him from the forehead to his hair, slicking them back a little. “It’s a new experience for you, but I promise it will be okay. At the end of the day, you will still come back home and live exactly as you’re doing now, okay?”

Astraea nodded, visibly more tranquil. He didn't seem entirely convinced, but at least he was able to get him to calm down before dinner. He would make up for all this later.

Phainon smiled again, ruffling his hair affectionately. “Let’s wrap this up, what do you think? Dad will feel lonely if he has to eat alone, right?”

As if a light just turned on in his head at the mention of Mydei, Astraea ran over to the kitchen, losing the towel on his shoulder behind him, not too far away from the door of the bathroom.

With an amused smile, Phainon picked it up and put it to dry again, ultimately opting to wash his hair after Astraea would have gone to bed. He doubted he and Mydei would have been up much later anyway.

As he walked toward the kitchen, the invading feeling that he matured upon the conversation with Astraea didn’t leave, staying right on his heart, reminding him of something that he wanted to avoid. He doubted it would have gone away any time soon, at least not until Astraea had gone to school and he had a proper conversation with Mydei about it.

Now, however, it wasn’t the time. Distracting Astraea for the rest of the day by spending time with him seemed a far more likely decision.

Phainon momentarily abandoned his thoughts as soon as he saw Mydei, almost swinging himself at Mydei’s waist, uncaring of what he was doing or what it may have looked like to the kid sitting at the table not too far away from them.

A hand caressed him on his hair, with no other muscle pushing him away, letting him rest on his shoulder instead. “It went well, I see.”

“Mhm,” Phainon hummed, raising his head from his shoulder. “But now I’m tired because I just taught our beautiful child how to fill a bath.”

“What a challenge it must have been.”

“No, we have the smartest kid in the world.”

“You aren’t wrong.”

A soft laugh could be heard from their right, where Astraea was sitting, and just with that, Phainon’s weight was lifted a little. He was probably still worried about school, but they would cross that bridge if they get to it, and he seemed to understand it as well.

“We’ll talk about whatever you’re thinking about tomorrow,” Mydei said, grabbing tha already full and hot plates from the counter. “Do you want to go to bed earlier today?”

Phainon smiled, his heart already fluttering over that proposal. “Maybe.” He casually caught the smell from the dish in his hands, feeling his muscles relaxing almost immediately. “This smells so good…”

“Luckily for you,” Mydei sighed as he approached the table, “this will be the food that you can eat for the rest of your life.”

Somehow, it was said in such a… natural way. Almost as if it was obvious.

Of course Phainon knew that Mydei had no intention of leaving him or Astraea, it wasn’t something that he learned he would ever do, even if he still asked for clarification when his mood was in a disastrous condition. What took him aback was the way he said it, as if he was teasing him, already happy where he was, but willing to go forward if he wished.

The smile appearing on his face had more meanings that he cared to admit, but he had time to process and think about it. All he cared about right now was eating with his family and growing further with them, no matter the obstacles and doubts in their way.

It was normal, maybe even comforting to know that those obstacles would have just made them grow as they have had in the last few months. That was something that he learned at his own expenses.

Sitting at the table with Mydei and Astraea discussing about whether or not it was hot enough to still having to dry the little child’s hair was familiar, something that greatly softened his heart.

And maybe he would have bought that ring and proposed, and he could have faced Mydei’s answer after knowing those underlying feelings of keeping on moving forward with him. All of them had time to move forward and figure everything out. Whether Mydei would have accepted his proposal or not, they would have done it together to catch this happiness for the rest of their lives.

Chapter End Notes

It was fast and a bit shorter this time, but hope it was an enjoyable read once again!! It's almost over but I wanted to write a little more of Cyrene before that, next time it's Mydei's turn for his wrap up and the happily ever after ^^

chapters.title: Chapter 14
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

“Sure, dear,” Mydei answered, voice soft and patient. “What did you want to ask?”
“Mh…” He paused, moments in which Astraea turned around again and asked carefully to crawl on his lap. As Mydei was about to nod, Phainon unloaded something that he thought wouldn’t be on the table for another few years. “Please, marry me.”

Chapter Notes

TW: slight mentions of child abuse, drug use and alcohol intoxication

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Mydei couldn’t believe that was where his life lied at that moment. Sitting in the living room after dinner, helping Astraea with the few things that Phainon explained him about basic math– something that he could still help with, despite his aversion to the subject– and waiting for his boyfriend to come back home after he went out to have some fun with his friends.

It wasn’t bad at all, he liked sitting there, reading a book and throwing an eye to his son once every few minutes to see how much he was suffering in front of that book.

Seeing as the sounds he was making were displeased and confused whines, Mydei rested his hand on the top of his head, causing him to turn around and look at him. “Are you suffering enough over there?”

“Daaaad… I hate math,” he sighed, puffing his cheeks in annoyance. “Is it ever useful?”

“This one is. You can stop listening to it when you will be older, half of it is useless for most people,” Mydei answered, refusing to tell him a lie for his well-being and education.

It was true, he only ever used what he learned up until he was thirteen, nothing more than that came in handy past that. There was no use lying to him about it, especially if it brought a little bit of hope in his future.

Astraea tilted his head, deeply confused eyes staring back at the sheets of paper. “Why does Papa like this then?”

“That’s because, honey, your father is a sick, strange, bizarre man.”

“Why are you together then?”

Mydei couldn’t keep in a soft laugh. The fact that Astraea still didn’t understand the reasons of their decisions as a couple was amusing, but not all that surprising. After all, he was still young and he didn’t have many other examples before meeting them, so he always had to explain it to him in a much simpler, concrete way, rather than talking about such complicated feelings that he had to yet clash with.

“He has more positives than negatives,” he said, slightly tilting his head. “His food is good, right? And it’s useful knowing what to ask the doctor with all those big words he knows.”

Astraea nodded, extremely convinced by those words. “And he knows fairies.”

“Oh, yeah,” Mydei laughed, “that’s really cool too, you’re right.”

One day they will have to break the news to him that fairies didn’t exist and Phainon was just playing into that endeavor for his sake and, to an extent, his own entertainment. Mydei could see how much he loved talking about fairies and magical worlds, maybe because he grew up with those stories thanks to Cyrene narrating them to him as well.

It was keeping that child alive and giving him some grace for what he went through, in a way. He just couldn’t take it away from either of them now.

“Where’s Papa now?” Astraea suddenly asked, laying down the pencil he held until that moment. The sheets were either scribbled on or decorated with actual answers to the questions posed in the book, but Mydei wasn’t surprised that he wanted to stop studying at that hour.

It was after dinner, the moon was shining already, and he was exhausted by that point of the day. On top of it, Phainon wasn’t home and Astraea would much rather stay up doing math all the time than go to bed without seeing him.

Mydei sighed as he answered him, far too familiar with how that night would have gone. “Out with your aunts, something about a party or an outing after a long time.”

The child looked a little melancholic, maybe disappointed with knowing that he had to go the entire night without his father because he was out with people he genuinely liked to be with. He didn’t look like he wanted to hold it against Phainon or that he necessarily needed a reassuring gesture being made toward him, but Mydei still thought about it.

Irrational fits were normal at his age, but he had never seen them through whenever they were something that could be interpreted as a selfish action. Whenever it was against either of them, he refused to feel it or act on it, no matter how upsetting it may be.

He just started playfully arguing with them or expressing little whines, though, so he couldn’t ask so much more from him right now. With time, he would have been able to be mad, have complaints as explosive as he wished, but he didn’t want to push him just yet. He was getting better and enjoying himself, and it was enough for the moment.

Just as he noticed Astraea wanting to say something else, Mydei’s phone started ringing.

With a fluid motion, he slipped a bookmark between the pages of the text he was reading, laying the book on the table and walking toward the source of the sound. Upon looking at the screen, he smiled warmly, only to look at Astraea again, busy fantasizing about who it could be from his seat.

“Talk of the devil,” Mydei whispered as he walked back and sat down, letting Astraea lean in to look at the contact on the phone.

With a confused expression, the little child knit his eyebrows together, part of his hair falling in front of his eyes as he questioned his father. “Papa is evil?”

Mydei laughed softly. “I’ll explain later, use your pretty spheres for those numbers, baby.”

“‘Kay…”

“Good boy.”

His attention shifted to Phainon’s incessant calling, refusing to hang up. He sighed and picked up, tilting his head slightly as he listened what his boyfriend had to say, given how much he was insisting with him picking up in the first place.

“Hey, Phainon,” he said, rather casually. “Do I have to come pick you up?”

“No… But I need to ask you something reaaaaally important…”

A sigh left his mouth without him wanting to. “You’re drunk.”

“No, no! I’m not, Mydei.” He let out a long, prolonged, very loud whine before a thump echoed through the phone. Probably his head hitting the table below him. “Everyone keeps saying it but I’m not… I promise. Do you believe me? Please?”

Mydei’s head threw itself back, trying not to think about the issues that a drunk Phainon might cause now. He was cute at least, but he didn’t know what was the relationship Astraea had with alcohol or with his parents drinking it, and he didn’t know how Phainon usually acted while he was… well, drunk.

Neither of them drank much if at all, but Phainon was the one most prone to do it, even if he had never drank to the point of being that drunk.

“Sure, dear,” Mydei answered, voice soft and patient. “What did you want to ask?”

“Mh…” He paused, moments in which Astraea turned around again and asked carefully to crawl on his lap. As Mydei was about to nod, Phainon unloaded something that he thought wouldn’t be on the table for another few years. “Please, marry me.”

He froze in place, looking at the void with a slightly open mouth.

Marriage wasn’t something that he thought about yet, in all honesty. They just moved in together and, sure, it wouldn’t have changed much if they married tomorrow, but that act had to have some more weight to it.

Yet, Phainon already thought about it enough for it to be the only reason why he would call him on a night out to basically propose to him.

Mydei could only let out relaxed breaths while he tried to process what he just heard and how to lead that conversation, wherever it went and however far it could go, given that he was talking to someone that barely knew what absurdities he was talking about.

His hand grabbed the phone a little more strongly, his brain trying not to take that as the truth of what he wanted to actually talk about. “Marry me? What are you talking about?”

“Please? Pretty please…” he whined from the other end of the phone, sounding genuinely desperate over his answer. “Got the ring and everything, Mydei…”

The ring.

He bought a ring already.

A heavy sigh pushed itself past his lips, thinking about those words again. A marriage proposal and a ring that was probably sitting somewhere in their house. He had to have thought about it for quite some time now if he was already that far into the planning stage.

“That’s…” Mydei let out a shaky breath, trying to steady himself enough to have this conversation. “Sober up before telling me this.”

Another timid tap on his knee made him aware of his child again, hesitantly asking to be let up his lap. Mydei nodded, welcoming him to sit where he wished to, cheek laid against his chest and little fingers holding his free hand, tracing the burn scars that littered the better half of the upper left part of his body.

He thought about his new appearance scaring people away, and it did, but Astraea and Phainon never treated him differently. One repeated how cool he looked and the other would still weave absurdly bad poetry about the features he deemed beautiful about him, inclusing his scars.

“They’re just the proof of what kind of person you are, Mydei,” he had said shortly after they removed the brace he had around his arm. “You’re a gentle, kind person that values other people’s life. Nothing about these scars is scary or ugly.”

Those words echoed in his head whenever others would look at him a little differently. Even if he never truly valued the words of strangers, it was comforting to have another voice in the back of his head telling him that those scars didn’t devalue him as a person.

A groan on the other side of the phone caught his attention again, now attentive and carefully listening to what his boyfriend wanted to tell him with whichever whining he preferred.

“You won’t, right?” he repeated, obviously heartbroken about an answer that Mydei didn’t even give. “I told Hyacine you wouldn’t, but–”

“Phainon,” he interrupted him immediately, unsure of how long he wanted to entertain that spectacle. He knew that he was drunk, but he hated hearing him sounding genuinely hurt if it was something he could help. “It’s not a rejection. Just ask me tomorrow morning.”

Phainon hummed. “But you didn’t say yes… do you hate me, Mydei?”

What a fool he fell in love with. Hating Phainon wasn’t something that he was capable of, for better or worse, and he doubted there was even more than one person that genuinely didn’t like him.

So, Mydei tried to take the situation from another angle.

“What if I was missing you right now?” he questioned, already hearing a loud slam that was far too similar to a hand being smashed on the table. He smiled as he continued. “Would you come home right now if I asked so we can talk about this face to face?”

A few other sounds could be heard, and Mydei tried to make something out of them. A chair being pushed back, then a few people chatting, then the soft flush of a jacket being worn, and lastly a chair being pushed again.

At the same time, Phainon hurriedly answered to Mydei with a series of words that could hardly form a structured sentence, obedient and eager at the same time. “Whatever you want. Immediately. I’ll be there. Promise.”

Mydei let out a small breath resembling a soft laugh, already imagining that imaginary dog tail wagging at his suggestion. “Stay there. I’m going to pick you up.”

“No, no… Cas is still sober. I think.”

“As long as you don’t drive.”

“It’s not even my car… See you super duper soon, Mydeiii…”

His phone started beeping, signaling the end of the call, and Mydei still didn’t know what to make of it.

Phainon thought about marrying him long enough to buy an engagement ring without him knowing. That was… hard to wrap his head around. Even if he jokingly called him husband in the last couple of months, he didn’t think he meant it.

Apparently he did, and now he wasn’t sure how to process it.

Saying that he had never thought about marrying him would be a lie, as it was thinking that things between them would change dramatically after that, especially in their relationship with Astraea, but it felt far too soon– then again, the same could be said for the entirety of their relationship.

“Is Papa being bizarre again?”

Astraea’s voice broke his train of thoughts, maybe for the better. He was thinking too much about something that they could use some bonus time to think about.

“More or less,” he answered, laying the phone back on the table. “He drank too much and now he’s saying nonsense.”

The child set on his lap, wiggling his tiny legs in the air, fairly relaxed for the topic at hand. Mydei knew that he had a hard time back when he still lived with his biological parents and they most likely drank or made use of substances, so he tended not to talk about it with him out of basic respect and empathy.

However, he didn’t want him to fear people who did enjoy drinking, his father included, and he hated having to lie to him, no matter how little it was. He was able to understand a lot of things as long as they were explained with words he knew, and this was no different.

He knew what alcohol was, he knew its effects, Phainon drank in front of him once already. He knew the situation, to an extent.

The little child hummed to himself. “Father used to do it too.” His head turned to Mydei, curious brown eyes staring at him in search of an answer– whether it was positive or negative, it was still unclear. “Will he be mad when he comes home?”

“No, he will just act stupid,” Mydei easily answered, even getting a tiny giggle from below him. “Did your old man do bad things when he drank?”

Old man. That was how they decided to call him during the rare times they talked about him, since Astraea didn’t like the words ‘your father’ being used to refer to his biological father. They both took note of it and decided to call him old man instead.

Mydei perfectly knew that he drank, he had no substantial proof of it past the signs of abandonment that Astraea showed, but he intimately knew the results of an alcoholic and absent father when he saw them. Since his parents almost always paid in cash, no one could answer him about which substances they brought into the house, but he was certain that his precious child had been exposed to some of them.

“He didn’t drink much,” Astraea muttered in such a soft whisper that Mydei feared to not be able to understand it. “Mom was the one angry after drinking. Father had little bags for that. He was quite jealous of them too.”

With every new detail added to his retelling of how his life was like, Mydei’s heart always dropped a little bit further. This time he couldn’t even talk without pausing several times.

He was getting better wit each passing day, he could see it clearly, but there was still a lot of work to do, both for him and Phainon and Mydei. They both wanted to help, but he needed his time and space to process everything too. It was a hard balance to mantain.

Mydei looked down again, noticing just then what he was doing; holding his own hands so strongly that his knuckles turned white, his hands started shaking and light marks were left on his skin wherever his nails could dive in before sliding away to the rest of the back of his hand.

It was so sudden that Mydei froze for a second before processing what was happening.

Almost as if he trained for this exact moment, he rested a hand slightly above the child’s own, reminding him that he wasn’t alone without touching him, in case he didn’t want to be touched directly. It was just a motion in front of his eyes and slight warmth spread across his hand, but it did its job. Astraea looked the hand for a second and then turned to Mydei, far more terrified than he would have liked to see him.

“Hey,” he whispered, voice warm and soft, careful about choosing his words. “I’m sorry for asking something so painful. Can I do something to make the pain a little more manageable?”

Astraea’s lips trembled as he looked at him, brown eyes barely present or grounded in reality. For a second, Mydei feared he would have started hyperventilating or have a panic attack.

Nothing he showed them in his lowest moments was comparable to that, maybe because it had been a while since the last time he had a breakdown as violent as that one.

Then, his face finally morphed into what Mydei was expecting for a few mintues already. Then, the cries filled the room, just as desperate and loud as they should be for being forced to remember those traumatic memories.

Mydei immediately picked him up and hugged him, keeping him as close as possible, letting him wrap his arms and legs around his shoulders and torso. He left a kiss on his temple, caressing his hair with his hand while his cries quickly turned to screams against his shirt.

It never got easier. Knowing how much he suffered just made it harder for him to face the latest one.

He probably barely had anyone to hold onto whenever he cried after everything happened, and now that he did, he was catching up on all those years of fear and pain all at once. Mydei only had the strength to offer that possibility and rub his hand against his back to try and calm him down without much success.

“I’ll never drink, and Phainon just acts stupider than usual on the rare occasions when he does,” he whispered when the cries came in again, replacing yells and screams. “No little bags will ever get into this house either. You’re safe and loved here. Everything will be fine, Astraea, I promise.”

A small fist closed around his shirt and the cries slowly stopped, leaving room for only a few whines and sobs. His hand moved up again, more than ready to offer as many caresses as he could, trying to both ground him and calm him down now that he was a little bit more aware of his surroundings.

“Shh, it’s okay, you’re safe,” he whispered again, now opting to hold him close and stand up, lulling his body in slow, calming motions. “Papa is going to come home and everything will be okay, you don’t need to be afraid anymore. I’m sorry I made you remember things that hurt you this much.”

A little whine came from below him, making sure he would turn his head toward it. Astraea wasn’t crying or smiling, he was just resting there, cheek laying against his shoulder, letting himself be taken care of, feeling all the love he was being given.

It was already a good thing, Mydei told himself. It was better than refusing to be held altogether or run away from him, but he was unsure what to think about his silence. Most likely, he was just tired, but he still wanted to make sure of it.

“Let’s make some tea while we wait for Papa,” he suggested, feeling his head turn around in interest already. “You can finish math tomorrow and then come to sleep with us tonight if you want to.”

Maybe he was being too lenient. He had to learn to sleep in his bed at some point, without going to search for them. However, he was six years old and he just had a breakdown about the very thing that gives him nightmares, so, perhaps, being lenient here is the best choice of action.

Astraea sniffled a couple of times before nodding. “The hot one?”

“Yes, the hot one,” Mydei laughed softly. “Do you want it to be warmer than usual? It’s cold today, how about you go take Fig Stew too?”

The child thought about it for a moment, then his head shook violently. “I wanna stay just with you today. You’re warmer than Fig Stew.”

Mydei’s heart swell, but he didn’t give any further signs of how much he valued that sentence. Perhaps he should have, but he didn’t want to mistake it for something that he had to do more frequently or when he didn’t need it.

Moreover, he wanted to give him a nice, hot tea to enjoy and try to heal all those negative feelings that had been harboring in his heart far more than necessary.

He walked to the kitchen and started to boil the water needed for it, thinking of making one for him as well. After what he had to do to calm down his child and Phainon’s sudden revelation, he certainly needed it.

“Can I get this?” Astraea asked all of a sudden, pointing at peach flavored tea. His voice was meek and a little hurt by the cry he just had, but full of eagerness moving toward that one choice.

Mydei smiled, looking at the little tea bag that his child was pointing at with a quite confused expression. “Peach? Since when do you like peach tea?”

He pouted, seemingly a little embarrassed about that choice. He refuged in his chest just so slightly, waiting to find the right words before speaking. “Auntie Reney likes peaches a lot,” he confessed, “I wanted to try it.”

It made sense and Mydei didn’t have the strength to question him about it anymore, so he dropped the topic, opting to wait in silence for the water to boil instead.

There was some kind of peace about that moment, just spent relaxing while he waited for his boyfriend to come home and his son safely resting in his arms. He would have to let him sit at the table eventually, but it wasn’t going to be a problem for the moment– now he just wanted to be sure that he was fine, safely held and awake.

He wondered if that was how his mother felt too during the first few days after they left their house to run away from his father. He remembered crying, being scared, confused about their current situation, asking where his father was and why they moved so suddenly into the night. He guessed that the situation back then was similar to what Astraea felt now, and he commended his mother even more after trying on his skin what she had to put up with every single day.

Parenting wasn’t easy, he was fully aware of it even before adopting Astraea, but it made him think further about how much his mother gave up on just for his well-being. He could just hope that all that he was doing would have helped Astraea just as much as what his mother did helped him.

And then there was Phainon.

Honestly, the marriage proposal caught him by surprise for the timing of it, but he heard calling him husband a few times already, maybe just to see what his reaction was and if he should move forward with it.

Simply put, he didn’t think too much about those times where he did explicitly call him his husband because he knew that he would have eventually agreed to marrying him. He just didn’t expect it to be so soon, but the longer he thought about it, the faster his excitement about it actually happening grew.

Knowing him, he probably asked several opinions about it first– Sunday and Jing Yuan surely, given their similar situation, then probably Hyacine or Castorice and most definitely his sister. It wasn’t something he thought about on a whim.

“Dad,” Astraea called out, breaking the silence abruptly, “did Papa say something weird on the phone?”

Mydei let out a tired sigh. “More or less. He asked me to marry him.”

He didn’t look at him as he said it, much more focused on what he had to do for that tea when the water eventually started boiling. It was stupid, maybe, but he didn’t know how to sustain eye contact with his own son right at that moment– it was too heavy and far too hard, so he limited himself to listening to him.

“Is it bad?” he asked with a curious voice.

“No, not at all. It’s just a big step and I don’t know what to answer.”

He told him the truth about anything if he could help it, especially something that greatly impacted him as well. Their marriage would change their life at home slightly for the first few weeks and they would be busy preparing for the wedding in the months before the ceremony, the least that he could do was talking about it with him.

“You think too much,” Astraea reflected out loud, his voice still a little more shy than usual. Mydei wondered if it was because of what happened earlier or because he was expressing his thoughts on his father’s behavior, but he let him speak his mind without interrupting him. “I’m really happy you do, because you always think about everything and I always feel safe, but sometimes you get hurt. And I don’t wanna see you suffer.”

He admittedly never thought about it. He was so focused on protecting him from anything that may have hurt him that he didn’t stop to think that Astraea would have noticed how much of a toll it was taking on him. If Phainon wouldn’t had been there in the past year or so, he would have probably ended up in the hospital for exhaustion.

Even then, he wouldn’t have stopped. He knew he wouldn’t. The existence of that little child in his life was so important to him that he refused to do anything less than that– to avoid what he went through and to put an end to the kind of life he was subjected to before meeting him.

Only the best that he could afford was a choice in his book.

Astraea shyly closed a hand around his shirt, right above his chest, and continued, seemingly unaware of the fact that his father was lost in his thoughts.

“The other day… when you said that we would leave Papa if he hurt me… I thought about it, and I was happy you always thought about me.” He bit his lower lip, but Mydei didn't press further, just waiting for him to express his feelings. “But then… what about you, Dad? What if… you want to be with Papa, but you won’t for something that he could do in the future?”

Mydei stared at him after that sentence.

He knew that it wasn't a weird question, but it was bizarre having to hear it from his six year-old son.

However, he knew that he was right. He was so worried for Astraea that he even entertained the thought of Phainon acting like his father and not his own person that he proved time and time again to be. It was wrong of him to assume that he would ever put him or Astraea in harm's way.

He wanted to be with him, he liked being called his husband, he wanted to marry him at some point– whether it was sooner or later it didn't really matter to him. The fact that he was punishing him for something that he didn't even do and implying that he didn't prove himself enough was childish and honestly insulting to him.

And it took his child to figure it out. Surely he needed to be better as a partner and a parent, no matter how he looked at it.

For the moment he just kissed his son's head with a smile on his lips. “You’re too smart for your own good. Thank you for sharing your thoughts with me.”

The child shyly smiled, almost proud of himself, finally letting those heavy, negative emotions go a little farther away from him the slightest bit more. Mydei brought him closer to his face, tiny arms wrapping around his shoulders and a cute giggle escaping from his lips.

At the end of the day, as long as he was doing better, he had to accept every kind of positive development, no matter how tiny or seemingly unimportant. It was going to be a long journey for all of them, and all he could do in a concrete way was support him and act as someone he could rely on and trust in.

There was no immediate healing in that situation, and he had to be graceful with himself enough to put more trust in his child and less unreachable responsibilities on himself.

Mydei turned his head to check on the boiling water, noticing that it was finally gurgling, filling the silence in the room. “And your tea is ready,” he announced. “Go sit where we were before, I’ll come with it ready.”

Astraea nodded as he put him back down, watching as he hurriedly ran to sit by the table and close the books, bringing them to his room as a mean to prepare the table accordingly. Mydei smiled upon seeing it while he thought back to when he taught him how a table had to look when he had to eat something to avoid anything to result as damaged.

The tea was quite quick to prepare after that, and Mydei soon reappeared in the living room by that table, ready to hand the drink over to his child. He seemed skeptical at first for how hot it was, but he was happy to drink something warm after the cry he just had.

It was normal, he probably wanted some kind of warmth and comfort now, but Mydei couldn’t help but worry further. He thought of himself as more than capable in recognizing his son and partner’s feelings and sensations most of the time by then, but he knew that there may be moments where he didn’t know what they thought or did the wrong thing– like he just did by pressing too much on that child’s past.

His eyes looked at him in an almost melancholic way, until he looked up and tilted his head in confusion. “Dad?” he asked with a pretty confident voice this time.

“I apologize,” Mydei whispered. “You know I worry when you tell me about your life before we met.”

He smiled. “It’s easier now. You and Papa are helping a lot.”

“That’s what we’re supposed to do. How have you been recently?”

“School sounds a little scary, but… Papa said you’re here anyway. Even if I go to school, I’ll come home after a few hours.”

“And he’s right. We’re always here for you, even when you’re at school.”

Thankfully, Phainon had already had that talk with him. It was a pretty important change and he needed to make pacts with it, especially since he lived so close so often with them while interacting and talking very little with kids his age. If he could have, Mydei would have had done more to get him more used to it, but ultimately, he had no idea how until recently.

They would just have had to get the band-aid off as soon as possible.

Astraea smiled at him, genuinely grateful to hear those words. “Thank you, Dad.”

Mydei smiled back to him, but he didn’t say anything more. He just threw a few glances at him whenever he would hear him blow on the tea while he held the mug with both of his hands to keep himself a little warmer.

Cute. Relaxing. Relieving.

He had calmed down already, but it was nice to see him actually settle down into his usual behaviors without fear or anxiety in his heart or mind. All that was left now was waiting for Phainon to come back, hopefully with Castorice’s help.

And that proposal.

Mydei kept on thinking about it, but it somehow didn’t bother him nearly as much as it did initially. They already lived together and they had been looking after Astraea for about a year now– on top of it, Phainon came into his life almost as soon as he adopted him and he trusted him more than words could describe. A marriage would only benefit them.

As he thought, his gaze moved back on his child again, now sleeping on the table. A smile sparked on his face, figuring that he had to be exhausted after studying and crying at that hour, well past his bed time.

Mydei exhaled to release a tension that he didn’t know he had. His hand raised his son’s hair from his eyes, sound asleep on the table to a point that he didn’t even feel the slightest movement. He looked peaceful enough to sleep on his own– perhaps he could sleep on his own until Phainon could come back home.

Moving his hand away, he stood up and carefully picked him up, keeping him close as he slowly let him rest his cheek on his shoulder. Astraea didn’t move a single muscle, completely unresponsive.

It was the first time, Mydei thought while he walked to his son’s room. He had always had a light sleep and he often woke up in the middle of the night for the slightest disturbance, but now he laid still, completely trusting in his father’s embrace, sleeping without a care in the world.

Putting him in his bed and tucking him in brought the same reaction from him. No movements, apart rolling on his side to hug Fig Stew, gracefully left there by his father.

At least, that was done. One less thing to think about.

He walked out of his room, almost closing the door to make sure that disturbing lights would come in and wake him up too early the following morning. While they were talking he didn't look at a clock, but it was past midnight already. No wonder he was so tired that he fell asleep on the table.

Mydei tidied the table, putting Astraea's tea in the kitchen, saving it for tomorrow morning, right after finishing his own. He didn't drink much of it and he didn't like throwing away perfectly good food.

A sudden click by the door and a groan that he would be able to recognize anywhere signaled him that Phainon came home, probably more drunk than he had ever seen him. It wasn't a problem, but it would have been difficult to force him to settle down and sleep.

“Mydei…” he lamented, stumbling across the living room. He couldn't walk straight, but he didn't give up on advancing toward him regardless.

“Calm down,” Mydei told him with a sweet voice as soon as he managed to catch him. “You need to sleep.”

“Mh, you didn't answer me yet…”

“Ask me tomorrow and–”

“I want the answer now. Please, Mydeimos.”

The insistence in those sentences almost made him lose his composure. Almost. He knew better than giving into his drunken requests. No matter how convincing he sounded in his pleas, he wasn’t in his right mind at the moment– even if he answered him, he would have to repeat it the following morning.

“You won't remember,” he pointed out, hopeful to push back his inevitable doom. “You’re not thinking straight, Phainon. Sit down at least.”

“Tell meeeee…” he lamented, struggling to see that groan through to the end. “I really, really love you. I want to call you my husband…”

Mydei sighed, already tired of the situation. “You can.”

“So you will!”

“I didn't say anything. But you can call me your husband regardless.”

It wasn’t like he had never done it in the past month or so anyway. The thing that shocked him was how promptly Phainon had already thought about buying the ring itself, rather than the proposal or his insistence in wanting to be his husband.

His boyfriend hummed rather loudly, throwing his head back. “So what's the answer… why should I call you my husband if you don't have an engagement ring, Mydeimos?”

“You're so annoying when you're drunk.” He picked him up, uncaring on where his head would fall, if on his shoulder or if he was already a dead weight. It turned out to be the latter, only getting an annoyed sigh when the upper part of his body plopped past his shoulder, hanging off of the ground almost lifelessly. Mydei huffed only when he threw him on the bed. “Sleep it off and I'll answer you.”

Phainon’s eyes flicker with newfound hope, shining of a light of their own even in the already illuminated room. “Will you? Really?”

“Yes,” Mydei sighed, quickly changing his clothes and lying next to him. “Sleep now.”

He was honestly tired, after the day he just had. The last thing he wanted was having to stay up much longer because his boyfriend was so drunk that he didn’t know what he was saying, since that was what was happening at the moment. He had no filter whatsoever and he was more than wide awake.

“I want a baby.”

Exactly the kind of talk that Mydei wanted to avoid.

For the record, he didn’t mind planning a sibling for Astraea, but there were pretty important barriers to that– firstly, they had limited money at the moment, secondly, they were all going through important changes and he didn’t want to overwhelm Astraea with something like that too and thirdly, it was biologically impossible for them to just decide to have a child.

Mydei shuffled below the covers, turning on a side to look at him. He was still holding hope in his eyes and, as much as he hated breaking it, there was nothing he could do about it. “We have a son already,” he only whispered, tracing his cheek with the back of his index finger.

“I want another one.” Phainon blinked, almost as if that news just broke his heart and he was trying to find a solution to reality not meeting his expectations. “Can you give one to me?”

“No. I don't have a vagina and neither do you, stop saying nonsense.”

“But Astraea will feel lonely…”

“We'll get him a dog, then. We don't have the time or money for a second child, you perfectly know that.”

It was rude, perhaps, but a second child was the last thing they needed at the moment. Maybe in the future, but not now. A dog was the closest thing he could suggest to let him relax and settle down for the rest of the night.

“Mh… I wouldn't be against that either,” he hummed with a dumb smile on his face that Mydei found far too charming for the situation at hand.

“You love dogs, I know.” Mydei humored him, even if he knew that it wasn’t what he should have done, given how chatty he was. With a sigh, he switched off the light and reached out, planting a kiss on his boyfriend’s lips, not expecting a kiss back from him in those conditions. “Try to sleep now, beloved.”

A low whine echoed in the room. “I like when you call me like that…”

A dog. His boyfriend was a dog in his past life and now he had to suffer the consequences.

“I know,” he hugged him a little closer, both for himself and to get him to drop the attempts at talking at that hour and while he was still drunk. He tucked his face in the crook of his neck, feeling his heart growing fonder of the moment they were sharing, despite the rather annoying ciscumnstance. “I'll answer you tomorrow morning, I promise.”

Phainon hummed, sounding more satisfied of the answer now. “Thank you…”

After that, silence filled the room entirely, only leaving the soft breathing between the two of them to be able to be heard. Phainon started snoring softly after a few minutes, most likely both because he was exhausted and for the alcohol still circulating in his body.

It was nice. Just a day like any other, but with enough happening that it had splashes of vivid colors all over it. Unlike how he felt before they barged into his life, he didn’t see a grayscale anymore even when they were seengly settling down and they were no longer experiencing the first few months of a relationship. He was convinced that he would have kept seeing everything that way, no matter how much time it passed– not even during the first few months with Hephaestion felt as exciting and vivid as the ones with Phainon.

He hoped that it was the same for him as well.

He hoped that they could get that dog, get married, see Astraea off to school trips and witness him growing up into his own person. He hoped to do all of it with Phainon.

Perhaps it was too heavy of a thought for the hour that it was, if he had to judge by the slight clech around his heart. He sifted slightly, ending on top of Phainon, but he didn’t even flinch from the sudden movement– instead, he pleasantly hummed, weakly closing his fist on the back of his shirt to keep him close.

The heat of his body was enough to lull Mydei to sleep, already exhausted from the rest of the day, but that meant that it was the absence of the same thing that woke him up the following morning.

He didn’t even register what happened or how long he slept, all he knew was that Phainon scrolled him off violently to the ther side of the bed and now he was wide awake with far too many curses reserved for his so-called boyfriend.

“Mydei,” the culprit called out, crawling next to him. “Mydei.” Hands grabbed his arm and started shaking him, not helping the annoyance that was quickly rising within his body. “Mydei!”

By then, he could be furious and push him off or scold him, but he didn’t. There was no point in any of it, after all. He just took a deep breath and he forced his head to turn around, staring right at his panicked face. “What.”

“What did I tell you last night?”

“Nothing. Just that you wanted to marry me and got the ring already.”

How could he forget? He gave him a headache as soon as he mentioned it. He spent hours thinking about it in circles, all the while his son was having a trauma-related breakdown in front of him and his boyfriend was who knows where and drunk out of his mind. He didn’t think he would ever forget a single detail of that night even if he got thrown out of the window and fell face-first into the concrete.

And here his boyfriend was, tearing up because he accindentally said it over the phone to the point that he thought that waking him up like that was necessary.

Mydei sighed, letting go of whatever kind of rage he had toward him. It was useless and he couldn’t bear seeing him suffer pathetically like that when he could do something about it. He extended a hand to offer a gentle caress on his cheek that he could hold onto, before asking with a soft voice, “Did you mean it?”

“I wanted it to be a surprise!” he answered, clearly frustrated by the situation. “I planned not to say anything for a while, I just knew that I wanted to marry you, but it was way too soon and now you’re mad at me and–”

“Well, it wasn't something that I expected you to ask,” Mydei immediately cut him off, not liking where the conversation was heading. He was mad, but not for his proposal… he was mad because he threw him off the bed far too early into the morning. “But did you mean it?”

Phainon blinked at him a couple of times, a little confused. “Yes.”

“Then, my answer is yes. I will marry you.”

“Really?”

“Why wouldn't I?”

“I mean, it's a little too soon…”

Mydei sighed, now finding that argument far too repetitive and one that he found tremendously annoying. “Phainon, we've been living together after mere months of meeting each other. At this point, this is our average pace.”

A couple of second went by before Phainon could say anything, almost as if those words were a revelation that he wasn’t expecting to hear from him. After what ran before them were only whispers for a few more moments, he pushed himself up. “I’ll get the ring.”

He disappeared as quickly as Mydei’s sleep was interrupted and, honestly, what was he supposed to do or say about it? That was how Phainon acted whenever he was excited or anxious about something, there was nothing he could ever do to change his behavior.

At least, now he could force himself up from the bed and check what hour it was, since Phainon refused to let in any sort of light except for the one coming from the living room. Slowly, he walked to the door of the bedroom, squeezing his eyes to force them to work properly despite the rough way they were jolted up that morning.

“Why is Papa excited?”

He suddenly looked down to find Astraea already dressed up properly with the clothes he often wore in the house, signaling that it probably was well into the morning and not as early as he initially feared. At least, that was good news.

Mydei crouched down, sensing that he would have had to explain what was going to happen again. Even if he did the night prior, he wanted it to be crystal clear for him too. “Papa is so excited because he asked me to marry him and I said yes. Do you know what that means?”

The child stilled to talk about it. “That you'll buy pretty outfits and be forever annoying to each other?”

Of course Cipher got to him before he could.

“I need to ask Cipher to put a filter on when she talks to you.”

“Is it not what happens?”

He laughed softly, caressing him on the top of his head. “It just means he will be your father in a more official way,” he explained. “And, you get to wear a pretty dress for the ceremony, yes.”

Astraea bounced on his place slightly, obviously excited about the shopping that they all will have to do for such an occasion. Splashes of yellow and pink filled the room once again, cleansing away all the annoyance he might have had when he woke up, while the news slowly settled in.

That marriage was something concrete, and he could reach out to it without many worries.

Some were still there and he knew that anything could happen, but that wasn’t something he had to think about too much now. Phainon was a nice man and the only one he would ever want to spend his time forever with, and that had to be enough for the moment.

“So,” Phainon announced himself, coming back with the ring and sitting down next to them. Mydei’s amber eyes fell on it, but he refused to let himself observe it further, giving his boyfriend the reins of the situation. “Do you want to marry me?”

It was hard to look straight faced with a proposal like that, just casually mentioning it while he sat down to him on the ground, but, somehow, Mydei saw it through. “Yeah,” he breathed out. “Definitely.”

Phainon just handed him the ring, obviously completely unaware on how something like this usually went. Detaching himself from a situation was something he was used to do, and it looked like he was doing the same here. He remembered he sounded similarly when that little girl died in the hospital, but he didn’t expect to hear it again. Apparently, some emotions still were too much for him, no matter if they were positive or negative.

However, he didn’t mention anything about it with him. He didn’t need it and he had already went through a humiliating morning, so he just took the ring off of his hand. Staring at it, he noticed that it seemed a pretty common engagement ring, of a silver color and three clear, transparent, shining minerals on a side of it.

It was nothing short of majestic.

“Pretty!” Astraea exclaimed, eyes shining as he looked at it from his place next to both of them.

Phainon gently wrapped an arm around his body, pulling him on his lap until he sat down on it without any whine. “It was quite expensive, but I made sure to buy one of the rings on sale,” he explained calmly, initially unfazed from his son squirming a little, only to look at him again. “Let Dad see it first, okay? I made him worry enough as it is, the least I can do is let him process it.”

Astraea tilted his head, mildly confused. “Is it that important? It’s just a question.”

“There are important questions sometimes,” Phainon said, caressing his hair. “This is one of them, and Dad needs a few seconds.”

After a couple of seconds, the child settled back, listening to his father’s words. Mydei stared at them for a second, reminding himself that was how Phainon was sometimes– extreme mood swings, detachment from his own feelings, feeling so strong that might be overwhelming for the people around him too. None of it was ever aimed at him or Astraea, but it was there.

It wouldn’t have been a problem. He had lived with it all his life and he noticed he was searching for therapists in the area in the last couple of weeks. He probably was fully aware of it already.

“It is really pretty,” Mydei finally said, looking at the ring around his finger again with a soft smile that he couldn’t manage to hide. Raising his head again, he noticed Phainon letting some emotion shine through him again, and he took the opportunity to lean in and kiss him right on his lips without leaving him room to react. “Thank you, beloved.”

Phainon’s face finally blushed with some color and, even if Mydei knew perfectly why it took him this long, he wished he would let himself feel happiness more often, even if it could be slightly debilitating sometimes. He would have liked seeing him like that more often.

As they looked in each other’s eyes, glittering, shining blue crystals staring at warm amber, a disgusted sound made itself known below them. Mydei shifted his head slightly, suddenly remembering Astraea sitting on Phainon’s lap from earlier.

The little child didn’t even try to hide that expression, looking at them with sheer disgust– so much that Mydei couldn’t hide a little snicker. “You'll understand someday,” he said, affectionately ruffling his hair.

He only groaned, limbs moving uncontrollably as if he had a visceral reaction to that kiss. “I don’t wanna!” he proclaimed, right before running off to his room.

Mydei wondered if it was about the kiss itself or the situation. It was no secret by then that he understood more than he let on, so it wasn’t entirely impossible that he thought that they would need some time alone– and if that meant he didn’t have to sit there and be forced to watch them kiss, it was probably a win-win situation for everyone.

“So…” Phainon suddenly whispered, “now what?”

What a stupid question.

“Now we just go on together.” Mydei wore a calm smile on his face, caressing the ring on his finger with his thumb while he turned around to look at him again. “We go to work, Astraea starts going to school, we keep contacts with our families and friends… Wasn't that always the plan?”

Phainon leaned back as he sighed. A smile appeared on his face, finally content. “Yeah. You’re right.”

Mydei could agree with that sentiment.

They didn’t need some greater objective now. They were doing fine enough, just existing together, and Mydei could see it clearly. Marriage or not, there wasn’t a thing in the world that would make him leave either of them if he could help it. This was far too gentle, beautiful and colorful for him to give up on it.

A second later, he found himself resting on Phainon’s shoulder, quietly closing his eyes, feeling the tiredness settling in again. An arm kept him close and a hand reached out for him, making the heat and kindness in those gestures impossible to ignore. Compared to a couple of years prior, this was something so precious that he wouldn’t have let go of, no matter how much time passed by.

“Rest if you’re tired, I’ll take care of everything else.” Phainon kissed him on the top of his head as he said it. “I’m sorry I woke you up like that.”

A faint smile appeared on his face, both for the sense of winning against his boyfriend– or, well, fiancèe now– and for how delicate his words were.

He could let him take care of it now. He could enjoy this life that he built thanks to the presence of so many people in it. He could listen to him and slip away into another dream.

And so, he did.

Mydei fell asleep on his shoulder without noticing or realizing when and how he was moved from that position. However, he didn’t dream. He didn’t need to, after all– everything that he wished for was at an arm’s reach and he intended to bathe in that happiness and kindness that they all had for each other for a long time.
